Step-3.7-Flash's NVFP4 checkpoint (`stepfun-ai/Step-3.7-Flash-NVFP4`, revision `4275532`, NVIDIA ModelOpt recipe) stores the routed-expert weights and their per-block scales already stacked on an expert axis (3-D tensors). The converter's NVFP4 path only knows the 2-D per-expert layout, so the model does not convert. This PR:

1. `conversion/base.py`: adds a branch for `moe.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight` tensors whose weight and scale pair are three-dimensional. It applies the existing 2-D NVFP4 packer per expert slice and emits the same tensor set as the per-expert path (packed weights, `.scale` per expert, and the calibrated `input_scale` sidecars).
2. `src/models/step35.cpp`: passes the model's `ffn_{up,gate,down}_exps_s` tensors to `build_moe_ffn` in the main decoder and in the MTP decoder. Without them the model loads and produces garbage.

**Activation scales.** ModelOpt's NVFP4 recipe for this model enables both weight and input quantizers, and the converter keeps the per-expert `input_scale` sidecars, which the loader already creates as `ffn_*_exps_in_s`. The graph does not use them. llama.cpp quantizes activations at run time with scales computed from the activations: Q8_0 on CPU, Q8_1 on the CUDA vector path and on pre-Blackwell tensor cores, and NVFP4 with a per-row global scale on Blackwell's block-scaled FP4 path. So the operation is dynamic W4A8 or W4A4, not W4A16. It differs from ModelOpt only in using a per-row dynamic activation global scale instead of the calibrated per-tensor one. This patch does not change that. It only makes the stacked weights convert and forwards the per-expert **weight** scales.

**Validation** (RTX 5090, master `bd4f514`, MSVC, CUDA 13.0, `sm_120a`):
- Converted the checkpoint above with `--outtype q8_0 --no-nextn` (114.3 GB). The output is tensor-for-tensor identical (SHA-256 of every one of the 1006 tensors, no metadata differences) to the file produced on 2 September with an earlier shape of this patch, on which the model has been in daily use and evaluated since.
- Served the file on this build and on that earlier build: `llama-perplexity --kl-divergence` over 8 × 4096 tokens on an English code text and a Portuguese prose text gives mean KLD 0.000000 (max 6.6e-5), same top-1 token 99.99 %.
- With the in-file MTP head (`--spec-type draft-mtp`), a greedy 700-token generation is identical on both builds, with identical draft acceptance (446 / 573).
- Earlier, on the same file: a 300-item paired evaluation within 0.004 nats of the UD-Q4_K_XL quantization of the same model.

Test: `tests/test-convert-nvfp4-stacked.py`, a CPU-only pytest on synthetic tensors that checks the stacked packer against the per-expert packer (byte equality, shapes, expert order). It needs torch and the repository's `gguf-py`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

## Motivation
In modern agentic workflows (e.g., ReAct, function calling, tool use), models spend significant wall-clock time autoregressively generating tokens just to make discrete routing decisions (e.g., spelling out `<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_weather"...}`).

## What is the proposed solution
A special agent mode to fasten tool calls through "Jev-like" hybrid mode

Currently, when tools are provided in `llama-server` or `llama-cli`:
1. The engine prefills the prompt.
2. It enters the autoregressive decode loop ($O(N)$ sequential token passes) using either GBNF grammar constraints or hoping the chat template emits tool tokens correctly.
3. If the model chooses *not* to call a tool, or chooses a simple tool, we still pay the latency penalty of sequential token decoding and grammar state-machine transitions before knowing the routing outcome.

Because the prompt prefill pass **already computes the full KV cache and logits for the final prompt token**, we can resolve binary tool-gating decisions and tool-name enums in **$O(1)$ single forward passes** via logit slicing, falling back seamlessly to standard text generation without wasting the prefilled KV cache.

---

## Proposed Architectural Flow

```
[Prompt + Registered Tools] 
          │
          ▼
   llama_decode() (Prefill)
          │
          ▼
Inspect logits of last token: P(Tool Call) vs P(Chat/Text)
          │
   ┌──────┴────────────────────────────────┐
   ▼                                       ▼
P(Chat) > Threshold               P(Tool) > Threshold
   │                                       │
   │ (Zero KV cache waste)                 ▼
   │ Direct stream to user        Slice logits over registered 
   │ (Standard Autoregressive)    tool names: P(tool_1...tool_N)
                                           │
                                  ┌────────┴─────────────────┐
                                  ▼                          ▼
                         Bounded Enums/Booleans     Unbounded String Args
                         (Parallel Logit Slices)    (Switch to GBNF / AR loop)
```

### 1. Zero-Cost Gating Check (Prefill Inspection)
Right after `llama_decode()` on the prompt batch, before initializing the autoregressive decode loop:
* Inspect the logits of the final sequence position (`llama_get_logits_ith(ctx, -1)`).
* Measure the probability mass of the model's tool delimiter token (e.g., `<tool_call>`, `[TOOL]`, or `{` depending on the active Jinja chat template) against normal text tokens.
* **If text generation is chosen:** Continue the decode loop immediately. The KV cache is already fully initialized; overhead is virtually $0$ ms.

### 2. $O(1)$ Discrete Tool Selection
If the model indicates a tool call:
* Instead of sequentially generating the tool name string (e.g., `"name": "get_weather_data"` across multiple decode steps), the engine can mask the logits over the first tokens of the user-registered tools:
  $$\text{Softmax}\left(\text{logits}[\text{id}(\text{tool}_1), \text{id}(\text{tool}_2), \dots]\right)$$
* Select the candidate with highest calibrated confidence in a single step.

### 3. Argument Resolution Split
* **Bounded arguments (Enums, Booleans):** Handled via single-pass logit slicing.
* **Unbounded arguments (Raw strings, free text):** Switch back to standard autoregressive generation, with GBNF constrained only to that specific string argument.

---

## Key Benefits
1. **Dramatic Latency Reduction in Agent Loops:** Eliminates 10–50 sequential autoregressive steps for routing decisions, reducing decision latency to the prefill time (~15–40 ms on modern hardware).
2. **Zero Wasted Computation on Fallback:** Because the prompt prefill already took place, falling back to standard conversational text streaming incurs zero recomputation or KV-cache invalidation.
3. **No Syntax Failures for Tool Routing:** Eliminates malformed tool name keys and invalid enum tool selections at the root.

---



## Alternatives Considered
* **Full GBNF Grammar Decoding:** Guarantees syntax correctness, but incurs full sequential decode latency ($O(N)$ forward passes) even for basic if/else decisions.
* **Draft Model Speculative Decoding:** Requires loading a second model into VRAM and doesn't solve the structural inefficiency of using autoregression for discrete enum selection.


### Motivation

Save a lot of inference and compute when performing tool calls

### Possible Implementation


1. **`llama-server` (`/v1/chat/completions`):**
   * Introduce an optional flag, e.g., `--speculative-tool-gating` or a request parameter `"tool_choice": "auto_fast"`.
   * If enabled, check the top-K logits of the prefill output against the model's configured tool-call trigger tokens before attaching the full GBNF grammar parser.
2. **C API (`llama.h`):**
   * Expose a helper utility or sampler stage:
     ```c
     // Evaluates probabilities exclusively across a masked subset of candidate tokens
     // on the current prefilled context position without advancing the decode sequence.
     LLAMA_API void llama_sample_token_distribution(
         struct llama_context * ctx,
         const llama_token    * candidate_tokens,
         size_t                 n_candidates,
         float                * out_probs
     );
     ```

### Edge Case: Multi-Token Tool Names & Shared Prefixes

To handle tools that share initial tokens (e.g., `get_weather` vs `get_stock`):

## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

items.body:
## Environment

- **llama.cpp**: master `8144f31` (2026-08-23) + also reproduced on release b10488 (Windows CUDA 13.3 build)
- **OS**: Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04 (both tested, same cliff)
- **GPU**: RTX 4080 SUPER 16GB, driver 591.86 (CUDA 13.1), nvcc 13.1, sm_89
- **Model**: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` UD-Q3_K_XL (12.2GB); also reproduced with UD-IQ4_XS (13.3GB) and IQ4_XS (14.6GB)
- **Backend**: CUDA, single GPU

## Symptom

With the model **fully resident on GPU** (zero "assigned to device CPU" lines, verified in logs), decode (tg) speed collapses non-linearly once the KV position exceeds roughly 80K tokens — from ~33 t/s at 68K position to **1.4 t/s (714 ms/token) at 91K position**, or outright timeouts. **Prompt processing (pp) stays fast (~1300 t/s) at the same positions.** Zero-context decode is normal (~38-39 t/s) on every configuration below.

## Reproduction matrix (WSL2, llama-server)

Command shape:
```
./llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -ngl 999 --load-mode none \
    -c <CTX> [-fa on] -ctk <Q> -ctv <Q>
```
Then send a chat completion with a ~91K-token filler prompt and `max_tokens=100`.

| Config | VRAM fit (CPU overrides) | pp @91K fill | tg @91K position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-c 131072 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits, 0 CPU lines | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` | fits | fast | **timed out (>25 min)** |
| `-c 98304  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **timed out** |
| `-c 73728  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **33.1 t/s @ 68K position ✅** |

Position sweep with the last config (UD-Q3_K_XL, q8 KV, no FA):

| KV position (prompt tokens) | decode t/s (server-side timing) |
|---|---|
| 45,574 | 35.6 |
| 60,309 | 33.9 |
| 68,642 | 33.1 |
| 91,077 | **1.4 (or timeout)** |

## Key observations

1. **The cliff is positional, not a memory-spill issue.** All 96K/128K configs above report 0 CPU tensor overrides and normal free VRAM headroom; KV quantization level (q4/q5/q8) and `-fa on/off` make no difference to the cliff. Only the *position* matters.
2. **pp is unaffected at the same positions** (~1300 t/s for the 91K fill), so this is specific to the decode path.
3. The drop is far steeper than any plausible O(n) attention-scan cost: 68K→91K position is a 1.34x context increase but a **~24x decode slowdown**.
4. Server logs at the cliff show `eval time = 1055.41 ms / 300 tokens (0.95 tokens per second)` with `graphs reused = 298`, i.e. CUDA graph reuse continues normally while per-token latency explodes.
5. Also reproduced on the same hardware under Windows native (b10488) at large `-c`, so it is not WSL2-specific.

## Suspected area

Decode-path attention over long KV for the hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers (Qwen3.8 / qwen35-family). Possibly a fallback/slow kernel engaged past some KV extent threshold. Possibly related family: #27442 (empty generation >16K on Metal for qwen35moe hybrids), #27572 (draft acceptance collapse with multi-ubatch batches).

## Logs

Full `llama-server` logs for the 131072/q4/FA and 73728/q8/no-FA runs available on request (happy to attach — they contain per-token timing lines, tensor placement, and KV buffer sizes).
items.title: Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid Gated DeltaNet): decode throughput collapses ~25x at context positions >~80K while prompt processing stays fast

items.body:
Hi, first of all thank you for llama.cpp — it runs my daily driver bot and
it's great. I'm fairly new to debugging this deep, so please let me know if
I'm holding it wrong or if there's a diagnostic you'd like me to run. Happy
to bisect or test anything.

## Name and Version

```
$ llama --version
version: 0.4.1-dev (build 11046, commit 60081bb2b)
built with Clang 19.1.7 for Linux x86_64
```

## Operating systems

Linux (CachyOS / Arch family, x86_64, RTX 3060 12GB, CUDA)

## Which modules are affected

llama-server, libllama (core library)

## Command line

```
llama serve -m /mnt/D/Mymodels/gemma412b/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --mmproj /mnt/D/Mymodels/gemma412b/mmproj-BF16.gguf \
  --model-draft /mnt/D/Mymodels/gemma412b/mtp-gemma-4-12B-it.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 \
  --fit off -ngl 99 -fa on -c 16384 --load-mode none --jinja -np 1 \
  -ub 8192 -b 1024 --image-min-tokens 1024
```

Model files: Gemma 12B IT QAT (`UD-Q4_K_XL`), matching `mmproj-BF16.gguf`,
and a community MTP draft (`mtp-gemma-4-12B-it.gguf`).

## Problem description & steps to reproduce

The server serves text perfectly (1000+ token generations, ~70-80 tok/s
with the MTP draft, never a hiccup), but **dies when serving images
repeatedly**. It takes a while — roughly 5+ images exchanged one by one in a
chat session — and then the process is gone with no error line in the log.
My shell just reports:

```
fish: Job 1, 'llama serve -m /mnt/D/Mymodels/…' terminated by signal SIGKILL (Forced quit)
```

There are two flavors of this I've seen, possibly related:

**Flavor A (loud, understood):** with a small `-ub` (default 512), the first
large image kills the server immediately with:

```
llamacpp/src/llama-context.cpp: GGML_ASSERT((cparams.causal_attn ||
cparams.n_ubatch >= n_tokens_all) && "non-causal attention requires
n_ubatch >= n_tokens") failed
```

That one makes sense to me — image embeddings need non-causal attention and
don't fit the micro-batch. Raising `-ub` fixes it deterministically.

**Flavor B (silent, the actual report):** with `-ub` raised (2024, then
8192), the assert is gone and dozens of image tasks complete fine —
including 2000+ token ones — but after sustained image traffic the process
still dies with SIGKILL and *nothing* in the log. 8GB+ free on both VRAM and
system RAM at the time, so it's not OOM as far as I can tell. Bigger `-ub`
delays the death but doesn't prevent it, which makes me think something
accumulates per image (context keeps the image tokens; my client re-sends
history) until some ceiling is hit on a path that doesn't print.

Repro sketch: serve the above command, send images one by one through
`/v1/chat/completions` (screenshots, ~1000 tokens of image content each,
history retained so context grows), wait. For me it dies after a handful of
images at `-ub 2024` and noticeably later at `-ub 8192`.

## What I already tried (and failed)

- Raising `-ub` 512 → 2024 → 8192 (and now testing 16384): fixes flavor A
  completely, only *delays* flavor B.
- `--image-min-tokens 1024` / default: crash happens either way once enough
  images accumulate (kept at 1024 for small-image detail).
- Disabling the MTP draft was my first suspect, but the assert deaths
  reproduce with **zero speculative flags** on plain commands, so spec
  decoding can't be the required cause. Text + spec decoding is flawless.
- Checked VRAM (`nvidia-smi`) and RAM (`free -h`) at max context: 8GB+ free
  on both. Not resource exhaustion as far as I can see.
- Text-only sessions of any length: never crash. It is image traffic
  specifically.

Possibly related issues I found (couldn't quite match mine, but close):
#22867 (MTP + vision slot corruption), #21550 (Gemma crashes when
image-min-tokens raised), #24366 (Gemma MTP buffer issue), #21461 (the
ubatch assert history).

## First Bad Commit

Unknown — I only run recent builds (11046). The ubatch assert threads above
go back a while, but the silent flavor I can only vouch for on this build.

## Excerpt from my run (`-ub 8192 --image-min-tokens 1024`)

Full command at the top of this report. Load looks clean, tasks complete
fine for a long while (trimming ~30 healthy tasks here), then SIGKILL out of

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 0.3.0-dev (build 1, commit 0f3a71b)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Reproduced against `ggml-org/llama.cpp` commit `0f3a71be15af836d277c9f918adfafb45732677e`.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```
llama-server \
  -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --model-draft mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-mtp \
  --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  --parallel 1 \
  -c 262144 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -fa on \
  --slot-save-path /slot-cache
```

### Problem description

`POST /slots/{id}?action=save|restore` only persists `ctx_tgt` (via
`llama_state_seq_save_file`/`llama_state_seq_load_file`) — on a deployment
running speculative decoding (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`), the draft
model's own context (`ctx_dft`) is never captured or restored at all.

This is a separate, narrower gap from #25913 (checkpoints not persisted,
addressed by #26004): even once #26004 lands, a restored slot's draft
model only gets its state back if a checkpoint happened to already exist
at save time (checkpoints carry their own `data_dft`) — a short
conversation that hasn't hit its first checkpoint yet restores with an
empty draft-model KV cache and no fallback. The raw, currently-live
`ctx_dft` state is simply discarded on save, independent of checkpoint
existence.

Not directly observable as a crash or an error — the restore reports
success either way — but on a speculative-decoding deployment it means
the draft model silently starts cold after every restore whenever no
checkpoint happens to cover the request, undermining part of the benefit
`--slot-save-path` is meant to provide alongside #26004's fix.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start `llama-server` with a draft model (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`)
   and `--slot-save-path`.
2. Send a short prompt (short enough that it completes before the first
   context checkpoint would be created) with `cache_prompt: true`.
3. `POST /slots/0?action=save`.
4. Inspect the save file: only the `ctx_tgt` payload
   (`llama_state_seq_save_file`'s own format) is present; there is no
   companion draft-model state anywhere.
5. `POST /slots/0?action=erase`, then `POST /slots/0?action=restore`.
6. The restore succeeds and reports the correct token count, but
   `ctx_dft` was never touched — the draft model's KV cache is empty,
   identical to a slot that just came up cold, regardless of what #26004
   restores for `ctx_tgt`/checkpoints.

### First bad commit

Not a regression — `SLOT_SAVE`/`SLOT_RESTORE` have never captured
`ctx_dft`; this predates both this report and #26004.

### Relationship to other issues/PRs

- #25913 / #26004: separate root cause (missing checkpoint persistence
  for `ctx_tgt`'s reuse-validity check), already well covered there. This
  report is about `ctx_dft` specifically, which #26004 does not touch.
- We have a working fix (raw `ctx_dft` capture/restore via
  `llama_state_seq_get_size_ext`/`get_data_ext`/`set_data_ext`, stored as
  a companion `<save-file>.dft`, verified live on a production
  Vulkan/AMD-APU draft-mtp deployment) and are happy to open it as a PR,
  either standalone or as a follow-up once #26004 merges (to avoid
  competing for review attention on the same file/handlers at once) —
  see our comment on #26004 for details.
items.title: Misc. bug: /slots save/restore never persists the draft-model context (ctx_dft) on speculative-decoding deployments

### Name and Version
0.3.0-dev (build 37, commit 8e53fce), built with AppleClang 21.0.0 for Darwin arm64 (Metal, default flags, Release)

### Operating systems
Mac

### GGML backends
Metal

### Hardware
2x Apple M1 Max (24-core and 32-core GPU), 64 GB unified memory each — reproduced on both

### Models
- unsloth-style AD-3.84bpw-IQ4_XS-M64 (28 shards) — 16K/64K OK, 128K FAIL
- AD-4.27bpw-Q4_K_M-M64 (33 shards) — 64K FAIL (q4v4 KV) / 16K FAIL (q8v8 KV)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce
llama-server, single slot, GPU flash attention (auto). With prompts beyond a config-dependent threshold:
- prefill completes normally (e.g. 118-140 tok/s at 64K)
- decode emits exactly 1 token then stops (EOS): `eval time = ... / 1 tokens`, answer empty
- server returns HTTP 200 — silent failure, no error anywhere
- at/near the threshold the failure is STOCHASTIC: same server, same config, same prompt size → 64K x3 = PASS, PASS, FAIL on consecutive runs
- threshold moves with model quant (Q4_K_M << IQ4_XS), KV quant (q8v8+b256: 16K vs q4v4+b512: 64K), and possibly n_ctx window size (64K probes 3/3 @ n_ctx 208896 vs 2/3 @ n_ctx 262144, same 64K prompts)
- with mixed-precision KV (-ctk q8_0 -ctv q4_0) Metal rejects FA → attention falls back to CPU → 200K needle tests pass 3/3 (correct but slow) — so the failure is specific to the GPU attention path
- `-fa off` cannot be tested with quantized KV ("quantized V cache requires flash_attn to be enabled"); with f16 KV + `-fa off` decode fails immediately with `Compute error. off = 0, n_batch = 256, ret = -3` on the first token
- memory pressure excluded (failures observed with < 600 MB swap)
- needle-in-haystack probe (3 pins at 10/50/90% depth), warmup, temperature 0

Matrix (all llama-server, GPU FA, IQ4_XS unless noted):
| model | KV | -b/-ub | n_ctx | 16K | 64K | 128K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IQ4_XS | q4v4 | 512 | 208896 | 3/3 | 3/3,3/3,3/3 | 0/3 (1 tok) |
| IQ4_XS | q4v4 | 1024 | 208896 (A machine, +ngram spec) | — | 3/3 (32K/64K) | 0/3 (1 tok) |
| IQ4_XS | q8v8 | 1024 | 262144 | — | 3/3,3/3,0/3 (stochastic!) | not reached |
| Q4_K_M | q4v4 | 512 | 208896 | — | 0/3 | — |
| Q4_K_M | q8v8 | 256 | 208896 | 0/3 | — | — |

### First Bad Commit
Unknown; qwen4exp support landed via #27742 (2026-08-27) — all failures observed on builds containing it. **Retested on master `df03399` (0.4.0-dev build 300, contains #27941, #28023, #28098): the bug reproduces identically.** 64K x1 = 3/3 (prefill 153.8 tok/s, decode 11.1 — sparse-FA perf improvements visible), 128K x1 = **0/3, decode 0.0 (1 tok)** — same signature, same threshold. So #27941 (block position keying), #28023 (indexer head summation) and Metal sparse FA do not resolve it.

### Related
#27856 (HIP: depth-decay only, output correct), #28734 (CUDA: dense top-k TODO), #25722 (Metal: degenerate-token silent empty output, different arch), #21450 (Metal mixed KV rejection — the mechanism that pushes attention to CPU and avoids this bug)

*Disclosure: issue text prepared with AI assistance (GLM-5.3-Flash via ZCode), verified against server logs and raw probe JSONs.*

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: b10752 (b96806d96)
```
Container image `ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-vulkan`, run in router mode
(`--models-preset`), one child `llama-server` per model.

### Operating systems

Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic)

### GGML backends

Vulkan (Mesa RADV)

### Hardware

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 — Radeon 8060S Graphics (RADV STRIX_HALO, gfx1151),
120 GiB GTT, unified memory.

### Models

`Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf` (dense, 27.3B params, `n_ctx_train = 262144`), which
carries MTP layers.

### Problem description

With `--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp` and a large `--ctx-size`, the server
fails **every** request — including a 13-token prompt — dying within ~2s of the
prompt/decode transition and exiting with status 1. The router respawns it, so
the failure presents as a ~53s crash-loop that silently discards all prompt
cache.

The trigger is the **total** `--ctx-size`, not the per-sequence context. That
appears to come from `common/speculative.cpp`, where the MTP draft context is
sized from the target's total context despite the comment stating per-sequence
intent:

```c
// common/speculative.cpp — common_speculative_init_result::common_speculative_init_result()
    auto cparams = common_context_params_to_llama(params);

    if (spec_mtp) {
        cparams.ctx_type = LLAMA_CONTEXT_TYPE_MTP;
    }

    // the draft context holds as many tokens per sequence as the target context
    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx(ctx_tgt);        // <-- total, not per-sequence
```

`llama_n_ctx()` returns the total; `llama_n_ctx_seq()` is the per-sequence
accessor:

```c
// src/llama-context.cpp
uint32_t llama_n_ctx    (const llama_context * ctx) { return ctx->n_ctx();     }
uint32_t llama_n_ctx_seq(const llama_context * ctx) { return ctx->n_ctx_seq(); }
```

The draft context then builds its own memory module from those cparams:

```c
    memory.reset(model.create_memory(params_mem, cparams));
```

Under `--no-kv-unified` this makes the draft context `n_parallel` times larger
than the comment intends. Under `--kv-unified` it is worse, because
`n_ctx_seq` is then set equal to the whole total:

```c
// src/llama-context.cpp
    if (cparams.kv_unified) { cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx;                 }
    else                    { cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx / n_seq_max;     }
```

Note also that `--kv-unified-per-slot` cannot bound this: `llama_context_params`
has `n_ctx`, `n_seq_max` and `kv_unified`, but no per-slot field, so the
server-level cap never reaches the draft context.

### Ablation matrix

All rows below are on the same build, model, and machine, and each was verified
by serving requests. "draft n_ctx" is the value the code above assigns.

| `--ctx-size` | `--parallel` | kv-unified | `--spec-type` | draft `n_ctx` | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 786432 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 786432 | **fails every request** |
| 786432 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod` | — | works (12.8 tok/s, 99.99% cache reuse) |
| 393216 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 393216 | works (24 tok/s) |
| 524288 | 3 | on + `--kv-unified-per-slot 262144` | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 524288 | works (23.7 tok/s) |

Removing `draft-mtp` at the failing `--ctx-size` fixes it outright; restoring
`draft-mtp` at a smaller `--ctx-size` also fixes it. So the fault requires
`draft-mtp` **and** a large total `--ctx-size` together.

Note the third and fourth rows: the working unified config has a draft
`n_ctx_seq` of 524288, larger than the failing split config's 262144. So
per-sequence size is not the trigger — the **total** is.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
llama-server \
  --model Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --ctx-size 786432 --parallel 3 --no-kv-unified \
  --spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp \
  --spec-draft-n-max 4 --spec-draft-n-min 0 --draft-p-min 0.25 \
  --n-gpu-layers 999 --flash-attn on \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 512 --jinja

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"...","max_tokens":8,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say: ok"}]}'
```

The model loads normally and reports `status=loaded`. The first request — any
size — kills the process.

### What was ruled out

- **GPU/driver watchdog.** This machine separately had `amdgpu.lockup_timeout`
  at its 2000 ms default, which produced `ring comp_1.x.1 timeout`, a compute
  queue reset and `vk::DeviceLostError`. That was raised to
  `10000,60000,10000,10000` and the machine rebooted. `dmesg` has shown **zero**
  ring timeouts since, yet the MTP failure persists — so the two are unrelated
  faults and this report is only about the second.
- **Out of memory.** The failing configuration loads cleanly at 82 GiB of 120
  GiB GTT, and no OOM appears in `dmesg`. The failure is on first use, not at
  allocation.
- **Prompt length.** A 13-token prompt fails identically to a 100k one.
- **Tool/grammar constrained sampling.** A request with no `tools` fails too.
- **Build drift.** `b10752-b96806d96` throughout, verified via
  `system_fingerprint`; the container was restarted, never re-pulled.
- **Slot count alone.** `--parallel 3` works fine at smaller `--ctx-size`.

### Suggested fix

```diff
-    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx(ctx_tgt);
+    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx_seq(ctx_tgt);
```

This matches the stated intent of the comment. It would also make the draft
context independent of `--parallel`, which currently multiplies it.

### Possibly related

#23658 reports MTP draft acceptance collapsing at particular `--ctx-size`
values on a ~2048-aligned pattern, attributed there to "slot indexing in how
the MTP draft context shares the KV cache with the target context". That may be
the same sizing/indexing surface presenting as degradation rather than a crash.

### Relevant log output

```
# router, at the moment of failure
E srv    operator(): http client error: Failed to read connection
I srv    operator():
items.title: Eval bug: draft-mtp draft context is sized from llama_n_ctx() (total) rather than llama_n_ctx_seq(), killing the server at decode entry on large --ctx-size

## Overview Currently with tensor/matrix cores we only use fp16 instructions, so dequant to shared memory -> fp16 GEMM. But many devices have higher throughput int8 tensor/matrix cores, so similar to the existing DP4A-based scalar MMQ path it would be good to have a coopmat int8 MMQ path. I have tried to make this work in the past, but failed due to architectural constraints in the coopmat extension. But based on @pwilkin's ideas in #27493, I finally managed to get it to work with good performance on RDNA3 and 4. This new MMQ cm1 shader supports q4_0, q4_1, q5_0, q5_1, q8_0, q3_k, q4_k, q5_k, q6_k, mxfp4, nvfp4 and iq4_nl on RDNA3 and RDNA4. Strix Halo prompt processing performance is significantly improved, RDNA4 is more neutral, but MoE prompt processing is also up significantly. The shader is limited to those two architectures since it hardcodes their specific coopmat access patterns. More architectures can be added if needed. q4_1, q5_1, q4_k, q5_k and nvfp4 on RDNA4 are disabled for MUL_MAT since they run slower than existing fp16 matmul. items.body:
*Context: I am submitting this on behalf of the LLamaSharp maintainer team (cc @martindevans). We needed a way to cleanly expose speculative decoding and MTP to our C# users without bloating the upstream core. This standalone C API has been heavily battle-tested across both C++ and C# environments.*

## Overview

This PR introduces a standalone, dependency-free C API for multi-sequence speculative decoding and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP). It extracts the core speculative execution loop from the internal `common/speculative.cpp` utilities into a public-facing implementation (`src/llama-speculative.cpp`). This enables downstream bindings (such as `llama-cpp-python`, `LLamaSharp`, etc.) to easily integrate draft-simple and Draft-MTP capabilities via native pointers, without needing to recreate complex draft/verify loops or context routing mechanics.

## Additional information

### Key Architectural Changes

* **Public C API (`include/llama.h`):** Introduced `llama_speculative_init`, `llama_speculative_decode`, `llama_speculative_free`, and the `llama_speculative_result` struct.
* **MTP Staging Integration:** Exposed `llama_set_embeddings_nextn` and `llama_get_embeddings_nextn_ith` to the public header. These are strictly required to route hidden states across MTP projection heads for architectures like DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen.
* **Standalone Engine (`src/llama-speculative.cpp`):** Implemented a core multi-sequence engine relying solely on `llama.h` and the C++ standard library, keeping the footprint minimal and avoiding `common` dependencies.
* **Continuous Batching:** Dynamically tracks `batch->n_seq_id` to draft and verify multiple independent sequences concurrently, mapping accepted tokens back to their origin sequence ID.
* **M-RoPE / RNN Safe Rollback:** Engineered an unconditional byte-level `llama_state_seq` backup mechanism prior to verification. If a sequence is rejected, the engine performs a hard memory wipe and transparent re-decodes accepted tokens. This specifically prevents fatal `X < Y` M-RoPE position collision crashes on hybrid recurrent architectures.
* **Verification Alignment:** Ensures the sampled base token is explicitly prepended to the verification batch so the target model evaluates draft tokens with perfect context alignment.

### Validation

* Added `tests/test-speculative.cpp` and integrated it into `CMakeLists.txt` using the `test-download-model` fixture.
* The test uses a self-speculation approach (where target and draft contexts share the same model) to validate decoding loops, cache rollbacks, sequence mapping, and state recovery in CI, requiring zero multi-model external dependencies.
* **Cross-Ecosystem Testing:** *(Note: This PR is paired with a companion PR in `LLamaSharp` [feat: Native Speculative Decoding & MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) - #1431](https://github.com/SciSharp/LLamaSharp/pull/1431). The API and underlying engine have been exhaustively tested across both C++ and C# environments. This includes the native CI test provided here, alongside extensive managed C# unit tests validating multi-sequence multiplexing, KV cache deduplication, and real-world interactive Tokens-Per-Second (TPS) benchmarks.)*

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - I used AI assistants to help brainstorm architectural approaches, assist with the C++ implementation, and structure the PR description. However, all testing, benchmarking, CI validation, and cross-ecosystem integration (C++/C#) were conducted manually, and I take full responsibility for the accuracy and maintenance of this code.

# ANNEX: Model Selection & Evaluation

## 1. Model Compatibility & Selection Rules

* **Dual-Model Speculation:** The target and draft models must share the exact same tokenizer architecture and vocabulary size to prevent immediate cache desynchronization crashes. Crucially, **the larger the target model and the smaller/faster the draft model, the higher the resulting speedup**.

* **Multi-Token Prediction (MTP):** This requires a single model with pre-trained speculative projection layers (`nextn_predict_layers >= 1`). **The more draft heads the model has, the higher the potential speedup**, as it can verify more tokens per native API call without context-switching overhead. The draft budget must match the available heads.

---

## 2. Real-World Benchmark Examples

### Draft-Simple

Pairing **Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-Q8_0.gguf** (Target) with **Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q4_0.gguf** (Draft) yielded a **1.26x speedup (+25.7%)**. Even on a fast GPU, the 1B draft model was lightweight enough to outpace the compute overhead of the 8B target.

### MTP Speculation

Running **Qwen3.5-4B-MTP-Q4_K_M.gguf** (1 MTP head) resulted in a **0.47x slowdown (-53.2%)**. Because the 4B base model is computed incredibly fast on high-end hardware, the API overhead and CUDA graph launch latency of evaluating the MTP head completely overshadowed the memory bandwidth savings. To achieve a speedup instead, you must use a much larger model (like 14B or 32B) where **the GPU's memory bandwidth becomes a true bottleneck as it fetches massive weight matrices from VRAM for every single token**. Alternatively, using an MTP model with multiple prediction heads allows you to verify several tokens in a single API roundtrip, making the overhead worthwhile.

### Multi-Token Prediction: Gemma 4 (Split-Weight MTP-4)

Unlike bundled MTP architectures where projection layers reside in the same weight file, Gemma 4 separates its multi-token prediction heads into a standalone assistant checkpoint (`gemma4-assistant`). This benchmark demonstrates **MTP-4 self-speculation** where 4 future tokens are drafted simultaneously via auxiliary projection layers using the target model's hidden states (`CtxOther`), verified in a single batched verification pass.

#### **Test Configuration**
* **Hardware:** NVIDIA GeF

items.body:
When ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft splits allocation on buft max_size, a view-only tail at the end of the context could skip the final alloc_tensor_range. Persistent views (e.g. KV k_stream / v_stream) were then left without ggml_backend_view_init.
Allocate only parent tensors in alloc_tensor_range and initialize all views in a final pass over the context after all splits complete.
## Overview
`ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft` can split a context across multiple buffers when a tensor would exceed the backend buffer-type `max_size` (for example Vulkan's default 1 GiB). If the remaining tail of the context contains only views, the final `alloc_tensor_range` may be skipped, so those views never get `ggml_backend_view_init`.
Persistent KV stream views (`layer.k_stream` / `v_stream`) then keep `tensor->data == NULL` while `view_src` is allocated. Host state save/restore later calls `ggml_backend_tensor_get` / `set` on those views and hits:
`GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated")`
This change:
- allocates only parent tensors inside each split range
- initializes all uninitialized views in one final pass over the context
Also adds `test_view_init_after_max_size_split` in `tests/test-alloc.cpp`
to cover the oversized-parent + view-only-tail case.
## Additional information
Fixes #19839
Fixes #23737
Fixes #21762

Related:
- #21576 (state-IO `!tensor->data` guards; complementary discussion)
I reproduced the assert with Qwen3.6-27B (MTP) when a parent KV tensor exceeded buft `max_size` and the context ended with a view-only tail.
Note on #21576: skipping tensors with `!tensor->data` avoids the assert, but can omit real KV still reachable via `view_src` and misalign the serialized state. This PR fixes the missing view init in the allocator instead.
Prior investigation commit (same patch on older master; kept for reference):
https://github.com/Yoshi4470/llama.cpp/commit/99655d5854e63e736a6a93280e01b7e785a59ba5
## Test plan
- [x] `test-alloc` (includes new `test_view_init_after_max_size_split`)
- [x] Vulkan A/B on the Qwen3.6-27B MTP speculative path (same command, 10 runs each):
  - before (`e3546c794`): 0/10 (assert every time)
  - after (this PR): 10/10 (no assert, completed normally)
- [x] Earlier `amdvlk64.dll` crash after the assert site was resolved by an AMD driver update; treated as separate from this allocator fix
- N/A: equivalent-size CPU repro (not practical on this machine)

### Command used for the A/B runs:
- Vulkan / AMDVLK, Windows, AMD Software 26.6.4
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)
```
llama-cli.exe -np 8 -c 2097152 --no-mmap -m models/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ctkd q4_0 -ctvd q4_0 \
--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 -p "Hello!"
```
## Requirements
- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - Cursor assisted with implementing the finalize-views pass and regression test after I identified the root cause in the alloc split path, and with local verification.

items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description


## Summary

Public GGUFs for [prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf](https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf) use two **new** GGML tensor types that stock `ggml-org/llama.cpp` does not know:

| Name | Tensor type ID | Role |
|------|---------------:|------|
| `PQ2_0` | **142** | 2-bit slots for ternary g128 (`{-1,0,+1}` + FP16 group scale) |
| `PTQ1_0` | **143** | dense trit packing of the same ternary g128 weights |

These are **not** upstream `Q1_0` (type 41) and **not** upstream `Q2_0` (type 42, group 64). They were given high IDs so they can coexist with those types.

Stock `llama-cli` rejects them as unknown types. If a loader treats an unknown type as `Q2_0`, Prism’s card says the result is **garbage** (no Hadamard activation transform).

This is a request to either:

1. **Upstream** `PQ2_0` / `PTQ1_0` (parse + dequant + matmul, including the Hadamard path), or
2. **Reject loudly** with the type name, and document that these files need the Prism fork until they land.

I am not affiliated with Prism ML. I hit this while importing the public GGUFs (also via Ollama `create`, which vendors llama.cpp and fails the same way).

## Public files (Apache 2.0)

Repo: https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf

| File | Size (bytes) | `general.file_type` | Dominant tensor type |
|------|-------------:|--------------------:|---------------------:|
| `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PQ2_0.gguf` | 7,206,168,928 | 141 | **142** (`PQ2_0`) |
| `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf` | 5,946,648,928 | 143 | **143** (`PTQ1_0`) |
| `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-F16.gguf` | 53,808,408,928 | F16 | 1 (not the issue) |
| `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-mmproj-Q8_0.gguf` | 629,246,976 | Q8_0 | 8 (loads; vision only) |

Architecture metadata: `qwen35`. Example tensor: `output.weight` / `token_embd.weight` shape `[5120, 248320]`, type 142 or 143.

Verified SHA256 (HF LFS):

- PQ2_0: `3907dc1658db1f78a9826bf8d5bcb8dc65db0d466388937af57f2294fae62ec1`
- PTQ1_0: `53107f530aa52eb00912263ab1ee29bd199261c87cd7b4ad4ca1318c1fe33ee3`

## How this differs from formats that already work

| Format | Typical file | Type ID | Mainline llama.cpp | Notes |
|--------|--------------|--------:|:------------------:|-------|
| 1-bit Bonsai `Q1_0` | `prism-ml/Bonsai-27B-gguf` `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf` | 41 | Yes (e.g. [#20048](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/20048) / follow-ups) | This is what Ollama listings like `*:bonsai-27b-q1_0` run |
| Ternary `Q2_0` g64 | `*-Q2_0_g64.gguf` | 42 | Yes (CPU/Metal/Vulkan; CUDA tracked separately) | Official upstream ternary packing |
| Fork ternary `Q2_0` g128 | `*-Q2_0.gguf` (Bonsai 1) | 42, **different block size** | No (same id, wrong layout) | [Bonsai-demo ternary status](https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/Bonsai-demo#upstream-status-for-ternary) |
| **Bonsai 2 `PQ2_0` / `PTQ1_0`** | files above | **142 / 143** | **No** | New IDs + Hadamard-rotated ternary |

Bonsai 2 is a new checkpoint (Qwen3.8-27B lineage, hybrid attention, 262K context), not a requant of Bonsai-27B `Q1_0`.

## What Prism’s fork already names

From [PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp](https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp) `ggml/include/ggml.h` (`prism` branch):

```c
GGML_TYPE_Q1_0    = 41,
GGML_TYPE_Q2_0    = 42,
// Prism-private Q2_0 at group size 128 (upstream Q2_0 is group 64). High id so it
// slots above upstream types; type_traits is sized to COUNT (143) with 43..141 unused.
GGML_TYPE_PQ2_0   = 142,
GGML_TYPE_PTQ1_0  = 143, // Prism-private ternary, group 128
GGML_TYPE_COUNT   = 144,
```

The same header also defines `GGML_HINT_SRC0_IS_HADAMARD`. The [HF card](https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf) says weights are stored after a blockwise Hadamard (block 1024); the runtime must apply the matching transform to activations or **refuse to load**. Registering a block size without that path is not enough.

Prism’s own demo README still lists `PQ2_0` as “planned / nothing yet” for the *previous* Ternary-Bonsai-27B drop. Bonsai 2 has already shipped files with types 142/143.

Reference implementation: https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp  
Demo / pinned binaries: https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/Bonsai-demo

## Reproduction (stock llama.cpp)

```bash
hf download prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf \
  Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PQ2_0.gguf \
  --local-dir .

# latest ggml-org/llama.cpp release binary
./llama-cli -m Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PQ2_0.gguf -p "ping" -n 16
```

**Expected:** model loads, or a clear `unknown type 142 (PQ2_0)` error.

**Actual (stock):** unknown type / load failure. Downstream Ollama 0.33.2 `ollama create` reports `Error: tensor "output.weight" size overflow` because its GGUF parser returns type size 0 for 142/143.

Same result for `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf` (type 143).

`Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-F16.gguf` is a standard F16 GGUF (~50.1 GiB) and is not the format users are meant to deploy.

## Packing (from Prism’s card + fork comments)

- Ternary g128: each weight in `{-1, 0, +1}`, one FP16 scale per 128 weights (~1.72 bits/weight including a small set of higher-precision tensors).
- `PTQ1_0`: dense trits, ~1.75 bpw, ~5.95 GB language model.
- `PQ2_0`: one trit in a 2-bit slot, ~2.13 bpw, ~7.21 GB; this is the pack Prism reports on Apple Silicon.
- Group size **128** (not upstream `Q2_0` group 64, not `TQ1_0`/`TQ2_0` group 256).

I do not have a public spec for the exact `block_pq2_0` / `block_ptq1_0` C layouts in this issue; those live in the Prism fork (`ggml-common.h` / quant kernels). Happy to help

### Name and Version

Latest llamacpp Master pull as of Second of August 2026.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

Ryzen 5950x, Ryzen 5600x
Tested with A770, RX6650XT and 9070XT.

### Models

gpt-oss-20b

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Issue: llama-spec failure at 16k boundary due to non-consecutive KV cache position tracking (Y != X + 1)

Behavior: During speculative decoding, llama_decode fails validation in init when sequence positions jump across boundaries (e.g., KV cache holds up to index $X = 16382$, but the incoming batch requests start position $Y = 16384$ or $Y = 32766$).

This worked without issue yesterday.

~~~~
E init: the tokens of sequence 0 in the input batch have inconsistent sequence positions:
 - the last position stored in the memory module of the context (i.e. the KV cache) for sequence 0 is X = 16382
 - the tokens for sequence 0 in the input batch have a starting position of Y = 16384
 it is required that the sequence positions remain consecutive: Y = X + 1
E decode: failed to initialize batch
E llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -1
E spec         draft: llama_decode returned -1
~~~~


### First Bad Commit

All I can give you is the time I git pulled last before it happened.

But the likely cullprit is the dspark merges that happened last night, since that seems to be the only thing touching speculative decode features.

items.body:
*Note up front: I used an AI assistant to read through the SYCL source and to parse the tensor tables out of the GGUF files, and to help me write this up. The measurements are from my own machine and I checked them myself. Flagging it so you know what you're reading.*

## What I ran into

I'm running Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE, 40 layers, 256 experts, 8 active) on an Arc Pro B50 16GB, SYCL backend, build b10499. Because the model doesn't fit in VRAM I offload part of the experts to CPU with `-ncmoe`, so I care a lot about which tensors get the reorder treatment.

While figuring out which quant to use, I found that reorder coverage does not go up as the quant gets bigger. It peaks at Q4_K and then falls off a cliff.

The reason is that the MoE path has a narrower type gate than the dense path — [`opt_for_reorder_id`, ggml-sycl.cpp#L4458-L4472](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/9a286ac98d2cab74231bd3f1fc3f2b8bdf05422e/ggml/src/ggml-sycl/ggml-sycl.cpp#L4458-L4472) (pinned at master `9a286ac`):

```c
static void opt_for_reorder_id(ggml_backend_sycl_context * ctx, const ggml_tensor * src0) {
    ...
    if (src0->type != GGML_TYPE_Q4_K && src0->type != GGML_TYPE_Q5_K && src0->type != GGML_TYPE_Q6_K) {
        return;
    }
```

The dense gates (`ggml_sycl_supports_reorder_dmmv` / `_mmvq`) also accept Q1_0, Q4_0, Q8_0, Q2_K and Q3_K. The MoE gate takes three types only.

This isn't a correctness problem — output is fine. It's just that a large part of the model silently skips the optimization.

## Why it matters on a real model

On a 35B-A3B, the expert tensors are around 85-90% of the file. So whatever the expert gate rejects is most of the model.

Unsloth's Dynamic quants promote expert tensors to Q8_0 at the higher tiers, and Q8_0 isn't on that list. I measured coverage by reading the tensor types straight out of each GGUF and weighting by bytes (expert tensors judged against `opt_for_reorder_id`, everything else against the dense gates):

| file | expert tensor types | reorder coverage |
|---|---|--:|
| UD-Q4_K_S | Q4_K 18.1G, Q6_K 0.7G | ~100% |
| UD-Q4_K_XL | Q4_K 12.1G, Q5_K 7.4G, Q6_K 0.7G | ~100% |
| UD-Q5_K_XL | Q5_K 14.8G, Q6_K 8.8G, Q8_0 0.9G | 96% |
| UD-Q6_K_XL | Q6_K 17.6G, **Q8_0 12.3G** | **62%** |
| UD-Q8_K_XL | **Q8_0 33.7G** | **7%** |

(files from `peculiar-ragdoll/Nail-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF-MTP`, which redistributes Unsloth's quants)

So on Intel, paying for Q6_K_XL gets you worse throughput than Q4_K_XL, on a file that is 10GB larger. Nothing in the filename hints at that, and there's no warning at load time.

I can't give you a clean before/after for Q8_0 experts specifically, since the code path doesn't exist to turn on. What I can say is that reorder on the expert path is clearly worth a lot on this hardware: UD-Q4_K_S (~100% covered) with 20 layers of experts spilled to CPU still beats UD-IQ3_XXS (0% expert coverage, IQ types aren't eligible anywhere) running entirely in VRAM — 42.8 t/s vs 35.9 t/s, despite being 8GB bigger and partly on DDR4. Different quant types so it's not a controlled comparison, but the gap is large enough that I don't think it's noise.

## The groundwork already landed

Q8_0 reorder exists for dense tensors — #21527 added `reorder_qw_q8_0` plus DMMV/MMVQ dispatch back in April, and it's a nice win there (3.1x reported).

The MoE variants exist too, just not for Q8_0. Current kernel list:

```
reorder_qw_q4_0     reorder_qw_q4_k     reorder_qw_q4_k_moe
reorder_qw_q8_0     reorder_qw_q5_k     reorder_qw_q5_k_moe
reorder_qw_q2_k     reorder_qw_q6_k     reorder_qw_q6_k_moe
reorder_qw_q3_k                         <- no q8_0_moe
```

From the outside it looks like the missing pieces are a `reorder_qw_q8_0_moe` alongside the three that are already there, and adding `GGML_TYPE_Q8_0` to the gate above. I haven't written or tested that, so I may well be underestimating it — the `_moe` variants handle the per-expert stride and I don't know how much of that carries over.

Q2_K, Q3_K and Q4_0 are in the same position (accepted on dense, rejected for experts), but Q8_0 is the one that actually shows up in expert tensors in the quants people download, so it seemed like the one worth raising.

## To reproduce

No special setup — the gate is visible in the source. To see the effect on a real file, read the tensor types from any Unsloth UD MoE quant at Q6_K or above and check how many bytes of `ffn_*_exps.weight` are Q8_0.

## Offering to test

I have an Arc Pro B50 (Battlemage, 16GB) and a set of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B quants from IQ3 up to Q6_K already benchmarked on it, with a repeatable harness (warmed runs, greedy sampling, fixed 25k-token prompt). If someone puts up a patch I'm happy to run it and report numbers, including the partial-offload case which is probably the interesting one.

Environment:
- Intel Arc Pro B50 16GB (Battlemage, `xe` driver)
- Ryzen 5 5600GT, 30GB DDR4, no swap
- llama.cpp b10499, SYCL AOT build
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE, 128k context, `--spec-type draft-mtp`

### Name and Version

llama.cpp 0.4.1-dev (build 50, commit 9575389); reproduced on latest master (same commit) as well
Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (Linux)

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

2× Intel Xeon Platinum 8269 (Cascade Lake, 52C/104T), 768 GB DDR4-2133 ECC,
8× NVIDIA RTX 3080 20GB (sm86), dual NUMA

### Models

Custom (official GGUF release): ggml-org/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-GGUF
(main: MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-MXFP4)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Running speculative decoding with the officially released MTP draft for
MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL, per the model repo README:
main model via `-m`, mtp sidecar via `-md`, plus `--spec-type draft-mtp`.
The main model loads and runs fine without the MTP flags (~18.6 tok/s decode
on this box with 40/48 expert layers offloaded to GPU). Crash occurs as soon
as the MTP draft is enabled. Command:

```
numactl --interleave=all ./build/bin/llama-server -m /mnt/data4t/models/mimo-v26rl-gguf/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-MXFP4-00001-of-00002.gguf -md /mnt/data4t/models/mimo-v26rl-gguf/mtp-MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-MXFP4.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 7 --spec-draft-ngl 999 -ngl 999 -t 48 -c 262144 -np 1 -fa on -b 4096 -ub 1024 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -ot 'blk\.(0|1|2|3)\.ffn_.*_exps\..*=CUDA0,blk\.(4|5|6|7)\.ffn_.*_exps\..*=CUDA1,blk\.(8|9|10|11)\.ffn_.*_exps\..*=CUDA2,blk\.(12|13|14|15)\.ffn_.*_exps\..*=CUDA3,blk\.(32|33|34|35)\.ffn_.*_exps\..*=CUDA4,blk\.(36|37|38|39)\.ffn_.*_exps\..*=CUDA5,blk\.(40|41|42|43)\.ffn_.*_exps\..*=CUDA6,blk\.(44|45|46|47)\.ffn_.*_exps\..*=CUDA7,blk\..*\.ffn_.*_exps\..*=CPU' -ts 1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1 --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --repeat-penalty 1.05 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' --path /home/cw/llama-ui-dist --port 8899 --host 0.0.0.0 --jinja

### First Bad Commit

## Expected Behavior

The MTP draft loads (reusing the main model's base weights, per the MTP
architecture) and speculative decoding runs.

## Current Behavior

Crash during model load. With MTP enabled, the main model itself fails first:
loader reports `check_tensor_dims: tensor 'blk.0.attn_q.weight' not found`,
then the draft sidecar load also fails with the same error. A retry pass then
attempts a ~50 GB CUDA0 allocation and OOMs. No request is ever served.
(The sidecar alone, loaded as `-m`, also fails with the same
`blk.0.attn_q.weight not found`.)

Analysis: the MTP draft is designed to reuse the main model's weights
(attention Q/K/V from base layers) and only adds its own small MTP layer set
(blk.48-50 + MTP head); the sidecar therefore only contains MTP-specific
tensors. The `-md` sidecar loading path appears to treat the draft as a
complete standalone model, requiring base-layer tensors not present in the
sidecar. The embedded-MTP packaging (MTP tensors inside the main GGUF, as in
tnhnyzc/MiMo-V2.5-MTP-GGUF) reportedly works with `--spec-type draft-mtp` on
the same build, so this is specific to the sidecar (`-md`) path.
Reproduced on latest master (9575389) as well.

### Relevant log output

## Failure Logs

```
0.00.000.704 I srv    llama_server: initializing ...
0.00.295.789 I cmn    common_param: common_params_print_info: verbosity = 3 (adjust with the `-lv N` CLI arg)
0.00.295.993 W srv    llama_server: security: no API key is set and CORS allows all origins (see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25655)
0.00.313.694 I srv      load_model: loading model '/mnt/data4t/models/mimo-v26rl-gguf/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-MXFP4-00001-of-00002.gguf'
0.02.576.976 E llama_model_load: error loading model: check_tensor_dims: tensor 'blk.0.attn_q.weight' not found
0.02.576.995 E llama_model_load_from_file_impl: failed to load model
0.02.577.065 W operator(): failed to measure the memory of the extra model, fitting without it: failed to load model
0.02.577.105 W common_fit_params: failed to fit params to free device memory: n_gpu_layers already set by user to 999, abort
0.02.839.485 W load: control-looking token: 128247 '</s>' was not control-type; this is probably a bug in the model. its type will be overridden
0.09.486.699 E ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
0.09.486.705 E alloc_tensor_range: failed to allocate CUDA0 buffer of size 53203257600
0.11.920.771 E llama_model_load: error loading model: unable to allocate CUDA0 buffer
0.11.920.806 E llama_model_load_from_file_impl: failed to load model
0.11.920.886 E cmn          common_init_: failed to load model '/mnt/data4t/models/mimo-v26rl-gguf/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-MXFP4-00001-of-00002.gguf'
0.11.920.928 E srv      load_model: failed to load model, '/mnt/data4t/models/mimo-v26rl-gguf/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-MXFP4-00001-of-00002.gguf'
0.11.920.959 I srv   operator(): operator(): cleaning up before exit...
0.11.925.110 E srv    llama_server: exiting due to model loading error
```

## Additional Context

Related: #25924 ("Feature Request: MTP support for MiMo V2.5") and #26228
("mimo2: add MTP draft support") — the same sidecar-vs-embedded MTP packaging
question. Issue #26605 / #25574 touch MTP layer memory allocation, possibly
relevant to the ~50 GB retry OOM above.<details>

### Name and Version

Bionic bundled llama.cpp Vulkan 2.41.0 (crash) / 2.39.0 (ok); llama-server reports version 0.4.1-dev build 1 commit b49650a

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

2x Intel Arc Pro B50 (driver 32.0.101.8805) + Intel Core Ultra 5 235HX, 64GB RAM

### Models

All of these fail identically on 2.40/2.41 Vulkan, all load fine on 2.39 Vulkan:
- bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- unsloth/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512-GGUF (Q5_K_M)
- empero-ai/Qwen3.8-35B-A3B-Distill-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
Counter-case: nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (Q4_K_M) loads fine on 2.41 Vulkan.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## What happened

`llama-server` with the Vulkan backend crash-aborts while loading sliding-window-attention
decoder models when the KV cache is offloaded to the GPU. The process dies with
`exitCode=3221226505` (`0xC0000409`, fail-fast) before becoming healthy.

Exact abort line (stderr):

```text
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)
```

## Regression info

- ✅ `llama.cpp ... 2.39.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **loads in ~5s, serves fine**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.40.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.41.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with `--no-kv-offload` — **loads and serves** (KV cache on CPU)
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with full offload + embedding model (`nomic-embed-text-v1.5.Q4_K_M`,
  full attention, `--embedding`) — **loads and serves**

So it is not a globally broken Vulkan backend: it is the
`Vulkan + KV-cache GPU offload + SWA/hybrid-attention decoder` path that regressed
between 2.39 and 2.40.

## Repro

```bat
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf -ngl 99 --port 18081
```

- Model: `bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF`, `Q4_K_S` (~2.4 GB)
- No other flags (all defaults). Crash happens during `load_model`, before listening.

Notable log lines on the crashing 2.41 run (before the abort):

```text
W resolve_fused_ops: layer 0 is assigned to device Vulkan1 but Flash Attention is assigned to device CPU (usually due to missing support)
W resolve_fused_ops: Flash Attention not supported, set to disabled
W ggml_vulkan: Failed to allocate pinned memory (Requested buffer size exceeds device buffer size limit: ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory)
```

On the working `--no-kv-offload` run the server reports `kv_unified = 'true'`,
`n_slots = 4`, then `model loaded` / `listening`.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 x64 (build 10.0.26200)
- GPU: Intel Arc Pro B50 (discrete) + Intel integrated Graphics
- Driver: Intel `32.0.101.8805` (06.07.2026), `vulkan-1.dll` present (system + app dir)
- Builds: LM Studio / Bionic bundled `llama.cpp-win-x86_64-vulkan-avx2` packs
  `2.39.0` (working) vs `2.40.0` / `2.41.0` (crashing), CPU 14 threads
- The same setup serves the models fine on engine 2.39, so driver / loader / model
  file are ruled out

## Suspected area

New fused-ops / unified-KV graph building for SWA models (`cache_k` pre-allocation
landing in a Vulkan buffer that reports no supported op) introduced between 2.39
and 2.40. Happy to test any debug build / extra logging on this machine
(Arc Pro B50 available).

### First Bad Commit

Regressed between bundled builds 2.39.0 (works) and 2.40.0 (broken). Exact upstream commit unknown — these are third-party Bionic/LM Studio bundles, not direct llama.cpp builds. Happy to bisect if given build instructions for Windows Vulkan.

### Relevant log output


Command:
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf --port 18081 -ngl 99

Log:
load_model: loading model '.../mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf'
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)

Process exits immediately with code 3221226505 (0xC0000409).

items.body:
We ran **#27952** ("Vulkan: int8 coopmat quantized matmul for RDNA3/4") through our own Vulkan build on a **Radeon RX 7900 XTX** (gfx1100, 24 GB, PCIe 3.0 x16, no ReBAR, 4-core W-2125) with a **27B** model, and wanted to share the results plus a small related fix.

## Context
On this box the 27B runs on the **Vulkan** backend (~3 GB lighter than ROCm/HIP, more VRAM for context). Model: **Qwen3.8-27B, ROCmFP4-FAST quant (~13.6 GB)**, `MTP n-max 4`, `--flash-attn on`, `--cache-type-k/v q8_0`, `-c 131072`.

## A/B benchmark (same GGUF + byte-identical flags, 3 repeats, greedy)

| workload | metric | base Vulkan | +#27952 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| agent (long-ctx) | prompt t/s | 631.0 | **670.1** | **+6.2%** |
| agent | token t/s | 103.1 | **104.9** | +1.7% |
| agent | MTP draft accept | 88% | **100%** | **+12 pp** |
| agent | wall (s) | 4.89 | **4.70** | -3.9% |
| tools (short-ctx) | prompt t/s | 417.0 | 421.8 | +1.2% |
| tools | token t/s | 117.4 | 117.2 | ~0 |

The gain concentrates on the **prefill-heavy / long-context** workload; the standout is **MTP draft acceptance 88% -> 100%**. Cross-reference: the upstream 7B harness (7900 XTX, ReBAR/PCIe4) reports int8-coopmat at +4.6% dense prefill and +18.5% MoE prefill, decode flat - same shape.

## Small related fix (patch below)

In `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/mul_mmq_cm1_funcs.glsl`, when `K` is not a multiple of `BK*BK_STEP`, the A-operand load reads `ib + ks` past `end_k` - which can land on the next row, or on bytes after the tensor whose f16 scale can be **NaN**. Clamping the block index re-reads the row's first block instead; its B side is zeroed, so it contributes nothing:

```
-                pre_a[li * BK_STEP + ks] = block_a_load(ib + ks, loadr_a);
+                /* K need not be a multiple of BK*BK_STEP: a k-step past end_k re-reads the  */
+                /* row's first block (finite), and its B side is zeroed, so it adds nothing. */
+                /* Reading on past the row instead picks up the next row, or bytes after the */
+                /* tensor whose f16 scale can be NaN.                                         */
+                const uint ib_k = ((blk) + ks * BK < end_k) ? (ib + ks) : ib;
+                pre_a[li * BK_STEP + ks] = block_a_load(ib_k, loadr_a);
```

One-line defensive correctness fix, no measurable cost. (Our `mul_mmq_cm1.comp` is otherwise byte-identical to #27952.)

## Offer
Happy to submit a PR - fold the `mul_mmq_cm1_funcs.glsl` fix into #27952, or as a small follow-up. Can share the benchmark harness if useful.

**Env:** RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) - Mesa 26.2.2 (RADV) - Vulkan - llama.cpp c550d2f6 + #27952.

## Overview

This release focuses on backend performance and correctness, broader model coverage, and more robust server/router operation. It adds HRM-Text (DFM Mimir 1B) support, MiMo-V2.6 and HunyuanOCR conversion support, ggml 0.25.0 backend improvements, multi-address HTTP binding, image outputs from function calls, and several chat parser/UI fixes.

### Highlights

- Accelerate CUDA `conv2d` with implicit GEMM ([#29135](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29135))
- Add Metal MoE and SSM_CONV fusion optimizations ([#28948](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28948))
- Allow the server to bind to multiple addresses ([#28690](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28690))

### API changes

- Add `llama_adapter_lora_init_from_file_ptr()` for loading LoRA from an open FILE ([#28993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28993))
- Document `llama_model_load_from_file_ptr()` as reading from the current position and requiring aligned mmap ([#28993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28993))
- Add `LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_TEST` dummy tokenizer ([#29084](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29084))
- Add `input_image` support to server function-call outputs ([#22575](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/22575))
- Allow `--host` to accept comma-separated TCP addresses and UNIX sockets ([#28690](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28690))

### New models

- Add HRM-Text / DFM Mimir 1B support ([#27625](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27625))
- Add MiMo-V2.6 conversion support ([#29257](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29257))
- Add DFlash support for HunyuanOCR ([#28890](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28890))
- Extend Nemotron MTP and Nemotron-H model handling ([#29018](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29018), [#28989](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28989))
- Add Qwen4Exp hyper-connection ops and sparse flash attention ([#28901](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28901), [#28770](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28770))
- Add `--fuse-qkv` support for Muse Glimmer ([#29203](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29203))

### Core changes

- Add graph input/input-tensor diagnostics during scheduler reserve ([#26625](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26625))
- Enable CUDA graphs for MTP drafting ([#28549](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28549))
- Fix tensor-parallel split state/granularity for fused QKV models ([#28965](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28965))
- Fix Mamba time-step projection input contiguity ([#28832](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28832))
- Write the SWA pattern in the model saver and round-trip 15 more architectures ([#29042](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29042))
- Add environment variables for temperature, top-p, min-p and penalties ([#27380](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27380))
- Reduce the sampler backend probe size ([#29285](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29285))
- Add Ling 3.0, DeepSeek V3.2/V4, qwen3-coder, Muse Glimmer and Gemma 4 parser fixes ([#28682](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28682), [#29008](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29008), [#28869](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28869), [#29242](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29242), [#29115](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29115))
- Improve JSON Schema and PEG handling ([#28518](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28518), [#29127](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29127), [#29161](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29161))
- Add ufakzeka pre-tokenizer and `llama-bench --version` ([#29033](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29033), [#28971](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28971))

### Multi-modality changes

- Add sanity checks for mtmd layer indices, SAM layer counts, resize targets and graph allocation ([#29276](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29276), [#28149](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28149))
- Fix SigLIP bucket buffer overrun for tall/wide images ([#29276](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29276))

### Server changes

- Fix router eviction races and child process lifecycle handling ([#29217](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29217))
- Do not pass log file or API key file to router-spawned children ([#29212](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29212), [#28938](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28938))
- Improve startup and model-source logging ([#29125](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29125))
- Update vendored cpp-httplib to 0.57.1 ([#29239](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29239))

### UI changes

- Accept WEBM video files ([#28622](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28622))
- Add close button to UI toasts ([#28246](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28246))
- Fix mobile breakpoint and content overflow issues, including horizontal table scrolling ([#29108](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29108))
- Restore the reasoning menu in single-model desktop mode ([#27985](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27985))
- Stop re-probing a disabled `/tools` endpoint on every message ([#28646](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28646))

### ggml changes

- Updated ggml to v0.25.0 ([release](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases/tag/v0.25.0))
- The release expands hyper-connection, flash-attention, and fused MoE/SSM support across backends, with robustness, quantization, data-layout, and RPC/meta improvements.
- API changes include gated `ggml_dsv4_hc_pre_gated()`, optional `ggml_dsv4_hc_post()` comb, and RPC protocol major v7.

items.body:
## Overview

When CUB has no DeviceTopK (every CCCL older than 3.2), ggml_cuda_op_top_k falls back to sorting every key of every row with a segmented radix sort and copying the first k. For wide rows the cost of the sort is large, the qwen4exp QSA indexer runs TOP_K over 4 rows x n_kv columns with k = 2051,and at 131k context that sort costs 5.1 ms per generated token which is about a third of the GPU time per token.

This PR makes the existing radix-select kernel (Until now this has been HIP-only) available to CUB builds without DeviceTopK and uses it in that fallback for rows of >= 8192 columns. The threshold was measured, it wasn't estimated or guessed. On an RTX 3090 (CUDA 12.0, CUB 2.0.1), the segmented sort was still faster at 4096 columns and the radix-select was faster from 8192 on. Builds that have CCCL >= 3.2 keep using DeviceTopK. HIP, MUSA and no-CUB builds are unchanged by this. GGML_CUDA_TOPK_ARGSORT=1 forces the old path so both can be compared within one binary.

## Additional information

Correctness: test-backend-ops -o TOP_K passes 525/525 on both paths (268 cases at >= 8192 columns, up to 524,299 columns, k up to 9,999, 112 with ties).

**Kernel only timings (test-backend-ops perf, TOP_K with k = 16, CUDA graphs off, GPU shared with a running server):** on all 46 test shapes with rows of 8192 columns or more, radix-select beats the segmented sort by about 1.42x at worst and 2.25x in the median and up to 11x for 16-row batches. On 4096-column rows, the sort was still faster (24.1 us vs 38.9 us for radix-select), so the switch happens at 8192 columns rather than the 1024 proposed in the earlier unmerged #28366.

**End to end (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4_K_XL, 131k context, MTP draft, same binary, kill-switch A/B, two windows run in both orders):** Nsight Systems traces show the top-k kernels dropping from 5.1 to 0.25 ms per generated token. Decode on cached 128-token continuations increased from 30.3 to 34.9 t/s, +13 to +18% on every one of six position-paired runs, and a fresh 128-token request after the prefill gained +10% as well (one pair). Prefill was unchanged as expected considering the sort does not run there. A separate production-sampling quality screen (480 requests at ~37k and ~119k context, three seeds, argsort path as the control) found no consistent quality regression and 9 to 12% higher decode throughput at ~119k on every seed.

**Some caveats:**
- Tie behaviour differs. The segmented sort always kept the lower index so its output was repeatable. Radix-select, like CUB's DeviceTopK keeps whichever of the exactly tied values it reaches first so the selected set can differ between runs when ties occur. Any tied choice is a valid top-k result and test-backend-ops accepts it. This is the same behaviour #28497 describes for DeviceTopK.
- The 4096/8192 crossover was measured at k = 16 without CUDA graphs on one GPU model. Other k and other GPUs may cross elsewhere. The threshold of 8192 is conservative for the 3090.
- Not measured: MUSA and no-CUB builds (unchanged by this PR), other k at the boundary, an idle GPU.

This was measured on 2x RTX 3090 (sm_86), driver 595.84, CUDA 12.0.140, CUB 2.0.1, where CUB_TOP_K_AVAILABLE is undefined and this fallback is the active path.

Related earlier work: #28366 proposed the same dispatch with a 1024-column threshold and no measurements. It was closed unmerged.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. The code change was written by an AI assistant (Claude) under my direction and reviewed by me. All builds, tests, profiles and quality measurements were run by me on my own hardware. This description and the commit message are my own words.
