items.body:
## Overview

The Metal `PAD` kernel only handled right padding (all left paddings `lp0/lp1/lp2/lp3 == 0`). For any PAD node with non-zero left padding, `ggml_metal_device_supports_op` returned `false`, silently skipping the op and breaking any model whose graph depends on it.

This was hit in the wild by CosyVoice's flow-matching decoder, which emits `PAD(lp0=2, rp0=0)`; the model could not run on Metal and fell back to CPU (~6x slower on Apple silicon).

## Root cause

```c
// ggml-metal-device.m
case GGML_OP_PAD:
    ...
    return (lp0 == 0) && (lp1 == 0) && (lp2 == 0) && (lp3 == 0);
```

`kernel_pad_impl` assumed source and destination were aligned at the origin of every dim (`i0x = i_x`), so it only produced correct results when there was no left padding.

## Fix

Compute source coords as `i0x = i_x - lp_x`, writing zero outside `[0, ne0x)`. This mirrors the CPU reference implementation (`ggml_compute_forward_pad_f32`).

- `ggml-metal-impl.h`: add `lp0..lp3` to `ggml_metal_kargs_pad`
- `ggml-metal.metal`: `kernel_pad_impl` applies the per-dim left offset
- `ggml-metal-ops.cpp`: populate `lp0..lp3` from op_params
- `ggml-metal-device.m`: drop the `lp == 0` requirement

Circular padding (`op_params[8] != 0`) is still not supported and keeps returning `false`; that is tracked separately by #16985.

## Compatibility

With all `lp == 0` the kernel is identical to the previous version (all pre-existing right-padding tests continue to pass).

## Verification

`test-backend-ops test -o PAD` on Apple M2 Ultra (Metal vs CPU reference), with new regression cases for left padding:

```
PAD(ne_a=[101,1024,1,1], lp0=2, rp0=0):           OK   [new]
PAD(ne_a=[512,512,1,1],  lp0=4, rp0=0):           OK   [new]
PAD(ne_a=[512,512,1,1],  lp1=3, rp1=0):           OK   [new]
PAD(ne_a=[64,64,3,1],    lp0=2, rp0=3, lp1=1):    OK   [new, mixed]
... all pre-existing cases still OK
PAD(..., circular=1):                              not supported [unchanged]
```

End-to-end, CosyVoice3-0.5B now runs on Metal: `tts_generate` for a 50-char prompt drops from ~14.5s (CPU) to ~2.4s (Metal).

## Overview

This PR removes the `sched_need_reserve = true` line from `llama_context::set_causal_attn()`, which previously marked the scheduler to do a full re-reserve on every change of the flag, and fixes the one architecture (`qwen4exp`) whose graph shape depended on the flag.

The re-reserve is unnecessary in this case because `causal_attn` only changes the values written to the KQ mask, not tensor shapes or any other buffer sizes. `qwen4exp` was the one exception that selected the per block/cell bias path based on the flag, so the causal and non-causal graphs differed in tensor shapes and ops. The second commit selects the block path independent of `causal_attn`, from the mask shape only and makes the non-causal case follow the reference rule: every visible block competes on score and only unpooled cells are always selected. The causal case works as before.


## Additional information
<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

For vision inputs, this flag is flipped twice around each non-causal image chunk for Gemma3, Gemma4, and DeepSeek-V4, resulting in two expensive `sched_reserve()` passes per image. This is especially slow for multi-image or video inputs.

The cost of a re-reserve scales with context and ubatch configurations, so larger settings pay more per image (see table below).

Note: `causal_attn` is a graph reuse key (`llm_graph_params` via `cparams`), so a new graph is built regardless of `sched_need_reserve`, so this doesn't change the graph rebuilding behaviour.

Speedup table: llama-server with gemma-4-26B-A4B Q4_0 + BF16 mmproj, 130-token images, cache_prompt=false, prompt_ms median of 3 (before -> after):

| images | config | H200 before -> after | RTX 4090 before -> after |
|-|-|-|-|
| 1 | `-c 8192 -ub 512` | 134 -> 105 ms (1.27×) | 201 -> 119 ms (1.69×) |
| 24 | `-c 8192 -ub 512` | 2278 -> 1562 ms (1.46×) | 3559 -> 1748 ms (2.04×) |
| 24 | `-c 32768 -ub 2048` | 5379 -> 1584 ms (3.40×) | 13377 -> 1759 ms (7.61×) |

Generated output remains identical before and after.

## Description:
A recent commit added the 'Current Time' and 'Runtime Info' browser commands to the WebUI. These commands are not opt-in like the other agent commands have been and are enabled by default regardless of whether you have a '--tools' CLI argument specified when launching llama-server.

## Environment:
- Server running a fresh CUDA build at b3c3b96a139d4ef1bdec926ac17aa040981cfc5d on Ubuntu Linux (Deepseek-V4-Flash).
- Launch CMD: `./llama-server --model {{PATH OMITTED}}/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731_IQ3_XS-L21_UBER_TEMPLATEFIX.gguf --alias DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --timeout -1 --fit on --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --no-mmap --cache-ram 6144 -c 524288 -lv 4 -fa on -b 2048 -ub 2048 -np 1 --jinja --reasoning-preserve`
- Firefox browser under Windows 11.

## Expected Behavior:
Tools should be opt-in in all cases. Or at a minimum, a global opt-out should be available. I prefer to keep my AI powered tool usage heavily sandboxed and one of my main uses for the llama.cpp WebUI was as a no-tool chat option with any of my models. Now, every time I fire up a new connection to my server from one of my PC's, Deepseek is trying to read the time and browser information immediately, blocking the chat on a permission request after a few minutes of waiting on prompt-processing. It can be turned back off, but the default is set on every browser, machine, and non-history-tracking tab.

I understand that these particular tools are mostly harmless, however as the WebUI currently stands, it doesn't match how the '--tools' CLI argument claims to work in the help menu and at least for my current model of choice, introduces an almost guaranteed permission request. Potentially halting the model after a few minutes of PP work after the user has moved attention elsewhere. All for some information which is extremely unlikely to actually be helpful to the model.

## Request & Motivation:
I would like to make a request that going forwards, all tool usage be gated behind either the existing '--tools' CLI argument, or a new opt-out style argument, regardless of its scope or simplicity.

I have seen a number of people in some of the PR's related to these newer features expressing security concerns, and I am certainly one to share them. At a minimum I would like to know that as long as I configure my server launch correctly, I won't have my models suddenly handed new tool calling abilities. Either in browser or on the servers host machine.

## Overview
PH1 (MTT S5000, MUSA architecture `31`) is the current MUSA target, but parts of the CUDA backend still assumed the first generation (MTT S80, `21`) or carried compile-time workarounds for older MUSA toolkits. This series lets those paths use the upstream code and fixes the operator failures that `test-backend-ops` reports on an MTT S5000 with MUSA SDK 5.2.0:
- **build and enablement** — 16-byte copies like `sm_70` and up, the CUB based paths, the cooperative launch query and the device warp size, `CUDA_SET_SHARED_MEMORY_LIMIT`, `cudaFuncSetAttribute`, and MUSA-only guards that a runtime architecture check already covers
- **operator fixes** — the `q8_0` dequantization kernel was compiled out on MUSA (moved to #29292), the fused `TOPK_MOE` kernel could hang in `__syncthreads()`, `MMQ` computes wrong values on PH1, `GATED_DELTA_NET` is enabled
- **flash attention** — availability is decided from the runtime compute capability, and `IQ4_NL` is supported as a KV cache type (moved to #29293)
- **graphs** — the stream capture query API is aliased for MUSA, so a `-DGGML_MUSA_GRAPHS=ON` build compiles

## Overview

This release focuses on backend performance and correctness, broader model coverage, and more robust server/router operation. It adds HRM-Text (DFM Mimir 1B) support, MiMo-V2.6 and HunyuanOCR conversion support, ggml 0.25.0 backend improvements, multi-address HTTP binding, image outputs from function calls, and several chat parser/UI fixes.

- Accelerate CUDA `conv2d` with implicit GEMM ([#29135](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29135))

- Enable CUDA graphs for MTP drafting ([#28549](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28549))

- Write the SWA pattern in the model saver and round-trip 15 more architectures ([#29042](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29042))

- Add close button to UI toasts ([#28246](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28246))

- Restore the reasoning menu in single-model desktop mode ([#27985](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27985))
- Stop re-probing a disabled `/tools` endpoint on every message ([#28646](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28646))

### ggml changes

- Updated ggml to v0.25.0 ([release](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases/tag/v0.25.0))
- The release expands hyper-connection, flash-attention, and fused MoE/SSM support across backends, with robustness, quantization, data-layout, and RPC/meta improvements.

## Overview

<!-- TODO(author): describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
Two fixes to the `ggml-cuda` dequantization kernels:
- `dequantize_block_q8_0_f16` is guarded by `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= GGML_CUDA_CC_PASCAL`. MUSA's `mcc` defines `__MUSA_ARCH__` in the device pass and not `__CUDA_ARCH__`, so the condition is false, the body is dropped and the kernel is launched empty — every `q8_0` dequantization produces garbage. Also guard on `__MUSA_ARCH__`; NVIDIA builds are unaffected because `defined(__MUSA_ARCH__)` is false there.
- `dequantize_block_iq4_nl` writes `QK_K` values per block, but an `IQ4_NL` row is only guaranteed to be a multiple of `QK4_NL`, and ops such as `MUL_MAT` do use shorter rows. Threads whose 32-value sub-block starts at or past the end of the row were reading and writing past the end of the output. Skip those sub-blocks. For rows that are a multiple of `QK_K` the check never fires.
Both were found with `test-backend-ops` on an MTT S5000 (MUSA architecture `31`); the `q8_0` case is MUSA specific, the `iq4_nl` case is backend independent.

## Overview

Adds Metal backend fusion optimizations for MoE / Gated Delta Net paths:

- Top-k MoE routing fusion: SOFT_MAX + ARGSORT + GET_ROWS with optional norm/scale
- MoE weighted reduction fusion: MUL + expert views + ADD chain
- RMS_NORM + SCALE fusion
- SSM_CONV + UNARY (silu) fusion
- Use Metal function constants for the runtime-variant branches (top-k MoE with_norm, RMS_NORM + SCALE)
- Rename moe_weighted_reduction to moe_reduce
- Regenerate the Metal fusion baseline

Also includes fusion infrastructure improvements:

- Refactor fusion alloc dependencies to a pattern-driven approach
- Use vector-based fusion op sequences and declarative multi-output fusion
- Hide the fusion pattern definition in the cpp file
- Add a memory-range guard that rejects fusions with aliased external sources
- Fix Metal cross-device copy synchronization by waiting on the destination completion event

The MUSA part of the guard is now additionally conditioned on `defined(__MUSA_ARCH__)`, and [the runtime check in the host code] rejects devices whose MUSA architecture has no FA device code (only `QY2` / `mp_22` and later have it).

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 10276 (6ea215d17)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

The defect is still present in current `master` (`cd0fa60`, b10286) — see line references below.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

6x RTX 5090 (sm120), x86_64

### Models

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (unsloth `UD-Q3_K_XL`), with the DSpark drafter (`--spec-type draft-dspark`).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama_kv_cache_dsv4::state_read()` clears the **entire** CSA/HCA/LID compressed caches — i.e. all sequences — before reading back the state of a **single** sequence:

```cpp
// src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1594-1604 (master cd0fa60)
    kv_raw->state_read(io, seq_id, flags);          // <-- correctly scoped to seq_id

    if (!partial_only) {
        kv_csa->clear(true);                        // <-- cache-wide: ALL sequences
        kv_hca->clear(true);
        kv_lid->clear(true);

        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_csa.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_hca.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_lid.get(), seq_id, flags);
    }
```

`llama_kv_cache::clear(bool)` is cache-wide, while the restore of the raw cache immediately above it is scoped to `seq_id`. The class already provides a sequence-scoped helper for exactly this:

```cpp
// src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1671
void llama_kv_cache_dsv4::clear_compressed(llama_seq_id seq_id, bool data);
```

That helper was introduced by #25521 ("DeepseekV4: clear cache only for seq rather than full", `13f2b28b0`) specifically so that per-sequence operations stop wiping the whole compressed cache, and `seq_rm()` (line 1447) and `seq_keep()` (line 1481) both use it correctly. `state_read()` is the one path that still does a full clear.

**Consequence.** With `--parallel N` (N > 1, which is also the server's auto default of 4), restoring the state of one sequence destroys the compressed KV of every *other* sequence while leaving their raw KV intact. Those sequences are left silently desynced — no error and no crash, they simply continue decoding against zeroed compressed caches. The user-visible symptom is one slot abruptly losing its context while other slots are being restored.

Affected paths are any single-sequence `state_read`: `POST /slots/{id}?action=restore`, `--prompt-cache`/checkpoint reload, and `llama_state_seq_set_data()` in the public API.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `llama-server` with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `--parallel 2` (or the auto default of 4) and `--slot-save-path <dir>`.
2. Build up a conversation on slot 0 and a second, different conversation on slot 1.
3. `POST /slots/0?action=save`, then `POST /slots/0?action=restore`.
4. Continue the conversation on **slot 1** — its continuation no longer reflects its own history.

**Suggested fix** — use the existing seq-scoped helper, which already treats `seq_id < 0` as "all":

```cpp
    if (!partial_only) {
        clear_compressed(seq_id, true);

        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_csa.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_hca.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_lid.get(), seq_id, flags);
    }
```

**Disclosure about how this was found.** This is from code inspection while investigating unrelated context-corruption on our rig, not from a captured reproduction — we run `--cache-ram 0` and avoid the restore path, so I do not have a log of the failure itself. The control flow above is unambiguous, but I have not bisected a live repro, hence no log section below. Happy to run the reproduction above and report back if that would help.

**Note on similar-looking reports.** #25171 ("forgets everything") and #25259 ("forgot context when hit cache or use checkpoint in long context") describe the same user-visible symptom, but both were opened (2026-06-30 and 2026-07-03) *before* the commit below landed, so this is not their original cause. Mentioning them only because the symptom class is identical and multi-slot users hitting it today may now be running into this instead.

### First Bad Commit

`91d2fc387` — "llama_dsv4: write only used rows in state" (#25325, 2026-07-20). That commit added the three cache-wide clears inside `state_read`; the patch hunk is `@@ -1366,6 +1419,10 @@ void llama_kv_cache_dsv4::state_read`. Before it, `state_read()` did not clear the compressed caches at all.

### Relevant log output

```
Not applicable — reported from code inspection, see disclosure above.
```

items.body:
### Summary

With `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (GGUF) served by `llama-server` with `--jinja` and tools armed, generation **terminated mid-tag with `finish_reason: "stop"`** on three consecutive agent turns — each time exactly at the point where the reasoning stream contained literal DSML closing fragments (`</｜DSML｜parameter>`, `</｜DSML｜invoke>`). The final streamed token was `tool_c` — an *incomplete* `</｜DSML｜tool_calls>` closing tag. The client-visible result is an agent that appears to stop mid-tool-call, and (because the truncated message is persisted into history) a self-perpetuating loop: each follow-up turn imitates the truncated pattern and gets cut at the same place.

### Environment

- `llama-server` build 10573, commit `d775b8967` (master, 2026-08-22), AppleClang 21, Darwin arm64
- Backends: Metal (M5 Max) + one RPC worker (DGX Spark GB10), `--split-mode layer`
- Model: `unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF` UD-Q8_K_XL (5 shards) + `dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf` draft
- Flags: `--spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max 3 -c 393216 --flash-attn on --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 --jinja --temp 0.6 --top-p 0.95`
- Effective slot state observed: `chat_format: "peg-native"`, `reasoning_format: "deepseek"`, `generation_prompt: "<｜Assistant｜><think>"`

### Observed (3 consecutive turns, harness session transcript)

| Turn | input tokens | output tokens | finish | stream ends at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~165,000 | ~120 (est.) | stop | reasoning text `...a1b2c3d` + `</｜DSML｜parameter>` |
| 2 | 168,991 | 126 | stop | `...a1b2c3` + `</｜DSML｜parameter>\n</｜DSML｜invoke>\n</｜DSML｜tool_c` |
| 3 | 169,132 | 119 | stop | same fragment, same cut point |

Final reasoning deltas for turn 3 (verbatim, from the client event log):

```
... 'c', '3', '</｜DSML｜', 'parameter', '>', '\n', '</｜DSML｜', 'inv', 'oke', '>', '\n', '</｜DSML｜', 'tool', '_c'
```

The model was composing a file-edit tool call whose parameter value contained backtick-quoted hex strings (`` `a1b2c3d4e5f6` ``). The reasoning text shows the model interleaving protocol markup into the thinking channel; the stream then terminates *mid-tag*. No EOS content token is visible in the client stream — the stop appears to come from the serving side's handling of the DSML structure, not from a deliberate EOS the model wrote.

### Expected

Reasoning/thinking content should be treated as opaque text: a stray or partial DSML closing tag inside reasoning must not end generation. If the model truly opens a tool call, the parser should wait for a well-formed close; a malformed close should yield a parse error or plain text — never a silent mid-tag `stop`.

### Minimal repro attempt (negative result at short context)

A direct request asking the model to quote `</｜DSML｜parameter>` inside its reasoning, with a dummy tool armed, completed normally at short context (`finish: stop`, 271 completion tokens, tag quoted intact). So the failure is **not** triggered by the tag alone — the incidents happened at **~165–169K context depth** in an agentic multi-tool flow (the harness session had ~100 prior tool calls). Possibly depth-dependent (parser state / attention degradation at depth making the model emit protocol markup mid-reasoning more likely, and/or the parser's early-stop engaging once it does).

### Why it matters

The truncated message is persisted by clients as a normal completed turn (`finish: stop`), and the model then imitates its own truncated pattern on the next turn — the failure is self-reinforcing within a session. Three identical stops in a row required abandoning the session.

### Related

- vllm-project/vllm#48931 — DSML parser fragility when the model omits the `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` START wrapper (V4, long context)
- ggml-org/llama.cpp#25618 — draft-dspark/draft-mtp greedy divergence on quantized targets
- ggml-org/llama.cpp#26554 — DSpark + V4-Flash long-generation abort

Happy to provide the full client event log (JSONL), server logs, or test patches.

items.body:
## Overview

Adds DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM`) under its own `deepseek41` architecture: conversion, the runtime graph, and the chat template. An earlier revision of this PR was conversion only, so a converted file had nowhere to load. It is now the full path.

16 commits, 23 files, +2090 / -77.

### Conversion

Subclasses the existing V4 model. Most of the V4 path carries over unchanged. What needed handling:

- Text parameters are nested under `text_config`, so they are promoted in `index_tensors`. Overriding `load_hparams` does not work, because `ModelBase.__init__` calls it explicitly rather than through the instance.
- `num_hash_layers` is absent in V4.1 while the V4 path reads it unconditionally.
- The FP8 scale block size is `[32, 32]` rather than `[128, 128]`. V4 hardcodes 128, and reusing that value rescales every dequantized weight without raising, so the block size is read from `quantization_config`.
- Indexer `k_norm` and `wk` map onto the existing `INDEXER_K_NORM` and `INDEXER_ATTN_K`. `attn.compressor.ape` and `attn.indexer.compressor.*` are absent in V4.1 and go unused.
- Four new tensors for the engram conditional memory (`ENGRAM_EMBD`, `ENGRAM_Q`, `ENGRAM_K`, `ENGRAM_WKV`).

The two engram tables need a separate write path. Each is `384,006,168 x 256`, and the inherited FP8 dequant computes `weight.float() * scale` over the whole tensor, which is about 393 GB as float32 for one table. They are read in row blocks from the safetensors shard, quantized per block, and accumulated into a disk backed memmap. Their scale layout also differs: `[rows, 8]`, one scale per 32 columns of a single row, rather than the `[rows/32, cols/32]` tiling the linear weights use.

### Runtime

`src/models/deepseek41.cpp` is the V4.1 graph. Three things are not V4, and two of them fail silently rather than raising:

- **Sparse attention.** V4 keys everything off `dsv4_compress_ratios[il]` being 4 or 128. In the released V4.1 checkpoint those ratios are 0, 1 and 2, so V4's builder matches neither branch and drops the long range half of attention while still producing fluent text. V4.1 puts compressors on a few source layers rather than every layer, applies a pooling gate only where the ratio is above 1, and takes index keys from the shared KV latent through `indexer.wk` and `k_norm` rather than a second compressor. Nothing here is hardcoded: the loader derives each layer's role from which tensors the file actually carries, since only a compressor owner has the compressor weights, only an index key owner carries `indexer_attn_k`, and only an index source carries `indexer_attn_q_b`.
- **No q head norm.** V4 applies an extra unweighted `rms_norm` to `q` after `wq_b`. V4.1 does not. Also silent: the output stays fluent and is wrong.
- **Engram.** Two tables, on layers 1 and 14, with different row counts (384,006,168 and 384,016,682) because each layer seeds its own prime sized buckets. The lookup is a prime modulo hash reading `(max_ngram_size - 1) * n_heads = 24` rows per token per engram layer, so 48 per token, every token. The tables want to be host resident rather than treated as ordinary weights.

The compressed stream helpers in `llama_kv_cache_dsv4` are shared with V4 rather than duplicated, which is most of the diff to `src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp` and `src/models/deepseek4.cpp`.

This path also exposed an upstream bug, fixed here: `llama_kv_cache::build_input_k_rot` loops forever when `n_embd_head_k_all` is 0, which is what a cache whose layer filter selected nothing leaves it at. It presents as a hang at 100% of one core in `graph_reserve` with no error. V4 never hits it because its compressed caches always have layers.

## The architecture name

An earlier revision of this PR rode on `MODEL_ARCH.DEEPSEEK4` and added the engram tensors to V4's own list. That was wrong twice over, and it now declares `deepseek41` instead. `DEEPSEEK4` is left untouched.

**Convention.** llama.cpp does not mirror the HF `model_type`, it drops the `_v`: `deepseek_v2` became `deepseek2`, `deepseek_v3.2` became `deepseek32`, `qwen2_moe` became `qwen2moe`. Only 11 of the 153 arch strings in `constants.py` contain an underscore at all, so vLLM's `deepseek_v41` would be the odd one out here.

**Failure mode.** V4.1 ships the per-layer `hc_attn_{fn,base,scale}` and `hc_ffn_{fn,base,scale}`, 40 of each, but none of `output_hc_fn`, `output_hc_base` or `output_hc_scale`. Routing a V4.1 file to the V4 loader therefore produces a confusing partial match rather than a clean refusal. The declared lists show the same thing: `DEEPSEEK4` carries 48 tensor families and `deepseek41` carries 39, and the 15 it does not use include all three `HC_HEAD_*` and all six `NEXTN_*`.

`deepseek41`'s tensor list is the 39 families the converter actually writes, derived by reverse mapping them through `TENSOR_NAMES` rather than by trimming V4's list. Against `DEEPSEEK4` it drops `HC_HEAD_{FN,BASE,SCALE}`, `FFN_GATE_TID2EID`, `ATTN_COMPRESSOR_APE`, the four `INDEXER_COMPRESSOR_*` and all six `NEXTN_*`, and adds six: the four `ENGRAM_*` plus `INDEXER_ATTN_K` and `INDEXER_K_NORM`.

## Additional information

**Conversion.** Converted `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` end to end on one machine with 121 GiB of RAM: 1046 tensors, 507.9 GB at `--outtype q8_0` with MXFP4 experts, peak host memory under 8 GB above baseline. Output checked with `GGUFReader`, all 8 engram tensors present. Quantized further to Q2_K and Q3_K_M to confirm the file is well formed downstream.

Measured rung sizes, for anyone estimating: Q8_0 staging 473.1 GiB (1046 tensors), Q2_K 246.3 GiB, Q3_K_M 323.4 GiB. Those ratios read high against the staging file because it is not uniformly Q8_0: routed experts land as MXFP4, so parts of the ladder move up rather than down. At Q3_K_M the expert down projection goes MXFP4 to q5_K and grows from 2295 to 2970 MiB.

`Q2_K_S` and `IQ2_M` both need an imatrix. Q1_0 is unusable on this model and it is the file rather than

items.body:
This is the successor to https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26563
People seem to want full performance, and other options I had not initially included. If a reviewer wants me to remove features, or apply some more "hacky"fixes and make a smaller diff version or a cleaner commit history, I am very willing to do both 

## Additions:

0. Everything is dependent on flags. The process without any of the flags active is simply a 1:1 original llama instance. I did not change defaults or make anything non opt-in
1. 2 different configurable ways to feed the heat-map with decay, from the cold path counts or from graph readback so it also works standalone
2. Expert-level offload granularity, so the store splits the MoE weights per expert instead of per layer
3. Device priority stores based on heatmap, so the hottest experts go to the best device and colder ones spill down to the weaker ones
4. Expert pinning and evicting on mmap, so the pages of stable GPU experts get dropped while the likely-next ones stay warm and evictions never refault from disk
5. Custom ram pool with reduced ram usage when -no-mmap is run along with multiple devices, since the expert tensors get ghost buffers and only what the cpu path needs is actually held
6. Auto-fit on new functionality (off by default, ehs -1 activates everything. Slots into existing autofit so that has to be enabled or the slots set manually)
7. Respects -ts and splits the expert slots according to it
8. Separate throttled pcie to pcie device queue to reduce thrashing on multi gpu, with one move per turn and per-pair scratch buffers
9. Multiple debug dials, examples of which include printing the heatmap every time stats print
10. May work in multiple backends (I have seen others confirm but can only verify myself on vulkan and cuda)
11. Fused cold op path, so the cold experts are calculated in one pass instead of three separate ones
12. Copy or move mode, since copying the experts to the gpu costs ram while moving frees the ram after a verified transfer
13. Verified swap handshake, since every expert move is hash verified before it is routed so corruption from torn copies is not a thing
14. Sidecar heatmap persistence, so the heatmap is saved to a file next to the model on exit and loaded on the next launch so the store starts already converged
15. Hit-rate driven adaptive resync cadence, so the swap period grows the longer the store proves itself stable and a settled store barely re-plans
16. Set Device GPU store and priority manually (currently follows default device priority, may add manual switch too if people want it)

## Quick start:
Use -ehs N to set number of expert slots. Never use in conjunction with -ncmoe as that takes away vram for static experts. In most cases its recommended to just set fit target. Otherwise you'll have to figure out the best value to set.
copy vs move mode.
Copy mode stores all experts on system RAM and only copies them over to vram. Takes up more RAM, but is faster to heat up
Move mode only keeps 1 copy of an expert at a time, moving them between your cpu and gpu. When run with -no-mmap (you cant copy experts back to mmap), it saves ram but slower to heat up
-expert-sidecar saves your heatmap next to your model file on exit or loads a previously saved heatmap if present. Helps a lot with initial speed.
-expert-pin N. Pins the N% of hottest experts on your mmap to your ram using willneed. early testing shows the optimal value is between 30 and 60 depending on model size. You can do 100 if you want to use heatmap but the model fits so you just want to have it set all memory as willneed. However pinning on its own has shown minimal benefit especially on well optimized linux distros.

## Who is this for?:
Everyone can test it, but most benefit will be visible to people with 1 gpu, who have a model they can fit at least 40% of the model in their vram. Configurations outside of that can also provide a benefit but it can be hit or miss.

## Known limitations:
Multi gpu performance. I have designed a swap system that in theory should not have overhead. However, I lack proper testing apparatus so multi gpu performance may not be optimal
Back-end support: Others have reported past versions working on other back-ends too. I hope thats the case. However, i am not rich. I only have access to 2 GPUs one of which is Vulcan only and old. So i can only test on Vulcan and CUDA.
Due to differences in floating point calculations depending on where each expert is calculated, even at temp 0, when different experts are cached, the output may slightly vary. I have run extended tests and confirmed this is not silent corruption and happens on the original llama too if you change "--n-cpu-moe"
High end hardware. I do not have access to any. So its impossible to optimise. Some have reported good results, some bad. But I would need to work closer with people to understand
Under 256 token generation sessions: When llama.cpp itself (client, server, etc) has processed less than 256 tokens it may be slower than stock. If you do not close and re open the client it will quickly start outpacing it. Benchmarks that generate 128 tokens and restart the server will produce uncharacteristically bad results that are not representative of real world performance.
While -np2 works, the slowdown will be bigger than on stock. So its probably better for -np 1, about on par with -np 2, and worse after that.

## Warnings:
Auto-fit. Relies on stock autofit. If you have manually set -cmoe, -ncmoe, -ngl, etc etc, it will fail and you will have to manually submit a -ehs value.
If your cpu or PCI express buss is your bottleneck, it may worsen performance
The flags equivalent of -no-mmap uses a bit more ram than no mmap on the same configuration on stock (without the flags, or the pull request) due to the need for a buffer to move experts around without overwriting each other. I designed it so it only has a buffer on the CPU side so vram usage would not increase. The

## Overview

This adds a ROCm matrix-core (MFMA) path for the DeepSeek-V3.2/V4 lightning indexer. The
current non-CUDA path runs the indexer on the scalar `lightning_indexer_kernel_vec`
kernel, which leaves the CDNA matrix cores idle; NVIDIA already has a tensor-core
(`wmma`) path 

The main motivation is DeepSeek-V4 long-context, where the lightning indexer scores every
KV token for top-k sparse-attention selection and its cost grows with context length.

## Performance

Tested with DeepSeek-V4 Flash GGUF (UD-IQ2_XXS, 84.6 GiB) on four MI250X (gfx90a) GCDs
using ROCm 7.2 (`-ngl 99 -fa on -sm layer -b 2048 -ub 512 -r 3`). Back-to-back A/B in the
same window; baseline is the existing `_vec` path (`GGML_INDEXER_NO_MFMA=1`).

 **Prefill (pp512):**
  | Context | master      | this change | Improvement |
  |---------|-------------|-------------|-------------|
  | 0       | 405.9 tok/s | 408.8 tok/s | +0.7%       |
  | 16K     | 277.3 tok/s | 311.9 tok/s | +12.5%      |
  | 64K     | 146.2 tok/s | 188.7 tok/s | +29.1%      |

  **Decode (tg16):**
  | Context | master     | this change | Improvement |
  |---------|------------|-------------|-------------|
  | 0       | 23.6 tok/s | 25.1 tok/s  | +6.4%       |
  | 16K     | 21.5 tok/s | 22.5 tok/s  | +4.8%       |
  | 64K     | 19.5 tok/s | 20.3 tok/s  | +4.0%       |

## Testing

Ran `test-backend-ops test -o LIGHTNING_INDEXER -b ROCm7`
144/144 LIGHTNING_INDEXER tests passed on gfx90a (all K types: f16, q8_0, q5_1, q5_0,
q4_1, q4_0; `max_nmse_err = 1e-6` vs the CPU reference).

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the contributing guidelines
- AI usage disclosure: Yes, AI assistance was used under my supervision. AI located the
  ROCm scalar-only indexer dispatch. The rocWMMA MFMA implementation was co-designed, at roughly a 60% AI / 40% me split. All results above were validated by me.

- I7-8700T 6C/12T + 128GB DDR4

### Models

[DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ2_M](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF/tree/main/UD-IQ2_M)
[dev7a/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/dev7a/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-GGUF/resolve/main/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-Q2_K-Q8_0-dflash.gguf)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Command line used

```bash
GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1 ./llama-server \
  --model ~/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/UD-IQ2_M/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ2_M-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  --model-draft ~/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-Q2_K-Q8_0-dflash.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max 5 \
  --ctx-size $((64*1024)) \
  --no-context-shift \
  --gpu-layers 999 \
  --n-cpu-moe 43 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 \
  --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --fit off \
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --min-k 20 \
  --threads 6 --threads-batch 6 \
  --batch-size 4096 --ubatch-size 2048 \
  --cache-ram 0 \
  --jinja \
  --parallel 1 \
  --log-verbosity 4 \
  --no-mmap \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8080
```

## Logs

Drafter metadata **does** declare the mask token:

```console
- kv  42:               tokenizer.ggml.model str              = no_vocab
- kv  43:               tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id u32      = 128799
...
print_info: vocab type  = no vocab
```

But the speculative implementation resolves it to -1 and fails on every draft decode:

```console
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: adding speculative implementation 'draft-dspark'
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - n_max=5, n_min=0, p_min=0.00
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - block_size=5, mask_token_id=-1, n_extract=3
...
E init: invalid token[1] = -1
E decode: failed to initialize batch
E llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -1
W draft: llama_decode returned -1
(repeats 8x per step, then stalls)
```
## Root cause

**`src/llama-vocab.cpp`** — the `no_vocab` branch sets `special_mask_id = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL` and returns before any metadata is read (~line 1933):

```cpp
if (tokenizer_model == "no_vocab" || tokenizer_model == "none") {
    type = LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_NONE;
    special_bos_id  = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL;
    ...
    special_mask_id = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL;   // hardcoded; metadata never consulted
    ...
    return;                               // skips the metadata read below
}
```

**`common/speculative.cpp`** (~line 970) trusts the vocab API with no fallback:

```cpp
mask_token_id = llama_vocab_mask(llama_model_get_vocab(model_dft));   // returns -1
```

That `-1` is then injected into the draft batch (~line 1153):

```cpp
common_batch_add(batch, i == 0 ? dp.id_last : mask_token_id, n + i, { seq_id }, true);
```

→ `invalid token[1] = -1` → `llama_decode` returns -1.

The metadata key is valid and correctly mapped in `src/llama-arch.cpp:345`:

```cpp
{ LLM_KV_TOKENIZER_MASK_ID, "tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id" },
```

It's simply unreachable on the `no_vocab` path.

## Suggested fix

`common/speculative.cpp` already reads another drafter field (`dflash.block_size`) directly from metadata via `llama_model_meta_val_str` for exactly this reason (~line 962). Applying the same pattern to the mask token is the smallest, most contained fix:

```diff
         mask_token_id = llama_vocab_mask(llama_model_get_vocab(model_dft));
+
+        // no_vocab drafters (DSpark/DFlash) nullify the mask token in the vocab, so
+        // fall back to the GGUF metadata key when the vocab API returns nothing.
+        // Mirrors the dflash.block_size metadata read above.
+        if (mask_token_id < 0) {
+            char buf[32] = {};
+            if (llama_model_meta_val_str(model_dft, "tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id", buf, sizeof(buf)) >= 0) {
+                mask_token_id = (llama_token) std::atoi(buf);
+            }
+        }
```

With this change, the log line flips from `mask_token_id=-1` to `mask_token_id=128799` and the `invalid token` / decode failures stop. No new includes needed — `llama_model_meta_val_str` and `std::atoi` are already used a few lines above for `dflash.block_size`.

(An alternative, broader fix would be to read `LLM_KV_TOKENIZER_MASK_ID` inside the `no_vocab` branch of `src/llama-vocab.cpp` so `llama_vocab_mask()` returns the right value for any caller — but the change above is sufficient for the speculative path and carries no risk to other vocab consumers.)

### Name and Version

Running llama.cpp through LM Studio runtime packs, b10760 through b11026 (runtime 2.31.2 - 2.41.0). All of them crash for me. I have Windows Error Reporting records pinning each crash to the exact engine binary via PE timestamp, so this is not a stale-process artifact.

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

7x Volta sm_70 (1x Quadro GV100 + 6x Tesla PG503-216, 32 GB HBM2 each), `--split-mode layer --tensor-split 0 --main-gpu 0`, CUDA graphs disabled via `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1`.

### Models

Reproduces across architectures (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF and DeepSeek-V4-Flash variants, various quantizations), so I don't think it's model-specific. UBatches 256 and 384 both crash at the same rate on the Qwen model.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

During normal long agent sessions (OpenAI-compatible server, one client, very long contexts with heavy prefix reuse) llama-server dies roughly daily — recently ~6 times a day — with a fail-fast (`0xc0000409` in ucrtbase.dll). The last engine line before death is always:

```
CUDA error: invalid argument
current device: 0, in function ggml_cuda_kernel_launch at ggml/src/ggml-cuda/common.cuh:<line varies by build: 1676/1710/1716>
```

The trigger pattern is consistent across three weeks of logs (~100 crashes): a large prefill (tens of thousands of tokens, up to ~112K context) with high partial prefix-cache reuse (`f_keep` 0.98-0.99), dying either right at the prefill→decode boundary (`progress = 1.00`) or mid-prefill around a batch boundary. It is probabilistic: replaying the same session mostly works, and a synthetic append-only stress run (growing prefix, ~3K new tokens per round) passed 40/40 rounds once and crashed in round 2 another time. Note it does NOT strictly require >100K context — I also have samples at 56K, 18K, and even a fresh slot crashing on its first 2-message prefill; deep context just raises the probability.

What I've ruled out by testing, not guessing:
- Engine version. Clean reinstall of runtime 2.33 still crashes (~1/day); 2.34 through 2.41 crash more often (6-10/day). #28177 and #28198 (merged Sep 3/4) look like amplifiers on the multi-GPU launch path, not the root cause.
- KV quantization (`q8_0` K/V): survived 9.5h / ~200K new prefill tokens once, then reproduced the exact same signature. Reduces frequency at best.
- `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1`: verified present in the process PEB environment. Helps on ≤2.33 builds; newer builds have launch paths that bypass it and crash anyway.
- `--no-kv-unified`, split strategy (spread vs priority-order fill): no effect.

Since both `cudaLaunchKernelEx` and the classic launch path reject the same configuration, I suspect a grid/block dimension goes out of range for some batch shape on sm_70 — similar in spirit to #27901 (gridDim.y overflow), but here it seems to need multi-GPU layer split plus partial slot reuse to show up. Volta is presumably not covered by any CI runner, which might be why this survives.

I could not reduce this to a clean `llama-completion` repro yet because the failure needs the prefix-cache reuse pattern of a long agent session; I'm happy to run bisects or test patches against my workload — I have crash logs with exact timestamps, token counts and f_keep values for every occurrence. Related but distinct signatures: #28661 (fattn-mma-f16.cuh:1945, non-standard head dim), #27871/#27901 (GB10 gridDim.y).

**First bad commit:** unknown — every runtime from b10760 to b11026 crashes; the frequency jump around Sep 3/4 suggests #28177 / #28198 amplified an older bug rather than introducing it.

## Overview
`test-save-load-state` previously required exact token sequences to match between the baseline and restored contexts. This is too strict because small numerical differences in restored state can change a sampled token even when the underlying logits are effectively identical.

This PR changes tests 3, 4, and 5 to:
- Store the raw logits for every baseline generated token.
- Compare regenerated raw logits against the baseline using NMSE.
- Fail only if NMSE exceeds `1e-5`.
- Feed the expected baseline token back into the context when the sampled token differs, so the remaining logits stay aligned.

## Overview

Adds reporting of graph inputs and input tensors to the `sched_reserve` log output in `llama-context.cpp`, and fixes the batch-size label used for the token-generation graph.

Specifically:
- The `bs` label for the token-generation graph is now reported as `n_seqs` instead of a hardcoded `1`, matching how the pp graph reports `n_tokens`.
- Reports the number of graph inputs (from `llm_graph_result::inputs`) for both the pp (prompt processing) and tg (token generation) graphs.
- Reports the number of input tensors: the distinct tensors in the graph (nodes and their `src` tensors) flagged with `GGML_TENSOR_FLAG_INPUT`.
- Logs a warning when an input tensor's op is not `GGML_OP_NONE`.
- Logs a trace (debug) line for each input tensor listing the nodes (name and op) that use it.

## Additional information

The graph-input tensors are identified by iterating over the graph nodes and their `src` tensors, tracking unique tensors via a hash map so that a tensor shared by multiple nodes is counted once.

## Overview

Fixes #29222.

The 5-argument `load_ldmatrix` added in 1884824fd only defined `tile<16, 8>`, so the Volta `tile<8, 4>` used by sm_70 had no matching overload and `fattn.cu` failed to compile.

This PR generalizes the 5-argument `load_ldmatrix` tile shape from `<16, 8>` to `<I, J>`. The non-swizzle branch forwards to the 3-argument loader, so any tile shape works. The swizzle branch is restricted to `<16, 8>` with newly added `static_assert(I == 16)` / `static_assert(J == 8)`.

This follows the existing pattern of `load_ldmatrix_trans` in the same file, which is already shape-generic plus `static_assert(I == 16)`.

Only sm70 was affected; other architectures were checked. CI does not build sm70, so this was not caught.

Local compile and test passed.

## Description:
A recent commit added the 'Current Time' and 'Runtime Info' browser commands to the WebUI. These commands are not opt-in like the other agent commands have been and are enabled by default regardless of whether you have a '--tools' CLI argument specified when launching llama-server.

## Environment:

- Firefox browser under Windows 11.

## Expected Behavior:
Tools should be opt-in in all cases. Or at a minimum, a global opt-out should be available. I prefer to keep my AI powered tool usage heavily sandboxed and one of my main uses for the llama.cpp WebUI was as a no-tool chat option with any of my models. Now, every time I fire up a new connection to my server from one of my PC's, Deepseek is trying to read the time and browser information immediately, blocking the chat on a permission request after a few minutes of waiting on prompt-processing. It can be turned back off, but the default is set on every browser, machine, and non-history-tracking tab.

I understand that these particular tools are mostly harmless, however as the WebUI currently stands, it doesn't match how the '--tools' CLI argument claims to work in the help menu and at least for my current model of choice, introduces an almost guaranteed permission request. Potentially halting the model after a few minutes of PP work after the user has moved attention elsewhere. All for some information which is extremely unlikely to actually be helpful to the model.

## Request & Motivation:
I would like to make a request that going forwards, all tool usage be gated behind either the existing '--tools' CLI argument, or a new opt-out style argument, regardless of its scope or simplicity.

I have seen a number of people in some of the PR's related to these newer features expressing security concerns, and I am certainly one to share them. At a minimum I would like to know that as long as I configure my server launch correctly, I won't have my models suddenly handed new tool calling abilities. Either in browser or on the servers host machine.

### Name and Version

```
version: 10276 (6ea215d17)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

The defect is still present in current `master` (`cd0fa60`, b10286) — see line references below.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

6x RTX 5090 (sm120), x86_64

### Models

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (unsloth `UD-Q3_K_XL`), with the DSpark drafter (`--spec-type draft-dspark`).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama_kv_cache_dsv4::state_read()` clears the **entire** CSA/HCA/LID compressed caches — i.e. all sequences — before reading back the state of a **single** sequence:

```cpp
// src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1594-1604 (master cd0fa60)
    kv_raw->state_read(io, seq_id, flags);          // <-- correctly scoped to seq_id

    if (!partial_only) {
        kv_csa->clear(true);                        // <-- cache-wide: ALL sequences
        kv_hca->clear(true);
        kv_lid->clear(true);

        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_csa.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_hca.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_lid.get(), seq_id, flags);
    }
```

`llama_kv_cache::clear(bool)` is cache-wide, while the restore of the raw cache immediately above it is scoped to `seq_id`. The class already provides a sequence-scoped helper for exactly this:

```cpp
// src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1671
void llama_kv_cache_dsv4::clear_compressed(llama_seq_id seq_id, bool data);
```

That helper was introduced by #25521 ("DeepseekV4: clear cache only for seq rather than full", `13f2b28b0`) specifically so that per-sequence operations stop wiping the whole compressed cache, and `seq_rm()` (line 1447) and `seq_keep()` (line 1481) both use it correctly. `state_read()` is the one path that still does a full clear.

**Consequence.** With `--parallel N` (N > 1, which is also the server's auto default of 4), restoring the state of one sequence destroys the compressed KV of every *other* sequence while leaving their raw KV intact. Those sequences are left silently desynced — no error and no crash, they simply continue decoding against zeroed compressed caches. The user-visible symptom is one slot abruptly losing its context while other slots are being restored.

Affected paths are any single-sequence `state_read`: `POST /slots/{id}?action=restore`, `--prompt-cache`/checkpoint reload, and `llama_state_seq_set_data()` in the public API.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `llama-server` with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `--parallel 2` (or the auto default of 4) and `--slot-save-path <dir>`.
2. Build up a conversation on slot 0 and a second, different conversation on slot 1.
3. `POST /slots/0?action=save`, then `POST /slots/0?action=restore`.
4. Continue the conversation on **slot 1** — its continuation no longer reflects its own history.

**Suggested fix** — use the existing seq-scoped helper, which already treats `seq_id < 0` as "all":

```cpp
    if (!partial_only) {
        clear_compressed(seq_id, true);

        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_csa.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_hca.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_lid.get(), seq_id, flags);
    }
```

**Disclosure about how this was found.** This is from code inspection while investigating unrelated context-corruption on our rig, not from a captured reproduction — we run `--cache-ram 0` and avoid the restore path, so I do not have a log of the failure itself. The control flow above is unambiguous, but I have not bisected a live repro, hence no log section below. Happy to run the reproduction above and report back if that would help.

**Note on similar-looking reports.** #25171 ("forgets everything") and #25259 ("forgot context when hit cache or use checkpoint in long context") describe the same user-visible symptom, but both were opened (2026-06-30 and 2026-07-03) *before* the commit below landed, so this is not their original cause. Mentioning them only because the symptom class is identical and multi-slot users hitting it today may now be running into this instead.

### First Bad Commit

`91d2fc387` — "llama_dsv4: write only used rows in state" (#25325, 2026-07-20). That commit added the three cache-wide clears inside `state_read`; the patch hunk is `@@ -1366,6 +1419,10 @@ void llama_kv_cache_dsv4::state_read`. Before it, `state_read()` did not clear the compressed caches at all.

### Relevant log output

```
Not applicable — reported from code inspection, see disclosure above.
```

items.body:
### Summary

With `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (GGUF) served by `llama-server` with `--jinja` and tools armed, generation **terminated mid-tag with `finish_reason: "stop"`** on three consecutive agent turns — each time exactly at the point where the reasoning stream contained literal DSML closing fragments (`</｜DSML｜parameter>`, `</｜DSML｜invoke>`). The final streamed token was `tool_c` — an *incomplete* `</｜DSML｜tool_calls>` closing tag. The client-visible result is an agent that appears to stop mid-tool-call, and (because the truncated message is persisted into history) a self-perpetuating loop: each follow-up turn imitates the truncated pattern and gets cut at the same place.

### Environment

- `llama-server` build 10573, commit `d775b8967` (master, 2026-08-22), AppleClang 21, Darwin arm64
- Backends: Metal (M5 Max) + one RPC worker (DGX Spark GB10), `--split-mode layer`
- Model: `unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF` UD-Q8_K_XL (5 shards) + `dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf` draft
- Flags: `--spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max 3 -c 393216 --flash-attn on --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 --jinja --temp 0.6 --top-p 0.95`
- Effective slot state observed: `chat_format: "peg-native"`, `reasoning_format: "deepseek"`, `generation_prompt: "<｜Assistant｜><think>"`

### Observed (3 consecutive turns, harness session transcript)

| Turn | input tokens | output tokens | finish | stream ends at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~165,000 | ~120 (est.) | stop | reasoning text `...a1b2c3d` + `</｜DSML｜parameter>` |
| 2 | 168,991 | 126 | stop | `...a1b2c3` + `</｜DSML｜parameter>\n</｜DSML｜invoke>\n</｜DSML｜tool_c` |
| 3 | 169,132 | 119 | stop | same fragment, same cut point |

Final reasoning deltas for turn 3 (verbatim, from the client event log):

```
... 'c', '3', '</｜DSML｜', 'parameter', '>', '\n', '</｜DSML｜', 'inv', 'oke', '>', '\n', '</｜DSML｜', 'tool', '_c'
```

The model was composing a file-edit tool call whose parameter value contained backtick-quoted hex strings (`` `a1b2c3d4e5f6` ``). The reasoning text shows the model interleaving protocol markup into the thinking channel; the stream then terminates *mid-tag*. No EOS content token is visible in the client stream — the stop appears to come from the serving side's handling of the DSML structure, not from a deliberate EOS the model wrote.

### Expected

Reasoning/thinking content should be treated as opaque text: a stray or partial DSML closing tag inside reasoning must not end generation. If the model truly opens a tool call, the parser should wait for a well-formed close; a malformed close should yield a parse error or plain text — never a silent mid-tag `stop`.

### Minimal repro attempt (negative result at short context)

A direct request asking the model to quote `</｜DSML｜parameter>` inside its reasoning, with a dummy tool armed, completed normally at short context (`finish: stop`, 271 completion tokens, tag quoted intact). So the failure is **not** triggered by the tag alone — the incidents happened at **~165–169K context depth** in an agentic multi-tool flow (the harness session had ~100 prior tool calls). Possibly depth-dependent (parser state / attention degradation at depth making the model emit protocol markup mid-reasoning more likely, and/or the parser's early-stop engaging once it does).

### Why it matters

The truncated message is persisted by clients as a normal completed turn (`finish: stop`), and the model then imitates its own truncated pattern on the next turn — the failure is self-reinforcing within a session. Three identical stops in a row required abandoning the session.

### Related

- vllm-project/vllm#48931 — DSML parser fragility when the model omits the `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` START wrapper (V4, long context)
- ggml-org/llama.cpp#25618 — draft-dspark/draft-mtp greedy divergence on quantized targets
- ggml-org/llama.cpp#26554 — DSpark + V4-Flash long-generation abort

Happy to provide the full client event log (JSONL), server logs, or test patches.

### Name and Version

version: 10318 (4cf5cab65)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

Linux m920s 6.8.0-136-generic #136-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed Jul  1 21:53:05 UTC 2026 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

- I7-8700T 6C/12T + 128GB DDR4
-  RTX 2000E Ada 16GB

### Models

[DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ2_M](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF/tree/main/UD-IQ2_M)
[dev7a/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/dev7a/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-GGUF/resolve/main/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-Q2_K-Q8_0-dflash.gguf)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Command line used

```bash
GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1 ./llama-server \
  --model ~/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/UD-IQ2_M/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ2_M-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  --model-draft ~/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-Q2_K-Q8_0-dflash.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max 5 \
  --ctx-size $((64*1024)) \
  --no-context-shift \
  --gpu-layers 999 \
  --n-cpu-moe 43 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 \
  --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --fit off \
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --min-k 20 \
  --threads 6 --threads-batch 6 \
  --batch-size 4096 --ubatch-size 2048 \
  --cache-ram 0 \
  --jinja \
  --parallel 1 \
  --log-verbosity 4 \
  --no-mmap \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8080
```

## Logs

Drafter metadata **does** declare the mask token:

```console
- kv  42:               tokenizer.ggml.model str              = no_vocab
- kv  43:               tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id u32      = 128799
...
print_info: vocab type  = no vocab
```

But the speculative implementation resolves it to -1 and fails on every draft decode:

```console
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: adding speculative implementation 'draft-dspark'
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - n_max=5, n_min=0, p_min=0.00
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - block_size=5, mask_token_id=-1, n_extract=3
...
E init: invalid token[1] = -1
E decode: failed to initialize batch
E llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -1
W draft: llama_decode returned -1
(repeats 8x per step, then stalls)
```
## Root cause

**`src/llama-vocab.cpp`** — the `no_vocab` branch sets `special_mask_id = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL` and returns before any metadata is read (~line 1933):

```cpp
if (tokenizer_model == "no_vocab" || tokenizer_model == "none") {
    type = LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_NONE;
    special_bos_id  = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL;
    ...
    special_mask_id = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL;   // hardcoded; metadata never consulted
    ...
    return;                               // skips the metadata read below
}
```

**`common/speculative.cpp`** (~line 970) trusts the vocab API with no fallback:

```cpp
mask_token_id = llama_vocab_mask(llama_model_get_vocab(model_dft));   // returns -1
```

That `-1` is then injected into the draft batch (~line 1153):

```cpp
common_batch_add(batch, i == 0 ? dp.id_last : mask_token_id, n + i, { seq_id }, true);
```

→ `invalid token[1] = -1` → `llama_decode` returns -1.

The metadata key is valid and correctly mapped in `src/llama-arch.cpp:345`:

```cpp
{ LLM_KV_TOKENIZER_MASK_ID, "tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id" },
```

It's simply unreachable on the `no_vocab` path.

## Suggested fix

`common/speculative.cpp` already reads another drafter field (`dflash.block_size`) directly from metadata via `llama_model_meta_val_str` for exactly this reason (~line 962). Applying the same pattern to the mask token is the smallest, most contained fix:

```diff
         mask_token_id = llama_vocab_mask(llama_model_get_vocab(model_dft));
+
+        // no_vocab drafters (DSpark/DFlash) nullify the mask token in the vocab, so
+        // fall back to the GGUF metadata key when the vocab API returns nothing.
+        // Mirrors the dflash.block_size metadata read above.
+        if (mask_token_id < 0) {
+            char buf[32] = {};
+            if (llama_model_meta_val_str(model_dft, "tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id", buf, sizeof(buf)) >= 0) {
+                mask_token_id = (llama_token) std::atoi(buf);
+            }
+        }
```

With this change, the log line flips from `mask_token_id=-1` to `mask_token_id=128799` and the `invalid token` / decode failures stop. No new includes needed — `llama_model_meta_val_str` and `std::atoi` are already used a few lines above for `dflash.block_size`.

(An alternative, broader fix would be to read `LLM_KV_TOKENIZER_MASK_ID` inside the `no_vocab` branch of `src/llama-vocab.cpp` so `llama_vocab_mask()` returns the right value for any caller — but the change above is sufficient for the speculative path and carries no risk to other vocab consumers.)

## Overview

Adds reporting of graph inputs and input tensors to the `sched_reserve` log output in `llama-context.cpp`, and fixes the batch-size label used for the token-generation graph.

Specifically:
- The `bs` label for the token-generation graph is now reported as `n_seqs` instead of a hardcoded `1`, matching how the pp graph reports `n_tokens`.
- Reports the number of graph inputs (from `llm_graph_result::inputs`) for both the pp (prompt processing) and tg (token generation) graphs.
- Reports the number of input tensors: the distinct tensors in the graph (nodes and their `src` tensors) flagged with `GGML_TENSOR_FLAG_INPUT`.
- Logs a warning when an input tensor's op is not `GGML_OP_NONE`.
- Logs a trace (debug) line for each input tensor listing the nodes (name and op) that use it.

## Additional information

The graph-input tensors are identified by iterating over the graph nodes and their `src` tensors, tracking unique tensors via a hash map so that a tensor shared by multiple nodes is counted once.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. llama.cpp:DeepSeek-v4-Flash-0731

items.body:
## Bug Description

GLM-5.2 crashes deterministically when attempting distributed inference across multiple DGX Spark nodes via ggml-rpc. The crash occurs during graph computation with `invalid data ptr` on the worker side and `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` abort on the orchestrator side. This appears analogous to #26424 (DeepSeek V4, Metal) but affects CUDA (sm_121).

## Environment

- **Hardware:** 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, Grace Blackwell, 128GB unified memory each)
- **OS:** DGX OS (Ubuntu-based, aarch64)
- **CUDA:** sm_121 native build
- **llama.cpp:** master `5788b510a` (ggml 0.18.1), built with `-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON`
- **Network:** 1Gbit Ethernet between nodes
- **Model:** GLM-5.2 UD-IQ4_NL (also reproduced with UD-Q4_K_M), unsloth GGUF split files

## Setup

**Workers (3 nodes):**

```
./build/bin/ggml-rpc-server -c --host 192.168.1.XXX --port 50052
```

**Orchestrator (1 node):**

```
./build/bin/llama-server \
  -m ~/models/gguf/glm-5.2/UD-IQ4_NL/GLM-5.2-UD-IQ4_NL-00001-of-00009.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  -ngl 999 -c 4096 \
  --tensor-split 1,1,1,1 \
  --rpc 192.168.1.121:50052,192.168.1.111:50052,192.168.1.128:50052
```

## Expected Behavior

Model loads across 4 nodes and serves inference (works with Gemma-4-26B, Qwen3.6-35B, Mistral-Small-3.2 on identical setup).

## Actual Behavior

Weights distribute successfully (~113GB cache per worker), but crashes during graph_compute:

**Worker output:**

[create_node] invalid data ptr[graph_compute] failed to create graph node 30 (id=197768091778640)
Client connection closed

**Orchestrator output:**

ggml-rpc.cpp:519: Remote RPC server crashed or returned malformed response
recv failed (bytes_recv=0, size_to_recv=8)

Stack trace: `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` → `ggml_backend_tensor_copy` → `ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async` → `llama_context::graph_compute` → `llama_context::decode` (during `common_init_from_params`).

## Reproducibility

- 100% deterministic — same worker, same graph node (30)
- Reproduced with UD-IQ4_NL (~348GB) and UD-Q4_K_M (~434GB)
- Reproduced with `-c 4096` and `-c 131072`
- Reproduced with and without `--no-warmup`
- All 4 nodes on identical commit (`5788b510a`, fresh pull)

## What Works

- Single-node llama.cpp on same hardware (Gemma, Qwen, Mistral)
- 2-node llama.cpp RPC with smaller models (Gemma-4-26B, ~51.8 tok/s)
- GLM-5.2 on single-node (4×RTX 6000, Ollama, Note: Different machine! But same model GLM 5.2 UD-IQ4_NL)

## Related

- #26424 — DeepSeek V4 Flash RPC crash (Metal, similar MoE/MLA architecture)
- GLM-5.2 uses IndexShare and MTP/NextN layers — likely unsupported ops in RPC graph distribution

## Logs

Full orchestrator and worker terminal output, dmesg are attached.

[glm-rpc-orch.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708516/glm-rpc-orch.log)

[glm-rpc-worker3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708521/glm-rpc-worker3.log)

[glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708525/glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log)

items.body:
*Filed by Claude (Anthropic's assistant) on behalf of @elimisteve, who reviewed it before posting. All logs and line references were produced on his machine at commit `11924d4c1`. What I could not verify is stated explicitly below.*

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 547 (11924d4c1)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Commit `11924d4c17abc27383376a1ac6a24fa3e36c1c0c` (master, 2026-08-02).

### Operating systems

Linux (Xubuntu, kernel 6.14)

### GGML backends

CUDA (13.1), CPU

### Hardware

Intel Core i9-13950HX · 188 GiB DDR5 · NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada Generation Laptop GPU, 12 GB

### Models

`unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF`, `UD-Q4_K_XL` (native MXFP4 experts), 5 shards.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` fails to start on `deepseek4` with the **default** `-np -1` (auto), and starts
normally with an explicit `--parallel 1`. Nothing else differs.

Auto mode is an unconditional `n_parallel = 4, kv_unified = true`
(`tools/server/server.cpp:151`):

```cpp
if (params.n_parallel < 0) {
    params.n_parallel = 4;
    params.kv_unified = true;
}
```

Under `kv_unified`, `n_ctx_seq` is deliberately **not** divided
(`src/llama-context.cpp:287`):

```cpp
if (cparams.kv_unified) {
    cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx;      // 131072
} else {
    cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx / cparams.n_seq_max;
```

Both values reach the dsv4 cache (`src/llama-model.cpp:2259-2268`) — `cparams.kv_unified`
(true) and `cparams.n_ctx_seq` (undivided).

`llama_kv_cache_dsv4` then **discards the unified flag**
(`src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1041-1053`):

```cpp
GGML_UNUSED(unified);

// Keep DSV4 KV/state streams per sequence even when public KV mode is unified.
const bool unified_raw = false;

kv_raw = std::make_unique<llama_kv_cache_iswa>(
        model, hparams_raw, type_k, type_v,
        v_trans, offload, swa_full, unified_raw, kv_size, n_seq_max, n_ubatch, n_pad,
        nullptr, filter_raw, reuse, nullptr);
```

`kv_size` is the constructor parameter received at line 1021 and is forwarded here
unchanged — it is not divided anywhere in between. Downstream, `n_stream` becomes
`n_seq_max` (`src/llama-kv-cache.cpp:82`):

```cpp
n_seq_max(n_seq_max), n_stream(unified ? 1 : n_seq_max), ...
```

So dsv4 combines the **non-unified stream layout** (`n_stream = n_seq_max`) with the
**unified sizing** (`kv_size = n_ctx`, undivided). Each mode is self-consistent on its own —
unified is 1 stream × `n_ctx`; non-unified is `n_seq_max` streams × `n_ctx/n_seq_max` — but
the combination appears to allocate `n_seq_max` streams of the *full* context.

The comment on line 1043 suggests forcing per-sequence streams is intentional for this
architecture. If so, the sizing may need to compensate.

#### Reproduction

Fails (default `-np`):
```
llama-server -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf \
  -ngl 999 --n-cpu-moe 43 --no-repack --load-mode mmap \
  --ctx-size 131072 -b 2048 -ub 512 -fa on -ctk f16 -t 8
```
```
E ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 672.00 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E alloc_tensor_range: failed to allocate CUDA0 buffer of size 704643072
E llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: failed to allocate buffer for kv cache
E srv  llama_server: exiting due to model loading error
```

Succeeds — only `--parallel 1` added:
```
llama-server -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf \
  -ngl 999 --n-cpu-moe 43 --no-repack --load-mode mmap --parallel 1 \
  --ctx-size 131072 -b 2048 -ub 512 -fa on -ctk f16 -t 8
```

3/3 reproductions each way.

**Stronger isolation — `-ngl 0`**, which puts no model weights on the GPU at all and still
fails, at a much smaller context:

```
# -ngl 0 --ctx-size 32768, ~4.0 GiB free VRAM reported by nvidia-smi
default -np -1 : E ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer:
                 allocating 1290.30 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
--parallel 1   : I srv load_model: initializing, n_slots = 1, n_ctx_slot = 32768,
                 kv_unified = 'false'      -> starts normally
```

Note the failing 1290 MiB allocation is smaller than the ~4.0 GiB nvidia-smi reported free.
That figure is whole-GPU free memory with other resident processes (a browser compositor and
two small CUDA clients) on the same card, and it precedes the allocations this run had
already made, so it is not directly comparable to the failing request. The meaningful
comparison is the controlled one: same machine, same instant, same command, `--parallel 1`
succeeds and the default does not.

### What I could NOT verify

- **Exact byte counts.** The failing run aborts before printing the KV/compute breakdown, and
  this GPU has other resident consumers, so I have no clean side-by-side `KV self size`
  comparison. I am therefore **not** claiming a specific multiplier — only that the default
  path allocates enough more to fail where `--parallel 1` succeeds.
- **`--parallel 4` with `kv_unified = false`** (i.e. explicit `-np 4` rather than auto). That
  would separate "4 slots" from "unified sizing" as the cause. I could not run it in time;
  the code reading suggests it should succeed, since `n_ctx_seq` would then be divided. If a
  maintainer runs only one extra experiment, this is the one.
- Whether other architectures that similarly override `unified` are affected.
- Which fix is correct.

### Possible directions (untested — no PR proposed)

1. When the caller requested unified but dsv4 forces per-sequence streams, size each stream
   as `kv_size / n_seq_max` rather than `kv_size`.
2. Or mark `deepseek4` as incompatible with `kv_unified`, so `llama-context.cpp` takes the
   dividing branch and the existing non-unified math applies unchanged.

I have not built or benchmarked either, so I am not opening a PR.

### Workaround

Pass `--parallel 1` explicitly. This also leaves `kv_unified` at its `false` default, which
[#19523](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp
items.title: Eval bug: DeepSeek-V4 (deepseek4) fails to start on CUDA with the default -np -1 (auto) — dsv4 KV cache forces per-sequence streams while kv_unified leaves n_ctx undivided

## Name and Version

llama.cpp 0.4.0, revs `18443257` and `96ffdc4`. My build pin/config: [pkgs/llama-cpp/default.nix](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/machines/blob/main/pkgs/llama-cpp/default.nix) (source rev + patches), and [shikanime-labs/machines#1357](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/machines/pull/1357) is the backend flip this issue motivated.

## Operating systems

Linux (NixOS 26.11.20260829.d2f6794).

## GGML backends

Vulkan (RADV) — fails as below. ROCm (HIP/rocblas), same rev, same GPU — qwen4exp passes (model loads and decodes: 8-token completion, ~19 tok/s, no asserts, no device loss). deepseek-v4 on ROCm: untested.

## Hardware

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 128 GB unified LPDDR5X (UMA) (Minisforum MS-S1 MAX)

## Models

- qwen4exp: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF`, revision `UD-Q4_K_XL`
- deepseek-v4: `lmstudio-community/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF`, revision `MXFP4`

## Problem description & steps to reproduce

On AMD Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S iGPU, gfx1151, RADV), any decode of qwen4exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) or deepseek-v4 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) fails. The same build and GGUF of qwen4exp runs cleanly on the same GPU with the ROCm backend (deepseek-v4 not yet retried on ROCm).

Failure modes on Vulkan/RADV:

1. Full offload (`--n-gpu-layers 999`, both archs): weights load to 100%, then the first `llama_context::decode` aborts:

   ```
   /build/source/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:283: GGML_ASSERT(offset + size <= ggml_nbytes(tensor) && "tensor read out of bounds") failed
   ```

2. Partial offload (deepseek-v4, `--n-gpu-layers 48`): the assert is bypassed, weights load, and the first graph compute loses the device:

   ```
   terminate called after throwing an instance of 'vk::DeviceLostError'
     what():  vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost
   ```

   Worker process dies with SIGSEGV (exit 139). Backtrace: `vk_queue_handle_unsynchronized::submit` → `ggml_backend_graph_compute` → `rpc_server::graph_compute`.

Backtrace of the assert path (router child, verbatim frames): `ggml_abort` → `ggml_backend_tensor_get_async` (ggml-backend.cpp:283) → `llama_context::decode` → `llama_decode` → `common_init_from_params` → `server_context_impl::load_model`.

Reproduced identically: over RPC (Vulkan device held by a worker) and node-local; with and without `--no-warmup`; with and without `--fit off`; on two revs (above), the newer of which equals master at test time.

Older-arch models (qwen3.8-27b) run continuously on the same RADV device without incident, so the defect is specific to these new-arch graphs.

The Kubernetes manifests: [shikanime-labs/manifests/apps/llama-cpp](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/manifests/tree/main/apps/llama-cpp) and [shikanime-labs/manifests/apps/llama-cpp-rpc](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/manifests/tree/main/apps/llama-cpp)

Steps to reproduce:

```
llama-server -hf unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL --n-gpu-layers 999 -c 2048
# send any single completion; the ggml-backend.cpp:283 abort fires at first decode
```

DeviceLost variant: lmstudio-community DeepSeek-V4-Flash MXFP4 GGUF with `--n-gpu-layers 48`.

## First Bad Commit

Unknown. Both tested revs fail; the newer (`96ffdc4`) equals master HEAD at test time, so this reproduces on current master.

## Relevant log output

Assert path (full offload, first decode):

```
/build/source/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:283: GGML_ASSERT(offset + size <= ggml_nbytes(tensor) && "tensor read out of bounds") failed
```

DeviceLost path (deepseek-v4, `--n-gpu-layers 48`, worker SIGSEGV exit 139):

```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'vk::DeviceLostError'
  what():  vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost
```

## Related but distinct (checked before filing)

- #27306: RADV/gfx1151 DeviceLost, but mid-prefill under draft-MTP draft decodes, process survives as a zombie. Mine: first decode, no speculative decoding, process dies.
- #27797: qwen4exp on gfx1151 outputs garbage (`//////`), no crash.
- #28497: QSA indexer top-k nondeterminism on CUDA, wrong results, no crash.
- Suspect area consistent with unmerged new-arch op work: deepseek-v4 CPU ops (#23122) and qwen4exp QSA decode reworks. At full offload the failure surfaces as a host-side tensor read OOB; at mixed placement it surfaces as a malformed submit that loses the device.

items.body:
## Environment

- llama.cpp: upstream master as of 2026-08-26 (build **b10643**), self-built Release / CUDA sm_86. The only local patches are unrelated GGML kernel optimizations; `common/chat.cpp` and the server chat pipeline are vanilla.
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M GGUF with embedded official jinja template (+mmproj)
- Server flags: `-c 120000 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 --split-mode layer -ts 1,1,1 --spec-type draft-mtp --tools all` (jinja default on)
- Client: OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, streaming, `tool_choice: auto`, ~33 tools (agentic CLI workload)

## Observed

Episodically (~2×/day under heavy agent use) a slot finishes a long generation normally and then the request dies:

```
I slot print_timing: id 3 | task 0 | eval time = 515042.58 ms / 11708 tokens
I slot print_timing: id 3 | task 0 | draft acceptance = 0.52296 (7151 accepted / 13674 generated)
I slot      release: id 3 | task 0 | stop processing: n_tokens = 37979, truncated = 0
W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <think>
W srv          stop: cancel task, id_task = 0
```

Note that `common_chat_peg_parse()` logs `effective_input.substr(result.end)` — i.e. **only the unconsumed tail**. In both captured occurrences that tail was literally `<think>\n` (8 bytes).

## Analysis

The model produced a fully valid turn — reasoning + content + one or more well-formed `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` blocks that match the per-request grammar — and then emitted a stray opening `<think>` immediately before stopping. Since the lazy grammar necessarily releases around/between tool calls, a few free tokens can land there; generation then stops (EOS / `n_predict`) leaving an unclosed tag behind.

The strict final parse (non-partial `common_chat_peg_parse()`) fails on that tail and throws:

```
The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format
```

…which makes the server cancel the task, so the client loses the entire already-generated response (~11.7k tokens here) purely because of 8 bytes of trailing garbage.

## Suggested remedies

Any of the following would remove the user-visible failure:

1. Make the autoparser's tool-call root tolerate trailing garbage after the last complete call (e.g. optional untagged `rest()` before end).
2. In `common_chat_peg_parse()` for non-partial input: before failing, retry the parse truncated right after the last complete `</tool_call>`; if it succeeds, return the structured message.
3. At minimum, don't throw on a *final* parse mismatch — degrade to raw-content passthrough instead of canceling the task.

We are running (2)+(3) locally with good results and would be happy to prepare a PR if this direction is acceptable.

## Related

- #27720 — gpt-oss malformed Harmony channel header fails the final PEG parse and errors the turn
- #27279 — peg-native + `response_format.json_schema`: parse throws → 500
- #27025 — same error string, Muse Glimmer tool calls
