items.body:
### Summary

`--spec-type draft-dflash` works well at low concurrency, but under concurrent slots the **draft model's predictions get corrupted**, draft acceptance collapses, and throughput goes into reverse (slower than no speculation). We traced this on an AMD gfx1151 APU across two ROCm versions and pinned down that the corruption **scales with the number of concurrently-drafting sequences, not with batch token count, server slot count, or draft length alone**:

| server `-np` | active requests | `--spec-draft-n-max` | noise-block batch | per-slot draft acceptance | aggregate throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 4 | 15 | 64 tok | **0.51 – 0.66** (healthy) | healthy |
| **16** | **4** | 15 | 64 tok | **0.51 – 0.66** (bit-identical to the row above, same seed) | healthy |
| 8 | 8 | 15 | 128 tok | 0.11 – 0.46 (degraded) | degraded |
| 16 | 16 | 7 | 128 tok | 0.22 – 0.74 (bimodal) | bad |
| 16 | 16 | 15 | 256 tok | **0.06 – 0.49** (bimodal; sustained load collapses to **0.0018**) | ~17–21 tok/s vs **37 tok/s** no-spec baseline |
| 16 | 16 | **1** | 32 tok | **0.83 – 0.92** | **~80 tok/s (2.2× the no-spec baseline)** |

Key observations that localize the defect:

1. **Per-slot corruption is established during prefill and persists for the request's lifetime.** 16 *identical* requests (same prompt, seed, temperature) produce an ~8× spread in acceptance across slots, visible from the very first speculative tick. The draft model's top-1 confidence is bimodal per slot: median 0.25 on "broken" slots vs 0.92–0.98 on "healthy" ones.
2. **It is not the server's slot configuration** — a `-np 16` server with only 4 in-flight requests produces bit-identical results to a `-np 4` server.
3. **It is not the drafter's intrinsic quality** — with `--spec-draft-n-max 1` the same 16-way load accepts 83–92 % of drafts and beats the no-spec baseline by 2.2×.
4. **It is not a ROCm-version regression** — identical pathology on ROCm 7.2.1 and 7.14.0 (we cannot test CUDA here; see "ask" at the end).

### Git commit

- Verified at `0b1bad14ff204627636aeb1de22ddcd5acb859d4` (2026-08-11).
- **Still reproduces on current master `0177dcc7300bad8914bb838baabce87899812491` (2026-08-15, freshly built)**: 16 identical concurrent requests → the same bimodal per-slot acceptance (0.05–0.50, broken slots waste 500–977 drafts per 160-token request); the 4-concurrent control on the same server recovers (0.19–0.61). The numbers below are from the pinned build.

Build: `-DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DROCM_PATH=…` (Release, GCC 13.3, `GGML_HIP_GRAPHS=ON` default).

Hardware/runtime: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S iGPU (gfx1151, 96 GB unified), kernel 6.17, ROCm 7.14.0 (side-by-side 7.2.1 with identical results).

Models: Muse-Glimmer-30B target (Q4_K "kquant" GGUF, ~17 GB, all layers on GPU) + the matching DFlash draft GGUF (`general.architecture = dflash`, 5 layers, `block_size=16`, 5 extracted target layers). Any supported dense target + DFlash pair should reproduce the concurrency dependence.

### Command line

```bash
llama-server -m muse-glimmer-30B-kquant-17gb.gguf -ngl 999 \
  -np 16 -c 131072 --jinja \
  -md dflash-kquant.gguf -ngld 99 \
  --spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 15 \
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64 --seed 42 \
  --port 8080 > server.log 2>&1
```

Reproduce (the server log is the instrument — `/metrics` spec counters stay 0 on these builds):

```bash
# 16 identical concurrent streaming requests
seq 16 | xargs -P16 -I{} curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain in detail why the sky is blue."}],
       "max_tokens":160,"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95,"top_k":64,"seed":42}' >/dev/null

grep 'draft acceptance' server.log
```

Controls (each on a fresh server):

- `-P4` instead of `-P16` (same `-np 16` server) → acceptance recovers to ~0.5–0.66.
- `--spec-draft-n-max 1` with `-P16` → acceptance 0.83–0.92, ~2.2× no-spec throughput.
- `-np 4` server, `-P4` → bit-identical to the `-np 16`/`-P4` run (same seed).

### Problem description & logs

Expected: draft acceptance roughly constant w.r.t. concurrency (speculative decoding is lossless; batching drafts from many sequences should not change per-sequence predictions), and DFlash at `-np 16` to at least not be slower than no speculation.

Actual (16 identical concurrent requests, fresh server, `0b1bad1`):

```
slot print_timing: id  1 | draft acceptance = 0.05333 (    4 accepted /    75 generated), mean len =  1.80
slot print_timing: id  7 | draft acceptance = 0.25424 (   45 accepted /   177 generated), mean len =  3.50
slot print_timing: id 10 | draft acceptance = 0.49074 (   53 accepted /   108 generated), mean len =  6.89
slot print_timing: id 12 | draft acceptance = 0.19048 (   44 accepted /   231 generated), mean len =  3.44
slot print_timing: id  0 | draft acceptance = 0.07289 (   32 accepted /   439 generated), mean len =  2.03
...
spec statistics: draft-dflash: #calls(b,g,a) = 16 31 294, #gen tokens = 3758, #acc tokens = 509,
                #mean acc len = 2.73, dur(b,g,a) = 0.020, 4133.404, 0.072 ms
```

Under sustained long-generation load this collapses completely — a 16×512, 5-rep run on ROCm 7.2.1 was aborted after 5 h 16 min with **3,270,000 drafted / 6,060 accepted (0.18 %)**.

Secondary symptoms at `-np 16` (measured on the same runs):

- Prompt processing with DFlash injection runs at ~57 ms/token (~17.5 tok/s) vs ~23 ms/token (~43 tok/s) without DFlash at the same `-np` — the per-sequence sequential `llama_encode` + inject `llama_decode` in `process()` is paid once per sequence per batch.
- Steady-state speculative tick is 1.15–1.5 s; `draft()` alone averages 133 ms per call (256-token noise block); per-token time grows ~3× over a 320-token request (207 → 570 ms/token), i.e. it decays as generations lengthen.
- The HIP backend logs `CUDA graph warmup reset` 1–2× per tick (54–194 per run) as batch composition chang

## Summary

FastMTP-style MTP draft models (e.g. a 32K-draft-vocab variant of Qwen3.8-27B) store
the draft MTP output projection over a **reduced draft vocabulary**, together with a
`d2t` (draft-to-target) index tensor mapping draft-vocab rows to full-vocab rows.

Before this change, a qwen35 MTP-only model containing a `d2t` tensor could not be
loaded: the MTP `output.weight` is sized `{n_embd, n_draft_vocab}` while the loader
expected `{n_embd, n_vocab}`.

The change mirrors the existing `d2t` handling in `eagle3.cpp` / `dflash.cpp`:

- `load_arch_tensors`: when loading the MTP part and a `d2t` tensor is present, load
  the output projection at the draft-vocab size (`d2t->ne[0]`).
- `graph_mtp`: scatter the draft logits into the full vocabulary with `ggml_set_rows`
  (uncovered full-vocab rows stay `-inf`), emitting the result as `result_output_d2t`
  in addition to `result_output`. `res->t_logits` ends up pointing at the full-vocab
  logits, which the speculative-decoding acceptance path needs.

## Testing

Verified with `--spec-type draft-mtp` + a 32K-draft-vocab qwen35 GGUF
(Qwen3.8-27B, dual RTX 5070 Ti): the draft model loads, MTP acceptance works, and
generation quality is unaffected.

items.body:
## Overview

This PR adds support for trimmed/compact draft vocabularies via the `d2t` (draft-to-target) mapping tensor in both `qwen35` and `qwen35moe` model architectures during MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) speculative decoding.

When loading an MTP draft model or sidecar trained with a reduced draft vocabulary (such as FastMTP / compact speculative heads), the LM head (`output.weight` or `layer.nextn.shared_head_head`) has dimensions `[n_embd, n_draft_vocab]` where `n_draft_vocab < n_vocab`. Previously, `llama_model_qwen35` and `llama_model_qwen35moe` unconditionally initialized output projections with `n_vocab`, causing loader dimension mismatches or runtime assertion failures.

With this PR:
1. When `d2t` is present, `output` and `layer.nextn.shared_head_head` are initialized with the draft vocabulary dimension `n_vocab_out = d2t->ne[0]`.
2. Fallback to `output = create_tensor(tn(LLM_TENSOR_TOKEN_EMBD), ...)` is prevented when `d2t` is present and an explicit draft head is provided.
3. In `graph_mtp`, draft candidate logits of shape `[n_draft_vocab, n_outputs]` are scattered onto a full-vocabulary `-inf` tensor of shape `[n_vocab_full, n_outputs]` using `ggml_set_rows`, consistent with existing `dflash.cpp` and `eagle3.cpp` implementations.
4. Validation assertions confirm that draft vocabulary dimensions match the active LM head.

---

## Technical Details

### 1. Root Cause
In standard MTP, the next-n prediction head shares the full vocabulary (`n_vocab = 152064` for Qwen 3.5). However, high-throughput speculative decoding optimizations often prune the draft vocabulary to the most frequent tokens (e.g. 32,768 tokens) mapped by a `d2t` tensor.
- Without `d2t` handling, `load_arch_tensors` expected `[n_embd, 152064]`, causing GGUF tensor loading failure (`tensor 'blk.0.nextn.shared_head_head.weight' size mismatch`).
- If fallback occurred, `tok_embd` was assigned to `output`, clobbering the compact draft head with target embedding weights.

### 2. Implementation
- **Detection:** `load_arch_tensors` inspects `ml.get_tensor_meta("d2t")` when `mtp_only` is true.
- **Tensors:** `output` and `layer.nextn.shared_head_head` allocate `n_vocab_out` rows.
- **Logits Projection:** In `graph_mtp`, after `cur = build_lora_mm(head_w, cur, head_s)`:
  ```cpp
  if (model.d2t) {
      const int64_t n_draft_vocab = cur->ne[0];
      const int64_t n_outputs     = cur->ne[1];
      const int64_t n_vocab_full  = (int64_t) model.vocab.n_tokens();

      GGML_ASSERT(model.d2t->ne[0] == n_draft_vocab);

      ggml_tensor * logits = ggml_fill(ctx0,
              ggml_new_tensor_3d(ctx0, GGML_TYPE_F32, 1, n_vocab_full, n_outputs), -INFINITY);
      cur = ggml_set_rows(ctx0, logits,
              ggml_reshape_3d(ctx0, cur,       1,             n_draft_vocab, n_outputs),
              ggml_reshape_3d(ctx0, model.d2t, n_draft_vocab, 1,             1));
      cur = ggml_reshape_2d(ctx0, cur, n_vocab_full, n_outputs);
      cb(cur, "result_output_d2t", -1);
  }
  ```

---

## Benchmarks & Verification

Tested on dual NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Ada / Blackwell GPUs running live inference:
- **Baseline (Autoregressive dense decoding):** ~44.5 tokens/sec (22.47 ms/token).
- **With FastMTP Draft-Vocab Trim:** **102.2 – 113.9 tokens/sec** (**8.78 – 9.84 ms/token**).
- **Speedup:** **~2.3x – 2.5x throughput improvement** with up to **82.89%** draft acceptance rate.
- **Compilation:** Clean build verified on GCC 13.3, Clang 18, and NVCC CUDA 12.0/13.3.

---

## Authors & Attribution
- **Sreesanth R** ([@Shreesh-Sree](https://github.com/Shreesh-Sree))
- **Allen Joseph** ([@unknownhackerworld](https://github.com/unknownhackerworld))

---

## Overview

Adds DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM`) under its own `deepseek41` architecture: conversion, the runtime graph, and the chat template. An earlier revision of this PR was conversion only, so a converted file had nowhere to load. It is now the full path.

16 commits, 23 files, +2090 / -77.

### Conversion

Subclasses the existing V4 model. Most of the V4 path carries over unchanged. What needed handling:

- Text parameters are nested under `text_config`, so they are promoted in `index_tensors`. Overriding `load_hparams` does not work, because `ModelBase.__init__` calls it explicitly rather than through the instance.
- `num_hash_layers` is absent in V4.1 while the V4 path reads it unconditionally.
- The FP8 scale block size is `[32, 32]` rather than `[128, 128]`. V4 hardcodes 128, and reusing that value rescales every dequantized weight without raising, so the block size is read from `quantization_config`.
- Indexer `k_norm` and `wk` map onto the existing `INDEXER_K_NORM` and `INDEXER_ATTN_K`. `attn.compressor.ape` and `attn.indexer.compressor.*` are absent in V4.1 and go unused.
- Four new tensors for the engram conditional memory (`ENGRAM_EMBD`, `ENGRAM_Q`, `ENGRAM_K`, `ENGRAM_WKV`).

The two engram tables need a separate write path. Each is `384,006,168 x 256`, and the inherited FP8 dequant computes `weight.float() * scale` over the whole tensor, which is about 393 GB as float32 for one table. They are read in row blocks from the safetensors shard, quantized per block, and accumulated into a disk backed memmap. Their scale layout also differs: `[rows, 8]`, one scale per 32 columns of a single row, rather than the `[rows/32, cols/32]` tiling the linear weights use.

### Runtime

`src/models/deepseek41.cpp` is the V4.1 graph. Three things are not V4, and two of them fail silently rather than raising:

- **Sparse attention.** V4 keys everything off `dsv4_compress_ratios[il]` being 4 or 128. In the released V4.1 checkpoint those ratios are 0, 1 and 2, so V4's builder matches neither branch and drops the long range half of attention while still producing fluent text. V4.1 puts compressors on a few source layers rather than every layer, applies a pooling gate only where the ratio is above 1, and takes index keys from the shared KV latent through `indexer.wk` and `k_norm` rather than a second compressor. Nothing here is hardcoded: the loader derives each layer's role from which tensors the file actually carries, since only a compressor owner has the compressor weights, only an index key owner carries `indexer_attn_k`, and only an index source carries `indexer_attn_q_b`.
- **No q head norm.** V4 applies an extra unweighted `rms_norm` to `q` after `wq_b`. V4.1 does not. Also silent: the output stays fluent and is wrong.
- **Engram.** Two tables, on layers 1 and 14, with different row counts (384,006,168 and 384,016,682) because each layer seeds its own prime sized buckets. The lookup is a prime modulo hash reading `(max_ngram_size - 1) * n_heads = 24` rows per token per engram layer, so 48 per token, every token. The tables want to be host resident rather than treated as ordinary weights.

The compressed stream helpers in `llama_kv_cache_dsv4` are shared with V4 rather than duplicated, which is most of the diff to `src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp` and `src/models/deepseek4.cpp`.

This path also exposed an upstream bug, fixed here: `llama_kv_cache::build_input_k_rot` loops forever when `n_embd_head_k_all` is 0, which is what a cache whose layer filter selected nothing leaves it at. It presents as a hang at 100% of one core in `graph_reserve` with no error. V4 never hits it because its compressed caches always have layers.

## The architecture name

An earlier revision of this PR rode on `MODEL_ARCH.DEEPSEEK4` and added the engram tensors to V4's own list. That was wrong twice over, and it now declares `deepseek41` instead. `DEEPSEEK4` is left untouched.

**Convention.** llama.cpp does not mirror the HF `model_type`, it drops the `_v`: `deepseek_v2` became `deepseek2`, `deepseek_v3.2` became `deepseek32`, `qwen2_moe` became `qwen2moe`. Only 11 of the 153 arch strings in `constants.py` contain an underscore at all, so vLLM's `deepseek_v41` would be the odd one out here.

**Failure mode.** V4.1 ships the per-layer `hc_attn_{fn,base,scale}` and `hc_ffn_{fn,base,scale}`, 40 of each, but none of `output_hc_fn`, `output_hc_base` or `output_hc_scale`. Routing a V4.1 file to the V4 loader therefore produces a confusing partial match rather than a clean refusal. The declared lists show the same thing: `DEEPSEEK4` carries 48 tensor families and `deepseek41` carries 39, and the 15 it does not use include all three `HC_HEAD_*` and all six `NEXTN_*`.

`deepseek41`'s tensor list is the 39 families the converter actually writes, derived by reverse mapping them through `TENSOR_NAMES` rather than by trimming V4's list. Against `DEEPSEEK4` it drops `HC_HEAD_{FN,BASE,SCALE}`, `FFN_GATE_TID2EID`, `ATTN_COMPRESSOR_APE`, the four `INDEXER_COMPRESSOR_*` and all six `NEXTN_*`, and adds six: the four `ENGRAM_*` plus `INDEXER_ATTN_K` and `INDEXER_K_NORM`.

## Additional information

**Conversion.** Converted `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` end to end on one machine with 121 GiB of RAM: 1046 tensors, 507.9 GB at `--outtype q8_0` with MXFP4 experts, peak host memory under 8 GB above baseline. Output checked with `GGUFReader`, all 8 engram tensors present. Quantized further to Q2_K and Q3_K_M to confirm the file is well formed downstream.

Measured rung sizes, for anyone estimating: Q8_0 staging 473.1 GiB (1046 tensors), Q2_K 246.3 GiB, Q3_K_M 323.4 GiB. Those ratios read high against the staging file because it is not uniformly Q8_0: routed experts land as MXFP4, so parts of the ladder move up rather than down. At Q3_K_M the expert down projection goes MXFP4 to q5_K and grows from 2295 to 2970 MiB.

`Q2_K_S` and `IQ2_M` both need an imatrix. Q1_0 is unusable on this model and it is the file rather than

## Overview

Add DFlash speculative decoding support for HunyuanOCR.

## How to run

```bash
MODELS=./models/HunyuanOCR

# 1. base model + vision projector
python convert_hf_to_gguf.py "$MODELS" --outtype f16 --outfile hyocr-f16.gguf
python convert_hf_to_gguf.py "$MODELS" --outtype f16 --mmproj --outfile mmproj-hyocr-f16.gguf

# 2. DFlash draft
python convert_hf_to_gguf.py "$MODELS/dflash" \
    --target-model-dir "$MODELS" --outtype bf16 --outfile hyocr-dflash-bf16.gguf

# 3. serve
build/bin/llama-server \
    -m  hyocr-f16.gguf \
    --mmproj mmproj-hyocr-f16.gguf \
    -md hyocr-dflash-bf16.gguf \
    --spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 15 \
    --parallel 1 -fa on --jinja
```

## Results

Tested on an Apple M5 Pro (6 performance + 12 efficiency cores, 48 GB unified memory), macOS 26.4.1, Metal backend, Release build, over 26 document-image OCR requests:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| draft acceptance | ~0.5 |
| mean accepted length | 8.6 |
| output | byte-identical to the non-speculative run |
| decode | 84.6 -> 167.1 t/s |
| prefill | 232 -> 192 t/s (the draft encodes the whole prompt) |

Decode is about 2x faster; prefill is about 17% slower because the draft encodes the entire prompt, so end-to-end is roughly break-even on short outputs and clearly faster on longer generations.

items.body:
## Summary
On AMD Strix Point (`gfx1150`) Vulkan with llama.cpp **b10724**, Qwen3.8-27B + z-lab DFlash2 (or ggml MTP draft) fails decode with:

```
init: invalid token[1] = 248320
decode: failed to initialize batch
```

**248320 equals `tokenizer.ggml.tokens` array length** — valid token ids are `0..248319`. This looks like a classic off-by-one in draft sampling / logits indexing.

## Environment
- GPU: AMD Strix Point `gfx1150`, Vulkan/RADV
- Runtime: llama.cpp **b10724** (also reproduced earlier on b10666)
- Target: `Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf` (architecture `qwen35`)
- Draft A: `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-GGUF` → `Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q4_K_M.gguf` (`dflash`)
- Draft B: Unsloth `mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_0.gguf` (`qwen35`) — same `248320` with ggml MTP
- Flags: `--spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 2` (or `draft-mtp`)

Note: Muse-Glimmer + DFlash on the same binary/hardware **works** (different vocab/arch ~200k). Vanilla Qwen3.8 without speculation is fine (~4.3 t/s).

## GGUF metadata (streaming count of `tokenizer.ggml.tokens`)
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| n_vocab (`tokenizer.ggml.tokens` len) | **248320** |
| bos_token_id | 248044 |
| eos_token_id | 248046 |

Same n_vocab / bos / eos on target, DFlash draft, and MTP draft.

## Expected
Draft sampling never emits token id `>= n_vocab`.

## Actual
First decode step emits token **248320** (exactly `n_vocab`). Server returns HTTP 500 / "Invalid input batch."

## Suggested fix
1. Clamp draft token ids to `[0, n_vocab - 1]` after sampling in the DFlash/MTP verify path.
2. Audit `qwen35` / `dflash` draft-head logits indexing for `< n_vocab` vs `<= last index` (or `argmax` over `n_vocab+1` slots).

## Repro
```bash
llama-server \
  --model Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --model-draft Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  --device Vulkan0 -ngl 999 --ctx-size 8192 \
  --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 --flash-attn on \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --no-webui
# POST /v1/chat/completions → 500; log shows invalid token 248320
```

## Related
- #27812 fixed Vulkan graph-optimizer wrong tokens for speculative acceptance (merged); this is a separate hard OOB failure that remains on tip after that fix.
- Unsloth Qwen3.8 MTP on the same stack loads without `248320` in one layout but reports **accept rate 0.0** (possible related draft-head issue; see also #28097).

Happy to provide full server logs / GGUF SHA if useful.

Linux m920s 6.8.0-136-generic #136-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed Jul  1 21:53:05 UTC 2026 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Operating systems

Linux

CUDA

### Hardware

- I7-8700T 6C/12T + 128GB DDR4
-  RTX 2000E Ada 16GB

### Models

[DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ2_M](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF/tree/main/UD-IQ2_M)
[dev7a/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/dev7a/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-GGUF/resolve/main/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-Q2_K-Q8_0-dflash.gguf)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Command line used

```bash
GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1 ./llama-server \
  --model ~/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/UD-IQ2_M/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ2_M-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  --model-draft ~/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-Q2_K-Q8_0-dflash.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max 5 \
  --ctx-size $((64*1024)) \
  --no-context-shift \
  --gpu-layers 999 \
  --n-cpu-moe 43 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 \
  --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --fit off \
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --min-k 20 \
  --threads 6 --threads-batch 6 \
  --batch-size 4096 --ubatch-size 2048 \
  --cache-ram 0 \
  --jinja \
  --parallel 1 \
  --log-verbosity 4 \
  --no-mmap \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8080
```

## Logs

Drafter metadata **does** declare the mask token:

```console
- kv  42:               tokenizer.ggml.model str              = no_vocab
- kv  43:               tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id u32      = 128799
...
print_info: vocab type  = no vocab
```

But the speculative implementation resolves it to -1 and fails on every draft decode:

```console
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: adding speculative implementation 'draft-dspark'
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - n_max=5, n_min=0, p_min=0.00
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - block_size=5, mask_token_id=-1, n_extract=3
...
E init: invalid token[1] = -1
E decode: failed to initialize batch
E llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -1
W draft: llama_decode returned -1
(repeats 8x per step, then stalls)
```
## Root cause

**`src/llama-vocab.cpp`** — the `no_vocab` branch sets `special_mask_id = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL` and returns before any metadata is read (~line 1933):

```cpp
if (tokenizer_model == "no_vocab" || tokenizer_model == "none") {
    type = LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_NONE;
    special_bos_id  = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL;
    ...
    special_mask_id = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL;   // hardcoded; metadata never consulted
    ...
    return;                               // skips the metadata read below
}
```

**`common/speculative.cpp`** (~line 970) trusts the vocab API with no fallback:

```cpp
mask_token_id = llama_vocab_mask(llama_model_get_vocab(model_dft));   // returns -1
```

That `-1` is then injected into the draft batch (~line 1153):

```cpp
common_batch_add(batch, i == 0 ? dp.id_last : mask_token_id, n + i, { seq_id }, true);
```

→ `invalid token[1] = -1` → `llama_decode` returns -1.

The metadata key is valid and correctly mapped in `src/llama-arch.cpp:345`:

```cpp
{ LLM_KV_TOKENIZER_MASK_ID, "tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id" },
```

It's simply unreachable on the `no_vocab` path.

## Suggested fix

`common/speculative.cpp` already reads another drafter field (`dflash.block_size`) directly from metadata via `llama_model_meta_val_str` for exactly this reason (~line 962). Applying the same pattern to the mask token is the smallest, most contained fix:

```diff
         mask_token_id = llama_vocab_mask(llama_model_get_vocab(model_dft));
+
+        // no_vocab drafters (DSpark/DFlash) nullify the mask token in the vocab, so
+        // fall back to the GGUF metadata key when the vocab API returns nothing.
+        // Mirrors the dflash.block_size metadata read above.
+        if (mask_token_id < 0) {
+            char buf[32] = {};
+            if (llama_model_meta_val_str(model_dft, "tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id", buf, sizeof(buf)) >= 0) {
+                mask_token_id = (llama_token) std::atoi(buf);
+            }
+        }
```

With this change, the log line flips from `mask_token_id=-1` to `mask_token_id=128799` and the `invalid token` / decode failures stop. No new includes needed — `llama_model_meta_val_str` and `std::atoi` are already used a few lines above for `dflash.block_size`.

(An alternative, broader fix would be to read `LLM_KV_TOKENIZER_MASK_ID` inside the `no_vocab` branch of `src/llama-vocab.cpp` so `llama_vocab_mask()` returns the right value for any caller — but the change above is sufficient for the speculative path and carries no risk to other vocab consumers.)


### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>
<!-- Copy-pasted short logs go into the "console" area here -->


items.body:
## Overview Today the model-based drafters throw away most of what the draft model knows. They run the sampler, discard its result, and take the top candidate, and the target then accepts that token only when its own draw lands on the same one. At temperature 0 that is the best available, since the target also always takes its top token. Above 0, they differ - the target samples while the draft still offers its single safest guess - and acceptance falls away as temperature rises. This PR adds two things to make this better. - Make the target use rejection sampling instead of requiring an exact match. - Despite the above, if the draft still gives its top candidate only, it evaluates to min(1, p(x)/1), same as p(x). Hence to make q(x) land, we make the draft probabilistic as well. This time the effective probability that a candidate is chosen from draft is sum_x(q(x)*min(1, p(x)/q(x))). The output distribution is preserved exactly. Accepting with `min(1, p/q)` and drawing the remainder from `norm(max(0, p - q))` is the standard construction; the residual cancels the over-delivery on tokens where the draft is more generous than the target. This is same as the mechanism in Leviathan et al. This PR applies to draft_simple and MTP only. Eagle3 is yet to be evaluated and DFlash is experimentally seen not to benefit with these changes. The likely reason for this is structural. DFlash reads every position of its block out of a single forward pass with no re-decode between them, so the positions are predicted jointly rather than conditioned on one another. Substituting a sampled token at one position leaves the rest of the block continuing from a token that was never drafted. The gain at that position is cancelled by the positions after it, which no longer follow from what was drafted — unlike draft-simple and draft-mtp, where each token is re-decoded and the substitution carries forward. A flag --spec-draft-sampling is added, controlling how the draft is sampled. It takes greedy or probabilistic, defaulting to greedy. This matches vLLM's convention, where draft_sample_method takes the same two values and also defaults to greedy. I have run sweeps with -bs enabled and disabled along with the changes in this PR. Based on the logs obtained, this PR does not affect the functionality of backend sampling, which ensures that the target sampling chain already happens on the GPU. With -bs on, I see the same accepted length and 1-2% change in throughput, which is consistent with what is observed on the master branch with -bs enabled.

items.title: Make the drafter probabilistic and the target verify by rejection sampling for simple draft and MTP

items.body:
## Overview

When llama.cpp splits a batch to process multiple requests (concurrency > 1), it can change the token order. With separate KV streams, the hidden states could reach DFlash in that changed order even though it expected the original order. This meant the draft sometimes received another token's hidden states, reducing acceptance.

The fix remembers each token's original position and puts its hidden states back in the correct row before DFlash reads them. This fixes the mismatch while keeping separate KV streams.

## Results

Tested on SPEED-Bench using Qwen3.8-27B with its DFlash2 drafter, both quantized to Q4_K_M with concurrency = 16.

Mean acceptance length (AL) improved from **3.3531 to 3.9211**, a **16.94% increase** overall.

| Coding | 3.4884 | 4.0518 | +16.15% |

items.body:
## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
Improve dynamic activation quantization in hexagon backend

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->
During the bring-up of LFM2.5-DSpark on hexagon, discrepancies were noticed when comparing target-only output to target+draft.  

Root cause of the N=1 tolerance failure was activation quantization sharing one scale per 128 values, even though the internal QK_Q8_0_TILED=128 format has space for a scale every 32 values.

Hexagon Dynamic Quantizer improvements
- Improved Q8_0 accuracy
- Support for 64bit DMA addresses for src1 (aka activation) tensors
- Remove/reroute legacy ddr paths to new vtcm/dma-based kernels

DMA validation included Gemma4 E2B audio/image and Qwen3.5 35B image.

*Context: I am submitting this on behalf of the LLamaSharp maintainer team (cc @martindevans). We needed a way to cleanly expose speculative decoding and MTP to our C# users without bloating the upstream core. This standalone C API has been heavily battle-tested across both C++ and C# environments.*

## Overview

This PR introduces a standalone, dependency-free C API for multi-sequence speculative decoding and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP). It extracts the core speculative execution loop from the internal `common/speculative.cpp` utilities into a public-facing implementation (`src/llama-speculative.cpp`). This enables downstream bindings (such as `llama-cpp-python`, `LLamaSharp`, etc.) to easily integrate draft-simple and Draft-MTP capabilities via native pointers, without needing to recreate complex draft/verify loops or context routing mechanics.

## Additional information

### Key Architectural Changes

* **Public C API (`include/llama.h`):** Introduced `llama_speculative_init`, `llama_speculative_decode`, `llama_speculative_free`, and the `llama_speculative_result` struct.
* **MTP Staging Integration:** Exposed `llama_set_embeddings_nextn` and `llama_get_embeddings_nextn_ith` to the public header. These are strictly required to route hidden states across MTP projection heads for architectures like DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen.
* **Standalone Engine (`src/llama-speculative.cpp`):** Implemented a core multi-sequence engine relying solely on `llama.h` and the C++ standard library, keeping the footprint minimal and avoiding `common` dependencies.
* **Continuous Batching:** Dynamically tracks `batch->n_seq_id` to draft and verify multiple independent sequences concurrently, mapping accepted tokens back to their origin sequence ID.
* **M-RoPE / RNN Safe Rollback:** Engineered an unconditional byte-level `llama_state_seq` backup mechanism prior to verification. If a sequence is rejected, the engine performs a hard memory wipe and transparent re-decodes accepted tokens. This specifically prevents fatal `X < Y` M-RoPE position collision crashes on hybrid recurrent architectures.
* **Verification Alignment:** Ensures the sampled base token is explicitly prepended to the verification batch so the target model evaluates draft tokens with perfect context alignment.

### Validation

* Added `tests/test-speculative.cpp` and integrated it into `CMakeLists.txt` using the `test-download-model` fixture.
* The test uses a self-speculation approach (where target and draft contexts share the same model) to validate decoding loops, cache rollbacks, sequence mapping, and state recovery in CI, requiring zero multi-model external dependencies.
* **Cross-Ecosystem Testing:** *(Note: This PR is paired with a companion PR in `LLamaSharp` [feat: Native Speculative Decoding & MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) - #1431](https://github.com/SciSharp/LLamaSharp/pull/1431). The API and underlying engine have been exhaustively tested across both C++ and C# environments. This includes the native CI test provided here, alongside extensive managed C# unit tests validating multi-sequence multiplexing, KV cache deduplication, and real-world interactive Tokens-Per-Second (TPS) benchmarks.)*

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - I used AI assistants to help brainstorm architectural approaches, assist with the C++ implementation, and structure the PR description. However, all testing, benchmarking, CI validation, and cross-ecosystem integration (C++/C#) were conducted manually, and I take full responsibility for the accuracy and maintenance of this code.

# ANNEX: Model Selection & Evaluation

## 1. Model Compatibility & Selection Rules

* **Dual-Model Speculation:** The target and draft models must share the exact same tokenizer architecture and vocabulary size to prevent immediate cache desynchronization crashes. Crucially, **the larger the target model and the smaller/faster the draft model, the higher the resulting speedup**.

* **Multi-Token Prediction (MTP):** This requires a single model with pre-trained speculative projection layers (`nextn_predict_layers >= 1`). **The more draft heads the model has, the higher the potential speedup**, as it can verify more tokens per native API call without context-switching overhead. The draft budget must match the available heads.

---

## 2. Real-World Benchmark Examples

### Draft-Simple

Pairing **Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-Q8_0.gguf** (Target) with **Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-Q4_0.gguf** (Draft) yielded a **1.26x speedup (+25.7%)**. Even on a fast GPU, the 1B draft model was lightweight enough to outpace the compute overhead of the 8B target.

### MTP Speculation

Running **Qwen3.5-4B-MTP-Q4_K_M.gguf** (1 MTP head) resulted in a **0.47x slowdown (-53.2%)**. Because the 4B base model is computed incredibly fast on high-end hardware, the API overhead and CUDA graph launch latency of evaluating the MTP head completely overshadowed the memory bandwidth savings. To achieve a speedup instead, you must use a much larger model (like 14B or 32B) where **the GPU's memory bandwidth becomes a true bottleneck as it fetches massive weight matrices from VRAM for every single token**. Alternatively, using an MTP model with multiple prediction heads allows you to verify several tokens in a single API roundtrip, making the overhead worthwhile.

### Multi-Token Prediction: Gemma 4 (Split-Weight MTP-4)

Unlike bundled MTP architectures where projection layers reside in the same weight file, Gemma 4 separates its multi-token prediction heads into a standalone assistant checkpoint (`gemma4-assistant`). This benchmark demonstrates **MTP-4 self-speculation** where 4 future tokens are drafted simultaneously via auxiliary projection layers using the target model's hidden states (`CtxOther`), verified in a single batched verification pass.

#### **Test Configuration**
* **Hardware:** NVIDIA GeF

```sh
hf download LiquidAI/LFM2.5-VL-3B-GGUF LFM2.5-VL-3B-F16.gguf mmproj-LFM2.5-VL-3B-F16.gguf --local-dir models
```

Support DSpark draft models for Gemma4
## How to run

Complete example from scratch (gemma-4-12B-it).

**1. Get the models** — target + its DSpark draft:
```bash
hf download google/gemma-4-12B-it --local-dir Gemma4-12B-it
hf download deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7 --local-dir dspark_gemma4_12b_block7
```

**2. Convert to GGUF** — the draft ships no tokenizer and reuses the target's, so pass `--target-model-dir`:
```bash
python convert_hf_to_gguf.py Gemma4-12B-it --outtype bf16 --outfile Gemma4-12B-it.gguf
python convert_hf_to_gguf.py dspark_gemma4_12b_block7 --outtype bf16 --target-model-dir Gemma4-12B-it \
  --outfile Gemma4-12B-DSpark.gguf
```
You may quantize the *target*; keep the draft bf16 — it's tiny, and acceptance is unaffected by target quant.

**3. Build** with CUDA:
```bash
cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON && cmake --build build --config Release -j
```

**4. Run** — the only DSpark-specific flags are `-md <draft>` and `--spec-type draft-dspark`
(`--spec-draft-n-max` = draft tokens per step; the released checkpoints use block size 7):
```bash
./build/bin/llama-server -m Gemma4-12B-it.gguf -md Gemma4-12B-DSpark.gguf --spec-type draft-dspark \
  --spec-draft-n-max 7 --temp 0 --top-k 1 -np 1 -c 4096 -ngl 99 -ngld 99 -fa on --jinja
```

**5. Send a request** (the server logs `draft acceptance = ...` per request):
```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
```

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 10276 (6ea215d17)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

The defect is still present in current `master` (`cd0fa60`, b10286) — see line references below.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

6x RTX 5090 (sm120), x86_64

### Models

`DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (unsloth `UD-Q3_K_XL`), with the DSpark drafter (`--spec-type draft-dspark`).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama_kv_cache_dsv4::state_read()` clears the **entire** CSA/HCA/LID compressed caches — i.e. all sequences — before reading back the state of a **single** sequence:

```cpp
// src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1594-1604 (master cd0fa60)
    kv_raw->state_read(io, seq_id, flags);          // <-- correctly scoped to seq_id

    if (!partial_only) {
        kv_csa->clear(true);                        // <-- cache-wide: ALL sequences
        kv_hca->clear(true);
        kv_lid->clear(true);

        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_csa.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_hca.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_lid.get(), seq_id, flags);
    }
```

`llama_kv_cache::clear(bool)` is cache-wide, while the restore of the raw cache immediately above it is scoped to `seq_id`. The class already provides a sequence-scoped helper for exactly this:

```cpp
// src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1671
void llama_kv_cache_dsv4::clear_compressed(llama_seq_id seq_id, bool data);
```

That helper was introduced by #25521 ("DeepseekV4: clear cache only for seq rather than full", `13f2b28b0`) specifically so that per-sequence operations stop wiping the whole compressed cache, and `seq_rm()` (line 1447) and `seq_keep()` (line 1481) both use it correctly. `state_read()` is the one path that still does a full clear.

**Consequence.** With `--parallel N` (N > 1, which is also the server's auto default of 4), restoring the state of one sequence destroys the compressed KV of every *other* sequence while leaving their raw KV intact. Those sequences are left silently desynced — no error and no crash, they simply continue decoding against zeroed compressed caches. The user-visible symptom is one slot abruptly losing its context while other slots are being restored.

Affected paths are any single-sequence `state_read`: `POST /slots/{id}?action=restore`, `--prompt-cache`/checkpoint reload, and `llama_state_seq_set_data()` in the public API.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `llama-server` with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `--parallel 2` (or the auto default of 4) and `--slot-save-path <dir>`.
2. Build up a conversation on slot 0 and a second, different conversation on slot 1.
3. `POST /slots/0?action=save`, then `POST /slots/0?action=restore`.
4. Continue the conversation on **slot 1** — its continuation no longer reflects its own history.

**Suggested fix** — use the existing seq-scoped helper, which already treats `seq_id < 0` as "all":

```cpp
    if (!partial_only) {
        clear_compressed(seq_id, true);

        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_csa.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_hca.get(), seq_id, flags);
        dsv4_state_read_k_cache(io, kv_lid.get(), seq_id, flags);
    }
```

**Disclosure about how this was found.** This is from code inspection while investigating unrelated context-corruption on our rig, not from a captured reproduction — we run `--cache-ram 0` and avoid the restore path, so I do not have a log of the failure itself. The control flow above is unambiguous, but I have not bisected a live repro, hence no log section below. Happy to run the reproduction above and report back if that would help.

**Note on similar-looking reports.** #25171 ("forgets everything") and #25259 ("forgot context when hit cache or use checkpoint in long context") describe the same user-visible symptom, but both were opened (2026-06-30 and 2026-07-03) *before* the commit below landed, so this is not their original cause. Mentioning them only because the symptom class is identical and multi-slot users hitting it today may now be running into this instead.

### First Bad Commit

`91d2fc387` — "llama_dsv4: write only used rows in state" (#25325, 2026-07-20). That commit added the three cache-wide clears inside `state_read`; the patch hunk is `@@ -1366,6 +1419,10 @@ void llama_kv_cache_dsv4::state_read`. Before it, `state_read()` did not clear the compressed caches at all.

### Relevant log output

```
Not applicable — reported from code inspection, see disclosure above.
```

items.body:
### Summary

With `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (GGUF) served by `llama-server` with `--jinja` and tools armed, generation **terminated mid-tag with `finish_reason: "stop"`** on three consecutive agent turns — each time exactly at the point where the reasoning stream contained literal DSML closing fragments (`</｜DSML｜parameter>`, `</｜DSML｜invoke>`). The final streamed token was `tool_c` — an *incomplete* `</｜DSML｜tool_calls>` closing tag. The client-visible result is an agent that appears to stop mid-tool-call, and (because the truncated message is persisted into history) a self-perpetuating loop: each follow-up turn imitates the truncated pattern and gets cut at the same place.

### Environment

- `llama-server` build 10573, commit `d775b8967` (master, 2026-08-22), AppleClang 21, Darwin arm64
- Backends: Metal (M5 Max) + one RPC worker (DGX Spark GB10), `--split-mode layer`
- Model: `unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF` UD-Q8_K_XL (5 shards) + `dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf` draft
- Flags: `--spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max 3 -c 393216 --flash-attn on --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 --jinja --temp 0.6 --top-p 0.95`
- Effective slot state observed: `chat_format: "peg-native"`, `reasoning_format: "deepseek"`, `generation_prompt: "<｜Assistant｜><think>"`

### Observed (3 consecutive turns, harness session transcript)

| Turn | input tokens | output tokens | finish | stream ends at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~165,000 | ~120 (est.) | stop | reasoning text `...a1b2c3d` + `</｜DSML｜parameter>` |
| 2 | 168,991 | 126 | stop | `...a1b2c3` + `</｜DSML｜parameter>\n</｜DSML｜invoke>\n</｜DSML｜tool_c` |
| 3 | 169,132 | 119 | stop | same fragment, same cut point |

Final reasoning deltas for turn 3 (verbatim, from the client event log):

```
... 'c', '3', '</｜DSML｜', 'parameter', '>', '\n', '</｜DSML｜', 'inv', 'oke', '>', '\n', '</｜DSML｜', 'tool', '_c'
```

The model was composing a file-edit tool call whose parameter value contained backtick-quoted hex strings (`` `a1b2c3d4e5f6` ``). The reasoning text shows the model interleaving protocol markup into the thinking channel; the stream then terminates *mid-tag*. No EOS content token is visible in the client stream — the stop appears to come from the serving side's handling of the DSML structure, not from a deliberate EOS the model wrote.

### Expected

Reasoning/thinking content should be treated as opaque text: a stray or partial DSML closing tag inside reasoning must not end generation. If the model truly opens a tool call, the parser should wait for a well-formed close; a malformed close should yield a parse error or plain text — never a silent mid-tag `stop`.

### Minimal repro attempt (negative result at short context)

A direct request asking the model to quote `</｜DSML｜parameter>` inside its reasoning, with a dummy tool armed, completed normally at short context (`finish: stop`, 271 completion tokens, tag quoted intact). So the failure is **not** triggered by the tag alone — the incidents happened at **~165–169K context depth** in an agentic multi-tool flow (the harness session had ~100 prior tool calls). Possibly depth-dependent (parser state / attention degradation at depth making the model emit protocol markup mid-reasoning more likely, and/or the parser's early-stop engaging once it does).

### Why it matters

The truncated message is persisted by clients as a normal completed turn (`finish: stop`), and the model then imitates its own truncated pattern on the next turn — the failure is self-reinforcing within a session. Three identical stops in a row required abandoning the session.

### Related

- vllm-project/vllm#48931 — DSML parser fragility when the model omits the `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` START wrapper (V4, long context)
- ggml-org/llama.cpp#25618 — draft-dspark/draft-mtp greedy divergence on quantized targets
- ggml-org/llama.cpp#26554 — DSpark + V4-Flash long-generation abort

Happy to provide the full client event log (JSONL), server logs, or test patches.

items.body:
## Overview

Adds DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM`) under its own `deepseek41` architecture: conversion, the runtime graph, and the chat template. An earlier revision of this PR was conversion only, so a converted file had nowhere to load. It is now the full path.

16 commits, 23 files, +2090 / -77.

### Conversion

Subclasses the existing V4 model. Most of the V4 path carries over unchanged. What needed handling:

- Text parameters are nested under `text_config`, so they are promoted in `index_tensors`. Overriding `load_hparams` does not work, because `ModelBase.__init__` calls it explicitly rather than through the instance.
- `num_hash_layers` is absent in V4.1 while the V4 path reads it unconditionally.
- The FP8 scale block size is `[32, 32]` rather than `[128, 128]`. V4 hardcodes 128, and reusing that value rescales every dequantized weight without raising, so the block size is read from `quantization_config`.
- Indexer `k_norm` and `wk` map onto the existing `INDEXER_K_NORM` and `INDEXER_ATTN_K`. `attn.compressor.ape` and `attn.indexer.compressor.*` are absent in V4.1 and go unused.
- Four new tensors for the engram conditional memory (`ENGRAM_EMBD`, `ENGRAM_Q`, `ENGRAM_K`, `ENGRAM_WKV`).

The two engram tables need a separate write path. Each is `384,006,168 x 256`, and the inherited FP8 dequant computes `weight.float() * scale` over the whole tensor, which is about 393 GB as float32 for one table. They are read in row blocks from the safetensors shard, quantized per block, and accumulated into a disk backed memmap. Their scale layout also differs: `[rows, 8]`, one scale per 32 columns of a single row, rather than the `[rows/32, cols/32]` tiling the linear weights use.

### Runtime

`src/models/deepseek41.cpp` is the V4.1 graph. Three things are not V4, and two of them fail silently rather than raising:

- **Sparse attention.** V4 keys everything off `dsv4_compress_ratios[il]` being 4 or 128. In the released V4.1 checkpoint those ratios are 0, 1 and 2, so V4's builder matches neither branch and drops the long range half of attention while still producing fluent text. V4.1 puts compressors on a few source layers rather than every layer, applies a pooling gate only where the ratio is above 1, and takes index keys from the shared KV latent through `indexer.wk` and `k_norm` rather than a second compressor. Nothing here is hardcoded: the loader derives each layer's role from which tensors the file actually carries, since only a compressor owner has the compressor weights, only an index key owner carries `indexer_attn_k`, and only an index source carries `indexer_attn_q_b`.
- **No q head norm.** V4 applies an extra unweighted `rms_norm` to `q` after `wq_b`. V4.1 does not. Also silent: the output stays fluent and is wrong.
- **Engram.** Two tables, on layers 1 and 14, with different row counts (384,006,168 and 384,016,682) because each layer seeds its own prime sized buckets. The lookup is a prime modulo hash reading `(max_ngram_size - 1) * n_heads = 24` rows per token per engram layer, so 48 per token, every token. The tables want to be host resident rather than treated as ordinary weights.

The compressed stream helpers in `llama_kv_cache_dsv4` are shared with V4 rather than duplicated, which is most of the diff to `src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp` and `src/models/deepseek4.cpp`.

This path also exposed an upstream bug, fixed here: `llama_kv_cache::build_input_k_rot` loops forever when `n_embd_head_k_all` is 0, which is what a cache whose layer filter selected nothing leaves it at. It presents as a hang at 100% of one core in `graph_reserve` with no error. V4 never hits it because its compressed caches always have layers.

## The architecture name

An earlier revision of this PR rode on `MODEL_ARCH.DEEPSEEK4` and added the engram tensors to V4's own list. That was wrong twice over, and it now declares `deepseek41` instead. `DEEPSEEK4` is left untouched.

**Convention.** llama.cpp does not mirror the HF `model_type`, it drops the `_v`: `deepseek_v2` became `deepseek2`, `deepseek_v3.2` became `deepseek32`, `qwen2_moe` became `qwen2moe`. Only 11 of the 153 arch strings in `constants.py` contain an underscore at all, so vLLM's `deepseek_v41` would be the odd one out here.

**Failure mode.** V4.1 ships the per-layer `hc_attn_{fn,base,scale}` and `hc_ffn_{fn,base,scale}`, 40 of each, but none of `output_hc_fn`, `output_hc_base` or `output_hc_scale`. Routing a V4.1 file to the V4 loader therefore produces a confusing partial match rather than a clean refusal. The declared lists show the same thing: `DEEPSEEK4` carries 48 tensor families and `deepseek41` carries 39, and the 15 it does not use include all three `HC_HEAD_*` and all six `NEXTN_*`.

`deepseek41`'s tensor list is the 39 families the converter actually writes, derived by reverse mapping them through `TENSOR_NAMES` rather than by trimming V4's list. Against `DEEPSEEK4` it drops `HC_HEAD_{FN,BASE,SCALE}`, `FFN_GATE_TID2EID`, `ATTN_COMPRESSOR_APE`, the four `INDEXER_COMPRESSOR_*` and all six `NEXTN_*`, and adds six: the four `ENGRAM_*` plus `INDEXER_ATTN_K` and `INDEXER_K_NORM`.

## Additional information

**Conversion.** Converted `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` end to end on one machine with 121 GiB of RAM: 1046 tensors, 507.9 GB at `--outtype q8_0` with MXFP4 experts, peak host memory under 8 GB above baseline. Output checked with `GGUFReader`, all 8 engram tensors present. Quantized further to Q2_K and Q3_K_M to confirm the file is well formed downstream.

Measured rung sizes, for anyone estimating: Q8_0 staging 473.1 GiB (1046 tensors), Q2_K 246.3 GiB, Q3_K_M 323.4 GiB. Those ratios read high against the staging file because it is not uniformly Q8_0: routed experts land as MXFP4, so parts of the ladder move up rather than down. At Q3_K_M the expert down projection goes MXFP4 to q5_K and grows from 2295 to 2970 MiB.

`Q2_K_S` and `IQ2_M` both need an imatrix. Q1_0 is unusable on this model and it is the file rather than

### Name and Version

./llama-server --version
version: 10318 (4cf5cab65)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

Linux m920s 6.8.0-136-generic #136-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed Jul  1 21:53:05 UTC 2026 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

- I7-8700T 6C/12T + 128GB DDR4
-  RTX 2000E Ada 16GB

### Models

[DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ2_M](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF/tree/main/UD-IQ2_M)
[dev7a/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/dev7a/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-GGUF/resolve/main/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-Q2_K-Q8_0-dflash.gguf)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Command line used

```bash
GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1 ./llama-server \
  --model ~/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/UD-IQ2_M/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ2_M-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  --model-draft ~/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-DSpark-Drafter-Q2_K-Q8_0-dflash.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max 5 \
  --ctx-size $((64*1024)) \
  --no-context-shift \
  --gpu-layers 999 \
  --n-cpu-moe 43 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 \
  --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --fit off \
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --min-k 20 \
  --threads 6 --threads-batch 6 \
  --batch-size 4096 --ubatch-size 2048 \
  --cache-ram 0 \
  --jinja \
  --parallel 1 \
  --log-verbosity 4 \
  --no-mmap \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8080
```

## Logs

Drafter metadata **does** declare the mask token:

```console
- kv  42:               tokenizer.ggml.model str              = no_vocab
- kv  43:               tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id u32      = 128799
...
print_info: vocab type  = no vocab
```

But the speculative implementation resolves it to -1 and fails on every draft decode:

```console
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: adding speculative implementation 'draft-dspark'
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - n_max=5, n_min=0, p_min=0.00
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - block_size=5, mask_token_id=-1, n_extract=3
...
E init: invalid token[1] = -1
E decode: failed to initialize batch
E llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -1
W draft: llama_decode returned -1
(repeats 8x per step, then stalls)
```
## Root cause

**`src/llama-vocab.cpp`** — the `no_vocab` branch sets `special_mask_id = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL` and returns before any metadata is read (~line 1933):

```cpp
if (tokenizer_model == "no_vocab" || tokenizer_model == "none") {
    type = LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_NONE;
    special_bos_id  = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL;
    ...
    special_mask_id = LLAMA_TOKEN_NULL;   // hardcoded; metadata never consulted
    ...
    return;                               // skips the metadata read below
}
```

**`common/speculative.cpp`** (~line 970) trusts the vocab API with no fallback:

```cpp
mask_token_id = llama_vocab_mask(llama_model_get_vocab(model_dft));   // returns -1
```

That `-1` is then injected into the draft batch (~line 1153):

```cpp
common_batch_add(batch, i == 0 ? dp.id_last : mask_token_id, n + i, { seq_id }, true);
```

→ `invalid token[1] = -1` → `llama_decode` returns -1.

The metadata key is valid and correctly mapped in `src/llama-arch.cpp:345`:

```cpp
{ LLM_KV_TOKENIZER_MASK_ID, "tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id" },
```

It's simply unreachable on the `no_vocab` path.

## Suggested fix

`common/speculative.cpp` already reads another drafter field (`dflash.block_size`) directly from metadata via `llama_model_meta_val_str` for exactly this reason (~line 962). Applying the same pattern to the mask token is the smallest, most contained fix:

```diff
         mask_token_id = llama_vocab_mask(llama_model_get_vocab(model_dft));
+
+        // no_vocab drafters (DSpark/DFlash) nullify the mask token in the vocab, so
+        // fall back to the GGUF metadata key when the vocab API returns nothing.
+        // Mirrors the dflash.block_size metadata read above.
+        if (mask_token_id < 0) {
+            char buf[32] = {};
+            if (llama_model_meta_val_str(model_dft, "tokenizer.ggml.mask_token_id", buf, sizeof(buf)) >= 0) {
+                mask_token_id = (llama_token) std::atoi(buf);
+            }
+        }
```

With this change, the log line flips from `mask_token_id=-1` to `mask_token_id=128799` and the `invalid token` / decode failures stop. No new includes needed — `llama_model_meta_val_str` and `std::atoi` are already used a few lines above for `dflash.block_size`.

(An alternative, broader fix would be to read `LLM_KV_TOKENIZER_MASK_ID` inside the `no_vocab` branch of `src/llama-vocab.cpp` so `llama_vocab_mask()` returns the right value for any caller — but the change above is sufficient for the speculative path and carries no risk to other vocab consumers.)


### First Bad Commit

_No response_

```console
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - block_size=5, mask_token_id=-1, n_extract=3
...
```

items.body:
## Overview

Assertion is failed on llama-server startup if using dflash2 draft model and `--split-mode tensor` flag:

```
ggml\src\ggml-backend-meta.cpp:543: GGML_ASSERT(src_ss[0].axis != GGML_BACKEND_SPLIT_AXIS_0) failed
```

The changes in this PR address two issues:
- Crash in GGML_ASSERT (root cause)
- Reducing the VRAM footprint of the DFlash2 model for **`--split-mode tensor`**

## Additional information

Issue for this case: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/27819

### Root cause

The DFlash2 candidate selector runs `ggml_top_k()` on the lm_head output (`t_logits`) inside the graph. Under tensor parallelism `output.weight` is split along the vocab axis, so `t_logits` is split along axis 0, which `GGML_OP_TOP_K` (a per-row op) cannot handle in the meta backend.

**Fix:** When a DFlash2 draft is used with tensor parallelism, the lm_head must be replicated in full on every device (`GGML_BACKEND_SPLIT_AXIS_MIRRORED`) so the whole vocabulary is available in-graph. 

### Reducing the VRAM footprint

DFlash2's in-graph selector (`ggml_top_k` over the lm_head output) cannot run on a vocab-split lm_head under `--split-mode tensor`. Rather than replicating the lm_head on every device (MIRRORED, ~+500 MiB/device), the **selector now runs on the CPU from the gathered logits** + decoder hidden states, so the lm_head stays split.

VRAM savings for `https://huggingface.co/z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-GGUF/blob/main/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q4_K_M.gguf`:
- lm_head stays vocab-split instead of replicated: ~-500 MiB/device.

items.body:
For models that share tensors with another model through ctx_other (e.g. Gemma4Assistant, Eagle3, DFlash, DSpark), add the other model's device backends to the context scheduler so that pre-allocated shared tensors (tok_embd, output) can be scheduled. Fixes an abort when the speculative draft model uses a device list that does not cover the GPU holding the target model's output projection.

Assisted-by: opencode

## Overview

## Bug (observed behavior)
- Abort during llama_context construction: "pre-allocated tensor (output.weight) in a buffer (CUDA10) that cannot run the operation (NONE)"
- Location: ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp (line ~898/930 depending on version), called from llama_context::sched_reserve -> graph_reserve -> resolve_fused_ops
- Trigger: speculative decoding with ctx_other (draft-dspark / draft-dflash / draft-mtp), draft model on its own device via --device-draft/--spec-draft-device, target model on other GPU(s)
- Root cause : the draft context scheduler only had backends for the draft's own devices; shared pre-allocated tensors (tok_embd/output.weight, taken from the target model via ctx_other in src/models/dflash.cpp) live in buffers on the target's devices; scheduler found no backend for those buffers and aborted

## Reproduction (your setup)
- llama-server in router mode, model preset:
  - device = CUDA3,CUDA4,CUDA5,CUDA7,CUDA8,CUDA9,CUDA10 (--split-mode layer)
  - spec-type = draft-dspark, spec-draft-n-max = 8
  - spec-draft-device = CUDA0
  - model-draft = dspark/dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf
- Before fix: GGML_ABORT, spec model failed to load
- After fix: draft context logs "adding backend for device CUDA3..CUDA10: shared tensors with the other model (e.g. tok_embd, output)", speculative implementation 'draft-dspark' initializes (n_max=8, block_size=5), server healthy
- Verified with CI-built image version 10282 (34ec9c9bb) on 15-GPU host (RTX 3080/4080/4090/3090), CUDA 12, 16x 3090-class workload


## Additional information

## Related issues
- #26475 - "using -devd CUDA0 on draft-dspark causes model to crash": same abort message (output.weight, CUDA8), same stack, draft-dspark + tensor split. Directly matches. (open)
- #24492 - Gemma 4 31B MTP, Vulkan: "pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l58) ... cannot run the operation (NONE)" - same abort class, ctx_other/KV sharing; mechanism may differ (Vulkan backend support), unknown whether fixed
- #24366 - Gemma MTP, tensor split, buffer "Meta()": same abort class; unknown whether fixed
- #26339 - "Dspark model fails to load with -sm tensor on MI50": possible same class; unknown

items.body:
## Environment

- Hardware: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121a, 128 GB unified memory, aarch64)
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.142
- Engine: unslothai/llama.cpp portable builds of this project (`llama-server`), OpenAI-compatible API
- Build A (stable): `b10830-mix-d5c17a0`
- Build B (issue): `b10909-mix-bea84f7`
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4_exp), IQ2_XXS/Q2_K imatrix GGUF (86.7 GB, checkpoint 0731), fully resident, `--ctx 32000`, DSpark speculative decoding enabled

## Summary

On build B, the `llama-server` process's host-side footprint (VmRSS + VmSwap) grows continuously during normal chat usage — roughly **+12 GiB per hour of ordinary multi-turn conversation**. On build A, host-side memory is flat at ~2 GiB regardless of usage. The growth makes build B unusable on 128 GB unified-memory systems once the GPU pool is heavily committed: the kernel spilled 15 GiB to swap and the host entered swap-thrash under concurrent load, twice, requiring a reboot.

## Measurements (process-level, `/proc/<pid>/status`)

| build | VmRSS | VmSwap | RSS + Swap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Build A (b10830-mix-d5c17a0) | 2.1 GiB | 0 | **2.1 GiB — flat across days of use** |
| Build B (b10909-mix-bea84f7), fresh load | 19.2 GiB | 9.6 GiB | 28.8 GiB |
| Build B, after ~1 h of chatting | 26.1 GiB | 14.7 GiB | **40.8 GiB** |

System-level effect on the 128 GB box: GPU allocations (~70 GiB) + host 26–40 GiB + OS ≈ the entire pool; the kernel filled the 16 GB swap file and the host entered swap-thrash. A second reproduction attempt after a clean reboot behaved identically.

## Hypothesis

The Flash-Next n-gram module's gather tables are read lazily (see unslothai #137, "batched readahead for lazily read gather tables"). We suspect build B stages the touched table regions into **anonymous host memory** rather than keeping them file-backed. Anonymous pages are not reclaimable without swap, so under unified-memory pressure they spill to swap and the host thrashes instead of cleanly evicting. A file-backed mmap-gather design (as used by community vLLM recipes for the same model, which mmap the PLE table file-backed and gather directly) does not exhibit this failure mode on the same class of hardware.

We have not yet tested a vanilla upstream build to confirm the behavior there; posting in case this is upstream-relevant and others on 128 GB unified-memory systems can reproduce.

## Workaround

Rolling back to build A restores a flat ~2 GiB host profile. All other settings unchanged.

Happy to provide more data (repeated `/proc` snapshots over a session, nvitop exports, traces) if useful.

## Overview This PR prevents repeated CUDA graph capture during MTP speculative decoding. MTP alternates between- Output-producing draft batches, and No-output prefill and catch-up batches. Previously both shapes reused one `llm_graph_result`, so they shared the same CUDA graph cache key and repeatedly replaced each other’s captured graph. items.body:
## Problem

The scheduler's hash set is sized once at init (to `graph_size`) and asserts when a graph exceeds it:

```cpp
GGML_ASSERT((int)sched->hash_set.size >= graph->n_nodes + graph->n_leafs);
```

Speculative-decoding graphs (`draft-mtp` / `draft-dspark` / `draft-eagle3`) grow with `--spec-draft-n-max`, so `n_max=9` pushes `n_nodes + n_leafs` one past the hash capacity and trips the assert. This is the crash behind #28614 — a maintainer repro there showed the exact off-by-one:

```
n_max=8: hash=2053  nodes=1706 leafs=294 total=2000  → fits
n_max=9: hash=2053  nodes=1760 leafs=294 total=2054  → overflow by 1 → assert
```

The code even carries the latent intent as a `FIXME` at init ("needs to be size*2 to account for leafs").

## Fix

Grow the hash set (and its two per-tensor arrays) before splitting when the graph is too large, with the same 25% margin the allocator (`ggml_gallocr_reserve_n_impl`) uses, instead of asserting. Replaces the three asserts in `reserve_size`, `reserve`, and `alloc_graph` with a single `ensure_graph_capacity` helper.

## Notes

- Cherry-picks cleanly onto `master`; builds (llama-server).
- I hit this on an AMD/Vulkan fork whose draft-dspark path has an additional earlier crash (`llama-graph.cpp` "layer input tensor is null"), so I could not exercise the full n_max=9 decode end-to-end in my environment — the change is the direct fix for the diagnosed assert, but please treat the repro in #28614 as the acceptance test.

Fixes #28614

### Name and Version

$ llama-cli --version
version: 9924 (90e0f5cfc)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64


### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

GPU: 5x NVIDIA CUDA (2x RTX 3090, RTX 5060 Ti, 2x RTX 4060 Ti), 96 GiB total VRAM
CPU: Intel Core i5-13600K (14 cores / 20 threads)
RAM: 128 GB DDR4-3200
OS: Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04)

### Models

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (DSV4-Flash), GGUF, MXFP4 quant, 5 shards.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

During an agentic coding session, after several turns, I get a crash with a false "Context size has been exceeded" at ~1250 tokens against a 16k context. It's SWA find_slot exhaustion of the 768-cell window, not a real context limit, with 0 CUDA errors (no OOM/abort).

Also, before the crash, throughout the session every divergent turn stalls. Every divergent turn re-prefills thousands of tokens from a checkpoint boundary instead of just the delta, so the agent sits on "Working" with nothing streaming. The same churn eventually crashes.

Both fall out of the same no-partial-rollback limitation; one proper seq_rm of the diverged suffix fixes both.

The window full so no slot even at ~1250 tokens, not a real ctx limit, 0 CUDA errors proves it's not a GPU fault.

The root cause:

DSV4-Flash raw attention is a 128-token sliding window on a 768-cell SWA KV cache, the only cache find_slot runs on. find_slot reuses an occupied cell only if SWA-masked. Also the same sequence causal reuse path is commented out (src/llama-kv-cache.cpp ~1043-1047) on the invariant "purge futures beforehand."

Normal models satisfy that with seq_rm(seq_id, n_past, -1) before re-decoding a divergent suffix. DSV4 can't do a partial seq_rm (src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp ~1153). The compressor ring state can't roll back mid-block. So the server rewinds via a checkpoint-restore that repopulates the SWA window without purging futures.

The crash: re decode refills positions inside the full 768-cell window and find_slot can neither reuse the occupied same-seq cells nor reclaim the live top ~128 window cells resulting in a false "context exceeded."

The stall: The same no partial rollback. Every divergent turn re prefills from a checkpoint boundary, no delta path.

The defect is in shared KV / server code not a CUDA kernel. Having no CUDA errors backs this so it's expected across backends.

A monotonic growing prompt never jams and the band probe reached 119,788 tokens clean. The crash needs reuse that re-fills occupied cells, not raw depth.

Reproduce with:

churn.py:
```python
import urllib.request, urllib.error, json, random, time
URL="http://127.0.0.1:10099/v1/completions"
random.seed(11)
def sent(i): return f"Paragraph {i}: quick brown fox {i} leaps over lazy dog {i}, counting {i} apples, {i} pears, {i} plums in crate {i} now. "
def comp(prompt,n=8):
    data=json.dumps({"prompt":prompt,"max_tokens":n,"cache_prompt":True,"temperature":0.6}).encode()
    req=urllib.request.Request(URL,data=data,headers={"Content-Type":"application/json"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req,timeout=600) as r: return r.status, r.read().decode()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: return e.code, e.read().decode()
    except Exception as e: return -1, str(e)
MAXLINES=340; lines=[]; peak=0; t0=time.time()
for it in range(1200):
    if len(lines)>=MAXLINES:
        lines=lines[:random.randint(30, 90)]          # DEEP rewind from high depth -> strands high-pos cells
    elif lines and random.random()<0.6:
        lines[-1]=("d",it)                             # shallow divergence -> checkpoint rewind
    lines.append(("a",it))
    prompt="".join(sent(hash(x)%99999) for x in lines)
    st,body=comp(prompt)
    if st==-1: print(f"[NETERR] it={it} {body[:150]}",flush=True); continue
    if st>=500 or "exceed" in body.lower():
        print(f"[JAM] it={it} elapsed={time.time()-t0:.0f}s lines={len(lines)} peak_ptok={peak} status={st} body={body[:200]}",flush=True); break
    try:
        u=json.loads(body).get("usage",{}); pt=u.get("prompt_tokens",0); peak=max(peak,pt)
        if it%10==0: print(f"it={it} t={time.time()-t0:.0f}s lines={len(lines)} ptok={pt} peak={peak}",flush=True)
    except Exception as e: print(f"[PARSE] it={it} {body[:100]}",flush=True)
else: print(f"[NOJAM] done 1200 iters peak_ptok={peak}",flush=True)
print("FIN",flush=True)
```

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

Introduces a deterministic plugin mechanism via a simple SPI that keeps changes to the core at a minimal. 
This is a generic mechanism however what makes it different from the current per token validation is that it plugs into the existing MTP pipeline, by default the plugin will determine if a token is filtered or not but any valid token will be verified by the target and the bonus token is always generated unless a valid termination completes such as a complete parse if using xgrammar. With the --det-draft-accept-all , only the plugin's logic is used to verify, the target model's verification is bypassed even the correction/bonus token is arbitrated and on low end commodity hardware can result in faster TPS along with the guaranteed verification. 

A working PoC that uses Xgrammar for verifying Java,Python,JavaScript and C is under `deterministic-draft-model-poc` 

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

Feature - Deterministic Draft Filter with pluggable SDK
- Add deterministic draft filter as a new speculative draft type
- Pluggable SDK via dlopen/dlsym with a single C API contract
- XGrammar based POC demonstrating plugin implementation. Bundled grammars for C, Java, Python, JavaScript Grammar format is XGrammar EBNF.
- Incremental draft validation: one persistent matcher per slot, per-token advance, no re-parse of concatenated text.
- --det-draft-n-max: -1=all, 0=disabled, >0 caps filter output and is copied to --spec-draft-n-max (auto-derive only when > 0).
- --det-draft-accept-all: skip target verification, filter is verifier
- Auto-derive --spec-draft-n-max from --det-draft-n-max (only when > 0)
- Benchmark tool with --compare, --n-runs, --det-draft-accept-all, --det-draft-language support.

The goal here is to provide a control mechanism for domain specific cases where speculation is not acceptable and the problem is well known.
This is a novel enhancement based on a time tested well known grammar based solution, instead of this being likely correct it is either correct or not. 

In addition since a grammar based intercept is cheaper and simpler than the heavy sampling of the target model it is also faster as benchmarks reveal. This is more evident in CPU only edge devices like the N100.
With the --det-draft-accept-all enabled the plugin is fully responsible for all verification, the target model is removed from the decision making.

In the default case, invalid tokens are pruned while the bonus token is verified by the target model. In the case where fewer tokens are accepted by the target model than what was verified by the plugin, the `deterministic_draft_rollback` rewinds the matcher to match what was emitted by the target model. The per-step final token is grammar-constrained before emission (post-fix; zero desync events observed since).
In short the real benefit is with the --det-draft-accept-all.
In this mode, the grammar is the sole verifier, the target model does no rejection sampling. Output distribution follows the grammar-constrained draft, not the target model an opt-in tradeoff.

Original RFC Link: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/25219

** sample results **
Grammar-verified speculative decoding with a pluggable SDK. Every emitted token passes the grammar in both modes. Zero `commit_token reject` lines across all runs.

### RTX 3060 (CUDA) - GPU

| Mode | Language | Model | n-max | MTP only | MTP + Filter | Speedup |
|------|----------|-------|-------|----------|--------------|---------|
| Accept-all | C | 2B | 16 | 1.10 t/s | 22.54 t/s | 20.5x |
| Accept-all | Java | 2B | 16 | 1.11 t/s | 15.62 t/s | 14.1x |
| Accept-all | JavaScript | 2B | 16 | 0.79 t/s | 22.90 t/s | 29.1x |
| Accept-all | Python | 2B | 16 | 2.11 t/s | 17.55 t/s | 8.3x |
| Default | C | 2B | 16 | 1.06 t/s | 2.01 t/s | 1.9x |
| Default | Java | 2B | 16 | 1.11 t/s | 1.23 t/s | 1.1x |
| Default | JavaScript | 2B | 16 | 0.98 t/s | 2.04 t/s | 2.1x |
| Default | Python | 2B | 16 | 2.08 t/s | 5.87 t/s | 2.8x |

### N100 (CPU-only oneAPI, 4C/4T Alder Lake-N)

| Mode | Language | Model | n-max | MTP only | MTP + Filter | Speedup |
|------|----------|-------|-------|----------|--------------|---------|
| Accept-all | C | 4B mxfp4 | 64 | 0.35 t/s | 5.97 t/s | 17.0x |
| Default | C | 4B mxfp4 | 16 | 2.02 t/s | 2.68 t/s | 1.3x |
| Default | C | 2B Q6_K | 16 | 4.38 t/s | 5.54 t/s | 1.3x |

N100 results report C only. The multi-language test was run before the n-max tuning with n-max 100 on a 4-core CPU, default-mode Java and JavaScript runs exceeded
the 1-hour timeout and Python managed 0.88 t/s, because low acceptance means nearly all
of the oversized draft is wasted compute (see the Tuning Cautionary Note in
benchmark-overview.md). That failure is what the n-max 16/64 guidance comes from.

### Key Observations

- **Accept-all** skips target model verification; grammar is sole verifier. Speedups measure a different algorithm than default mode.
- **Default mode** target-verifies all filter-accepted tokens. Speedup is real but modest.
- **n-max matters**: on weak CPUs, oversized n-max (100) wastes draft compute (0.21x). Properly tuned (16-64) gives 1.3-17x.
- **Low baseline MTP acceptance** (3.8%-17.6% on N100 fine-tunes): speculative decoding alone is nearly worthless; the filter makes it viable.
- **Output validity**: 0/1 in all N100 runs (models write broken C). Filter guarantees grammar-valid tokens, not gcc-clean programs -- CFGs cannot check static semantics.

All numbers: single-run, n_runs=1, indicative not statistical. See benchmark-overview.md for full methodology.
