items.body:
The causal flag only changes the contents of the KQ mask inputs, not the graph topology, and llama_context::encode() already flips it without a reserve. llm_graph_params::allow_reuse() compares causal_attn, so the next decode still rebuilds the graph.

mtmd toggles the flag twice per image chunk. Each toggle forced a full sched_reserve (new scheduler + worst-case graph + compute buffers), which costs hundreds of milliseconds at high n_ctx. On video inputs that was two reserves per frame and made video processing crawl.

## Overview

Remove `sched_need_reserve = true` from `llama_context::set_causal_attn()` while preserving its early return and assignment.

Changing `cparams.causal_attn` affects only the values written to the KQ mask by `set_input_kq_mask`; it does not change graph topology or tensor sizes. The existing graph-reuse check includes `causal_attn`, so changing the flag still causes the next decode to rebuild the graph inside the already-reserved buffers.

This also makes `set_causal_attn()` consistent with `llama_context::encode()`, which temporarily changes `cparams.causal_attn` around `process_ubatch()` without requesting a scheduler reserve.

## Additional information

The issue is especially visible with mtmd because `tools/mtmd/mtmd-helper.cpp::scope_non_causal` disables causal attention before every image chunk and restores it afterward. Before this change, both calls triggered a full scheduler reserve.

At `n_ctx = 262144` with two slots, each reserve took approximately 700 ms. At `n_ctx = 131072`, each took approximately 330 ms and allocated a 612 MiB CUDA-host compute buffer. GPU utilization remained around 3% while one CPU core was saturated.

Benchmarks from a CUDA build on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell using Gemma 4 31B Q4_K_M, two slots, `--kv-unified`, flash attention, and the same server flags before and after:

| Configuration    | Input                                       |  Before |                After |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------: | -------------------: |
| `n_ctx = 131072` | 10-second clip, 10 frames, 4,527 tokens     | 10.46 s |               3.18 s |
| `n_ctx = 131072` | Single-image embedding decode               |  405 ms |                66 ms |
| `n_ctx = 262144` | 10-second clip                              |  18.2 s |                3.3 s |
| `n_ctx = 262144` | 280-second clip, 280 frames, 114,949 tokens |   489 s | 118 s / 978 tokens/s |

After the change, verbose logs show only the four startup reserves. Output-generation performance was unchanged.

Output quality and causal-attention restoration were checked with:

* Video description
* Two images in one message with thinking enabled
* Tool calling
* A text-only follow-up after image input (`17 × 23 → 391`)

Not yet tested:

* Audio chunks, which use the same path
* M-RoPE vision models such as Qwen VL
* CPU-only backends
* `--no-mmproj-offload`

A possible follow-up is to decode consecutive image chunks in a single non-causal operation. Their encodings are already batched up to `--mtmd-batch-max-tokens`; batching their decode would also reduce per-frame decode overhead.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: Yes: Claude Fable 5.1 was used to find this bug and to do benchmarking.

items.body:
## Overview

llama-server rejects the OpenAI-standard `video_url` content type, and rejects `data:` URIs for video, so any OpenAI-conformant client (OpenAI SDK, llama-cpp-python wrappers, agent frameworks) fails with `400 unsupported content[].type`.

This PR makes `tools/server/server-common.cpp` accept:
- `video_url` as an alias of `input_video` (media read from whichever key was used),
- `data:` URIs for video (`data:video/*`), matching what `image_url` already allows.

Relevant context: [mostlygeek/llama-swap#1047](https://github.com/mostlygeek/llama-swap/issues/1047) — the llama-swap maintainer confirmed the 400 comes from the client/server format mismatch and that llama-swap will not patch around it.

## Additional information

Tested locally on llama.cpp 0.3.0 (Vulkan) with a VLM + video mmproj. Before/after for the same request:

| content part | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `video_url` + `data:video/mp4;base64,...` | `unsupported content[].type` | accepted, model describes the video |
| `input_video` + `{"data": "<raw base64>"}` | works | works (unchanged) |
| `input_video` + `data:` URI | `Failed to load image or audio file` | accepted |

Happy to adjust the shape if maintainers prefer a different alias or want the `data:` URI acceptance gated differently.

## Requirements

- [x] I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES — an AI agent (Hermes, running locally) wrote the change and the local test script, with the contributor reviewing the diff, running the tests against a local llama-server build, and taking full responsibility for the change and its future maintenance. I can explain and defend each line without AI assistance.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Draft models from Hugging Face defined in model preset entries, will appear on the list of models (including the `/models` endpoint) when `dedup-cache-models` is used in a models_preset.ini file.

Steps to reproduce:
1. create a `models_preset.ini` file with a model preset and a draft model from Hugging Face, while using `dedup-cache-models`:
```
[*]
dedup-cache-models   = true
[gemma-4-31b]
hf                   = google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf:Q4_0
spec-type            = draft-mtp
spec-draft-hf        = mradermacher/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized-assistant-GGUF
```
2. Start the server `./llama-server --models-preset models_preset.ini`.
2. load the model preset (`gemma-4-31b`) and let the server download to cache the models from Hugging Face.
3. Restart the server.
4. check the list of available models, or the /models endpoint (http://127.0.0.1:8080/models).
    - The LLM defined after `hf` won't show in the list, as expected when using `dedup-cache-models`.
    -  `gemma-4-31b` will show, since it is defined as a preset.
    - The draft MTP model defined after `spec-draft-hf` will show, despite `dedup-cache-models = true`, this behavior is undesired.

items.body:
Hello,
Thank you for your amazing job.

Official prebuilt llama-b11065-bin-win-vulkan-x64 binaries.

Operating systems
Windows 11 (10.0.26200), x86_64

GGML backends
Vulkan

Hardware
AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 + Radeon 890M iGPU (Strix Point, GFX115x, unified memory / UMA — 64 GB LPDDR5X-8000 shared CPU/GPU). Single GPU, no split mode.

Models
Main: unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-GGUF → gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf (arch gemma4, MoE 25.2B total / 3.8B active, 30 blocks = 25 SWA-1024 + 5 global layers, 2 KV heads × dim 512 on global layers, ctx train 262144)
mmproj-F16.gguf optional (crashes with and without it)
Also reproduced with a second gemma4-26B quant (llmfan46 ...-ultra-uncensored-heretic-Q4_K_M.gguf, same arch).

Problem description & steps to reproduce
With -np 4 (and -np 5), the server loads fine and the first request completes normally, but the second request aborts the whole server:


D:/a/llama.cpp/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:359: GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated") failed
(process exits with status -1073740791 / 0xC0000409)

Minimal repro (no mmproj, no speculative decoding):


llama-server.exe -m gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  -c 1048576 -np 4 -ngl 999 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --port 9999
then two sequential POST /v1/chat/completions with short prompts (~25 tokens): request 1 → normal completion; request 2 → assert + server death.

What we ruled out (all still crash at -np 4):

speculative decoding: crashes with and without --spec-type draft-mtp + external mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it.gguf (gemma4-assistant) drafter
prompt cache: crashes with --no-cache-prompt
batch sizes: crashes with -b 2048 -ub 1024
vision: crashes with and without --mmproj
multi-model router mode (llama-server serve --models-preset ...): also reproduces with plain single-instance llama-server (commands above)
What works:

Vulkan -np 1, -np 2, -np 3: fully stable (sequential + 3-concurrent requests, ~20 requests incl. prompt-cache reuse and an external MTP drafter with 0.52–0.66 acceptance). Only from -np 4 upward it crashes.
CPU backend, same version, same machine: -np 4 fully stable (4-concurrent
sequential, zero crash) → looks Vulkan-backend-specific, not a scheduler issue per se.
qwen35moe (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) at -np 4 works fine on Vulkan on the same machine/build → gemma4-specific, not MoE-generic.
Diagnostic hint: in every crashing run, the crashing request had just been assigned to slot id 3 (LRU or LCP-similarity selection), whether that slot was fresh or had a reusable prefix. With -np 3 (slot ids 0–2) no crash was ever observed. This suggests something about the 4th slot's reserved buffers/graph for gemma4 on Vulkan, but we have no way to pin a request to a slot to confirm. Every crash we captured happened during the 2nd request's prompt processing, right after a slot get_availabl: ... selected slot ... f_keep = ... line.

Not a memory-size problem: at -np 4 the model + KV use ~25 GB of the 48.8 GB Vulkan device heap (device reports 46.3 GB free at init), and the same build at -np 5 also loads and answers before crashing, while the system has 24+ GB of free RAM throughout.

First Bad Commit
No response (official release binaries; not bisected)

Relevant log output
Load is clean, first request OK, second request dies:


console
0.10.824.972 I srv    load_model: loaded multimodal model, '...\mmproj-F16.gguf'   <- only in the mmproj variant
0.11.221.236 I srv    load_model: initializing, n_slots = 4, n_ctx_slot = 262144, kv_unified = 'false'
0.11.239.674 I srv  llama_server: model loaded
0.11.239.688 I srv  llama_server: listening on http://127.0.0.1:9999
0.48.520.356 I slot get_availabl: id  3 | task -1 | selected slot by LRU, t_last = -1
0.48.520.436 I slot launch_slot_: id  3 | task 0 | processing task, is_child = 0
0.54.217.138 I slot print_timing: id  3 | task 0 | prompt eval time =    5074.18 ms /    30 tokens
0.54.217.149 I slot print_timing: id  3 | task 0 |        eval time =     622.17 ms /    20 tokens
0.54.217.153 I slot print_timing: id  3 | task 0 |    graphs reused =         19
0.54.217.212 I slot      release: id  3 | task 0 | stop processing: n_tokens = 49, truncated = 0
0.54.234.189 I slot get_availabl: id  3 | task -1 | selected slot by LCP similarity, f_sim_best = 0.467 (> 0.100 thold), f_keep = 0.286
D:/a/llama.cpp/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:359: GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated") failed
(The assert line is the last line; no stack trace beyond it on Windows release binaries. Exit code -1073740791 / 0xC0000409.)

Related issues (possibly same root area — gemma4 shared-KV global layers vs backend schedulers)
#25522 — Gemma 4 crashes with MTP on the 2nd prompt (CUDA, multi-GPU tensor-split + MTP; still open, "racy rather than always the 2nd prompt"). Ours: single GPU, no MTP required, Vulkan-only.
#24492 — Gemma 4 31B MTP crashes on Vulkan at init (draft shared-KV cache_k_l58 pre-allocated tensor, NONE op). Ours: crashes at runtime without any MTP drafter.
#28917 — gemma4:26b concurrent decode loses EOS (same model, concurrency related, different symptom).
Workaround for our deployment: keep gemma4 at -np 3 on Vulkan (or use the CPU backend, which is stable at -np 4).

# Title

Eval bug: draft-mtp (self-speculative) models crash on Vulkan/RADV after Linux kernel bump 7.1.3 → 7.1.7 — same class as #24492, different GPU/model

# Body

### Related issue
This looks like the same crash class as #24492 ("Gemma 4 31B MTP (draft-mtp) crashes on Vulkan backend, pre-allocated tensor cannot run operation NONE"), reproduced here on different hardware (RADV GFX1201 instead of RX 7900 XTX) and a different model family (Qwen3.8-27B instead of Gemma 4 31B). Unlike that report, I have a clean bisection: the exact same llama.cpp binary and Mesa version work or crash depending solely on which Linux kernel is booted, which may help narrow down whether this is a Vulkan/amdgpu KMD interaction rather than a pure userspace bug.

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-cli --version
WARNING: radv is not a conformant Vulkan implementation, testing use only.
version: 0.1.2-dev (build 10517, commit dc72703fc)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Built from source at that commit; binary/libs timestamped 2026-08-19.

### Operating systems

Linux (Debian 13 "trixie" + trixie-backports)

### GGML backends

Vulkan (RADV)

### Hardware

- GPU: AMD Radeon R9700, reported by RADV as `AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV GFX1201)`
- `amdgpu` reports `HMM registered 32624MB device memory`
- Vulkan driver: `driverID=DRIVER_ID_MESA_RADV`, `driverInfo=Mesa 26.1.2-1~bpo13+1`, `apiVersion=1.4.348` (from `vulkaninfo --summary`)
- Mesa packages: `mesa-vulkan-drivers` / `mesa-libgallium` `26.1.2-1~bpo13+1` (held constant across the whole test below — only the kernel changed)

### Models

Custom preset `qwen3.8-27b`, self-speculative multi-token-prediction (no separate draft-model file):

```
/usr/local/bin/llama-server \
  --api-key-file /opt/llama/api-key.txt \
  --model /opt/llama/models/qwen3.8-27b.gguf \
  --mmproj /opt/llama/models/qwen3.8-27b-mmproj.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-mtp \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --n-gpu-layers 999 \
  --parallel 1 \
  --batch-size 512 --ubatch-size 512 \
  --context-shift --jinja --webui-mcp-proxy
```

Other presets on the same box that use an *external* draft-model `.gguf` file (e.g. `gemma4-e2b`, which loads a separate `gemma4-e2b-mtp.gguf`) do **not** crash under the same conditions — only presets doing shared-layer self-speculation without a separate draft file are affected (`qwen3.8-27b`, `qwen3.8-27b-low`, `qwen3.8-27b-medium`, `qwen3.6-35b`, `thinkingcap-qwen3.6-27b`, `fable-fusion-27b`, `gemma4-31b`).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

This model/preset was benchmarked as working the day before the crash first appeared — on this exact llama.cpp commit and this exact Mesa version — with recorded numbers up to 58.75 tok/s at spec depth n=4 (kept as a comment in our local config for reference). Nothing about the llama.cpp build, Mesa version, or model files changed between the working and broken state. The only thing that changed was a Debian backports kernel upgrade + reboot:

| Boot | Kernel | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-19, 14:57–2026-08-20 07:24 | `7.1.3+deb13-amd64` (`linux-image-amd64 7.1.3-1~bpo13+1`) | Works — this is the boot the benchmark numbers above came from |
| 2026-08-20, 07:28–14:35 | `7.1.3+deb13-amd64` (same) | Works |
| 2026-08-20, 14:35–15:18 | `7.1.7+deb13-amd64` (`linux-image-amd64 7.1.7-1~bpo13+1`, first boot after `apt` upgraded and rebooted) | **Crashes**, 100% reproducible on every load attempt |
| 2026-08-20, 15:20– (later) | `7.1.7+deb13-amd64` (same, fresh reboot) | **Crashes**, reproduced again |
| After manually pinning GRUB back to `7.1.3+deb13-amd64` and rebooting | `7.1.3+deb13-amd64` | Works again — same binary, same Mesa, same model files, only the kernel changed back |

Steps to reproduce on affected kernel:
1. Boot `7.1.7+deb13-amd64` (Debian backports) with `mesa-vulkan-drivers` `26.1.2-1~bpo13+1` and an AMD RDNA4/GFX1201 GPU (R9700).
2. Start `llama-server` with the `qwen3.8-27b` config above (`--spec-type draft-mtp`, `--cache-type-k/v q8_0`, `--flash-attn on`, no separate `--model-draft` file).
3. Send any completion request that forces the model to load.
4. Server child process aborts immediately during context construction, before any tokens are generated.

Reverting only the kernel (staying on the same llama.cpp build, same Mesa) makes it work again, which points at an amdgpu KMD ↔ RADV interaction rather than a pure Mesa or llama.cpp-side regression — though given #24492 is already open against different hardware without any kernel mentioned, it's also possible this is a latent/racy bug in the Vulkan backend's cross-context KV-cache-sharing scheduling (`ggml_backend_sched_backend_id_from_cur` / `resolve_fused_ops`) that the kernel change merely made more likely to trigger, rather than something the kernel changed correctness-wise on its own.

### First Bad commit

Not a llama.cpp commit — llama.cpp build and Mesa version were held constant throughout. The regression tracks the Debian backports kernel package bump `linux-image-amd64` `7.1.3-1~bpo13+1` → `7.1.7-1~bpo13+1` (upstream Linux 7.1.3 → 7.1.7 stable point releases). I don't have a narrower bisection within that kernel range.

### Relevant log output

Short-form message (seen on the previous boot, layer index varies by run):
```
[52709] /home/subsolar/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:930: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l64) in a buffer (Vulkan0) that cannot run the operation (NONE)
```

Full backtrace (from `llama-server`'s built-in crash handler, current boot on 7.1.7, `qwen3.8-27b`):
```
[33317] [New LWP 2214]
[33317] [New LWP 2213]
[33317] [New LWP 2212]
[33317] [Thread debugging using libthread_db enabled]
[33317] Using host libthread_db library "/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libthread_db.so.1".
[33317] 0x00007ff434aa69ee in ?? () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6
[33317] #0  0x00007ff434aa69ee in ?? () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6
[33317] #1  0x00007ff434a9b668 in ?? () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc

items.title: Eval bug: Gemma 4 crashes with MTP

items.body:
## Overview

The existing small-batch mat-vec path (`kernel_mul_mv_ext`, 2 <= ne11 <= 8) assigns one
weight row per thread and re-reads the full activation columns for every row, so its cost
grows linearly with ne11. Measured op-level: each added column costs about one full
n=1 matvec (q8_0, 4096x14336: 53.1 us at n=1, 108.8 at n=2, 403.9 at n=8).

That is exactly the regime of speculative-decoding verification (draft-mtp with
n_max = 2..8). On master, raising n_max from 1 to 2 makes decode slower, not faster
(34.2 -> 32.5 t/s end-to-end, Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0): verifying the draft tokens costs about
as much as generating them, so there is nothing to gain from raising n_max above 1.

This PR adds kernels where each thread handles NR0 = 4 weight rows x R1 activation
columns (R1 = 2..4): the y slice of the R1 columns stays in registers and is reused
across the rows, and each weight block is loaded once and reused across the columns.

Dispatch is added in `ggml_metal_op_mul_mat` ahead of the existing small-batch path and
fires only when all of the following hold:

- src0 type is Q4_0 or Q8_0
- src1 type is F32
- `ne00 % 32 == 0`
- `2 <= ne11 <= 8`

Everything else keeps the current kernels.

## Additional information

Related open PR on the same path from a different angle: #27776. It reports that the
K-quant `mul_mv_ext` path (ne11 4..8) runs much slower than the regular `mul_mv` on
M3 Pro and disables it there for K-quants; the author noticed the same spec-decoding
symptom (depth 4 slower than depth 1). This PR does not touch that K-quant branch -
the new gate is Q4_0/Q8_0 only - and for those two types it replaces the `mul_mv_ext`
path with faster kernels instead of disabling it.

## How it works

New kernels in `kernels/mul_mv.metal`:
`kernel_mul_mv_q4_0_f32_r1_{2,3,4}_nr0_4` and `kernel_mul_mv_q8_0_f32_r1_{2,3,4}_nr0_4`.

- Q4_0: same layout as the existing `kernel_mul_mv_q4_0_f32` - each simdgroup covers its
  rows over the full K and reduces with `simd_sum`, no threadgroup memory.
- Q8_0: the K dimension is split across the NSG simdgroups - each pass strides `NSG*NQ`
  blocks with NQ = 8 (8 blocks of QK8_0, 32 elements each, per simdgroup); one
  threadgroup covers NR0 = 4 rows, and the cross-simdgroup reduction reuses the existing
  `helper_mv_reduce_and_write` (32 floats x NR0 in threadgroup memory).
- R1 selection (activation columns per thread):
  - ne11 = 2, 3, 4 -> R1 = ne11
  - ne11 = 5, 6 -> R1 = 3
  - ne11 = 7, 8 -> R1 = 4
  For ne11 = 5 and 7, the last column of the final threadgroup is out of range and is
  clamped to the previous one; that clamped duplicate is computed but not written.
- NR0 = 4 was measured on M3 Ultra: for Q8_0 it beats 2 (the current `N_R0_Q8_0`) and
  8 (register pressure); Q4_0 keeps `N_R0_Q4_0`.

## Performance

Machine: Mac Studio M3 Ultra (60-core GPU), 96 GB, macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 27.
Release build, `-DGGML_METAL=ON -DGGML_METAL_EMBED_LIBRARY=ON`.
A/B on the same commit `4fea119de`: clean master ("up", `mul_mv_ext` path) vs this
branch ("pr", kernel active by default, no env vars).

### Op-level

`test-backend-ops perf -o MUL_MAT -b MTL0`, us/run (same test binary, only the Metal
dylib swapped):

| type | m x k | n | up (us) | pr (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| q4_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 1 | 39.2 | 39.1 | 1.00x |
| q4_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 2 | 107.5 | 60.8 | 1.77x |
| q4_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 3 | 157.1 | 82.8 | 1.90x |
| q4_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 4 | 206.7 | 122.2 | 1.69x |
| q4_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 5 | 255.2 | 188.0 | 1.36x |
| q4_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 8 | 412.0 | 262.0 | 1.57x |
| q4_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 512 | 3974.9 | 3988.8 | 1.00x |
| q4_0 | 17408 x 5120 | 1 | 50.3 | 50.6 | 0.99x |
| q4_0 | 17408 x 5120 | 2 | 152.9 | 112.8 | 1.36x |
| q4_0 | 17408 x 5120 | 3 | 218.0 | 172.8 | 1.26x |
| q4_0 | 17408 x 5120 | 4 | 294.1 | 233.9 | 1.26x |
| q4_0 | 17408 x 5120 | 8 | 572.6 | 450.5 | 1.27x |
| q8_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 1 | 53.1 | 55.8 | 0.95x |
| q8_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 2 | 108.8 | 65.1 | 1.67x |
| q8_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 3 | 158.8 | 88.9 | 1.79x |
| q8_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 4 | 203.1 | 134.9 | 1.51x |
| q8_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 5 | 250.1 | 158.3 | 1.58x |
| q8_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 8 | 403.9 | 229.8 | 1.76x |
| q8_0 | 4096 x 14336 | 512 | 4071.3 | 4057.0 | 1.00x |
| q8_0 | 17408 x 5120 | 1 | 114.2 | 112.2 | 1.02x |
| q8_0 | 17408 x 5120 | 2 | 131.6 | 122.3 | 1.08x |
| q8_0 | 17408 x 5120 | 3 | 210.1 | 129.5 | 1.62x |
| q8_0 | 17408 x 5120 | 4 | 284.7 | 157.8 | 1.80x |
| q8_0 | 17408 x 5120 | 8 | 555.1 | 296.9 | 1.87x |

n = 1 and n = 512 do not reach the new kernel (the dispatch gate requires
2 <= ne11 <= 8): both builds run the identical existing path there, so these rows are
controls and the 0.95x-1.02x spread is measurement noise. 17408 x 5120 is a 27B-class
FFN shape.

### Model-level, llama-batched-bench

Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 (29.0 GB), KV q8_0, ctx 16384, npp 512, ntg 64:

| B | up tg (t/s) | pr tg (t/s) | up ms/step | pr ms/step | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 21.91 | 21.92 | 45.6 | 45.6 | 1.00x |
| 2 | 35.00 | 38.66 | 57.1 | 51.7 | 1.10x |
| 3 | 36.63 | 52.50 | 81.9 | 57.1 | 1.43x |
| 4 | 37.37 | 56.39 | 107.0 | 70.9 | 1.51x |
| 8 | 40.11 | 64.66 | 199.5 | 123.7 | 1.61x |

### End-to-end, llama-server with draft-mtp

400 tokens, temperature 0, ctx 131072, median of 3 repetitions:

| model | n_max | up (t/s) | pr (t/s) | delta | accept | output identical |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 | 1 | 34.2 | 35.4 | +3% | 0.891 | yes |
| Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 | 2 | 32.5 | 44.5 | +37% | 0.836 | yes |
| Gemma-4-31B UD-Q8_K_XL | 2 | 28.9 | 41.4 | +43% | 0.809 | yes |
| Gemma-4-12B UD-Q8_K_XL | 2 | 63.8 | 85.5 | +34% | 0.784 | yes |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q8_0 (MoE) | 2 | 114.0 | 118.7 | +4% | 0.812 | yes |

Outputs are byte-identical between up and pr in every run (sha1 of all 3 repetitions).
KV type: Qwen3.8-27B ran with KV q8_0, Gemma-4-31B/12B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with KV f16
(each model's production configuration).

### Depth

Real 89575-token code prompt, Qwen3.8-2

items.body:
Fixes crash when running with Gemma MTP and Tensor. Originally found while playing with [beelama](https://github.com/Anbeeld/beellama.cpp), discovered it also affected mainline, and found others with the issue. 

Two contexts sharing memory under SPLIT_MODE_TENSOR (e.g. Gemma4 MTP or EAGLE3 draft + target) both create views into the same meta-backend buffers. Reusing a stale graph after the peer has rebuilt leaves dangling per-device tensor references, causing fattn.cu:579 crashes.

Fix: disable graph reuse for both contexts when either uses tensor split and they share memory. Backend-agnostic, applies to Gemma4 MTP and EAGLE3. 

Confirmed on 2x 7900 XTX (ROCm/HIP/RCCL) with 3 sequential same-slot requests.
Also confirmed on NVIDIA by testers in #24314.

Fixes #24324, #24314, #24440  

- [x] I have read and agree with the contributing guidelines
- [x] AI usage disclosure: AI assistance used for codebase exploration, hypothesis testing, and verification. I understand the patch as written.

items.body:
For models that share tensors with another model through ctx_other (e.g. Gemma4Assistant, Eagle3, DFlash, DSpark), add the other model's device backends to the context scheduler so that pre-allocated shared tensors (tok_embd, output) can be scheduled. Fixes an abort when the speculative draft model uses a device list that does not cover the GPU holding the target model's output projection.

Assisted-by: opencode

## Overview

## Bug (observed behavior)
- Abort during llama_context construction: "pre-allocated tensor (output.weight) in a buffer (CUDA10) that cannot run the operation (NONE)"
- Location: ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp (line ~898/930 depending on version), called from llama_context::sched_reserve -> graph_reserve -> resolve_fused_ops
- Trigger: speculative decoding with ctx_other (draft-dspark / draft-dflash / draft-mtp), draft model on its own device via --device-draft/--spec-draft-device, target model on other GPU(s)
- Root cause : the draft context scheduler only had backends for the draft's own devices; shared pre-allocated tensors (tok_embd/output.weight, taken from the target model via ctx_other in src/models/dflash.cpp) live in buffers on the target's devices; scheduler found no backend for those buffers and aborted

## Reproduction (your setup)
- llama-server in router mode, model preset:
  - device = CUDA3,CUDA4,CUDA5,CUDA7,CUDA8,CUDA9,CUDA10 (--split-mode layer)
  - spec-type = draft-dspark, spec-draft-n-max = 8
  - spec-draft-device = CUDA0
  - model-draft = dspark/dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf
- Before fix: GGML_ABORT, spec model failed to load
- After fix: draft context logs "adding backend for device CUDA3..CUDA10: shared tensors with the other model (e.g. tok_embd, output)", speculative implementation 'draft-dspark' initializes (n_max=8, block_size=5), server healthy
- Verified with CI-built image version 10282 (34ec9c9bb) on 15-GPU host (RTX 3080/4080/4090/3090), CUDA 12, 16x 3090-class workload


## Additional information

## Related issues
- #26475 - "using -devd CUDA0 on draft-dspark causes model to crash": same abort message (output.weight, CUDA8), same stack, draft-dspark + tensor split. Directly matches. (open)
- #24492 - Gemma 4 31B MTP, Vulkan: "pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l58) ... cannot run the operation (NONE)" - same abort class, ctx_other/KV sharing; mechanism may differ (Vulkan backend support), unknown whether fixed
- #24366 - Gemma MTP, tensor split, buffer "Meta()": same abort class; unknown whether fixed
- #26339 - "Dspark model fails to load with -sm tensor on MI50": possible same class; unknown
 
## Requirements

<!-- IMPORTANT: Please do NOT delete this section, otherwise your PR may be rejected -->

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - opencode + ds4

I am seeing a reproducible HIP/ROCm correctness issue on Windows with an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201).

Using the same Gemma 4 31B model, the same token prefix, the same absolute token positions and seq_id=0, changing only the target scoring shape changes the HIP logits enough to flip the greedy top-1 token.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Load the model using the HIP backend.

2. Use a fixed sequence consisting of 29 prompt tokens followed by 26 teacher-forced suffix tokens.

3. Clear KV state before each scoring request.

4. Score the same 27 prediction positions using:

   * single-token scoring
   * three-token batched scoring

CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5900X
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (RDNA3, gfx1100), 24GB VRAM
ROCm 7.1.1, Mesa RADV NAVI31 (Vulkan)

### Models

Main:  https://huggingface.co/unsloth/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-GGUF/blob/main/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
Draft: https://huggingface.co/unsloth/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-GGUF/blob/main/MTP/gemma-4-31B-it-Q4_0-MTP.gguf

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Gemma 4 31B with --spec-type draft-mtp crashes immediately on context
initialization when using the Vulkan backend. The crash does not occur with
ROCm (--device ROCm0), which works correctly at 45-60 tok/s with MTP.

The crash happens during draft model KV cache setup, specifically when
llama.cpp tries to schedule a pre-allocated shared KV tensor (cache_k_l58)
on Vulkan0. The Vulkan backend scheduler aborts because it cannot run the
NONE operation on a pre-allocated tensor in its buffer.

The KV sharing warnings immediately precede the crash:
  llama_kv_cache: layer 3: sharing with layer 59
  llama_kv_cache: layer 0: sharing with layer 58
  llama_kv_cache: layer 1: sharing with layer 58
  llama_kv_cache: layer 2: sharing with layer 58

This is Gemma 4's MTP draft KV sharing pattern (layers 0-3 of the draft
sharing with layers 58-59 of the main model). The Vulkan backend scheduler
does not support this cross-context pre-allocated tensor assignment.

Tested with both f16 and q8_0 KV cache — same crash either way.
--fit off is already set; this is not the fit-path crash from issue #24117.

Build command:
  HIPCXX="$(hipconfig -l)/clang" HIP_PATH="$(hipconfig -R)" \
  cmake -S . -B build -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGGML_VULKAN=ON \
  -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1100 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DGGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=ON -DLLAMA_CURL=ON

Reproduce with:
  llama-server \
    --model gemma-4-31B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
    --spec-draft-model gemma-4-31B-it-Q4_0-MTP.gguf \
    --device Vulkan0 \
    --spec-type draft-mtp \
    --spec-draft-n-max 4 \
    --ctx-size 16384 \
    --n-gpu-layers 99 \
    --parallel 1 \
    --fit off \
    --flash-attn on \
    --cache-type-k f16 \
    --cache-type-v f16 \
    --reasoning on \
    --jinja

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. PR #23398 (Gemma 4 MTP support) merged recently, this may be
a pre-existing Vulkan limitation rather than a regression. ROCm was not
tested before #23398 so cannot confirm if this is a new regression.

### Name and Version

```
version: 10107 (c0bc8591e)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Also reproduced after rebuilding with `-DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON` added to the CMake configuration (same base commit).

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (16 GB VRAM each, Blackwell), driver 595.71.05, CUDA 13.2, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89` (Ada Lovelace target, used as a workaround — direct Blackwell arch build was not attempted/needed for this report).

### Models

Reproduced on **two independently produced GGUF quantizations** of Gemma 4 31B, sourced from different origins (one traced back to a direct conversion of Google's original safetensors via a third-party "uncensored/heretic" fine-tune, the other from Unsloth's official quantization):

* `gemma-4-31B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized-uncensored-heretic.Q4_K_M` (mradermacher-hosted repack)
* `gemma-4-31B-it-qat-UD.Q4_K_XL` (Unsloth)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` reliably enters an infinite generation loop of the `<unused49>` token (vocabulary ID **62** in this model's tokenizer) after the model has been loaded and left idle (no requests sent) for an extended period — typically several hours up to overnight (\~19 hours in the most recent controlled test). Once triggered, **every subsequent request** on the affected slot produces only `<unused49>` repeated until `n_predict`/max tokens is reached, or forever if unbounded.

Steps:

1. Start `llama-server` with a Gemma 4 31B GGUF (either quant source above).
2. Send one initial warm-up request — this succeeds normally.
3. **Leave the server idle with no further requests for several hours (reproduced most reliably after \~19h).**
4. Send a new request. Prompt processing is abnormally slow (see log below, \~2.4 tok/s vs. the \~600-700 tok/s seen on the same hardware/model shortly after a fresh restart), and generation either produces only `<unused49>` or the request has to be cancelled.
5. Restarting `llama-server` (recomputing KV cache from scratch) immediately resolves the issue — until the next long idle period.

### Key isolating observations from this investigation

* **Not correlated with cumulative token usage or conversation length.** Reproduced with a single short warm-up request followed by pure idle time — no long conversation or heavy prompt history involved.
* **Not specific to one GGUF quant source.** Reproduced on both an Unsloth quant and an independently-produced quant (different conversion pipeline, different uploader), ruling out a single quantizer's conversion bug as the sole cause.
* **Not resolved by fixing missing `tokenizer.ggml.eot_token_id` metadata.** One of the two GGUFs tested was missing this field entirely (confirmed via `gguf-py`); the other (Unsloth) had it set to ID 106. Directly verified via `gguf-py` that `tokens[106] == '<turn|>'` (the correct Gemma-4 end-of-turn token) on both GGUFs before patching. Patching the missing field in with `gguf_new_metadata.py --special-token-by-id eot 106` reduced/delayed but did not eliminate the issue.
* **Not resolved by changing KV cache quantization.** Tested both `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` (symmetric) and `-ctk q8_0 -ctv f16` (asymmetric, after rebuilding with `-DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON` to avoid the known CPU-fallback/hang issue with asymmetric K/V types — see #20866, #24485). Both configurations eventually reproduced the `<unused49>` loop after sufficient idle time.
* **No corresponding kernel/driver-level errors.** `dmesg` around the time of the failure shows no Xid errors, no ECC errors, no OOM killer activity, and no GPU reset. Persistence mode was confirmed enabled. This suggests the fault is not a GPU/driver-level recovery issue but something in the server process's own state (CUDA context, KV cache bookkeeping, or similar) degrading over idle time.
* `-np 1` (single slot, no `--parallel` specified) in all tests, so the same KV cache slot is reused across all requests via LRU/LCP-similarity selection (`selected slot by LRU, t_last = ...`).

### Related issues that appear connected

* \#23677 — grammar sampler crash on `<unused49>` (ID 62) for Gemma 4, confirming this is a recognized special/reserved token that the codebase already has trouble handling in at least one other code path.
* \#24311 — Gemma 4 12B QAT outputs `<unused49>` continuously on Vulkan when GPU-offloading (CPU-only offload reportedly avoids it).
* \#21516 — separate report of Gemma 4 emitting a different reserved token (ID 14) in an infinite loop on Vulkan.
* \#21321 — separate report of `<unused24>` looping.
* unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF HF discussion — multiple independent users report the same `<unused49>` loop after "extended thinking" or long-running sessions, with one user noting the issue also reproduces on non-Unsloth quants (bartowski, ggml, lmstudio) at higher bit-depths but not lower ones, and another explicitly noting restart-fixes-it-temporarily behavior identical to what's described here.

## Summary

Across the two quant sources tested and two different KV cache quantization configurations, the one consistent reproducing factor is **elapsed idle time with the model loaded**, not token throughput, not a specific quantizer, and not (as far as `dmesg` shows) a GPU/driver fault. Since the model weights themselves are static once loaded, a bug in the model file itself seems unlikely to fully explain a fault that only appears after hours of idle time with no requests processed — though this can't be ruled out with certainty. The more likely explanation is some runtime state (KV cache bookkeeping, CUDA context, slot/LRU timestamp handling, or similar) degrading over idle time, with Gemma 4's vocabulary/architecture determining which specific token (62 / `<unused49>` in most reports) the output collapses into once that state is corrupted. ## Overview

Stream-k tries to split chunks of 256 K elements evenly across all SMs. Workgroups that finish a tile write to dst, others write to scratch, and there's a resolve shader similar to split-k.

The shader code is implemented for scalar+cm1+cm2, but only currently enabled for cm2. The heuristic for enabling on coopmat2 is pretty simple due to the large tile size (one workgroup per SM), but would be more complex for the tile sizes being used for cm1, and it doesn't make sense for me to tune that on NVIDIA devices.

## Overview

#22780 adds the option to fuse QKV for models which previously had either no QKV tensors (`gemma4`) or for which QKV tensors only existed for specific layers (`qwen35`, `qwen35moe`, ...).

Gemma 4 31B: `n_embd` is 5376 but Q is 8192 (raising `GGML_ASSERT(tensor->ne[axis] == n_embd + 2*n_embd_gqa);`), so calculate from `n_head * n_embd_head_k` instead.

Qwen 27B/35B-A3B: added a copy of the default qkv handler for full attention layers, with `n_embd` doubled for Q gate tensors, and add the doubling in `get_split_granularity` as well.

## Additional information

I tested Gemma 4 31B, Qwen 3.8 27B and Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B on 4 P100 cards.

## Requirements

<!-- IMPORTANT: Please do NOT delete this section, otherwise your PR may be rejected -->

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. I used Qwen 3.8 27B to analyze the errors I was getting with the fused models and then to reason through the changes required.

## Overview

For `MUL_MAT_ID` on the coopmat1 path, each workgroup's real row count (`_ne1 - ic*BN`) is frequently less than the full `BN`/`WN` tile once expert routing is accounted for. This adds `required_work_items`/`required_warp_c` bounds computed right after the existing "workgroup has no work" early-return, and uses them to skip the B-matrix memory load and the coopmat compute loop for subgroups/warps beyond what's actually needed for that workgroup.

### Name and Version

version: 10126 (2cfc7670e)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

3x RTX3090

### Models

`--swa-full` combined with `-sm tensor` causes an abort during model load for Gemma4-31B on any multi-GPU config. Related to closed #23294 (same backtrace, different trigger — `--swa-full` rather than MTP).

**Hardware:** 3× RTX 3090 (72GB total VRAM), ASUS Pro WS X570-ACE, Ubuntu 24.04, b10126 (fill in actual version after build)

**Models:** Gemma4-31B-it Q8\_0 (3 GPUs, `-ts 1,1,1`) and Q6\_K\_L (2 GPUs, `-ts 1,1,0`)

**Command (crashes):**
```
llama-server -m gemma-4-31B-it-Q8_0.gguf -ngl 999 -ts 1,1,1 -sm tensor -np 1 \
  --ctx-size 131072 --swa-full --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 -fa on --jinja
```

**Backtrace:**
```
ggml_backend_meta_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft
llama_kv_cache::llama_kv_cache (constructor)
llama_kv_cache_iswa::llama_kv_cache_iswa (constructor)
llama_model::create_memory
llama_context::llama_context
```

**Root cause hypothesis:** the meta-backend tensor allocation fails for the ISWA dual-cache layout when `-sm tensor` is active. `--swa-full` triggers the ISWA path (setting `size_swa = size_base`), and the meta-backend cannot allocate tensors for the resulting layout. The same `ggml_backend_meta_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft` abort was seen in #23294 with MTP + `-sm tensor` on a MoE model — this is the same failure path triggered by a different ISWA consumer.

**Workarounds attempted — all fail:**
- `-sm row`: rejected at load with "device CUDA0 does not support split buffers"
- `-sm layer` + `--swa-full` + ctx 131072: OOM — `--swa-full` sizes SWA sub-cache to full context across all 62 layers (~130GB KV equivalent on 72GB VRAM)
- `-sm layer` + `--swa-full` + ctx 131072 + `-ts 1,2,2`: still OOM on GPU0

**Practical consequence:** cache reuse (fixed in #21468 via `--swa-full`) is completely inaccessible for Gemma4-31B in any multi-GPU configuration on this hardware. The only working path is `-sm tensor` without `--swa-full` — no cache reuse, full re-prefill every turn.

Note: #22527 is a related but distinct Gemma4 SWA interaction bug.


### Problem description & steps to reproduce

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Build mainline llama.cpp (no patches) at b10127 or later
2. Load Gemma4-31B Q8_0 with -sm tensor + --swa-full:
   llama-server -m gemma-4-31B-it-Q8_0.gguf -ngl 999 -ts 1,1,1 -sm tensor -np 1 \
     --ctx-size 131072 --swa-full --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 -fa on --jinja --port 9999
3. Server aborts immediately during model load with the backtrace above.

Workarounds attempted to enable --swa-full on multi-GPU:
4. Replace -sm tensor with -sm row → fails: "device CUDA0 does not support split buffers"
5. Replace -sm tensor with -sm layer, keep -ts 1,1,1 → OOM on GPU0
6. -sm layer + -ts 1,2,2 → still OOM on GPU0

Root cause of OOM in steps 5-6: --swa-full at ctx 131072 sizes the SWA sub-cache
to full context across all 62 layers. Estimated KV cache: ~130GB — exceeds 72GB
total VRAM regardless of tensor split ratio.

Result: cache reuse (--swa-full, fixing #21468) is inaccessible on 3x RTX 3090
in any multi-GPU configuration.

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs — -sm tensor + --swa-full crash</summary>

```console

#4  llama_kv_cache::llama_kv_cache(llama_model const&, llama_hparams const&, ggml_type, ggml_type, bool, bool, bool, unsigned int, unsigned int, unsigned int, unsigned int, llama_swa_type, llama_memory_i*, ...)

### Models

_No response_

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Problem description

Short prompts (< ~20 tokens) generate correctly. Large prompts
(~5000+ tokens) produce garbled, incoherent, multi-script output
starting from the first generated token — not a formatting/parser
issue, the underlying generation itself is corrupted. This occurs
despite `GGML_SYCL_DISABLE_OPT=1` being set, which should disable the
weight-reorder optimization implicated in issue #21893.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
curl http://<host>:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -d '{"model":"gemma4-12b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":128}'
# -> clean response

# vs. a ~5800-token prompt (see test2 payload in this pack)
curl http://<host>:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -d @test2_payload.json
# -> garbled response from the first token
```

Full reproduction script: `test-gemma4-corruption.sh` (included in this
pack) — runs a small-prompt/short-gen baseline, a large-prompt/short-gen
test, and a small-prompt/long-gen test to separate prompt size from
generation length as variables.

## Observed vs expected

**Expected:** coherent output regardless of prompt size, consistent with
short-prompt behavior.

**Observed:** `usage.prompt_tokens: 5780`, response `content` is
incoherent multi-script token soup from the start of generation. Example
(truncated) — see `sample-responses/test2_large_prompt_short_gen.json`
in this pack for the full payload.

**Critically: the corruption persists after the triggering request.**
A subsequent trivial request (`"hi"`, 17 prompt tokens, `cached_tokens: 7`
— reusing cache from the corrupted instance) on the *same* model
instance also returns garbled output, even though the identical request
was clean before the large-prompt request ran. Reproduction:

```bash
# 1. Fresh model load, trivial request — clean
curl .../v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"general","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":128}'
# -> clean

# 2. Large prompt (~5800 tokens), same instance — garbles
curl .../v1/chat/completions -d @test2_payload.json
# -> garbled from first token

# 3. Immediately after, same instance, no reload — the SAME trivial request as step 1
curl .../v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"general","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":128}'
# -> ALSO garbled now
```

This indicates the corruption is sticky — likely persistent VRAM/weight
or KV-cache state damage, not a per-request numerical fluke isolated to
the large prompt itself. Only a full model reload recovers clean output.

**Refinement — likely per-slot, not global:** the server runs
`n_slots=4`. The corrupted large-prompt request was handled by slot 2.
The subsequent trivial "hi" request that also came back garbled was
*not* randomly assigned — the server's slot-selection logic routed it to
the same slot 2 via LCP (longest-common-prefix) cache-similarity
matching (`selected slot by LCP similarity, sim_best = 0.647`). A
separate trivial request handled earlier by slot 3 (before the large
prompt ran) was clean.

This suggests the corruption may be confined to that slot's KV
cache/compute buffers rather than the shared model weights — which
would be a different, and likely more tractable, bug than global weight
corruption. **Not yet confirmed:** need a test where a trivial request
is forced onto a different, untouched slot immediately after the large
prompt corrupts slot 2 — if that comes back clean, it confirms per-slot
scope; if it's also garbled, it points back to global state.

**Update — cache-reuse ruled out, points to compute-level corruption:**
Ran with `-sps 1.0` (`--slot-prompt-similarity 1.0`), which disables
fuzzy prefix-cache reuse and forces every request onto a fresh, isolated
slot. Confirmed via logs — all follow-up requests after the large prompt
now show `selected slot by LRU` (fresh slot, full prompt re-eval), not
`LCP similarity` (partial cache reuse), so slot/cache reuse is
definitively not happening. **All requests were still garbled anyway.**

This rules out KV-cache-reuse-as-spreading-vector. The corruption is not
confined to a reused cache region — it persists at a deeper level (most
likely GPU-side scratch/compute buffers shared across all slots) after
the triggering large-prompt prefill, regardless of how later requests
are routed. Only a full model reload clears it. This is closer to the
original global-corruption theory (#21893's class of bug), now with a
specific, confirmed trigger condition: long-sequence (~5780 token)
prefill on this hardware/build.

**Confirmed — generation length alone is not a trigger.** Isolated test:
fresh model reload, then *only* the small-prompt/long-generation request
(38 prompt tokens, 1500 generated tokens) — no large prompt run first.
Result: fully coherent throughout (`cached_tokens: 0`, confirming fresh
state). This ru

## Overview

The internal AllReduce implementation is disabled on HIP due to missing functionality (`cudaHostAllocPortable`, `cudaHostAllocMapped`, `cudaHostGetDevicePointer`,` __nanosleep`).
However, with the exception of `__nanosleep`, these functions DO exist on HIP (at least by now, see [here](https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/HIP/en/docs-7.2.4/reference/hip_runtime_api/modules/memory_management.html#_CPPv412hipHostAllocPPv6size_tj), and [here](https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/HIP/en/docs-7.2.4/reference/hip_runtime_api/modules/memory_management.html#_CPPv423hipHostGetDevicePointerPPvPvj)).
I have emulated `__nanosleep` via `__builtin_amdgcn_s_sleep`, which lowers to `S_SLEEP` and sleeps a wavefront for an approximate number of cycles (see [here](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna4-instruction-set-architecture)). This instruction appears to be available on all ISAs listed [here](https://gpuopen.com/amd-gpu-architecture-programming-documentation/), i.e., across RDNA, CDNA, Vega, back to GCN 3.
I have assumed a clock rate of about 2500 MHz (my RX 9070 clocks to ~3000 MHz, my RX 6800XT to ~2400 MHz, an MI 300A to 2100 MHz), which would mean the wavefront has to sleep for 250 cycles, or around 4 * 64 cycles to approximately match the 100 ns of `__nanosleep`. Even if it does not sleep for the exact same time, I think it should not impact correctness and merely result in busier waiting, or slightly longer sleep times.

On my test system (aforementioned RX 9070 and RX 6800XT), this PR provides a very noticeable performance uplift over the meta butterfly implementation:

```
./llama-bench -p 2048 -n 512 -d 4096 -b 1024 -ub 512 -t 3 -sm tensor -mg 1 -fa on -dev ROCm0/ROCm1 --load-mode none -m /models/gemma-4-31B-it-Q6_K.gguf
ggml_cuda_init: found 2 ROCm devices (Total VRAM: 32672 MiB):
  Device 0: AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT, gfx1030 (0x1030), VMM: no, Wave Size: 32, VRAM: 16368 MiB
  Device 1: AMD Radeon RX 9070, gfx1201 (0x1201), VMM: no, Wave Size: 32, VRAM: 16304 MiB
  ```
  
| model                          |       size |     params | backend    | ngl | threads | n_batch |   main_gpu |     sm |  fa | dev          |         lm |            test |                  t/s |                  t/s | uplift   |
| ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | --: | ------: | ------: | ---------: | -----: | --: | ------------ | ---------: | --------------: | -------------------: | -------------------: | -------: |
| gemma4 31B Q6_K                |  23.46 GiB |    30.70 B | ROCm       |  -1 |       3 |    1024 |          1 | tensor |   1 | ROCm0/ROCm1  |       none |  pp2048 @ d4096 |        384.15 ± 0.83 |        445.25 ± 0.10 | ~15.91 % |

items.body:
## Overview

One of llama.cpp's strength is the availability of a variety of quantizations which reduce the memory usage and allow running quantized big models on modest hardware.

Running a qwen3.8-flash-next, I was surprised to see high memory usage of 2 GB of compute buffers on each card, which is a lot. This PR cuts compute buffer usage by more than a third in two steps, one of which is very invasive. Further reductions are possible, reducing compute buffer sizes to ~800MB per card on my setup, halving the current utilization.
The two steps are:
- Providing fusions to elide the memory requirements, fusing trivial operations with follow-up kernels
- (Invasive): Providing a callback to enable removal of "deleted" nodes.

| Device | Master | Allocator branch | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SYCL0 | 1893.85 MiB | 1173.85 MiB | 720.00 MiB (38.02%) |
| SYCL1 | 1901.10 MiB | 1181.10 MiB | 720.00 MiB (37.87%) |
| SYCL2 | 1901.10 MiB | 1181.10 MiB | 720.00 MiB (37.87%) |
| Total | 5696.05 MiB | 3536.05 MiB | 2160.00 MiB (37.92%) |
| SYCL host | 415.87 MiB | 415.87 MiB | 0 MiB |


<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
One of the key offenders of high memory usage are OP_CAST nodes, which currently expand the full ubatch into a buffer.

This branch extends the SYCL with support for eliding fused intermediate tensors:

- F16 cast plus F32 add fusion
- QSA score generation, ReLU, and head reduction fusion
- QSA gather fusion
- QSA gather, mask add, and radix top-k fusion

## Additional information


The removal of the buffer has only limited performance impact, because the sizes of the copied structures at 720MB are not prohibitive for GPUs which handle multiple hundred GB/s of throughput, and these operations are saturating this bandwidth.

| Metric | Master median | Allocator fusion median | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| pp16384 | 298.327 tok/s | 305.876 tok/s | +2.53% |
| tg16384 | 15.391 tok/s | 15.555 tok/s | +1.07% |
| pp65535 | 246.356 tok/s | 255.423 tok/s | +3.68% |
| tg65535| 8.830 tok/s | 8.885 tok/s | +0.62% |

However, it saves 720MB of buffers to create more headroom.

I'm not sure how to go about this; the change is very invasive because it needs to interact with the memory allocator to really reduce the number of compute buffers.  This is therefore more a basis for discussion / inspiration, as there are some fundamental dirty parts:
- The graph allocation / de-allocation is aimed to be as non-intrusive as possible, but still creates a bit of a mess
- The Fusions are HUGE, consuming multiple nodes, which may lead to increased maintenance efforts


Still, I believe being able to ditch compute buffers and reduce the insane dead copying from reshapes and casts by integrating them into fusions would help the project overall, and allow users to use the gained memory for MTP or more parallel processing. What are your feelings on this ( @arthw )?
Due to the massive change, I'm not sure this will ever be pulled, so I'm keeping it as a draft.

### Name and Version b11010 (vendored in llama.rn 0.13.0-rc.4); test-gbnf-validator built from the same tag on macOS ### Operating systems Mac ### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected? libllama (core library) ### Command line ```shell test-gbnf-validator gemma4-required.gbnf input.txt ``` ### Problem description & steps to reproduce I was chasing why a `tool_choice: required` Gemma 4 extraction occasionally returns arguments the grammar should have made impossible. a `]` closing a list where the last dict was never closed: ``` …new_facts_learned:[{category:<|"|>background<|"|>,…},{category:<|"|>personality<|"|>,…},{category:<|"|>goals<|"|>,confidence:0.95,insight:<|"|>…<|"|>],user_trait_exhibited:… ``` The PEG parser (non-lenient final parse) correctly rejects it, so the completion comes back with no tool call. But the grammar sampler should never have let the `]` through. Running the exact GBNF the format builder produced (captured from `common_chat_params_init_gemma4` for a one-tool `required` call) through `test-gbnf-validator` shows why. ### Repro with `test-gbnf-validator` (b11010) Grammar: the Gemma 4 tool grammar for one tool, `tool_choice: required`, `parallel_tool_calls: false`. Its top is ``` root ::= start message* scan-to-toolcall tool-call message ::= (thought | ) content content ::= until-165 # until one of <|channel> / / <|tool_call> scan-to-toolcall ::= until-162 # until <|tool_call> tool-call ::= ("<|tool_call>call:" (tool-extract-soul-data) "") ``` and every `until-N` rule is compiled as a chain in which each partial-delimiter state has an empty alternative: ``` until-165 ::= | [<] until-165-01 | [^<] until-165 until-165-01 ::= | [<] until-165-01 | [|] until-165-02 | [c] until-165-11 | [^] until-165 # after "<|tool_call": ">" excluded ``` Results (`valid` = accepted as complete; `incomplete` = accepted as a prefix, "Unexpected end of input"; `INVALID` = rejected): | input | result | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------- | | `<\|tool_call>call:extract_soul_data{a:<\|"\|>x<\|"\|>}` | valid | | `<\|tool_call>call:extract_soul_data{a:<\|"\|>x<\|"\|>]}` | incomplete | | `<\|tool_call>call:extract_soul_data{a:<\|"\|>x<\|"\|>ZZZ` | incomplete | | `<\|tool_call>call:extract_soul_data{a:<\|"\|>x<\|"\|>}ZZZ` | incomplete | | `anything ] } { <\|tool_call>call:nope{` + the valid call | **valid** | | the valid call twice | **valid** | The second, third and fourth rows should be `INVALID` at the first bad byte; instead every byte is accepted. The last two rows say why: the grammar has a live parse in which `content` consumes `<|tool_call` (stopping before the `>` it may not take), and `scan-to-toolcall`, a fresh `until`, then consumes `>call:…` and everything after it as plain scan text, waiting for a _later_ `<|tool_call>`. The delimiter is split across two adjacent `until` rules. Because llama.cpp's grammar sampler constrains the next token by the union of all live stacks, that stack alone makes any byte legal for the rest of the generation, the dict/array/string rules only ever bite if the model happens to emit a second `<|tool_call>`. So for this format, `tool_choice: required` produces a grammar that is effectively unconstrained once the call begins. On device (Gemma 4 E2B, Q4 QAT) we see the consequence as roughly one extraction in 15–25 with a structurally impossible token in it (`]` for `}`, an unclosed string, a doubled key), all rejected by the PEG parse, all with the raw text accepted as a prefix by the grammar. ### Where I think the fix goes The `until` compilation needs its partial-delimiter states to be non-final, the empty alternative should exist only at `until-N` itself (before any delimiter byte has been consumed), not at `until-N-01…28`. Equivalently: an `until(d)` must not be able to end with a proper prefix of `d` consumed. With that, `content` cannot stop after `<|tool_call` and the only way past a `<|tool_call>` is the `tool-call` rule. I'm happy to test a patch against the same inputs; the validator makes it a five-second check.
The full grammar used above (recorded from a one-tool required call, b11010) ``` content ::= until-165 gemma4-array ::= "[" space ("]" | gemma4-value ("," space gemma4-value)* space "]") gemma4-bool ::= json-bool gemma4-dict ::= "{" space ("}" | gemma4-dict-kv ("," space gemma4-dict-kv)* space "}") gemma4-dict-key ::= gemma4-dict-key-name ":" gemma4-dict-key-name ::= [^:}]+ gemma4-dict-kv ::= gemma4-dict-key space gemma4-value gemma4-null ::= json-null gemma4-number ::= json-number gemma4-string ::= "<|\"|>" gemma4-string-content "<|\"|>" gemma4-string-content ::= until-28 gemma4-value ::= gemma4-string | gemma4-dict | gemma4-array | gemma4-number | gemma4-bool | gemma4-null json-bool ::= "true" | "false" json-null ::= "null" json-number ::= "-"? ("0" | [1-9] [0-9]*) ("." [0-9]+)? (("e" | "E") [+-]? [0-9]+)? message ::= (thought | ) content root ::= start message* scan-to-toolcall tool-call scan-to-toolcall ::= until-162 space ::= | " " | "\n"{1,2} [ \t]{0,20} start ::= "<|turn>model\n"? thought ::= "<|channel>thought" space until-7 "" tool-call ::= ("<|tool_call>call:" (tool-extract-soul-data) "") tool-extract-soul-data ::= ("extract_soul_data") gemma4-dict until-162 ::= | [<] until-162-01 | [^<] until-162 until-162-01 ::= | [<] until-162-01 | [|] until-162-02 | [^<|] until-162 until-162-02 ::= | [<] until-162-01 | [t] until-162-03 | [^

items.body:
## Summary

On a Google Pixel 11 Pro (Imagination PowerVR C-Series CXTP-48-1536 MC1, `VK_DRIVER_ID_IMAGINATION_PROPRIETARY`, Vulkan 1.4.317, `subgroupSize=128`, `maxComputeWorkGroupInvocations=1024`, `maxComputeSharedMemorySize=32768`), the Vulkan backend crashes the GPU firmware during prompt processing.

Every compute pipeline compiles. The first 128-token batch returns from `llama_decode`. About 9 seconds after the context is created, Android logs a PowerVR subsystem restart, the compositor wedges, and the device usually reboots. No tokens are produced.

The same app and models work on a Pixel 8 Pro (ARM Mali/Immortalis).

I don't expect a fix in llama.cpp; the fault is almost certainly in Imagination's driver. This is filed so the next person who tries Vulkan on a Tensor G6 finds it, and in case the subgroup-128 detail suggests a workaround to someone who knows the backend.

## Android's GPU crash record

`adb shell dumpsys dropbox --print | grep -A12 SubsystemRestart` gives a per-crash reason. Across builds:

| llama.cpp | flash attn | submissions | OS build | crash reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| b10621 | on | default | 2026-07 | `GUILTY_OVERRUNING` |
| b10731 | on | default | 2026-07 | `[0]:[addr=0x8056288700]:[FW_PAGEFAULT]` |
| b10731 | off | default | 2026-07 | `[0]:[addr=0x805730fd80]:[FW_PAGEFAULT]` |
| b10731 | on | serialised | 2026-07 and 2026-09 | `GUILTY_OVERRUNING` |
| b10731 | on | default | 2026-09 | `[0]:[addr=0x8047852d80]:[FW_PAGEFAULT]` |

`GUILTY_OVERRUNING` reads as a job that never terminated and hit the GPU watchdog. `FW_PAGEFAULT` reads as an MMU fault on an unmapped GPU address. The fault address is stable within a process (allocations move between runs), so the access is deterministic rather than a race.

`b10621 -> b10731` changed the failure class but fixed nothing.

## Ruled out, all measured on the device

- llama.cpp version: b10621 and b10731 (the latter includes #27726's warptile clamp for subgroup > 64).
- Flash attention: `LLAMA_FLASH_ATTN_TYPE_DISABLED` for this vendor. No change.
- Submission structure: `GGML_VK_SERIALIZE_SUBMISSIONS=1`. No change except the crash class. Since every submit then waits for completion, this also shows that the first 128-token chunk finishes on the GPU and a later one faults. It is not a cross-submission race.
- Memory: reproduced on a fresh boot with 14 GB available and zero swap.
- Model architecture: a hybrid model (Qwen 3.5 2B, gated delta net + SSM) and a plain transformer (Gemma 4 E2B) fail identically.
- Quantisation: `Q4_0` crashes exactly like `Q4_K_M` and `UD-Q4_K_XL`. This matters because a user on Imagination's own forum found that on the Pixel 10's D-series DXT-48-1536, k-quant compute shaders return wrong results while `Q4_0`, `Q5_0`, `Q8_0`, `F16` and `F32` are correct (https://forums.imgtec.com/t/powervr-dxt-48-1536-incorrect-results-from-k-quant-vulkan-compute-shaders-in-llama-cpp/4291). That is a different bug. The D-series computes wrong answers; the C-series crashes its firmware.
- Driver: the September 2026 Pixel OTA (`CD1A.260905.001.A1`, new vendor image) behaves identically. The driver still reports 1.4.317.

## Configuration

Vulkan only, all layers offloaded, `n_batch=128`, `n_ctx=7168-7424`, prompt of about 2,850 to 3,000 tokens, `type_k` and `type_v` left at F16.

## Related

- #8437: Vulkan on an Imagination GPU (RISC-V, warp size 1). Different symptom, stale.
- #25734: Adreno `subgroupSize=128`, wrong matmul results, fixed by #27726.
- pytorch/executorch#17299: PowerVR D-series on the Pixel 10 Pro produced all-zero outputs from ExecuTorch's Vulkan backend, root-caused to a command-sequencing defect where dispatches after the first in a command buffer lost their writes.

## Repro

So far only reproduced from an app embedding libllama, not from `llama-bench`. I can run a standalone repro on the device if someone suggests the exact invocation. Each attempt costs a reboot.

## Overview

I have been discussing with @am17an regarding the high difference in prompt processing rate for Gemma 4 model on llama.cpp and mlx-lm. On debugging I found that the TODO in the  `src/models/gemma4.cpp` by @ngxson states that the prompt processing can be improved by stripping the unused tokens after the last KV layer.

This PR skips the computations that are happening after the calculation of attention for the tokens that do not require to calculate the logits. The improvement in the prompt processing rate is mentioned below:

The commit: 3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d  has the following prompt processing rate:
| model                          |       size |     params | backend    | threads |            test |                  t/s |
| ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: |
| gemma4 E2B BF16                |   8.66 GiB |     4.65 B | MTL,BLAS   |       4 |          pp2048 |        641.61 ± 5.41 |
| gemma4 E2B BF16                |   8.66 GiB |     4.65 B | MTL,BLAS   |       4 |           tg128 |         19.31 ± 0.18 |


Current PR's prompt processing rate:

| model                          |       size |     params | backend    | threads |            test |                  t/s |
| ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: |
| gemma4 E2B BF16                |   8.66 GiB |     4.65 B | MTL,BLAS   |       4 |          pp2048 |       1126.27 ± 1.38 |
| gemma4 E2B BF16                |   8.66 GiB |     4.65 B | MTL,BLAS   |       4 |           tg128 |         19.61 ± 0.50 |


I have tested this using the following command:
```
./llama-bench -m ../models/gguf/gemma-4-E2B-it-BF16.gguf \
    -p 2048 \
    -n 128 \
    -r 5
```



## Additional information
I am testing this on the MacBook Air M3, 16GB RAM.
I have used the following model: [ggml-org/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF/blob/main/gemma-4-E2B-it-BF16.gguf)

There are still a few things that I want to improve in this PR:

- Currently all the tokens in the microbatch should not require to calculate logits.
Need to make changes here by optimizing for the microbatches which contains both the tokens: ones which require logits and other which do not.
- There are a few more operations that are performed after the KV cache is calculated, need to safely optimize them.
I tried putting the same condition after the layers loop in the graph construction, however it throws error. Need to debug that.


## Requirements

# Title

Eval bug: draft-mtp (self-speculative) models crash on Vulkan/RADV after Linux kernel bump 7.1.3 → 7.1.7 — same class as #24492, different GPU/model

# Body

### Related issue
This looks like the same crash class as #24492 ("Gemma 4 31B MTP (draft-mtp) crashes on Vulkan backend, pre-allocated tensor cannot run operation NONE"), reproduced here on different hardware (RADV GFX1201 instead of RX 7900 XTX) and a different model family (Qwen3.8-27B instead of Gemma 4 31B). Unlike that report, I have a clean bisection: the exact same llama.cpp binary and Mesa version work or crash depending solely on which Linux kernel is booted, which may help narrow down whether this is a Vulkan/amdgpu KMD interaction rather than a pure userspace bug.

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-cli --version
WARNING: radv is not a conformant Vulkan implementation, testing use only.
version: 0.1.2-dev (build 10517, commit dc72703fc)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Built from source at that commit; binary/libs timestamped 2026-08-19.

### Operating systems

Linux (Debian 13 "trixie" + trixie-backports)

### GGML backends

Vulkan (RADV)

### Hardware

- GPU: AMD Radeon R9700, reported by RADV as `AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV GFX1201)`
- `amdgpu` reports `HMM registered 32624MB device memory`
- Vulkan driver: `driverID=DRIVER_ID_MESA_RADV`, `driverInfo=Mesa 26.1.2-1~bpo13+1`, `apiVersion=1.4.348` (from `vulkaninfo --summary`)
- Mesa packages: `mesa-vulkan-drivers` / `mesa-libgallium` `26.1.2-1~bpo13+1` (held constant across the whole test below — only the kernel changed)

### Models

Custom preset `qwen3.8-27b`, self-speculative multi-token-prediction (no separate draft-model file):

```
/usr/local/bin/llama-server \
  --api-key-file /opt/llama/api-key.txt \
  --model /opt/llama/models/qwen3.8-27b.gguf \
  --mmproj /opt/llama/models/qwen3.8-27b-mmproj.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-mtp \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --n-gpu-layers 999 \
  --parallel 1 \
  --batch-size 512 --ubatch-size 512 \
  --context-shift --jinja --webui-mcp-proxy
```

Other presets on the same box that use an *external* draft-model `.gguf` file (e.g. `gemma4-e2b`, which loads a separate `gemma4-e2b-mtp.gguf`) do **not** crash under the same conditions — only presets doing shared-layer self-speculation without a separate draft file are affected (`qwen3.8-27b`, `qwen3.8-27b-low`, `qwen3.8-27b-medium`, `qwen3.6-35b`, `thinkingcap-qwen3.6-27b`, `fable-fusion-27b`, `gemma4-31b`).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

This model/preset was benchmarked as working the day before the crash first appeared — on this exact llama.cpp commit and this exact Mesa version — with recorded numbers up to 58.75 tok/s at spec depth n=4 (kept as a comment in our local config for reference). Nothing about the llama.cpp build, Mesa version, or model files changed between the working and broken state. The only thing that changed was a Debian backports kernel upgrade + reboot:

| Boot | Kernel | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-19, 14:57–2026-08-20 07:24 | `7.1.3+deb13-amd64` (`linux-image-amd64 7.1.3-1~bpo13+1`) | Works — this is the boot the benchmark numbers above came from |
| 2026-08-20, 07:28–14:35 | `7.1.3+deb13-amd64` (same) | Works |
| 2026-08-20, 14:35–15:18 | `7.1.7+deb13-amd64` (`linux-image-amd64 7.1.7-1~bpo13+1`, first boot after `apt` upgraded and rebooted) | **Crashes**, 100% reproducible on every load attempt |
| 2026-08-20, 15:20– (later) | `7.1.7+deb13-amd64` (same, fresh reboot) | **Crashes**, reproduced again |
| After manually pinning GRUB back to `7.1.3+deb13-amd64` and rebooting | `7.1.3+deb13-amd64` | Works again — same binary, same Mesa, same model files, only the kernel changed back |

Steps to reproduce on affected kernel:
1. Boot `7.1.7+deb13-amd64` (Debian backports) with `mesa-vulkan-drivers` `26.1.2-1~bpo13+1` and an AMD RDNA4/GFX1201 GPU (R9700).
2. Start `llama-server` with the `qwen3.8-27b` config above (`--spec-type draft-mtp`, `--cache-type-k/v q8_0`, `--flash-attn on`, no separate `--model-draft` file).
3. Send any completion request that forces the model to load.
4. Server child process aborts immediately during context construction, before any tokens are generated.

Reverting only the kernel (staying on the same llama.cpp build, same Mesa) makes it work again, which points at an amdgpu KMD ↔ RADV interaction rather than a pure Mesa or llama.cpp-side regression — though given #24492 is already open against different hardware without any kernel mentioned, it's also possible this is a latent/racy bug in the Vulkan backend's cross-context KV-cache-sharing scheduling (`ggml_backend_sched_backend_id_from_cur` / `resolve_fused_ops`) that the kernel change merely made more likely to trigger, rather than something the kernel changed correctness-wise on its own.

### First Bad commit

Not a llama.cpp commit — llama.cpp build and Mesa version were held constant throughout. The regression tracks the Debian backports kernel package bump `linux-image-amd64` `7.1.3-1~bpo13+1` → `7.1.7-1~bpo13+1` (upstream Linux 7.1.3 → 7.1.7 stable point releases). I don't have a narrower bisection within that kernel range.

### Relevant log output

Short-form message (seen on the previous boot, layer index varies by run):
```
[52709] /home/subsolar/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:930: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l64) in a buffer (Vulkan0) that cannot run the operation (NONE)
```

Full backtrace (from `llama-server`'s built-in crash handler, current boot on 7.1.7, `qwen3.8-27b`):
```
[33317] [New LWP 2214]
[33317] [New LWP 2213]
[33317] [New LWP 2212]
[33317] [Thread debugging using libthread_db enabled]
[33317] Using host libthread_db library "/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libthread_db.so.1".
[33317] 0x00007ff434aa69ee in ?? () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6
[33317] #0  0x00007ff434aa69ee in ?? () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6
[33317] #1  0x00007ff434a9b668 in ?? () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc

### Name and Version

b11010 (vendored in llama.rn 0.13.0-rc.4); first seen on b10256. llama-kv-cache-iswa.cpp seq_pos_max and the derivation in llama-batch.cpp are unchanged between them.

### Operating systems

Mac

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library)

### Command line

```shell

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

This is the llama.cpp end of a problem I tracked down in a downstream wrapper (llama.rn, issue linked below). I think the wrapper is doing something llama.cpp tells it not to (`llama_batch_get_one` after a partial `seq_rm`), so I'm mainly asking whether `seq_pos_max` for iSWA is returning what you intend, because the consequence is a silent KV leak rather than an error.

### What happens

`llama-kv-cache-iswa.cpp`:

```cpp
llama_pos llama_kv_cache_iswa::seq_pos_min(llama_seq_id seq_id) const {
    // the base cache is a superset of the SWA cache, so we can just check the SWA cache
    return kv_swa->seq_pos_min(seq_id);
}

llama_pos llama_kv_cache_iswa::seq_pos_max(llama_seq_id seq_id) const {
    return kv_swa->seq_pos_max(seq_id);
}
```

The superset argument holds for `seq_pos_min` in the normal flow, but after `seq_rm(seq, p0, -1)` with `p0` below the sliding window the two caches disagree: the base cache still holds positions 0…p0−1, the sliding cache holds nothing for that sequence (its cells for those positions were purged as the sequence grew), and `seq_pos_max` returns −1 while the base cache's answer would be p0−1.

A caller that then decodes a batch without positions gets, in `llama_batch_allocr::init`:

```cpp
p0[s] = memory->seq_pos_max(s) + 1;   // = 0
```

so the new tokens are written at positions 0, 1, 2, … on top of the base cache's existing cells 0…p0−1. No error: the consecutive-positions check is skipped when `seq_pos_max` is −1. Each such turn adds `min(n_new, p0)` duplicate base cells that sit below anything a later `seq_rm(seq, n_past, -1)` reaches. They accumulate until `find_slot` fails ("failed to find a memory slot"), which then persists until a full clear. The turn is also computed at the wrong positions.

Measured on Gemma 4 E2B (12 sliding + 3 global KV layers, `n_swa` 512, sliding cache 1,024 cells, base 6,144): with `saveSession`'s file size as the cell count (it writes every non-empty cell), a sequence of deep-divergence turns went +277 → +699 → +1,099 → +1,542 → +1,954 → +2,808 → +3,559 cells above the live sequence, then both caches full, then the failure.

### Why I'm raising it here rather than only downstream

`llama.h` already says of `llama_batch_get_one`: "this is a helper function to facilitate transition to the new batch API — avoid using it", and llama-server never relies on derived positions (it always uses `common_batch_add` with explicit positions and has its own `pos_min` guard against reusing a prefix past the window, `server-context.cpp`, referencing #13194). So the wrapper is at fault for using the helper, and I've fixed it there with explicit positions plus a port of the server's guard.

But two things seem worth a look on this side:

1. **`seq_pos_max` for iSWA.** If the base cache is the superset, `kv_base->seq_pos_max(seq_id)` is the true maximum of the sequence and would give the derived-positions path the right answer (p0) in this situation. Is answering from the sliding cache deliberate — e.g. so `seq_pos_max` agrees with `seq_pos_min` about what the sliding layers can actually attend to?
2. **No error on the collision.** `llama_batch_allocr::init` validates consecutive positions only when `seq_pos_max ≥ 0`. When the derived start is 0 but the base cache already holds cells at those positions, a check against `kv_base` (or against any cache in the iSWA pair) would turn a silent leak into a decode error, which is much easier to find. The `probeStateCache`-style TODO in the wrapper existed for months without anyone connecting it to this.

### Version

b11010 (vendored in llama.rn 0.13.0-rc.4); first seen on b10256. `llama-kv-cache-iswa.cpp` `seq_pos_max` and the derivation in `llama-batch.cpp` are unchanged between them.

### Minimal reproduction

Any iSWA model, default `swa_full = false`, one sequence, plain `llama_decode` with `llama_batch_get_one`:

1. Decode ~1,500 tokens (prompt or prompt + generation).
2. `llama_memory_seq_rm(mem, 0, 400, -1)`.
3. `llama_memory_seq_pos_max(mem, 0)` → −1 (expected 399 from the base cache's point of view).
4. Decode 500 more tokens with `llama_batch_get_one` → no error; `llama_state_save_file` grows by ~400 base cells more than the token count explains.
5. Repeat 2–4 with fresh tokens until `find_slot` fails.

Downstream issue with the wrapper-side fix and before/after numbers: mybigday/llama.rn#396.

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

<!-- Copy-pasted short logs go into the "console" area here -->

```console
decode: failed to find a memory slot for batch of size 402
decode: failed to find a memory slot for batch of size 512
```
</details>
