### Name and Version

binaries where I confirmed the affected
- llama-b9037-bin-win-cuda-13.1-x64.zip  
- llama-b9033-bin-win-cuda-13.1-x64.zip  
- llama-b9031-bin-win-cuda-13.1-x64.zip  

### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server.exe --model "gemma-4-31B-it-Q5_K_M.gguf" -c 128000 -ngl 99 -fa on -t 8 -b 512 -ub 256 --jinja -ctk q8_0 -ctv q4_0 -np 1 --fit off -ts 0.6,0.43 -fitt 256 -fitc 1024 -sm layer -mg 0 --no-mmap --cache-ram 2048 -ctxcp 2 --no-mmproj-offload --reasoning on --host 0.0.0.0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Description:
Since version b9031, inference is performed on the CPU even though the layers appear to be offloaded to the GPU and VRAM is consumed. 
As far as I have been able to ascertain, this issue has been confirmed on b9031, b9033 and b9037.
The b9030 operates without any problems.

Key Observations:
1.Contradictory GPU Detection: The log starts with warning: no usable GPU found, --gpu-layers option will be ignored. However, it later detects CUDA devices and reports offloading layers to them.
2.Inference on CPU: Despite the offload reports, actual inference is executed on the CPU.
3.Not Multi-GPU Specific: I have tested with set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 to force a single GPU setup, but the symptoms remain exactly the same.

## Overview

#21863 added support for /v1/audio/transcriptions API with the assumption that models expect `[{"role":"user","content":"Transcribe audio to text<__media__>"}]` format.

This doesn't hold, e.g., for [LiquidAI/LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B-GGUF).

In PR, I try to relax this assumption by defining the model-specific strategy and using it in the server.

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

With this change, transcription works correctly for [LiquidAI/LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B-GGUF) and adds a mechanism for defining a strategy for future models.

To test, start server with
```
llama-server -hf LiquidAI/LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B-GGUF
```

Use the code below to inference
```python
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.9"
# dependencies = [
#     "openai",
# ]
# ///
import io
import urllib.request

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key="your-api-key", base_url="http://localhost:8080/v1")

url = "https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/raw/master/samples/jfk.wav"
audio_file = io.BytesIO(urllib.request.urlopen(url).read())
audio_file.name = "jfk.wav"
streaming = True

if streaming:
    transcription = client.audio.transcriptions.create(
        model="whisper-1",
        file=audio_file,
        stream=True
    )

    for chunk in transcription:
        try:
            print(chunk.delta, end="", flush=True)
        except Exception as e:
            print("\n", chunk)

else:
    transcription = client.audio.transcriptions.create(
        model="whisper-1",
        file=audio_file
    )
    print(transcription.text)

```

items.title: mtmd: correct get_n_pos / get_decoder_pos

items.body:
## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #27174.

This PR enables support for `echo=true` combined with `logprobs=N` in the `/v1/completions` endpoint without triggering memory assertions or KV cache errors. Previously, the server ignored the `echo` setting for logprobs, returning an empty list for prompt tokens and breaking downstream evaluation frameworks like `lm-eval`.

## Additional information

### Motivation
Evaluation frameworks like `lm-eval` grade a model by feeding it a specific correct answer as a prompt and adding up the logprobs for those prompt tokens to calculate a total score[cite: 1]. Because prompt scores were missing, `lm-eval` received blanks and assumed the model was randomly guessing[cite: 1]. Furthermore, naive attempts to fix this caused a `GGML_ASSERT(n_outputs_max <= cparams.n_outputs_max)` hard abort on large prompts due to buffer overflow.

### Changes
* **Dynamic Capacity Query**: Expose `llama_n_outputs_max` in the core API (`include/llama.h` and `src/llama-context.cpp`) to safely query runtime output capacity.
* **Main Loop Chunking**: Integrate chunked prompt logprob extraction directly into the main prompt processing loop in `tools/server/server-context.cpp`.
* **Memory and Cache Safety**: Bound prompt token ingestion per iteration by `llama_n_outputs_max(ctx_tgt)` when `need_prompt_logits()` is true. This prevents output buffer overflow (fixing the hard abort) and ensures the KV cache timeline advances consecutively (fixing sequence inconsistency errors).
* **Zero VRAM Bloat**: Extract logprobs within existing memory limits without requiring extra startup VRAM allocation.
* **OAI JSON Formatting**: Correctly populate `token_logprobs` and `top_logprobs` for the echoed prompt tokens, ensuring the first prompt token explicitly returns `null`.

## Requirements

- [x] I have read and agree with the contributing guidelines (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - I used AI to understand the code structure and data flow but wrote and fully understand the submitted logic myself.

**Co-author:** @simongonzalezdc

items.body:
This is a draft that we will keep iterating on: the description and commit messages will be revised before marking ready for review.

Adds two Metal matmul kernels for small batches (8 < `ne11` <= 32) — the speculative-decoding verify/draft regime:

- `kernel_mul_mm_s`: `mul_mm` with 32x16 tiles instead of 64x32. The stock tile pads N to 32 and launches `ne01/64` threadgroups, which under-fills the GPU at these sizes (on M3/M4, `pp16 == pp32` in wall time).
- split-K variant (4 slices) for shapes with few row tiles. Partials are written to scratch at the tail of the dst allocation (same pattern as `mul_mat_id`) and summed by a fixed-order reduce, so results are deterministic.

Kernel selection is unchanged by default: mv-ext keeps `ne11` 2..8, the mm branch keeps its stock break-even and uses the new tiles for 8 < `ne11` <= 32. `ne11` > 32 and tensor-API devices (M5+) use the stock path. `GGML_METAL_MM_SKINNY_MAX=0` restores stock behavior; `GGML_METAL_MM_SPLITK`, `GGML_METAL_MM_MIN`, `GGML_METAL_MV_EXT_MAX/_R1` are available for tuning.

Companion to #27383 — DSpark verify/draft batches run at `ne11` ~ 8..16. The kernels themselves are model-independent.

Numbers so far (M4 Max, 36 GB): `llama-bench -p 10` on LFM2.5-2.6B F16 goes 334 -> 460 t/s; end-to-end speculative decoding on a 150-prompt suite at temp 0 goes 1.84x -> 2.27x mean speedup, accept length unchanged. tg and large-batch pp are unaffected. Split-K changes f16 summation order, so occasional greedy ties differ from the stock kernel; outputs are bit-reproducible run to run.

End-to-end speculative decoding, this branch + #27383 merged (LFM2.5-2.6B F16 target + block-9 DSpark drafter, M4 Max, temp 0, speedup vs the same server without spec flags; accept length identical between configs):

| dataset | accept | stock | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| math500 (n=20) | 4.45 | 1.79x | 2.26x |
| humaneval (n=20) | 5.24 | 2.04x | 2.62x |
| mtbench (n=10) | 3.33 | 1.28x | 1.62x |

With the block-7 drafters linked from #27383 the verify batch is 8 tokens (`ne11` = 8, outside the changed range) and speedups are unchanged (1.85x vs 1.87x mean) — block-9 LFM2.5 drafter GGUFs are being published.

`test-backend-ops test -o MUL_MAT -b Metal` passes with the new paths enabled and disabled.

llama-bench on this branch, M4 Max 36GB (`-p 8,10,16,32 -n 16 -b 32 -ub 32 -fa 1 -r 3`), t/s stock (`GGML_METAL_MM_SKINNY_MAX=0`) → this PR:

| model | pp8 | pp10 | pp16 | pp32 | tg16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| LFM2.5-2.6B-F16 | 291 → 292 | 353 → 478 | 563 → 804 | 1138 → 1316 | 64 → 64 |
| LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-F16 | 662 → 658 | 794 → 1107 | 1258 → 1768 | 2563 → 2946 | 142 → 142 |
| Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-F16 | 201 → 201 | 247 → 307 | 386 → 507 | 790 → 858 | 43 → 43 |
| Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-Q4_0 | 204 → 205 | 268 → 454 | 419 → 718 | 871 → 942 | 117 → 115 |

Kernels by @fernando-neto-ai, developed on Liquid AI's fork. This PR keeps the stock crossover thresholds; the fork's retuned (M3-measured) values were slightly slower on M4.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. The kernels were developed with Claude on Liquid AI's fork (AI-drafted, human-benchmarked and reviewed there and on this branch); the upstream adaptation (cherry-pick + defaults commit) was likewise AI-assisted, and this PR description was co-written with Claude.

## Bug Report: LFM2.5-8B-A1B chat-template path degenerates at ~44K context (repeated "P"), raw path is fine

**Environment**: llama.cpp `b0539c4` (0.2.0-dev), CUDA 13.3, RTX 4060 Laptop 8GB, `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-8B-A1B-GGUF` Q4_K_M (sha256 `4923ec14…`)

### Symptom
With a ~44K-token prompt through any **chat-template path**, generation degenerates into repeated `P` tokens (with a stray `</think>`), regardless of `-rea on/off`, `-ub` 256/1024, `-c` size, or KV cache quant (f16 / q8_0):

- `llama-cli -st` (chat template): outputs `P\n</think>\nP\nP\nP…`
- `llama-server /v1/chat/completions`: same `P\n</think>\nP…`
- Same content through **raw `/completion`** (plain prompt, or manually templated prompt incl. BOS): **correct output** (retrieves hidden passkey).

### Observations
- First-token logprobs are **finite and sane** (`P:-0.52`, `PASS:-1.10`, `<think>:-3.01`) — model genuinely prefers `P`; not a NaN/overflow issue.
- Template-rendered prompt is 44,008 tokens vs 44,024 for the manual equivalent (16-token difference) — rendering differs from hand-built template.
- `LFM2.5-2.6B` (same family, dense) works fine on the identical chat path at the same length.
- 4K/32K/60K (raw) all fine; breakage appears between ~43K and 44K on chat path only.
- Log line seen: `chat format: peg-native`, `reasoning budget: tokens=-1, generation_prompt='<|im_start|>assistant\n'`.

### Repro
```bash
# 1) generate a ~44K-token NIAH doc (repeated filler, secret in middle)
# 2) chat path (broken):
llama-cli -m LFM2.5-8B-A1B-Q4_K_M.gguf -f niah_44k.txt -n 64 --temp 0 -ngl 99 -fa on -ub 1024 -b 1024 -st -c 50000 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0
# 3) raw path (works):
#    POST /completion {"prompt": "<|startoftext|><|im_start|>system\n...<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\n<doc><|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n", "n_predict": 64, "temperature": 0}
```

Suspect: template autoparser rendering for LFM2.5 diverges from the native template at long user-content lengths (16-token delta), steering the model into a degenerate continuation. Happy to provide the exact doc/prompts or run instrumented builds.

## Summary

The official LiquidAI LFM2.5-2.6B DSpark GGUF sidecar loads successfully, but llama-server crashes on the first generation request with a native graph assertion on macOS Apple Silicon.

## Environment

- OS: macOS on Apple Silicon
- llama.cpp: Homebrew build 10470
- Target: LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B-GGUF, LFM2.5-2.6B-Q4_K_M.gguf
- Draft sidecar: official LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B-DSpark-GGUF, LFM2.5-2.6B-DSpark-F16.gguf
- Official sidecar model card: https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B-DSpark-GGUF

## Reproduction

Start:

```bash
llama-server \
  -m LFM2.5-2.6B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  -md LFM2.5-2.6B-DSpark-F16.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-dspark \
  --spec-draft-n-max 9 \
  --spec-draft-n-min 0 \
  -ngl 99 \
  --jinja \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8083 \
  -c 4096
```

The server reports that the model loaded and DSpark was initialized:

```text
adding speculative implementation 'draft-dspark'
- n_max=9, n_min=0, p_min=0.00
- block_size=9, mask_token_id=125017, n_extract=5, sample_from_anchor=true
model loaded
listening on http://127.0.0.1:8083
```

Send:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8083/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"LFM2.5-2.6B-Q4_K_M","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello."}],"max_tokens":16,"temperature":0}'
```

Observed result: the client receives an empty reply and the server exits.

Relevant crash:

```text
src/llama-graph.cpp:1352: GGML_ASSERT(t_layer_inp[il] != nullptr && "layer input tensor is null") failed
```

The same crash occurs with a 32768-token context and with flash attention disabled. The non-DSpark router using the same target GGUF continues to work normally.

## Expected behavior

The request should complete successfully with DSpark speculative decoding, or llama-server should return a clear compatibility error instead of aborting via a native assertion.

### Name and Version

version: 0.1.2-dev (build 10540, commit 07822bddf)
built with GNU 16.1.1 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395)

### Models

Ling-3.0-flash-Q5_K_M from https://huggingface.co/bloomer010/Ling-3.0-flash-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

In a multi-turn tool using chat, the model sometimes emits `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` from inside its reasoning channel and stops without ever closing `</think>`. The whole turn is then swallowed into reasoning_content.

Root cause
Bailing V3 has no specialized parser in common/chat.cpp, so it falls through to the generic autoparser, which sets a single reasoning terminator (`thinking_end_tags = {"</think>"}`) with no <tool_call> fallback. When the model opens a tool call before closing `</think>`, nothing terminates reasoning and the output is mis-routed.

Behaviour like this is already handled for some other models (these thinking+tool models add tool call openers as reasoning terminators).

For example:
Qwen3-Coder: `thinking_end_tags = {"</think>", "<tool_call>"}`
DeepSeek V3.2: `thinking_end_tags = {THINK_END, FC_START}`
Kimi K2 (common_chat_params_init_kimi_k2) handles this exact behavior, with the maintainer comment: "this model is CRAZY … it can call tools at the end of reasoning without closing reasoning", and adds `<|tool_calls_section_begin|> / <|tool_call_begin|>` as terminators.
Bailing V3's Kimi-K2-like tendency to call tools mid-reasoning isn't covered by the generic autoparser.

Suggested fix
Add <tool_call> to Bailing V3's reasoning terminators (similar to Kimi K2/Qwen3-Coder fixes)

Reproduction code I used to test this exact behaviour which produces a high fail rate with Ling 3.0 flash:
https://gist.github.com/chielteuben/54efbb6b1a75eb7310246f34c54e3465

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

Easily reproduceable using the gist I added.
Note for this response: no tool calls, no content.

## Overview

Adds support for [Ling-3.0-flash-VL](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-VL), the vision-language variant of Ling 3.0 Flash (124B total / 5.1B active, hybrid KDA + gated MLA, 512-expert MoE). The text backbone is identical to `bailingmoe3`; the release adds a 27-block vision tower (qwen3_moe_vit family), a norm-only 2x2 merger, a two-layer projector, and uses M-RoPE with sections [8, 12, 12] shared between text and vision positions.

## Additional information

- `test-llama-archs --arch bailingmoe3` passes (MoE fixture round-trip).
- Converted the full model to BF16 GGUF (917 tensors, 248.9 GB) and mmproj (334 tensors) from the released safetensors.
- End-to-end image + video inference on llama-server successful. 

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- AI usage disclosure: Yes, I used AI to help write and check the code.  I personally, thoroughly reviewed the CONTRIBUTING.md file.

items.body:
## Overview

This release focuses on backend performance and correctness, broader model coverage, and more robust server/router operation. It adds HRM-Text (DFM Mimir 1B) support, MiMo-V2.6 and HunyuanOCR conversion support, ggml 0.25.0 backend improvements, multi-address HTTP binding, image outputs from function calls, and several chat parser/UI fixes.

### Highlights

- Accelerate CUDA `conv2d` with implicit GEMM ([#29135](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29135))
- Add Metal MoE and SSM_CONV fusion optimizations ([#28948](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28948))
- Allow the server to bind to multiple addresses ([#28690](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28690))

### API changes

- Add `llama_adapter_lora_init_from_file_ptr()` for loading LoRA from an open FILE ([#28993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28993))
- Document `llama_model_load_from_file_ptr()` as reading from the current position and requiring aligned mmap ([#28993](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28993))
- Add `LLAMA_VOCAB_TYPE_TEST` dummy tokenizer ([#29084](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29084))
- Add `input_image` support to server function-call outputs ([#22575](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/22575))
- Allow `--host` to accept comma-separated TCP addresses and UNIX sockets ([#28690](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28690))

### New models

- Add HRM-Text / DFM Mimir 1B support ([#27625](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27625))
- Add MiMo-V2.6 conversion support ([#29257](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29257))
- Add DFlash support for HunyuanOCR ([#28890](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28890))
- Extend Nemotron MTP and Nemotron-H model handling ([#29018](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29018), [#28989](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28989))
- Add Qwen4Exp hyper-connection ops and sparse flash attention ([#28901](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28901), [#28770](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28770))
- Add `--fuse-qkv` support for Muse Glimmer ([#29203](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29203))

### Core changes

- Add graph input/input-tensor diagnostics during scheduler reserve ([#26625](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26625))
- Enable CUDA graphs for MTP drafting ([#28549](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28549))
- Fix tensor-parallel split state/granularity for fused QKV models ([#28965](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28965))
- Fix Mamba time-step projection input contiguity ([#28832](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28832))
- Write the SWA pattern in the model saver and round-trip 15 more architectures ([#29042](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29042))
- Add environment variables for temperature, top-p, min-p and penalties ([#27380](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27380))
- Reduce the sampler backend probe size ([#29285](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29285))
- Add Ling 3.0, DeepSeek V3.2/V4, qwen3-coder, Muse Glimmer and Gemma 4 parser fixes ([#28682](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28682), [#29008](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29008), [#28869](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28869), [#29242](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29242), [#29115](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29115))
- Improve JSON Schema and PEG handling ([#28518](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28518), [#29127](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29127), [#29161](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29161))
- Add ufakzeka pre-tokenizer and `llama-bench --version` ([#29033](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29033), [#28971](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28971))

### Multi-modality changes

- Add sanity checks for mtmd layer indices, SAM layer counts, resize targets and graph allocation ([#29276](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29276), [#28149](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28149))
- Fix SigLIP bucket buffer overrun for tall/wide images ([#29276](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29276))

### Server changes

- Fix router eviction races and child process lifecycle handling ([#29217](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29217))
- Do not pass log file or API key file to router-spawned children ([#29212](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29212), [#28938](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28938))
- Improve startup and model-source logging ([#29125](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29125))
- Update vendored cpp-httplib to 0.57.1 ([#29239](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29239))

### UI changes

- Accept WEBM video files ([#28622](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28622))
- Add close button to UI toasts ([#28246](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28246))
- Fix mobile breakpoint and content overflow issues, including horizontal table scrolling ([#29108](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29108))
- Restore the reasoning menu in single-model desktop mode ([#27985](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27985))
- Stop re-probing a disabled `/tools` endpoint on every message ([#28646](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28646))

### ggml changes

- Updated ggml to v0.25.0 ([release](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases/tag/v0.25.0))
- The release expands hyper-connection, flash-attention, and fused MoE/SSM support across backends, with robustness, quantization, data-layout, and RPC/meta improvements.
- API changes include gated `ggml_dsv4_hc_pre_gated()`, optional `ggml_dsv4_hc_post()` comb, and RPC protocol major v7.

## Overview

An opt-in `--no-fallback` flag for llama-quantize that will exit with an error when tensor shapes would otherwise force a
fallback quant - before any tensor data is read. More information can be found in the issue #26616 with related
discussion.

_This PR contains_:

- Opt-in flag on `llama-quantize`. When any tensor shape would force a type substitution, it errors out before any
  tensor data is read, through the same error path the `imatrix` check uses, so the tool exits non-zero
- Why a flag: dry run reports the substitutions but cannot gate on them. `--dry-run --no-fallback` is a preflight check
  that finishes in seconds
- The existing end-of-run fallback warning now carries a summary in both modes:
    - count
    - parameter share
    - byte share
    - nominal versus actual bpw
    - the recipe's own no-substitution bpw
    - the substitutions grouped by column count and type pair, largest first, capped at eight lines. Per-tensor warning
      lines are unchanged
- New field in the public params struct, default off, inserted after dry_run the same way dry_run was added. Pointer
  members after it shift so any code built with the old struct layout must rebuild; identical trade to
  the [dry-run PR](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/19526)
- Help text and README bullet

## Additional information

- Ref: #26616
- Ref: PR #3747 as the PR that introduced the fallback behavior
- Parity with [ggufaudit](https://github.com/JoshBolding/ggufaudit):
    * same units and denominators as ggufaudit: tensor count, % of params, % of bytes, bpw; projected bpw exact on
      lmstudio's Q4_K_M, within 0.01 bpw on bartowski's imatrix quant
    * the ggufaudit census count runs n+1 per affected model: output.weight. The recipe itself sends it to Q8_0
      when its width is not a multiple of 256 so it never reaches `tensor_type_fallback()` and is not a substitution;
      ggufaudit cannot tell a recipe choice from a fallback. Nemotron below: 141 in the banner, 142 in the ggufaudit
      census row for the same 417-tensor model
    * i-quant rungs: without the maker's imatrix the recipe requests different types (q2_K where the ggufaudit census
      file has IQ2_XXS), so counts and bpw agree but type names differ
    * non-256 labels (Q4_0 etc.): ggufaudit does not apply its test; the flag still catches the substitution
- Testing details:
    * macOS arm64, Debug, LLAMA_FATAL_WARNINGS=ON, GGML_OPENMP=OFF
    * full build of all targets clean; ctest -L main subset (ci/run.sh's Debug set) 50/50; test-quant-type-selection
      pass
    * both no-fallback modes on the 61 GiB BF16 return in <1s and write nothing to disk
    * full ci/run.sh run locally, 100% tests pass

### Examples

#### Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B, public BF16 (61 GiB, 417 tensors; https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16)

## Overview

Models may occasionally emit invalid UTF-8 which fails during parsing. This records invalid utf-8 sequences during parse and provides a `sanitized_text()` at every node in the AST.

Tool names/args are not passed through this, as they should be grammar constrained to only produce UTF-8. If this becomes a problem, we can easily change them to use `sanitize_text()` instead.

ref: #28724
fixes #24327
fixes #27543

## Additional Information

Invalid UTF-8 runs are replaced with a single `U+FFFD`, aka the "maximal subpart" per https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode16.0.0/core-spec/chapter-3/#G66453.

items.body:
## Overview
TL;DR:  3-7x faster CPU mul_mat using VNNI with IMO minimal complexity

I noticed that the vec_dot approach currently taken for mul_mat duplicates the work of unpacking quants a bunch of times.  I put together a generic tiled mul_mat that works with 256x256 windows of int8.  We slide a 256-long window across the source tensors, unpacking quants 256x256 at a time, (this amortizes the unpacking work 256x compared to baseline), and then we sweep an optimized 16x16 microkernel across them to build up a 256x256 float32 output tile.  If this results in too little work for our number of CPUs, I step down the chunk size to 128, 64 etc so that we have more chunks to saturate available cores.

For tall src1 (prefills), this results in 3-7x performance gain (2x compared to repack) on my x86 machine using the optimized microkernel.  The gain goes away as we shrink the rows in src1, reaching break-even at 32 rows and falling behind to 80% of stock performance at pure GEMV.  Error rates are on the order of 5e-04 for max single scalar error, 6e-05 for RMSE across the whole tensor compared to standard vec_dot based mul_mat (microscopically better than repack).  

Integration with the main mul_mat path is similar to llamafile, we return false if we don't support or if we think it will be unprofitable (< 64 rows).

The majority of the code is portable C++ with only the microkernel and 3 inlined bit-unpacking routines as pieces to fill in for a new architecture.  This means we could expand the approach to ARM and other architectures with minimal code addition.

So far, this only supports the k-quant types.  I'm reasonably sure we could expand it to the iq-quants as well, but I haven't gone through all of them to ensure their codebooks stay in bounds of the range my unpacked tiles support.


## Additional information

The VNNI path has some additional complexity.  VNNI takes one chunk of 4 scalars from src0, broadcasted 16x to a 512 bit vector  from one row, and another vector of 4 scalars each from 16 columns of src1 all packed together to execute 16 partial dot products.  This requires a somewhat ugly additional repack of the q8_k quants to enable contiguous reads in the VNNI kernel.  I gated it away from everything else so it only exists for VNNI (and other future archs which may require bespoke packing).  The normal path for AVX2 and other future archs can ignore it.

We assume that K % 256 == 0, this seems safe given that all of the quant types we support use QK_K = 256.

Benchmarks all run using 8 threads on an AMD 9950x3D.  Used 8 instead of 16 to reduce impact of the rest of the system on the benchmarks (it's my desktop).

items.body:
## Overview

Ling 3.0 templates pre-open <think> in the generation prompt, so the model never emits an opening tag and tool calls can appear before `</think>`. The generated parser classified that output entirely as `reasoning_content` and clients received `content=""` with no `tool_calls`.

This adds a dedicated Ling parser (modeled on the hand-written Qwen3-Coder and Kimi parsers) that terminates reasoning at `</think>` or a tool-call marker, prefers the close tag when both are present, defers the streaming split to the final parse so delivered deltas are never reclassified, and keeps trailing prose after the last tool call as content. Adds the Ling 3.0 Flash chat template (byte-identical to the GGUF-embedded template) and tests covering the unclosed-think tool call (full and streaming), closed-think paths, trailing prose, parallel calls, marker-like strings in argument values, and `reasoning_format=none`.

## Additional information

This builds upon the initial work that added BailingMoE 3 support #26608.  Ling 3.0 also emits stray byte-level tokenizer pieces that decode to invalid UTF-8, which hard-fails the parse layer with a 500.  That is fixed separately in #28724.  Please note that both changes are needed for reliable usage of Ling 3.0 Flash in llama.cpp.

Validated against Ling 3.0 Flash GGUF on llama-server with `--jinja --reasoning-format deepseek`. With this parser and #28724 applied, a 29-task agentic benchmark went from 5 reasoning-only tool-call stops and 1 parse `500` to 0 of both. 

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- AI usage disclosure: Yes, I used AI to help write and check the code.  I personally, thoroughly reviewed the CONTRIBUTING.md file.

items.body:
## Overview

Byte-level BPE vocabularies contain pieces that decode to invalid UTF-8 (e.g. lone continuation bytes), and models occasionally sample them mid-generation. On llama-server the final parse then fails with "The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format" (or the Content-only equivalent on /completions), and an HTTP 500 occurs, and no text after the bad byte is ever streamed.

Reproduced on unpatched master with Ling 3.0 tiny at Q8_K_XL and at BF16 (the release dtype): emoji-heavy checklist generations produced invalid emissions at roughly 1 per 11k and 1 per 39k tokens respectively, byte signature e2 9c 85 followed by a lone 0x85 piece after a valid U+2705. 

This sanitizes generated text at the accumulation and finalization boundaries in server-common: invalid sequences are replaced with U+FFFD; trailing incomplete sequences are held back while streaming and dropped at finalization. Strict parsing is unchanged. The replacement diverges from the token stream by the replaced bytes; the current behavior loses the entire turn to a 500.

## Additional information

vLLM handles the same class at the detokenizer boundary (vllm-project/vllm#17448).  SGLang's incremental detokenizer handles the same class at the boundary as well: text ending in U+FFFD is held back and retried with subsequent tokens (`detokenizer_manager.py`).  

The invalid pieces were discovered on Ling 3.0 Flash, but are not Ling-specific. The Qwen3 and DeepSeek-V4 vocabularies also contain them (944 and 1,470 invalid-UTF-8 pieces respectively, including a lone 0x85).

Verified no output change on a non-Ling model (Qwen3.5-9B): greedy completions under this patch are byte-identical to unpatched master.

Ling 3.0 Flash requires this, together with #28682.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- AI usage disclosure: Yes, I used AI to help write and check the code.  I personally, thoroughly reviewed the CONTRIBUTING.md file.

Vulkan

Also seen with Qwen3.5-9B and Gemma 4, not with Ling-3.0-tiny (no thorough testing).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Note: I have used the Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1 chat to help me narrow this down and write the PowerShell script that ran the tests and produced the logs.

On this laptop, as soon as model layers are placed on the GPU with the Vulkan backend, the output is garbage: llama-perplexity gives NaN from the first chunk, llama-completion writes nonsense. With -ngl 0 everything is correct.

It does not depend on how many layers are offloaded but the batch settings. Tests with the same model:
```
llama-perplexity -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf -f wiki.test.raw -c 128 --chunks 4 -fit off -ngl 16 -b 128 -ub 128
-> NaN (12 runs out of 12)

llama-perplexity -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf -f wiki.test.raw -c 128 --chunks 4 -fit off -ngl 999 -b 512 -ub 512
-> NaN (16/16)

llama-perplexity -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf -f wiki.test.raw -c 128 --chunks 4 -fit off -ngl 999 -b 2048 -ub 512
-> correct (16/16)

llama-perplexity -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf -f wiki.test.raw -c 128 --chunks 4 -fit off -ngl 0 -b 128 -ub 128 -ot "^blk\.([0-9]|1[0-5])\.=Vulkan0"
-> correct (20/20)
```

The correct outputs are [1]4.5951,[2]7.6200,[3]7.4222,[4]7.4062.
Correct runs are within KL divergence 0.003 of the CPU backend.
Failing runs are NaN from chunk 1.

With llama-eval-callback, I compared a run with layers on the CPU and a run with layers on the GPU (all other settings identical):
```
llama-eval-callback -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf -c 512 -b 128 -ub 128 -t 8 -fit off -p "The committee met on Tuesday to review the harbour proposal. Engineers had surveyed the eastern pier in March and found that several of the older pilings needed replacement before any new cranes could be installed. The mayor asked whether the work could be finished before the fishing season, and the contractor replied that it depended on the weather and on how quickly the steel could be delivered from the mill. Two council members raised concerns about noise near the school, so the board agreed to limit pile driving to the hours between nine and four." -ngl 0

llama-eval-callback -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf -c 512 -b 128 -ub 128 -t 8 -fit off -p "The committee met on Tuesday to review the harbour proposal. Engineers had surveyed the eastern pier in March and found that several of the older pilings needed replacement before any new cranes could be installed. The mayor asked whether the work could be finished before the fishing season, and the contractor replied that it depended on the weather and on how quickly the steel could be delivered from the mill. Two council members raised concerns about noise near the school, so the board agreed to limit pile driving to the hours between nine and four." -ngl 999
```

In the -ngl 999 run, the first 178 nodes (layers 0 and 1) match the -ngl 0 run. Then z-2 = MUL_MAT(blk.2.attn_gate.weight, attn_norm-2) gives NaN, while its input attn_norm-2 is identical in both runs (sum 2461.443). It is the same node in all 6 runs. So one specific weight tensor (blk.2.attn_gate.weight, 15 MiB, iq4_xs) is read incorrectly when it is on the GPU.

Two additional notes:
1. The failing -ngl 16 command becomes correct (8 runs out of 8) when the Khronos Vulkan validation layer is enabled, and the layer reports no error.
2. test-backend-ops -b Vulkan0 passes 18702/18702.

Things that seem to have no effect: --no-mmap, -fa off, -nkvo, --no-warmup, the GGML_VK_DISABLE_* environment variables, a newer GPU driver, VT-d off in the BIOS.

items.body:
## Summary

On a gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU, RDNA3.5) system with ROCm 7.2.4, the **HIP/ROCm** backend
produces corrupted output where the **Vulkan** backend, running the **same weights, the same
build, and byte-identical flags on the same machine**, is correct on every attempt.

Measured on three architectures. Two fail on HIP, with **different severity**; one is
unaffected:

| model | `general.architecture` | topology | Vulkan | HIP/ROCm |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct `Q4_K_M` | `llama` | dense | **16/16** @30,516 · 6/6 @1,616 | **0/16** @30,516 · **0/6 @1,616** |
| Qwen3.8-27B `UD-Q8_K_XL` | `qwen35` | dense | **16/16** @29,355 | **0/16** @29,355 · 6/6 @1,349 |
| Ling-3.0-flash `IQ4_XS` | `bailingmoe3` | 512-expert MoE | **16/16** @29,275 | **16/16** @29,275 |

(`@N` = prompt tokens. Each cell is 8 requests run twice; the repeat is deliberate, because a
single 8/8 is not enough to call a backend clean.)

Backend and binary path were read from `/proc/<pid>/exe` on **every** run, not inferred from
the launcher — an earlier "Vulkan" result in this investigation turned out to be the HIP server
still answering after a boot script silently failed.

### Two severities, deliberately not merged

- **`llama` is broken outright on HIP** — at *every* depth tested, including a 1,616-token
  prompt. Output is degenerate word salad:
  `'for 4\n<|contextual background\nline keep track\nTheater in line while mind the material and context in'`
  The same model, flags and template on Vulkan is 6/6 shallow and 16/16 at 30,516 tokens, so
  this is not a configuration error.
- **`qwen35` is correct at shallow depth and fails past roughly 29k tokens** when the request
  also carries a moderately large tool array. Output stays fluent and well-formed; the model
  confidently mis-states **its own tool list**. With an array of `read_file`, `tool_00` …
  `tool_15`:

  > I don't have a `read_file` tool available in my current toolset. The tools I have access to
  > are `tool_01` through `tool_15`, which are placeholder utilities that accept a single string
  > argument. None of them are file-reading tools.

  It has read the placeholders' *descriptions* correctly while losing the entries at the **head**
  of the array. Other samples invented tool names absent from the request entirely, or ran to
  the token limit emitting `finish_reason: "length"` with empty content and no tool call.

Whether these are one defect with severity varying by model, or two, is **not established here**.

### Hypothesis, on a single data point — please treat as a lead, not a finding

The two failing models are **dense**; the one that passes is a **512-expert MoE**. Dense and
MoE matmuls take different paths (`mul_mat` vs `mul_mat_id`), which may be where to look. This
rests on **one** MoE observation and no second MoE was tested. It is offered as a starting
point, not a claim.

## Still present on current master

Reproduced on stock upstream **`b21e4de74567f5eef213765c9476a843c2e43f0d`** — `master`
re-fetched immediately before building — from a clean detached worktree with no local patches,
built for gfx1151 with ROCm 7.2.4.

The same result holds on **`3a653fea932e`** (12 days earlier). **The two SHAs agreeing is
expected rather than corroborating:** there are 7 commits between them and **none touch
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda` or `ggml/src/ggml-hip`**, so it simply means nothing has been attempted on
this code path in that window. It should not be read as an independent second confirmation.

### It is not `e79e4bf66` — please do not close this as a duplicate of that commit

`e79e4bf66` ("ggml-hip : remove -funsafe-math-optimizations", #26696) is **present in every
tested tree and does not fix this.** It is the obvious suspect and it matched on every checkable
detail:

- its message describes `-fassociative-math` reassociating FP reductions and *"can flip greedy
  argmax on **RDNA3.5** (e.g. **MTP speculative decode** diverging from the non-speculative
  baseline)"*;
- the hardware here is gfx1151, which **is** RDNA3.5;
- one of the failing workloads runs `--spec-type draft-mtp`;
- an older tree used here still carries the flag at `ggml/src/ggml-hip/CMakeLists.txt:130`,
  while every tree tested above does not.

With that flag already removed, the defect reproduces at 0/16. This is either a second,
independent problem or the same one with another cause.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Build | stock `b21e4de74567f`; also reproduced on `3a653fea932e` |
| GPU | gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU), 128 GB unified memory |
| ROCm | 7.2.4 (hipcc 7.2.53211-97f5574fe2, AMD clang 22.0.0git roc-7.2.4) |
| OS | Linux |
| Build flags | `-DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=<rocm>/lib/llvm/bin/clang++ -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=ON` |

## Server flags — identical on both backends, only the binary differs

```
-ngl 999 --flash-attn on
--ctx-size 65536 --ubatch-size 1024 --batch-size 2048
--parallel 1 --threads 16
--cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16
--cache-prompt --cache-reuse 256 --cache-ram 0
--ctx-checkpoints 32 --checkpoint-min-step 8192
--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0
--jinja        # each model uses its own embedded chat template
```

Verified byte-identical with `diff` between the two launcher files; the only differences are a
comment header, the slot-save path, and the binary path.

## Causes eliminated, each by changing ONE variable

Listed so nobody spends replies asking. Every row was measured; all remained failing:

| varied | result |
|---|---|
| Context depth | not the cause — 1 tool at 36,335 tokens is 5/5 correct, *longer* than the failing case |
| Tool count | not the cause — 17 tools at 1,349 tokens is 6/6 correct |
| Total prompt length | not the cause — see the 36,335-token row above |
| KV cache type | `q4_0`, `q8_0`, `f16` all fail |
| Flash attention | `--flash-attn off` still fails; it changes the failure *mode*, not the failure. (Note `--flash-attn off`

## Bug report: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4exp) garbage output on SM110 (Jetson Thor) when >8 layers offloaded to GPU

**Hardware**: NVIDIA Jetson Thor (SM110, Blackwell), aarch64, 122GB unified memory, CUDA 13.0
**llama.cpp**: master `035e227` (llama: hold the qwen4exp indexer cache in a new llama_memory_hybrid_idx), built with:
`-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=110 -DGGML_CUDA_FA=ON -DGGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON -DGGML_CUDA_NCCL=ON`
**Model**: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` UD-IQ4_XS (93.7GB, 3 split shards, qwen4exp arch)

### Symptom
- `llama-cli -ngl 8` (layers 0-7 on GPU): output is **fully coherent** ✅
- `llama-cli -ngl 9` or more (layers 0-8+ on GPU): output is **garbage** (incoherent token salad) ❌
- `llama-cli -ngl 0` (pure CPU): fully coherent ✅
- Same model works coherently on CPU; prefill/decode rates are sane in all cases (no crashes, no CUDA errors logged)

### What was excluded (all still garbage at `-ngl 999`)
- flash attention on/off
- `--no-mmap`
- PLE table forced to CPU (`--override-tensor per_layer_token_embd=CPU`)
- `GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1`
- rebuild with `-DGGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=OFF`
- `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1`
- layers 8-9 pinned to CPU via `--override-tensor` (blk.8.*/blk.9.*) while all other layers on GPU

### Additional data points
- The exact same build flags run **Ling-3.0-tiny** (a different MoE/linear-attention arch) on this same box at 88-90 tok/s with fully coherent output — so SM110 CUDA generally works.
- The qwen4exp garbage appears from the first generated token, and (without EOS) generation loops indefinitely writing huge logs.
- Threshold is exactly at the 9th offloaded layer (index 8); `-ngl 8` stable, `-ngl 9` always broken across many attempts.

### Suspected area
A scale-dependent CUDA path in the qwen4exp hybrid memory / QSA indexer (the recently refactored `llama_memory_hybrid_idx`), or a kernel launch path that corrupts silently once GPU-resident layers exceed ~8.

Happy to run any additional diagnostics or test candidate fixes on this hardware.

items.body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.3.0-dev (build 1, commit 5d4a3be)
built with IntelLLVM 2026.1.1 for Linux x86_64



### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

SYCL

### Hardware

UHD770 in 14900K cpu.

### Models

Ling 3.0 tiny

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Model will not load and a stack trace happens...

This is  Claude's description

```
The abort is fixed. I found the root cause and patched it: ggml_backend_sycl_device_get_memory() in ggml-sycl.cpp:6049 called GGML_ABORT whenever the precise free-memory query failed — but I confirmed (via gdb, --fit off, and forcing every GGML_SYCL_GET_MEM_API/GGML_SYCL_USE_LEVEL_ZERO_API combination) that the underlying query is unconditionally broken on this WSL2 host, same root cause as the earlier Sysman warning: it needs a real Linux DRM sysfs device tree that WSL2's GPU passthrough doesn't expose. Every code path already computes a usable fallback (total device memory) before returning failure — the abort was just needlessly throwing that away instead of using it. I changed the abort to a warning that keeps that fallback value; this is unrelated to your Vulkan removal, it's a llama.cpp bug that was always going to hit the first time any SYCL model load was attempted here.

Rebuilt and reran — the abort is gone.
```

This is Claude's patch

```
diff --git a/ggml/src/ggml-sycl/ggml-sycl.cpp b/ggml/src/ggml-sycl/ggml-sycl.cpp
index 290fb46..d8c00d5 100644
--- a/ggml/src/ggml-sycl/ggml-sycl.cpp
+++ b/ggml/src/ggml-sycl/ggml-sycl.cpp
@@ -6051,7 +6051,18 @@ static void ggml_backend_sycl_device_get_memory(ggml_backend_dev_t dev, size_t *
     bool res = get_memory_size(dpct::dev_mgr::instance().get_device(ctx->device), *free, *total,
                                (MemoryAPIType) g_ggml_sycl_get_mem_api);
     if (!res) {
-        GGML_ABORT("[%s] failed to get device memory size", __func__);
+        // get_memory_size() always populates *free/*total with a usable
+        // fallback (global device memory) before returning false -- every
+        // path through it (query_free_memory_by_ze, then
+        // get_memory_size_by_sycl_api) sets both, whether the precise
+        // free-memory query itself succeeded or not. Aborting the whole
+        // process here throws that fallback away for what is, at worst, a
+        // less precise estimate -- fatal on hosts where the free-memory
+        // query is structurally unavailable (WSL2 GPU passthrough: Sysman
+        // device enumeration needs a real Linux DRM sysfs device tree
+        // WSL2 does not expose), even though model loading itself does
+        // not depend on it.
+        GGML_LOG_WARN("[%s] precise free memory query unavailable; using total device memory as an estimate\n", __func__);
     }
 }
```

And now the models load.

items.body:
## Overview

This enables CUDA graphs on Pascal (sm_61) by changing one line in `ggml_cuda_graph_set_enabled`: the architecture gate goes from `GGML_CUDA_CC_VOLTA` to `GGML_CUDA_CC_DP4A`.

With the help of Claude, and for purely personal needs at the beginning, i have been exploring ways to speed up inference on a GTX 1080 (pascal, sm_61), an old card that still holds enormous value for running today's state-of-the-art small models (8gb vRam)

One of these is manually unlocking CUDA graphs. Below are tests run on both dense and MoE models, with very positive results.

GTX 1080, driver 581.57, CUDA 12.4, build b10549 / commit b2e5e9b, MSVC 14.38, Windows

MoE Ling-3.0-tiny Q6_K, from 41.2 to 57.6 tok/s (+39.8%)
47.7 to 72.2 long gen (+51.4%)
prefill 857.0 to 853.0 tok/s (-0.5%)

Dense Qwen-based 9B Q5_K_M, from 26.3 to 28.0 tok/s (+6.4%), and again on a second run 25.3 to 27.2 (+7.7%)
prefill 586.7 to 583.7 (-0.5%) and 582.6 to 580.0 (-0.4%)

With llama-bench the gain is even higher(no context so ofc)
| build | pp512 | tg64 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| graphs off | 1935.42 ± 27.27 | 41.47 ± 6.15 |
| graphs on  | 1908.80 ± 40.07 | 73.85 ± 4.63 |

pp512 -1.4% (noise), tg64 +78%.

The less context there is, the bigger the gain. +78% on an almost empty context (llama-bench tg64), +51% on short prompts, +40% with a 7000 token prompt. That is what you would expect if graphs remove a fixed per-token launch cost: with a large KV cache the per-token work grows and the saved fixed cost weighs relatively less.

So prefill doesn't change much, it stays inside the noise, the whole gain is in generation. How i measured: median of 3 samples, one thrown as warmup, alternating A-B-A-B for thermal drift and anything under 3% i call it noise.


I checked correctness and speed. temperature 0, top_k 1, fixed seed, same prompts on both builds. 10 different prompts of 200 tokens each (math, prose, translation, python, sql, lists), 10/10 identical. Dense too. With --verbose the line "disabling CUDA graphs due to GPU architecture" disappears.

## Additional information

GGML_CUDA_CC_DP4A is 610 so this only opens sm_61 and leaves sm_60 (P100) alone, i have no sm_60 to test on. GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 still works if someone needs to turn it off.

About the 2024 regression that explains why was disabled on purpose. PR #6766 turned graphs off for CC<8 after measuring a regression on a P40 (53.84 to 51.67 tok/s). The P40 is GP102 so it's the same sm_61 as my card, but that test was a dense model with around 700 graph nodes, and back then MoE was excluded from graphs completely. Two years later, a dense model doesn't regress anymore (+6.4% and +7.7% on two runs) BUT MOST IMPORTANTLY a MoE with 1794 nodes gains 40%. The gain follows the number of nodes in the graph, which makes sense if the decode is launch bound. Volta was already re-enabled by #25749.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - AI was used to produce the patch, to run the benchmarks, and to translate this description from italian. Some of the explanation paragraphs were drafted by it too and then reviewed by me. I have reviewed the change and the benchmarks myself and can explain them, and i am responsible for everything submitted here.

items.title: Misc. bug: test-chat-template hangs on Windows (MSYS2 UCRT64 + GCC)

items.body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.1.2-dev (build 10540, commit 07822bddf)
built with GNU 16.1.1 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395)

### Models

Ling-3.0-flash-Q5_K_M from https://huggingface.co/bloomer010/Ling-3.0-flash-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

In a multi-turn tool using chat, the model sometimes emits `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` from inside its reasoning channel and stops without ever closing `</think>`. The whole turn is then swallowed into reasoning_content.

Root cause
Bailing V3 has no specialized parser in common/chat.cpp, so it falls through to the generic autoparser, which sets a single reasoning terminator (`thinking_end_tags = {"</think>"}`) with no <tool_call> fallback. When the model opens a tool call before closing `</think>`, nothing terminates reasoning and the output is mis-routed.

Behaviour like this is already handled for some other models (these thinking+tool models add tool call openers as reasoning terminators).

For example:
Qwen3-Coder: `thinking_end_tags = {"</think>", "<tool_call>"}`
DeepSeek V3.2: `thinking_end_tags = {THINK_END, FC_START}`
Kimi K2 (common_chat_params_init_kimi_k2) handles this exact behavior, with the maintainer comment: "this model is CRAZY … it can call tools at the end of reasoning without closing reasoning", and adds `<|tool_calls_section_begin|> / <|tool_call_begin|>` as terminators.
Bailing V3's Kimi-K2-like tendency to call tools mid-reasoning isn't covered by the generic autoparser.

Suggested fix
Add <tool_call> to Bailing V3's reasoning terminators (similar to Kimi K2/Qwen3-Coder fixes)

Reproduction code I used to test this exact behaviour which produces a high fail rate with Ling 3.0 flash:
https://gist.github.com/chielteuben/54efbb6b1a75eb7310246f34c54e3465

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

Easily reproduceable using the gist I added.
Note for this response: no tool calls, no content.

```
{
  "choices": [
    {
      "finish_reason": "stop",
      "index": 0,
      "message": {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "",
        "reasoning_content": "<tool_call>get_forecast\n<arg_key>location</arg_key>\n<arg_value>Berlin</arg_value><arg_key>day</arg_key>\n<arg_value>2026-08-22</arg_value>\n</tool_call>"
      }
    }
  ],
  "model": "/models/Ling-3.0-flash-Q5_K_M/Ling-3.0-flash-Q5_K_M.gguf",
  "system_fingerprint": "b10540-07822bddf",
  "object": "chat.completion",
  "usage": {
    "completion_tokens": 32,
    "prompt_tokens": 589,
    "total_tokens": 621
  }
}
```

## Overview

This release focuses on backend performance and correctness, broader model coverage, and more robust server/router operation. It adds HRM-Text (DFM Mimir 1B) support, MiMo-V2.6 and HunyuanOCR conversion support, ggml 0.25.0 backend improvements, multi-address HTTP binding, image outputs from function calls, and several chat parser/UI fixes.

- Accelerate CUDA `conv2d` with implicit GEMM ([#29135](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29135))

### New models

- Add HRM-Text / DFM Mimir 1B support ([#27625](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27625))
- Add MiMo-V2.6 conversion support ([#29257](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29257))
- Add DFlash support for HunyuanOCR ([#28890](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28890))

- Add `--fuse-qkv` support for Muse Glimmer ([#29203](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29203))

- Enable CUDA graphs for MTP drafting ([#28549](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28549))
- Fix tensor-parallel split state/granularity for fused QKV models ([#28965](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28965))
- Fix Mamba time-step projection input contiguity ([#28832](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28832))
- Write the SWA pattern in the model saver and round-trip 15 more architectures ([#29042](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29042))
- Add environment variables for temperature, top-p, min-p and penalties ([#27380](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27380))
- Reduce the sampler backend probe size ([#29285](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29285))
- Add Ling 3.0, DeepSeek V3.2/V4, qwen3-coder, Muse Glimmer and Gemma 4 parser fixes ([#28682](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28682), [#29008](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29008), [#28869](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28869), [#29242](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29242), [#29115](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29115))

### Multi-modality changes

- Add sanity checks for mtmd layer indices, SAM layer counts, resize targets and graph allocation ([#29276](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29276), [#28149](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28149))
- Fix SigLIP bucket buffer overrun for tall/wide images ([#29276](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29276))

### Server changes

- Fix router eviction races and child process lifecycle handling ([#29217](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29217))
- Do not pass log file or API key file to router-spawned children ([#29212](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29212), [#28938](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28938))
- Improve startup and model-source logging ([#29125](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29125))
- Update vendored cpp-httplib to 0.57.1 ([#29239](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29239))

### UI changes

- Accept WEBM video files ([#28622](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28622))
- Add close button to UI toasts ([#28246](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28246))
- Fix mobile breakpoint and content overflow issues, including horizontal table scrolling ([#29108](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29108))
- Restore the reasoning menu in single-model desktop mode ([#27985](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27985))
- Stop re-probing a disabled `/tools` endpoint on every message ([#28646](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28646))

### ggml changes

- Updated ggml to v0.25.0 ([release](https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/releases/tag/v0.25.0))
- The release expands hyper-connection, flash-attention, and fused MoE/SSM support across backends, with robustness, quantization, data-layout, and RPC/meta improvements.
- API changes include gated `ggml_dsv4_hc_pre_gated()`, optional `ggml_dsv4_hc_post()` comb, and RPC protocol major v7.

items.body:
## Overview

Ling 3.0 templates pre-open <think> in the generation prompt, so the model never emits an opening tag and tool calls can appear before `</think>`. The generated parser classified that output entirely as `reasoning_content` and clients received `content=""` with no `tool_calls`.

This adds a dedicated Ling parser (modeled on the hand-written Qwen3-Coder and Kimi parsers) that terminates reasoning at `</think>` or a tool-call marker, prefers the close tag when both are present, defers the streaming split to the final parse so delivered deltas are never reclassified, and keeps trailing prose after the last tool call as content. Adds the Ling 3.0 Flash chat template (byte-identical to the GGUF-embedded template) and tests covering the unclosed-think tool call (full and streaming), closed-think paths, trailing prose, parallel calls, marker-like strings in argument values, and `reasoning_format=none`.

## Additional information

This builds upon the initial work that added BailingMoE 3 support #26608.  Ling 3.0 also emits stray byte-level tokenizer pieces that decode to invalid UTF-8, which hard-fails the parse layer with a 500.  That is fixed separately in #28724.  Please note that both changes are needed for reliable usage of Ling 3.0 Flash in llama.cpp.

Validated against Ling 3.0 Flash GGUF on llama-server with `--jinja --reasoning-format deepseek`. With this parser and #28724 applied, a 29-task agentic benchmark went from 5 reasoning-only tool-call stops and 1 parse `500` to 0 of both. 

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- AI usage disclosure: Yes, I used AI to help write and check the code.  I personally, thoroughly reviewed the CONTRIBUTING.md file.
items.title: chat: add dedicated Ling 3.0 (Bailing V3) parser

items.body:
## Overview

Byte-level BPE vocabularies contain pieces that decode to invalid UTF-8 (e.g. lone continuation bytes), and models occasionally sample them mid-generation. On llama-server the final parse then fails with "The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format" (or the Content-only equivalent on /completions), and an HTTP 500 occurs, and no text after the bad byte is ever streamed.

Reproduced on unpatched master with Ling 3.0 tiny at Q8_K_XL and at BF16 (the release dtype): emoji-heavy checklist generations produced invalid emissions at roughly 1 per 11k and 1 per 39k tokens respectively, byte signature e2 9c 85 followed by a lone 0x85 piece after a valid U+2705. 

This sanitizes generated text at the accumulation and finalization boundaries in server-common: invalid sequences are replaced with U+FFFD; trailing incomplete sequences are held back while streaming and dropped at finalization. Strict parsing is unchanged. The replacement diverges from the token stream by the replaced bytes; the current behavior loses the entire turn to a 500.

## Additional information

vLLM handles the same class at the detokenizer boundary (vllm-project/vllm#17448).  SGLang's incremental detokenizer handles the same class at the boundary as well: text ending in U+FFFD is held back and retried with subsequent tokens (`detokenizer_manager.py`).  

The invalid pieces were discovered on Ling 3.0 Flash, but are not Ling-specific. The Qwen3 and DeepSeek-V4 vocabularies also contain them (944 and 1,470 invalid-UTF-8 pieces respectively, including a lone 0x85).

Verified no output change on a non-Ling model (Qwen3.5-9B): greedy completions under this patch are byte-identical to unpatched master.

Ling 3.0 Flash requires this, together with #28682.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- AI usage disclosure: Yes, I used AI to help write and check the code.  I personally, thoroughly reviewed the CONTRIBUTING.md file.

## Summary

On a gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU, RDNA3.5) system with ROCm 7.2.4, the **HIP/ROCm** backend
produces corrupted output where the **Vulkan** backend, running the **same weights, the same
build, and byte-identical flags on the same machine**, is correct on every attempt.

Measured on three architectures. Two fail on HIP, with **different severity**; one is
unaffected:

| model | `general.architecture` | topology | Vulkan | HIP/ROCm |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct `Q4_K_M` | `llama` | dense | **16/16** @30,516 · 6/6 @1,616 | **0/16** @30,516 · **0/6 @1,616** |
| Qwen3.8-27B `UD-Q8_K_XL` | `qwen35` | dense | **16/16** @29,355 | **0/16** @29,355 · 6/6 @1,349 |
| Ling-3.0-flash `IQ4_XS` | `bailingmoe3` | 512-expert MoE | **16/16** @29,275 | **16/16** @29,275 |

(`@N` = prompt tokens. Each cell is 8 requests run twice; the repeat is deliberate, because a
single 8/8 is not enough to call a backend clean.)

Backend and binary path were read from `/proc/<pid>/exe` on **every** run, not inferred from
the launcher — an earlier "Vulkan" result in this investigation turned out to be the HIP server
still answering after a boot script silently failed.

### Two severities, deliberately not merged

- **`llama` is broken outright on HIP** — at *every* depth tested, including a 1,616-token
  prompt. Output is degenerate word salad:
  `'for 4\n<|contextual background\nline keep track\nTheater in line while mind the material and context in'`
  The same model, flags and template on Vulkan is 6/6 shallow and 16/16 at 30,516 tokens, so
  this is not a configuration error.
- **`qwen35` is correct at shallow depth and fails past roughly 29k tokens** when the request
  also carries a moderately large tool array. Output stays fluent and well-formed; the model
  confidently mis-states **its own tool list**. With an array of `read_file`, `tool_00` …
  `tool_15`:

  > I don't have a `read_file` tool available in my current toolset. The tools I have access to
  > are `tool_01` through `tool_15`, which are placeholder utilities that accept a single string
  > argument. None of them are file-reading tools.

  It has read the placeholders' *descriptions* correctly while losing the entries at the **head**
  of the array. Other samples invented tool names absent from the request entirely, or ran to
  the token limit emitting `finish_reason: "length"` with empty content and no tool call.

Whether these are one defect with severity varying by model, or two, is **not established here**.

### Hypothesis, on a single data point — please treat as a lead, not a finding

The two failing models are **dense**; the one that passes is a **512-expert MoE**. Dense and
MoE matmuls take different paths (`mul_mat` vs `mul_mat_id`), which may be where to look. This
rests on **one** MoE observation and no second MoE was tested. It is offered as a starting
point, not a claim.

## Still present on current master

Reproduced on stock upstream **`b21e4de74567f5eef213765c9476a843c2e43f0d`** — `master`
re-fetched immediately before building — from a clean detached worktree with no local patches,
built for gfx1151 with ROCm 7.2.4.

The same result holds on **`3a653fea932e`** (12 days earlier). **The two SHAs agreeing is
expected rather than corroborating:** there are 7 commits between them and **none touch
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda` or `ggml/src/ggml-hip`**, so it simply means nothing has been attempted on
this code path in that window. It should not be read as an independent second confirmation.

### It is not `e79e4bf66` — please do not close this as a duplicate of that commit

`e79e4bf66` ("ggml-hip : remove -funsafe-math-optimizations", #26696) is **present in every
tested tree and does not fix this.** It is the obvious suspect and it matched on every checkable
detail:

- its message describes `-fassociative-math` reassociating FP reductions and *"can flip greedy
  argmax on **RDNA3.5** (e.g. **MTP speculative decode** diverging from the non-speculative
  baseline)"*;
- the hardware here is gfx1151, which **is** RDNA3.5;
- one of the failing workloads runs `--spec-type draft-mtp`;
- an older tree used here still carries the flag at `ggml/src/ggml-hip/CMakeLists.txt:130`,
  while every tree tested above does not.

With that flag already removed, the defect reproduces at 0/16. This is either a second,
independent problem or the same one with another cause.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Build | stock `b21e4de74567f`; also reproduced on `3a653fea932e` |
| GPU | gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU), 128 GB unified memory |
| ROCm | 7.2.4 (hipcc 7.2.53211-97f5574fe2, AMD clang 22.0.0git roc-7.2.4) |
| OS | Linux |
| Build flags | `-DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=<rocm>/lib/llvm/bin/clang++ -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=ON` |

## Server flags — identical on both backends, only the binary differs

```
-ngl 999 --flash-attn on
--ctx-size 65536 --ubatch-size 1024 --batch-size 2048
--parallel 1 --threads 16
--cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16
--cache-prompt --cache-reuse 256 --cache-ram 0
--ctx-checkpoints 32 --checkpoint-min-step 8192
--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0
--jinja        # each model uses its own embedded chat template
```

Verified byte-identical with `diff` between the two launcher files; the only differences are a
comment header, the slot-save path, and the binary path.

## Causes eliminated, each by changing ONE variable

Listed so nobody spends replies asking. Every row was measured; all remained failing:

| varied | result |
|---|---|
| Context depth | not the cause — 1 tool at 36,335 tokens is 5/5 correct, *longer* than the failing case |
| Tool count | not the cause — 17 tools at 1,349 tokens is 6/6 correct |
| Total prompt length | not the cause — see the 36,335-token row above |
| KV cache type | `q4_0`, `q8_0`, `f16` all fail |
| Flash attention | `--flash-attn off` still fails; it changes the failure *mode*, not the failure. (Note `--flash-attn off`

## Bug report: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4exp) garbage output on SM110 (Jetson Thor) when >8 layers offloaded to GPU

**Hardware**: NVIDIA Jetson Thor (SM110, Blackwell), aarch64, 122GB unified memory, CUDA 13.0
**llama.cpp**: master `035e227` (llama: hold the qwen4exp indexer cache in a new llama_memory_hybrid_idx), built with:
`-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=110 -DGGML_CUDA_FA=ON -DGGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON -DGGML_CUDA_NCCL=ON`
**Model**: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` UD-IQ4_XS (93.7GB, 3 split shards, qwen4exp arch)

### Symptom
- `llama-cli -ngl 8` (layers 0-7 on GPU): output is **fully coherent** ✅
- `llama-cli -ngl 9` or more (layers 0-8+ on GPU): output is **garbage** (incoherent token salad) ❌
- `llama-cli -ngl 0` (pure CPU): fully coherent ✅
- Same model works coherently on CPU; prefill/decode rates are sane in all cases (no crashes, no CUDA errors logged)

### What was excluded (all still garbage at `-ngl 999`)
- flash attention on/off
- `--no-mmap`
- PLE table forced to CPU (`--override-tensor per_layer_token_embd=CPU`)
- `GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1`
- rebuild with `-DGGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=OFF`
- `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1`
- layers 8-9 pinned to CPU via `--override-tensor` (blk.8.*/blk.9.*) while all other layers on GPU

### Additional data points
- The exact same build flags run **Ling-3.0-tiny** (a different MoE/linear-attention arch) on this same box at 88-90 tok/s with fully coherent output — so SM110 CUDA generally works.
- The qwen4exp garbage appears from the first generated token, and (without EOS) generation loops indefinitely writing huge logs.
- Threshold is exactly at the 9th offloaded layer (index 8); `-ngl 8` stable, `-ngl 9` always broken across many attempts.

### Suspected area
A scale-dependent CUDA path in the qwen4exp hybrid memory / QSA indexer (the recently refactored `llama_memory_hybrid_idx`), or a kernel launch path that corrupts silently once GPU-resident layers exceed ~8.

Happy to run any additional diagnostics or test candidate fixes on this hardware.

items.body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.1.2-dev (build 10540, commit 07822bddf)
built with GNU 16.1.1 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395)

### Models

Ling-3.0-flash-Q5_K_M from https://huggingface.co/bloomer010/Ling-3.0-flash-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

In a multi-turn tool using chat, the model sometimes emits `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` from inside its reasoning channel and stops without ever closing `</think>`. The whole turn is then swallowed into reasoning_content.

Root cause
Bailing V3 has no specialized parser in common/chat.cpp, so it falls through to the generic autoparser, which sets a single reasoning terminator (`thinking_end_tags = {"</think>"}`) with no <tool_call> fallback. When the model opens a tool call before closing `</think>`, nothing terminates reasoning and the output is mis-routed.

Behaviour like this is already handled for some other models (these thinking+tool models add tool call openers as reasoning terminators).

For example:
Qwen3-Coder: `thinking_end_tags = {"</think>", "<tool_call>"}`
DeepSeek V3.2: `thinking_end_tags = {THINK_END, FC_START}`
Kimi K2 (common_chat_params_init_kimi_k2) handles this exact behavior, with the maintainer comment: "this model is CRAZY … it can call tools at the end of reasoning without closing reasoning", and adds `<|tool_calls_section_begin|> / <|tool_call_begin|>` as terminators.
Bailing V3's Kimi-K2-like tendency to call tools mid-reasoning isn't covered by the generic autoparser.

Suggested fix
Add <tool_call> to Bailing V3's reasoning terminators (similar to Kimi K2/Qwen3-Coder fixes)

Reproduction code I used to test this exact behaviour which produces a high fail rate with Ling 3.0 flash:
https://gist.github.com/chielteuben/54efbb6b1a75eb7310246f34c54e3465

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

Easily reproduceable using the gist I added.

items.body:
## Overview

An opt-in `--no-fallback` flag for llama-quantize that will exit with an error when tensor shapes would otherwise force a
fallback quant - before any tensor data is read. More information can be found in the issue #26616 with related
discussion.

_This PR contains_:

- Opt-in flag on `llama-quantize`. When any tensor shape would force a type substitution, it errors out before any
  tensor data is read, through the same error path the `imatrix` check uses, so the tool exits non-zero
- Why a flag: dry run reports the substitutions but cannot gate on them. `--dry-run --no-fallback` is a preflight check
  that finishes in seconds
- The existing end-of-run fallback warning now carries a summary in both modes:
    - count
    - parameter share
    - byte share
    - nominal versus actual bpw
    - the recipe's own no-substitution bpw
    - the substitutions grouped by column count and type pair, largest first, capped at eight lines. Per-tensor warning
      lines are unchanged
- New field in the public params struct, default off, inserted after dry_run the same way dry_run was added. Pointer
  members after it shift so any code built with the old struct layout must rebuild; identical trade to
  the [dry-run PR](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/19526)
- Help text and README bullet

## Additional information

- Ref: #26616
- Ref: PR #3747 as the PR that introduced the fallback behavior
- Parity with [ggufaudit](https://github.com/JoshBolding/ggufaudit):
    * same units and denominators as ggufaudit: tensor count, % of params, % of bytes, bpw; projected bpw exact on
      lmstudio's Q4_K_M, within 0.01 bpw on bartowski's imatrix quant
    * the ggufaudit census count runs n+1 per affected model: output.weight. The recipe itself sends it to Q8_0
      when its width is not a multiple of 256 so it never reaches `tensor_type_fallback()` and is not a substitution;
      ggufaudit cannot tell a recipe choice from a fallback. Nemotron below: 141 in the banner, 142 in the ggufaudit
      census row for the same 417-tensor model
    * i-quant rungs: without the maker's imatrix the recipe requests different types (q2_K where the ggufaudit census
      file has IQ2_XXS), so counts and bpw agree but type names differ
    * non-256 labels (Q4_0 etc.): ggufaudit does not apply its test; the flag still catches the substitution
- Testing details:
    * macOS arm64, Debug, LLAMA_FATAL_WARNINGS=ON, GGML_OPENMP=OFF
    * full build of all targets clean; ctest -L main subset (ci/run.sh's Debug set) 50/50; test-quant-type-selection
      pass
    * both no-fallback modes on the 61 GiB BF16 return in <1s and write nothing to disk
    * full ci/run.sh run locally, 100% tests pass

### Examples

#### Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B, public BF16 (61 GiB, 417 tensors; https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16)

**Note**: I used llama.cpp's convert_hf_to_gguf.py to produce the gguf file used. This matches the unsloth and bartowski
HF repo files in tensor layout, 417 tensors.

##### dry run, fail on substitution

exit code 1, output file not written

```
$ ./build/bin/llama-quantize --dry-run --no-fallback ~/models/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b-BF16.gguf /tmp/out.gguf Q4_K_M
...
warning: blk.52.ffn_up_shexp.weight           - ncols   2688 not divisible by 256 (required for type    q4_K) -> falling back to    q5_0

============================================================================
 ERROR: 141 of 417 tensor(s) have shapes incompatible with their target types
        and fallback quantization is disabled (see warnings above)
        - substituted: 141 tensors, 97.9% of params, 97.6% of bytes
        - nominal:     q4_K 4.50 bpw -> 6.18 bpw with substitutions (+37.3%)

## Overview
TL;DR:  3-7x faster CPU mul_mat using VNNI with IMO minimal complexity

I noticed that the vec_dot approach currently taken for mul_mat duplicates the work of unpacking quants a bunch of times.  I put together a generic tiled mul_mat that works with 256x256 windows of int8.  We slide a 256-long window across the source tensors, unpacking quants 256x256 at a time, (this amortizes the unpacking work 256x compared to baseline), and then we sweep an optimized 16x16 microkernel across them to build up a 256x256 float32 output tile.  If this results in too little work for our number of CPUs, I step down the chunk size to 128, 64 etc so that we have more chunks to saturate available cores.

For tall src1 (prefills), this results in 3-7x performance gain (2x compared to repack) on my x86 machine using the optimized microkernel.  The gain goes away as we shrink the rows in src1, reaching break-even at 32 rows and falling behind to 80% of stock performance at pure GEMV.  Error rates are on the order of 5e-04 for max single scalar error, 6e-05 for RMSE across the whole tensor compared to standard vec_dot based mul_mat (microscopically better than repack).  

Integration with the main mul_mat path is similar to llamafile, we return false if we don't support or if we think it will be unprofitable (< 64 rows).

The majority of the code is portable C++ with only the microkernel and 3 inlined bit-unpacking routines as pieces to fill in for a new architecture.  This means we could expand the approach to ARM and other architectures with minimal code addition.

So far, this only supports the k-quant types.  I'm reasonably sure we could expand it to the iq-quants as well, but I haven't gone through all of them to ensure their codebooks stay in bounds of the range my unpacked tiles support.


## Additional information

The VNNI path has some additional complexity.  VNNI takes one chunk of 4 scalars from src0, broadcasted 16x to a 512 bit vector  from one row, and another vector of 4 scalars each from 16 columns of src1 all packed together to execute 16 partial dot products.  This requires a somewhat ugly additional repack of the q8_k quants to enable contiguous reads in the VNNI kernel.  I gated it away from everything else so it only exists for VNNI (and other future archs which may require bespoke packing).  The normal path for AVX2 and other future archs can ignore it.

We assume that K % 256 == 0, this seems safe given that all of the quant types we support use QK_K = 256.

Benchmarks all run using 8 threads on an AMD 9950x3D.  Used 8 instead of 16 to reduce impact of the rest of the system on the benchmarks (it's my desktop).
