items.body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 9960 (a935fbffe)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000099 for Darwin arm64
```

Homebrew build, Metal backend.

### Operating systems

Mac (macOS 26.5.1, build 25F80), Apple M5, 24 GB unified memory.

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Ornith-1.0-35B-UD-Q3_K_M.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 262144 -np 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa auto --port 8080
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When a Metal allocation fails during init, the server logs the failure, logs that the
backend is unrecoverable, and then finishes starting up anyway. It prints `model loaded`,
binds the port, and answers `/health` with `{"status":"ok"}`. Every completion request
after that returns HTTP 500.

The per-request errors are reported correctly, so this isn't silent corruption. The
problem is that startup completes and `/health` reports ready for a process that can
never serve a request. Anything using `/health` as a readiness probe treats it as up.

I should say up front that `-ngl 99` disabled the auto-fit that would otherwise have
prevented this:

```
W common_fit_params: failed to fit params to free device memory: n_gpu_layers already set by user to 99, abort
```

So the OOM itself is arguably my own fault. The part I think is still a bug is what
happens afterwards — the backend reports itself unrecoverable and the server starts
anyway.

Steps:

1. Pick a context size where the allocation cannot fit. On a 24 GB M5 the Metal device
   reports 18186 MiB, and this model at `-c 262144` needs 19005 MiB. llama.cpp's own
   memory breakdown says so directly:
   ```
   cmn  common_param:   - MTL0    : Apple M5 (18186 MiB, 18185 MiB free)
   load_tensors:  MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 15897.19 MiB
   llama_kv_cache:       MTL0 KV buffer size =  2720.00 MiB
   common_memory_breakdown_print: |   - MTL0 (Apple M5)    | 18186 = ... + (19005 = 15897 +    2782 +     325) +         398 |
   ```
   At `-c 65536` the KV cache drops to ~680 MiB and it fits.
2. Start the server with the command line above.
3. 15 `Insufficient Memory` errors during init, then the backend declares itself
   unrecoverable and the decode fails.
4. Server prints `model loaded` and `listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080`.
5. `/health` → 200 `{"status":"ok"}`.
6. Any completion request → 500, and the OOM count roughly doubles.
7. Re-run at `-c 65536` and the same model starts and serves normally.

### What I'd expect

Exit non-zero at startup, the way other unrecoverable init failures already do — a
quantized V cache without flash attention returns `nullptr` and the server refuses to
start (b9960 `src/llama-context.cpp:3518`; on master the same check is at `:3602`,
reworded to `quantized V cache requires flash_attn to be enabled`).

Failing that, `/health` should reflect it. It currently returns `{"status":"ok"}`
unconditionally once the model is marked loaded (b9960
`tools/server/server-context.cpp:4322`, master `:4448`); the only gate is the
server-state middleware, which fires solely on `!is_ready`.

### Relevant log output

Init (timestamps and log-level prefixes trimmed):

```
ggml_metal_synchronize: error: command buffer 0 failed with status 5
error: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
   ... 15 occurrences ...
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
graph_compute: ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async failed with error -1
process_ubatch: failed to compute graph, compute status: -1
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
cmn  common_conte: llama_decode() failed: -3
srv  llama_server: model loaded
srv  llama_server: listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080
```

One completion request afterwards:

```
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
srv        decode: Compute error. off = 0, n_batch = 2048, ret = -3
srv    send_error: task id = 0, error: Compute error.
srv  update_slots: decode() failed: Compute error.
```

Observed from the client:

```
$ curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' localhost:8080/health
{"status":"ok"}
200

$ curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' localhost:8080/completion \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"prompt":"int add(int a,int b){","n_predict":20,"temperature":0}'
{"error":{"code":500,"message":"Compute error.","type":"server_error"}}
500
```

`Insufficient Memory` count: 15 after init, 28 after one request, 29 including shutdown.

### Notes

Reproduced on b9960 (`a935fbffe`). I haven't run master, but both relevant paths look
unchanged there: the init probe still treats a failed `llama_decode` as non-fatal and
continues (master `common/common.cpp:1576`, b9960 `:1497`), and `/health` is still
unconditional. Worth confirming against master before acting on it.

One model, one machine, Metal only. Speculative decoding was not involved
(`speculative decoding not supported by this context` appears in the log).

### Name and Version

E:\lamma-cpp\llama-bin-win-cuda-x64>llama-server.exe --version
version: 0.3.0-dev (build 10679, commit 50f068fff) built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x64
```

Also reproduced on b10639 and on current master sources (checked `src/llama-memory-recurrent.cpp` and `tools/server/server-context.cpp` — identical in master).

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA, CPU

### Hardware

Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 96 GB RAM, RTX 4080 16 GB + RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB (tensor-split across both, `-sm tensor -ts 1,1`)

### Models

Ornith-1.5-35B Q8_0 (qwen3_5_moe architecture: 48 Gated DeltaNet layers + 10 attention layers, embedded MTP) + mmproj BF16 vision projector

https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When using llama-server with a hybrid (recurrent/DeltaNet) multimodal model, the server dies mid-request in real workloads where text messages and image recognition requests alternate (my agent client re-sends the full conversation history each turn, cache_prompt on). The process exits silently; Windows Event Log records `0xc00000fd` (STACK_OVERFLOW) or `0xc0000005` (ACCESS_VIOLATION) in ggml-base.dll, or `0xc0000409` (fail-fast) in ucrtbase.dll.

Key observations:

1. Right before dying, the log fills with repeated warnings from `llama_memory_recurrent::find_slot`:
```
W find_slot: non-consecutive token position 49799 after 49798 for sequence 0 with 128 new tokens
W find_slot: non-consecutive token position 49799 after 49799 for sequence 0 with 128 new tokens
(repeats ~20x at the same frozen position, then)
W find_slot: non-consecutive token position 49853 after 49799 for sequence 0 with 4 new tokens
I slot print_timing: ... prompt processing, progress = 1.00
<process exits>
```

2. Deterministic reproducer: with `-b 1024 -ub 1024` the crash happens on the FIRST image turn (access violation in ggml-base.dll at offset 0x1c620, before "encoding image slice" is even logged). 100% reproducible across b10639 / b10679 / master. With `-ub 128` the same workload instead produces a fixed number of `non-consecutive` warnings per image turn (+18 with `--image-min-tokens 1024`, +4 without) and the server survives short tests, but real agent sessions (~50K context, multiple images, streaming) eventually crash the same way.

3. Server command for the deterministic repro (any CUDA GPU works; two-GPU split is not required for the warning storm):
```
llama-server -m Ornith-1.5-35B-Q8_0.gguf --mmproj mmproj-Ornith-1.5-35B-BF16.gguf ^
  -c 249856 --flash-attn on --split-mode tensor --tensor-split 1,1 -ngl 99 ^
  -np 1 -t 16 -b 1024 -ub 1024 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --jinja --reasoning-preserve
```
Then: (a) send one ~38K-token text turn via /v1/chat/completions, let it finish; (b) send a second request with full history plus one small image (base64 data URL). The server dies during step (b) right after `launch_slot_`.

A self-contained reproduction script is attached (**repro-server-crash.sh**, bash + curl only, no other dependencies; the test image is embedded as base64). Run it while the server is up:

```
./repro-server-crash.sh killer   # expects: [turn 1] http=200, then SERVER DIED on image turn
./repro-server-crash.sh soak     # alternating turns; grep the server log for
                                 # "find_slot: non-consecutive token position" (grows per image turn)
```

Verified output on my machine (killer mode):

```
[turn 1] sending text preamble (~1350 items, ~38K tokens)...
[turn 1] http=200
[turn 2] sending image turn (the server dies here with -b 1024 -ub 1024)...
[turn 2] http=000
SERVER DIED on image turn (expected in killer mode)
```

4. Root-cause analysis (from reading the source):

- The warning is emitted at `src/llama-memory-recurrent.cpp:651`, where the comment admits: "Clearing the state mid-batch would require special-casing which isn't done."
- `llama_memory_recurrent::seq_rm` (`src/llama-memory-recurrent.cpp:150-193`) returns `false` when a partial rollback is larger than the snapshot ring (`n_rs_seq`) or a pending rollback exists. The caller does not handle this failure: the stale recurrent tail is never rolled back, and subsequent ubatches walk over stale cells (the frozen-position warning storm).
- In `tools/server/server-context.cpp` (~line 3233) the divergence path only restores a context checkpoint / forces full re-processing when `pos_min >= pos_min_thold`. For a non-SWA hybrid model `pos_min` stays 0, so this safety net never fires; `slot.prompt.tokens.keep_first(n_past)` truncates the token list, but the recurrent state keeps the discarded tail.
- Independently of cache divergence, every image turn injects non-consecutive positions into the recurrent memory via the mtmd embedding-decode passes (this happens even in a fresh conversation with a single image), which is where the warnings and the state pollution originate.
- Net effect: the SSM/DeltaNet state silently continues from a position that includes discarded tokens (visible output degradation: the model "sees" stale content), and with certain batch geometries (`-ub 1024` observed) the process crashes inside ggml-base.dll.

5. What does NOT help (all tested): removing `--reasoning-preserve`; `--cache-reuse 64`; `--ctx-checkpoints 4`; `--image-min-tokens 512` instead of 1024. `--cache-reuse` is explicitly disabled for mtmd prompts in server-context.cpp (`can_cache_reuse = ... && !slot.prompt.tokens.has_mtmd`), so it cannot apply here.

6. The same warning pattern appears in multimodal smoke-test logs of third-party projects (e.g. elizaOS plugin-local-inference verify JSONs: `find_slot: non-consecutive token position 4 after 3 ...`), which suggests the mtmd + recurrent path is generally affected, not specific to my setup. A llama.cpp-derivative build (beellama v11207) shows identical warnings with the same model.

7. Note on `llama-completion`: the issue lives in the server's slot/prompt-cache handling, so it cannot be re

## Overview

Follow up to #28086, applying the same `mul_mv` row split from `iq3_xxs` to the six other IQ kernels with the same thread mapping:

* `iq1_s`
* `iq1_m`
* `iq2_xxs`
* `iq2_xs`
* `iq2_s`
* `iq3_s`

These kernels assign one 32-element chunk to each simdgroup lane with `ix = tiisg`. When `nb32 < 32`, some lanes have no chunk to process. At `ne00 = 512`, 16 of 32 lanes are idle; at `ne00 = 256`, 24 are idle.

As in #28086, when `nb32 < 32` and `nb32` divides 32, the idle lanes share the existing chunks and split the `nr0` output rows between them.

The split path uses `N_R0_*_SPLIT = 8`. The non-split path keeps the existing `N_R0_* = 4` and the original thread mapping.

K-quants are left out because they use different thread mappings as mentioned before.

## Testing

```sh
./build/bin/test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT    -b MTL0
./build/bin/test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID -b MTL0
```

* `MUL_MAT`: 1256/1256 against CPU
* `MUL_MAT_ID`: 810/810 against CPU
* Covers `k = 256` on the split path and `k = 768` on the non-split path

## Performance

All measurements were run on an Apple M5 24gb (macOS 26.6.2), on AC power, against master `f3f1a8f27`.

### Kernels

```sh
./build/bin/test-backend-ops perf -b MTL0 --test-file shapes.txt
```

`shapes.txt` contains `MUL_MAT` cases with `src0 = [k, 4096]` and `src1 = [k, 1]`, for `k` in {256, 512, 768, 1024, 4096} across the seven IQ types.

The default `perf` set does not include these narrow shapes. Its quantized `MUL_MAT` cases use `k >= 2048`, so they do not take the split path, I used --test-file shapes.txt to run k = 256, 512, 768, 1024, 4096 across the seven IQ types; the file is included below so the results can be reproduced.

| `iq2_s`   | -50.1% | -27.2% |
| `iq3_s`   | -53.1% | -30.1% |

Median across these 12 shapes is **-37.2%**. Keeping the original `N_R0 = 4` and applying only the thread remapping gives **-30.9%**, so most of the gain comes from the remapping.

`iq3_xxs`, already fixed by #28086, was measured in the same runs and stayed within 1.5% of master.

For the non-split shapes (`k = 768, 1024, 4096`, 18 measurements), the median change is **+1.0%**, with a range of -2.3% to +2.7%. Spread between repeated runs is of similar size, so I cannot distinguish a consistent effect on these shapes. The non-split path keeps the existing `N_R0 = 4` and original thread mapping.

### End to end

`bartowski/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF` has 512-wide expert tensors, which use the split path.

```sh
./build/bin/llama-bench -m Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-IQ2_XXS.gguf \
  -fa 1 -ub 512 -p 512 -d 0,4096,16384 -r 3 -n 64 -t 1
```

The same command was run with the IQ2_XS and IQ2_S model files.

Token generation, master -> patch -> master (ABA), with the patch compared against the mean of the two master runs:

| quant     |  tg64 | tg64 @ d4096 | tg64 @ d16384 |
| --------- | ----: | -----------: | ------------: |
| `IQ2_XXS` | +3.6% |        +5.2% |         +1.7% |
| `IQ2_XS`  | +4.0% |        +0.8% |         +3.3% |
| `IQ2_S`   | +2.8% |        +3.3% |         +4.5% |

All nine token-generation measurements improved, with a median of **+3.3%**.

Prefill over the same nine cases ranged from -7.8% to +3.7% with no consistent direction. The two master runs differed by as much as 10% on prefill. These batches use `mul_mm` / `mul_mm_id`, which this patch does not change.

items.title: Eval bug: MTP retains inter-request state causing non-deterministic output and model degradation (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP)

items.body:
## Overview

This fixes `create_checkpoint()` deleting the checkpoint a later rewind needs whenever the prompt is shorter than `checkpoint_min_step`.

`create_checkpoint()` currently runs a spacing eviction before appending the new checkpoint. Walking from the oldest entry, it removes checkpoints from another task whose `n_tokens` is within `checkpoint_min_step` (8192 by default) of the previous surviving checkpoint. On prompts shorter than 8192 tokens, effectively every checkpoint falls within that range, so only the oldest one survives.

This removes the recent checkpoint that the prompt-fill loop placed near the end of the prompt at `n_tokens - 4` (`checkpoint_offsets = {4 + n_ubatch, 4}`, #20288). For hybrid/recurrent models, whose recurrent state cannot simply be rolled back, that recent checkpoint is the useful one when a later request rewinds the conversation.

The functional change is about ten lines: apply the spacing rule only once the checkpoint list has reached `n_ctx_checkpoints`, which already provides a hard capacity bound, and replace an existing checkpoint at the same `n_tokens` instead of appending a duplicate.

I found this while replaying a coding-agent transcript on `Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B-MTP-UD-IQ3_XXS.gguf` (HF: `peculiar-ragdoll/Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B-GGUF-MTP`), a dynamic UD-IQ3_XXS re-quantization of Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B. It is a hybrid GDN MoE: 30 of its 40 trunk layers use Gated DeltaNet recurrent state and only 10 use full attention with a KV cache, so rewinding requires restoring the recurrent state from a checkpoint.

The symptom was that reopening each session caused a few hundred already-cached tokens to be processed again, while the server log repeatedly printed `erasing context checkpoint too close`.

**When it shows.** Normal linear chat is unaffected: each turn resumes from the checkpoint created by the previous request before that checkpoint can be evicted. Switching between conversations is also unaffected because the prompt cache saves and restores the slot together with its checkpoints.

The problem appears when a request rewinds within a conversation after it has already advanced: editing or branching an earlier turn, agent harnesses that retry or compact a session, or reopening a session at an earlier point.

Tested on my 14inch MacBook Pro M5 24 GB and my 16inch MacBook Pro M1 Pro 32 GB.

## Additional information

**Stock Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M (Unsloth), `upstream/master = 7798007`, M5**, using 6 turns of ~150 tokens after a 390-token system prompt, then editing turn 4, continuing for two more turns, and finally regenerating the last answer. Generation was greedy with 120-token replies. `prompt_n` is the number of tokens `llama-server` actually processed:

| step                     | master `prompt_n` | master prompt ms | PR `prompt_n` | PR prompt ms |
| ------------------------ | ----------------: | ---------------: | ------------: | -----------: |
| turns 2-6, each          |           144-154 |          440-448 |       144-154 |      440-451 |
| edit turn 4 after turn 6 |               702 |             1459 |            26 |          229 |
| turns 5-6 again          |           145-149 |              448 |       145-149 |      449-451 |
| regenerate last answer   |                 4 |               69 |             4 |           67 |
| total, 9 warm requests   |              1753 |             4647 |          1077 |         3407 |

Both sides produced the same greedy output.

**Same scenario on the M1 Pro**, run as master, PR, then master again as an ordering control:

| step                                                       | master            | PR              | master again      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------- | ----------------- |
| turns 2-6, prompt ms per turn                              | 840-1176          | 831-846         | 840-851           |
| edit turn 4 after turn 6                                   | 704 tok / 3355 ms | 26 tok / 264 ms | 704 tok / 3323 ms |
| regenerate last answer                                     | 4 tok / 102 ms    | 4 tok / 101 ms  | 4 tok / 101 ms    |
| `erasing context checkpoint too close` lines in server log | 23                | 0               | 23                |

The ordering control reproduces the original behavior after the PR run, which makes the edit-turn difference unlikely to be explained by thermal state or cache warming.

**Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B-MTP-UD-IQ3_XXS (Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B, hybrid GDN MoE), `b10488` tree, M5**, using a fixed replay of a 3-session coding-agent transcript, 13 generations, and a ~5.6K-token system prompt, measured as the mean of 3 warm repetitions. Each repetition reopens the sessions at turn 1, which exercises the rewind case.

The three session openers re-processed 260/254/272 tokens before the patch and 40/34/52 after it. Total warm re-processed tokens per repetition dropped from 2436 to 1776, and warm wall time from 18.25 to 17.12 s (−6.2%). In the same plain-chat edit-turn-4 scenario used above, re-processed tokens dropped from 715 to 26.

**Memory.** Master effectively retains 2 to 4 checkpoints on short prompts because the spacing pass removes the rest. After this change, a slot may retain up to `n_ctx_checkpoints` checkpoints before the existing capacity rule starts evicting them.

At the default limit of 32, that means up to 32 times the model's checkpoint state size: about 74 MiB per checkpoint on Tiel and 50 MiB on Qwen3.5-9B. The highest observed usage in the agent replay was 8 live checkpoints / 596 MiB after duplicate positions were removed, and the Qwen3.5-9B chat reached 13 live checkpoints.

`--ctx-checkpoints` already provides an explicit bound. A byte-based budget in addition to the count would be a reasonable follow-up, but I would prefer to keep that separate from this eviction fix unless maintainers want it included here.

items.body:
(First time filing an issue here, sorry if I get some formatting wrong.)

Quick disclosure since it's relevant to how thorough this writeup is: I noticed my self-hosted fitness app's AI chat was giving wrong/missing results when I asked about two foods in one message. I used Claude Code (I run it locally against my own model-serving box) to help dig into why. It's the one that actually ran the isolation tests below, ruling out MTP, ruling out `--reasoning-preserve`, checking whether it was tool-count vs. one specific tool, capturing the `--verbose` log that found the actual grammar issue, and searching for related issues. I'm filing this myself, in my own words, based on what we found.

### Name and Version

```
$ ./llama-server --version
version: 0.3.0-dev (build 1, commit c1d0e7a)
```
Debian 13 (trixie), built with GCC 14.2.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

2x AMD RX 6900 XT, 16GB each (gfx1030 / Navi 21), split across both cards with tensor-split. ROCm 7.2.4 from AMD's own repo, no dkms.

### Models

Main one: Qwen3.8-27B, the unsloth `UD-Q5_K_XL` GGUF quant, running with `reasoning_effort: low` via `--chat-template-kwargs`. Also tested and affected: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP and Qwen3.6-27B-MTP (both unsloth GGUFs, UD-Q4_K_XL).

Tested and NOT affected on the identical schema: Gemma 4 26B-A4B (unsloth `UD-Q4_K_XL` GGUF + mmproj), `--chat-template-kwargs {"enable_thinking":true}`, vendor sampling (temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64, min_p 0.0), `-ctk f16 -ctv f16`, `-b 2048 -ub 1024`, 64k ctx.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I run a home server setup with a bunch of local apps hitting llama-server through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, one of them is a self-hosted fitness/nutrition app (SparkyFitness, open source) that has a "food" tool with a lot of optional fields (48 of them, one action enum plus params for every possible action). When I ask it to look up two foods at once ("how many calories in 200g chicken breast and 150g rice"), instead of getting two separate tool calls back I get one, and it's broken: the `"action"` key shows up multiple times in the same JSON arguments, duplicated, and the actual field I need (the food name) just isn't there at all. Technically still valid JSON I guess (duplicate keys, last one counts) so it doesn't error out, it just silently returns garbage.

I got a `--verbose` log of one of these requests and found what's actually going on: llama-server logs the full compiled grammar for tool calls, and for this one tool the grammar only has ONE of its 48 parameters in it:

```
tool-sparky-manage-food ::= ("<function=" "sparky_manage_food" ">\n") ((tool-sparky-manage-food-arg-action)*) "</function>\n"
```

Compare a tool with 3 params, all present:

```
tool-sparky-get-food-diary ::= ("<function=" "sparky_get_food_diary" ">\n") ((tool-sparky-get-food-diary-arg-date | tool-sparky-get-food-diary-arg-start-date | tool-sparky-get-food-diary-arg-end-date)*) "</function>\n"
```

And a bigger tool with 27 params, all present too:

```
tool-sparky-manage-checkin ::= ("<function=" "sparky_manage_checkin" ">\n") ((tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-action | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-entry-date | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-weight-unit | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-steps | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-height | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-height-unit | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-neck | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-waist | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-hips | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-measurements-unit | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-body-fat | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-muscle-mass | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-bone-mass | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-body-water | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-value | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-unit | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-notes | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-data-type | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-mood-tags | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-end-time | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-fasting-status | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-fasting-type | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-sleep-score | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-bedtime | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-wake-time | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-source | tool-sparky-manage-checkin-arg-end-date)*) "</function>\n"
```

So the model isn't confused, it's grammar-constrained into only being able to emit `<parameter=action>` for this one tool, because that's the only alternative that made it into the compiled rule. Given that, repeating "action" several times is the only legal way for it to keep producing tokens inside that function call. The duplicate-key output is a direct result of the grammar, not a separate mistake on top of it.

What I don't know: why 48 params breaks it here but 27 (on `manage_checkin`) doesn't. Two guesses:
1. Some per-tool limit on number of parameters, somewhere between 27 and 48.
2. Some limit on the combined size of the whole grammar across all tools in the request. I have about 50 tools active at once, and `manage_food` is the 12th tool compiled and by far the biggest single one, so if there's a shared budget I first thought it could be running out right around there. But my whole tools-array JSON is only about 42.6 KB, which is well under half of the ~97-98 KB where I found a *different* issue (#25895, below) reports its cumulative-size crossover, so a shared-budget explanation doesn't fit as well as I first thought. The per-tool theory looks more likely to me, but I really don't know.

I tested this 6 times across 3 different food pairs and it happens every single time, doesn't matter if temp is 0 or the normal sampling settings. Two smaller tools called in parallel at the same time work completely fine, no issue at all.

I also ran the exact same setup (same tool schema, same 3 food pairs, same llama-server build) against a different model, Gemma 4, and it was clean every time: 9/9 across 3 reps, correct two separate tool_calls, correct arguments. So it doesn

items.body: ### Name and Version version: 9204 (726704a16) built with GNU 11.4.0 for Linux x86_64 ### Operating systems Linux ### GGML backends Vulkan ### Hardware amd 395 ### Models Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q8_K_XL.gguf ### Problem description & steps to reproduce cmmand: ``` ./llama/llama-default-bin-ubuntu-vulkan-x64/llama-server --flash-attn on --gpu-layers 3000 --fit on --fit-ctx 50000 --no-mmap --api-key cyia -ub 2048 -b 2048 -np 1 --host 0.0.0.0 --model ./models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q8_K_XL.gguf --mmproj ./models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-mmproj-F16.gguf --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --min-p 0.0 --top-k 20 --repeat-penalty 1.0 --presence_penalty 1.5 -cram 32768 --jinja --reasoning off --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6, env: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./llama/llama-default-bin-ubuntu-vulkan-x64 ``` The issue is intermittent and cannot be reliably reproduced. When speculative decoding is enabled, the streaming output may appear to hang abruptly. However, the connection remains active even though no new data is being sent. Since there is no explicit end-of-stream signal, the process only terminates once the configured timeout expires. I first noticed this problem because llama-swap consistently had tasks that exceeded 300 seconds before stopping, and their response content remained perpetually incomplete. Removing the `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6` parameters eliminates the timeout issue. I’ve tested this over several days: with those flags enabled, timeouts occurred a few times each day, but they stopped completely once the parameters were removed. It's worth noting that this timeout issue occurs during speculative decoding, not just with MTP. The same problem was also observed when using the following configuration: `--spec-type ngram-mod --spec-ngram-mod-n-match 24 --spec-ngram-mod-n-min 12 --spec-ngram-mod-n-max 48` ### First Bad Commit unkown ### Relevant log output I'm sorry, but I can't provide that information. This issue occurs randomly and infrequently (with a probability of less than 1%). Each time it happens, we can only determine from the logs that the API call timed out.

Model loads and generates tokens but "content" field in API response is empty or 
contains number spam (e.g. 03129816571033482510583...). All output goes to 
"reasoning_content" as corrupted tokens. On b8477 the same models produce clean 
coherent output in "content".

IMPORTANT CONTEXT - why this is hard to diagnose:
server-intel is a rolling latest tag. Not sure when build/image broke but when I tried most recent build or 2026-06-03 get the broken build. Same 
image tag, completely different behavior depending on pull date. At one point I randomly tested Coder-Next about a week ago and although slow it worked. Now I randomly couldn't get any model 3.5 or above to work without gibberish outputs .... Coder-Next had been working in earlier sessions, then 
silently broke when the image updated i'm guessing, I just can't pinpoint when, unless this is known already.

Pure attention MoE models (qwen3moe arch, no SSM layers) are completely unaffected 
on both builds and work correctly throughout.

Steps to reproduce (using Docker):

1. Pull latest server-intel:
   docker pull ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-intel

2. Run with dual Arc Pro B60:

   docker run --rm \
     --device /dev/dri:/dev/dri \
     --group-add 993 --group-add 44 \
     -e ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0;level_zero:1 \
     -e ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=1 \
     -e UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_LEVEL_ZERO=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_VMM=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_DISABLE_GRAPH=1 \
     -p 8010:8010 \
     ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-intel \
     --model /models/Qwen3-Coder-Next-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
     --ctx-size 8192 \
     --host 0.0.0.0 \
     --port 8010 \
     -ngl 999 \
     --split-mode layer \
     --tensor-split 1,1 \
     --flash-attn off \
     --threads 1

3. For qwen3next: crash during warmup at ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat line:3093
   For qwen35: server starts, responds, but content field is empty or number spam

4. Replace image with server-intel-b8477 — identical command — both symptoms fixed

---

Side note for Ollama SYCL users:

This same regression affects users of https://github.com/eleiton/ollama-intel-arc
— an excellent community-maintained project providing native SYCL Ollama builds 
for Intel Arc GPUs. It is not a bug in that project. Ollama 0.30.2 pins 
LLAMA_CPP_VERSION=b9479 (confirmed via 
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/v0.30.2/LLAMA_CPP_VERSION) which 
pulls the broken llama.cpp commit via FetchContent at build time.

    RUN echo "ec2b787eb" > LLAMA_CPP_VERSION

automatically pick up the fix.

### Name and Version

./llama-cli --version
version: <BUILD> (2d8d612e4)
built with ROCm 7.14 for x86_64-linux-gnu

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo), Radeon 8060S iGPU, gfx1151 / RDNA3.5, 128 GB unified memory.
Two nodes, the second attached via `rpc-server`.

### Models

A 35B-A3B MoE at Q8_0. Any MoE model should do — the fault is in the `MUL_MAT_ID` path.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Since #27621 (`41ef91f7c`), MoE models emit nothing but repeated punctuation (`///////…`) on
gfx1151. The model loads normally, token generation runs at full speed (41 t/s), and every
sampled token is garbage. So this is a numerical fault, not a crash and not a scheduling
failure.

I bisected it to a single condition in `ggml_cuda_should_fuse_mul_mat_vec_q()`
(`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu`):

```diff
-    if (tensor->op == GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID && dst->ne[2] != 1) {
+    if (tensor->op == GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID && dst->ne[2] > get_mmvq_mmid_max_batch(src0->type, cc)) {
         return false;
     }
```

Restoring `dst->ne[2] != 1` on HIP makes the output correct again. Toggling only that
condition flips the behaviour reliably in both directions, so the multi-token
`mul_mat_vec_q_moe` path is where it goes wrong. The single-token path is fine.

**Steps:**

1. Build `master` for gfx1151: `cmake -B build -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151`
2. Run any MoE model and send a prompt of a few hundred tokens (the fusion only engages
   when several tokens share an expert matmul, so a one-word prompt shows nothing)
3. Output is `///////…`
4. Change the condition above back to `dst->ne[2] != 1`, rebuild, output is correct

It reproduces the same way with the RPC backend, where the affected matmuls execute on the
remote worker.

**What I already ruled out:**

- Host and device batch limits agree for RDNA3.5. `GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA3(cc)` and
  `defined(RDNA3)` both select `get_mmvq_mmid_max_batch_rdna3()`, so
  `block_dims(warp_size, ncols_dst)` stays inside the kernel's `__launch_bounds__`.
- The MMVQ parameter tables are not involved. `mul_mat_vec_q_moe` and its launch wrapper
  never call `calc_nwarps()` or `get_device_table_id()`, and use a fixed
  `rows_per_block = 2`.

I have no theory beyond that. Can anyone with RDNA3.0 hardware (gfx1100/gfx1101) check
whether it happens there too? The device path takes the same
`get_mmvq_mmid_max_batch_rdna3()` branch, so if it affects both, this is an RDNA3 issue
rather than an RDNA3.5 one.


### First Bad Commit

41ef91f7c8046087cdfbb276b79bff311ecf1c6d — CUDA: extend MOE fusion to specdec (#27621)

### Relevant log output

can't provide as the model behaves normally in the logs, just output gets '/////////////////'

### Models

- **Ornith 1.5 35B-A3B — I-Compact**
  `Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-APEX-MTP-I-Compact.gguf`
  [Hugging Face – Ornith 1.5 35B-A3B GGUF](https://huggingface.co/AtomicChat/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF)

- **Ornith 1.0 35B — I-Compact**
  [Hugging Face – Ornith 1.0 35B GGUF](https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.0-35B-GGUF)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Summary 
On hybrid SSM/attention MoE models (general.architecture=qwen35moe, carrying ssm.* keys and
full_attention_interval), llama-server grows RSS by a fixed ~126 MiB on every request and never
releases it. Growth is perfectly linear and does not decelerate — 40 consecutive requests took RSS from 1340
MiB to 6379 MiB at exactly +126 MiB each. 
The allocation is anonymous (RssAnon grows; RssFile stays flat at 110 MiB) and is reclaimed only by
restarting the process. 
A non-SSM model on the identical build, GPU and driver does not leak at all (gpt-oss-20b mxfp4: +0 MiB
request over 12 requests), which is what points at the hybrid/recurrent path rather than at the server or the
backend generally. 
Environmentllama.cpp b9722 (159d093a4) and b10673 (f5e85d43a) — identical behaviourBackend ROCm/HIP, -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1100GPU AMD RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, 24 GB)OS Ubuntu, kernel 6.14.0-27-genericCompiler GNU 13.3.0 
Reproduction 
llama-server -m Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-APEX-MTP-I-Compact.gguf \
-ngl 99 --n-cpu-moe 0 --ctx-size 147456 \
--cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0 \
--parallel 1 --jinja --flash-attn on --no-mmap \
--batch-size 4096 --ubatch-size 256 --port 8099

Then repeat any trivial completion and sample VmRSS from /proc/<pid>/status after each: 
curl -s -X POST localhost:8099/v1/chat/completions \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"one obscure fact, briefly."}],"max_tokens":40}'

Observed (b10673, 40 requests): 
startreq 12req 24req 36req 40
RSS=1340RSS=2851RSS=4363RSS=5875RSS=6379MiB
MiBMiBMiBMiBdelta=+126
delta=+126
delta=+126
delta=+126
What it is NOT — controlled matrix 
Every row is the same measurement protocol; only the named variable changed.variable value A value B leakllama.cpp build b9722 b10673 (~950 newer) 126.3 / 125.9MTP spec-decode on off 126.5 / 126.3context size 147456 32768 126.3 / 126.3context size 163840 (Ornith 1.0) — 126vision / mmproj on off 126.3 / 126.9max_tokens 220 / 90 40 126.5 / 126.3 / 126KV cache type q4_0 f16 126.3 / 127flash attention on off 126.3 / 127model file Ornith 1.5 Ornith 1.0 (different file) 126 / 126architecture qwen35moe (SSM) gpt-oss-20b (no SSM) 126 / 0 
So it is independent of build, MTP, context length, vision, generated tokens, KV quantization and flash attention
— and it tracks the architecture. 
Why we suspect the recurrent/SSM state path 
The leak is a fixed size per request, unaffected by context length or tokens generated. That matches an
allocation sized by the SSM state dimensions rather than by sequence length. The affected GGUFs carry: 
qwen35moe, ssm.conv_kernel, ssm.group_count,
ssm.inner_size, ssm.state_size, ssm.time_step_rank,
full_attention_interval

Both affected models are hybrid (3 of every 4 layers linear/SSM). The unaffected control model has no ssm.*
keys. 
Our reading is that per-sequence recurrent state is allocated per request and not freed on sequence teardown,
but we have not instrumented the allocator — that part is inference from the measurements above, not
established. 
Impact 
On a 32 GB host this exhausts RAM in roughly 120 requests. In our case that interacted with an amdgpu
VRAM→GTT eviction of the model (~16.6 GB) which then could not fit in host RAM, taking the machine down.
We now mitigate by restarting the lane on an RSS threshold, but the allocation itself looks like a genuine bug

## Summary

Under parallel mixed load (`-np 4 --kv-unified`), `llama-server` on an **integrated HIP GPU** (Strix Halo / gfx1151, 128 GB UMA) returns **complete responses that verbatim belong to a different, earlier request**. A large-prompt request receives, as its entire response, the literal answer text of a short request from an earlier round. We also observed a **chimeric** response fusing tokens of two different requests' expected outputs.

**Bisected to a single commit: c7d87229 "ggml-cuda : restore prop.integrated on HIP builds" (#24233).**

| build | result (validated responses, nonce-checked) |
|---|---|
| 505b1ed1 (parent window start) | clean — 0 violations / 168 |
| 5839ba35 (= parent of c7d87229) | clean — 0 / 36 |
| **c7d87229** | **cross-request replays: 3 hard / 36** |
| e8f19cc0 (window end) | cross-request replays: 7 hard + 1 chimera / 96 |

The same harness against **CPU builds** of both window endpoints shows no build-dependent difference (model-compliance noise only) — consistent with the culprit being the HIP integrated-memory path. This presumably explains why it went unnoticed: discrete GPUs are unaffected; it needs an **integrated** AMD GPU (`prop.integrated == 1`), multiple slots and concurrent mixed traffic.

## Environment

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo), gfx1151, 128 GB unified memory, ROCm 7.14, Ubuntu 24.04
- Build: `cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang++` (Release)
- Server: `llama-server -m <model> -ngl 999 -c 65536 -np 4 --kv-unified --jinja --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'`
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE (Q4-class quant). First hit this in production behind LocalAI (same symptom after its vendored-llama.cpp bump crossed this commit); reproducing on vanilla `llama-server` rules the wrapper out.

## Reproduction

Load pattern per round (~30 s, script below): (B) short "repeat exactly this code: <nonce>" request → (C) large-prompt (~10k tokens) request whose system prompt requires echoing a per-request nonce in the first line → (D) burst of 4 concurrent short nonce requests (2 streamed / 2 plain). Every response is validated to contain its **own** nonce and no nonce of an **earlier** request.

On affected builds the round-N large-prompt request receives a literal foreign nonce as its complete response, typically from a round-(N−1) burst request. Verbatim from run logs at e8f19cc0:

```
R4/C got='pd-20260722-115649-3-d1'      (expected: reply echoing pc-...-4-c + a summary)
R5/C got='pd-20260722-115649-4-d2'
R6/C got='pd-20260722-115649-1-d1'
R7/C got='pd-20260722-115649-6-d1'
R8/C got='pd-20260722-115649-7-d1'
R3/C got='<!-- run:pc-20260722-115649-2-d0 -->'   <-- chimera: pc-...-2 stem fused with a -d0 burst suffix
```

In production we additionally observed: a poisoned slot re-serving its stored answer to unrelated requests **20+ minutes later** (the victim's `usage` then reports the foreign request's token counts), and occasional degeneration into repeated single characters (`/////...`).

<details><summary>repro-crossover.py (needs httpx)</summary>

```python

Each round: (B) short "repeat exactly: <nonce>" request, (C) large-prompt

(D) burst of 4 concurrent short nonce requests (2 streamed / 2 plain).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Hybrid-attention (`qwen35moe`) models generate an **empty completion through `llama-server` when the prompt exceeds a context-dependent threshold (~16.5K with `-c 65536`, ~18-19K with `-c 32768`)**. The response has `predicted_n = 1`, empty `content`, and `eval time = 0.00 ms`. The same setup works fine below the threshold.

**Key refinement discovered while preparing this report (2026-08-20):**

1. **The threshold depends on `-c` (context size)**, not just prompt length:
   - With `-c 65536`: 16.5K prompt tokens fails consistently (3/3 trials), 15.4K works
   - With `-c 32768`: 16.5K works (2/2), 17.6K is **intermittent** (2 pass / 2 fail), 19.8K fails consistently (4/4)
   - This is NOT flash-attn related: reproduced with `--flash-attn on` and off, identical results
2. **There is randomness near the threshold**: the same request at 17.6K (`-c 32768`) succeeded on one attempt and failed on the next, with no code change between them. The failure looks like an uninitialized/stale recurrent-state restore that sometimes happens to work.
3. **Not all DeltaNet/recurrent architectures are affected**: `Mellum2-12B-A2.5B-Thinking` (GGUF, `mellum` arch, 28 layers with fused Gated Delta Net) generates **normally up to 48K prompt tokens** on the same build (`-c 65536`). This isolates the bug to the **`qwen35moe` hybrid attention implementation** (mixed KV-attention + DeltaNet layers), not the DeltaNet operator itself.

The native context length of these models is 262K, so being effectively hard-capped at ~16-19K via the server is a severe practical limitation.

Reproduction (server):

```
llama-server -m <model>.gguf \
  -c 65536 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ngl 99 -np 1 --no-warmup -ub 512 \
  --port 8080
```

Send a chat completion request whose prompt is >= ~16.5K tokens, `max_tokens > 1`.

Boundary sweep results (`-c 65536`, identical across b10470 / dc72703 / b10502):

| prompt tokens | result |
|---|---|
| 111 (short) | OK, 12 tokens generated |
| 15401 | OK, 12 tokens generated |
| 16501 | FAIL - predicted_n=1, empty content, eval 0.00 ms |
| 17601 | FAIL - empty |
| 19801 | FAIL - empty |
| 23981 | FAIL - empty |

Same sweep with `-c 32768` (b10502, no flash-attn):

| prompt tokens | result |
|---|---|
| 15401 | OK |
| 16501 | OK (2/2) |
| 17601 | **INTERMITTENT (2 pass / 2 fail)** |
| 19801 | FAIL (4/4) |
| 23981 | FAIL |

Control: `Mellum2-12B-A2.5B-Thinking-MXFP4_MOE.gguf` (mellum arch, fused Gated Delta Net) with `-c 65536`:

| prompt tokens | result |
|---|---|
| 15401 / 16501 / 17601 / 19801 / 23981 / 30K / 48K | **ALL OK** (12 tokens generated) |

Prefill completes normally and takes the expected time (24K-token prefill ~ 92 s); the failure happens before the first generated token. No crash, no log errors - just an immediate empty completion.

Builds tested, all reproduce:
- Homebrew `llama.cpp` b10470 (commit `34af94cd9`)
- Self-built master `dc72703` (2026-08-19, `GGML_METAL=ON`)
- Official prebuilt b10502 (commit `0adcc3bb5`)
- Earlier: b10450, b10488, PrismML b9599 (also affected)

What has been ruled out:
- **Not memory/swap**: with `-c 65536 -ngl 99` the model loads and runs with zero swap (RSS ~5-11 GiB depending on build; the difference is due to Metal unified-memory mapping changes between builds)
- **Not KV quantization**: reproduced with both f16 and q4_0 KV caches
- **Not flash-attn related**
- **Not the compute graph**: `llama-bench` with a pure graph `pp20000+tg128` succeeds (268.93 t/s) - the graph layer is fine. The bug is in the **server's prompt-cache / context-checkpoint restore path for recurrent layers**
- **Not specific to one build or quant**: 4+ builds and 3 models all reproduce

Workarounds tried (all ineffective):
- `--ctx-checkpoints 0 --cache-reuse 0` - still empty output
- `--cache-ram 0` (disables prompt cache entirely) - still empty output
- `cache_prompt=false` per request - still empty output

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>

Server startup (b10502, truncated):

```console
llama-server -m Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-IQ2_XXS.gguf -c 65536 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ngl 99 -np 1 --no-warmup -ub 512 --port 8093
...
llama_model_load: loading model
...
server is listening on http://127.0.0.1:8093 - starting the main loop
```

Request at 16.5K prompt tokens - empty completion:

```console
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8093/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<16.5K token prompt>"}],"max_tokens":12}'
{"choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":""},"finish_reason":"stop"}], ...}
```

Server timing line for the failing request:

```console
slot print_timing: id  0 | task NNNN | prompt eval time = 55328.02 ms / 16501 tokens (3.35 ms per token, 298 tokens per second)
slot print_timing: id  0 | task NNNN |        eval time =      0.00 ms /     1 tokens
slot print_timing: id  0 | task NNNN |       total time =  55328.02 ms / 16502 tokens
```

</details>

<!-- Long logs that you upload as files go here, outside the "console" area -->

[repro_c32768_noflash.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31267657/repro_c32768_noflash.log)

[repro_c65536_noflash.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31267670/repro_c65536_noflash.log)

### Name and Version

```
$ ./build/bin/llama-cli --version
ggml_cuda_init: found 2 ROCm devices:
  Device 0: AMD Radeon Graphics, gfx906:sramecc+:xnack- (0x906), VMM: no, Wave Size: 64
  Device 1: AMD Radeon Graphics, gfx906:sramecc+:xnack- (0x906), VMM: no, Wave Size: 64
version: 8179 (ecbcb7ea9)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64
```

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

2x AMD Instinct MI50 32GB (gfx906), ROCm 7.0.2

### Models

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (Gated Delta Networks / linear attention architecture)

### Problem description

Related to #19442 (closed as rocBLAS issue).

When running models that use `GGML_OP_SOLVE_TRI` (e.g. Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next, Kimi Linear - all using Gated Delta Networks / linear attention), the operation crashes on gfx906 (MI50) GPUs:

```
rocBLAS error from hip error code: 'hipErrorInvalidDeviceFunction':98
ggml_cuda_compute_forward: SOLVE_TRI failed
```

**Root cause analysis:**

In `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/solve_tri.cu`, the dispatch logic at line 264 is:

```cpp
if (n <= MAX_N_FAST && k <= MAX_K_FAST) {   // MAX_N_FAST=64, MAX_K_FAST=32
    solve_tri_f32_cuda(...)   // custom CUDA/HIP kernel - works fine on gfx906
} else {
    solve_tri_f32_cublas(...)  // calls cublasStrsmBatched -> rocBLAS strsm -> CRASHES on gfx906
}
```

The custom `solve_tri_f32_fast` kernel works perfectly on gfx906 since it uses standard CUDA/HIP intrinsics (warp shuffle, shared memory). The crash only happens when dimensions exceed `n=64` or `k=32`, triggering the `cublasStrsmBatched` (rocBLAS `Strsm`) path.

rocBLAS in ROCm 7.x does not include pre-compiled Tensile kernels for `Strsm` on gfx906, as AMD deprecated gfx906 support since ROCm 5.7. Even the Arch Linux rocBLAS package (which does build for gfx906) does not include Strsm-family kernels.

For Qwen3.5-35B-A3B specifically, the model uses `n=64, k=14` which fits within the fast kernel limits and runs fine. But other models in this family (e.g., Qwen3-Coder-Next with `k=64`) exceed `MAX_K_FAST=32` and crash.

### Workaround

Commenting out `GGML_OP_SOLVE_TRI` from the HIP backend's `ggml_cuda_supports_op()` forces the scheduler to fall back to the CPU backend. This works but is suboptimal:

```cpp
// in ggml-cuda.cu, ggml_cuda_supports_op():
case GGML_OP_TRI:
case GGML_OP_DIAG:
//case GGML_OP_SOLVE_TRI:  // disabled: rocBLAS Strsm lacks gfx906 kernel
    return true;
```

With this workaround, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B runs successfully on dual MI50:
- Prompt processing: 85.7 t/s
- Generation: 48.3 t/s

### Suggested fix

Rather than relying on the rocBLAS `Strsm` fallback (which is broken on multiple older AMD architectures), consider one of:

1. **Extend the custom `solve_tri_f32_fast` kernel** to handle larger dimensions (`k > 32`, `n > 64`). The existing kernel is well-written and uses standard CUDA/HIP primitives - extending it would eliminate the rocBLAS dependency entirely.

2. **Runtime architecture detection for HIP**: In `ggml_cuda_supports_op()`, detect the GPU architecture and return `false` for `GGML_OP_SOLVE_TRI` on architectures known to lack rocBLAS Strsm support (gfx906, and potentially others), allowing automatic CPU fallback.

3. **Graceful fallback**: Instead of crashing, catch the `hipErrorInvalidDeviceFunction` error in `solve_tri_f32_cublas()` and fall back to a CPU implementation or the custom kernel with tiling.

Option 1 would be the most robust solution as it benefits all users and removes the external library dependency for this operation.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx906 -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx906 -B build
cmake --build build --config Release -j$(nproc)

# Run any model using Gated Delta Networks / linear attention with k > 32:
./build/bin/llama-cli -m Qwen3-Coder-Next-MXFP4.gguf -p "Hello" -n 10
# Crashes with: rocBLAS error hipErrorInvalidDeviceFunction
```

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Full error log</summary>

```console
common_init_from_params: warming up the model with an empty run - please wait ...
rocBLAS error from hip error code: 'hipErrorInvalidDeviceFunction':98
/root/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:97: ROCm error
ggml_cuda_compute_forward: SOLVE_TRI failed
ROCm error: invalid device function
  current device: 0, in function ggml_cuda_compute_forward at ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:2758
Aborted
```
</details>

items.body:
## Summary

For recurrent/hybrid-memory architectures that support state rollback (e.g. `LLM_ARCH_QWEN4EXP`, per `llm_arch_supports_rs_rollback()` in `src/llama-arch.cpp`), the rollback mechanism (`n_rs_seq`, checked in `llama_memory_recurrent::seq_rm()`) is only ever populated by `common_params_speculative::need_n_rs_seq()` (`common/common.h`), which returns a nonzero value **only** when `--spec-type` is one of `draft-mtp` / `draft-eagle3` / `draft-dflash` / `draft-dspark`.

In ordinary `llama-server` usage without speculative decoding (the common case for a hybrid/recurrent model serving multi-turn chat), `n_rs_seq` is always `0`. This means:

```cpp
// src/llama-memory-recurrent.cpp, seq_rm()
if (0 < p0 && p0 <= cell.pos && p1 > cell.pos) {
    const llama_pos rollback = cell.pos - (p0 - 1);
    const bool pending = rs_idx[seq_id] != 0;
    if (!pending && rollback >= 1 && rollback <= (llama_pos) n_rs_seq) {
        ...
        return true;
    }
    return false;  // <-- always hit when n_rs_seq == 0
}
```

`seq_rm()` cleanly returns `false` whenever a caller asks for a partial trim (`p0 > 0`) on one of these architectures with no speculative decoding enabled — which is exactly what happens whenever the server's prompt-cache reuse ("LCP similarity" prefix matching in `tools/server`) finds a partial prefix match and tries to trim the KV/recurrent state back to a shared prefix instead of reprocessing the whole prompt.

## Impact

1. The server's prompt-cache-reuse path in `tools/server/server-context.cpp` does not check the return value of this particular `llama_memory_seq_rm()` call before proceeding as if the trim had succeeded. Since it silently returns `false` for these architectures, `n_past` bookkeeping goes out of sync with the actual recurrent/SSM state, and the next decode step reads/writes out of bounds, producing a hard GPU fault:
   ```
   Memory access fault by GPU node-X ... Reason: Page not present or supervisor privilege.
   ```
   Reproducible on the second request that shares a prefix with a previous one (any multi-turn conversation, or even two back-to-back identical requests), with `--cache-prompt` on (default) and `--spec-type none`.

2. A local workaround (checking the return value and forcing `n_past = 0` / full reprocess whenever the partial trim fails) avoids the crash, but every such forced full reprocess appears to leave a small, non-recovering amount of device memory allocated (a few MB per occurrence, observed consistently across all devices in a multi-GPU tensor-split setup). This accumulates over a long multi-turn conversation — since essentially every turn hits this same "partial trim requested, always fails, force full reprocess" path — until the available device memory margin on the tightest device is exhausted, at which point generation degrades to 1-5 tokens per response for the remainder of the session. Confirmed via repeated *identical, fixed-size, independent* requests (no growing context at all) that per-request device memory usage decreases monotonically and plateaus exactly at the point generation starts degrading — which rules out KV-cache/context-size growth or the server's context-checkpoint mechanism (`--ctx-checkpoints`) as the cause.

## Suggested fix directions

- At minimum, guard the general (non-speculative) partial-trim call path in `tools/server/server-context.cpp` the same way the speculative-decoding path already does: check the return value of `llama_memory_seq_rm()` and force a full reprocess when it fails, instead of assuming success. This would at least turn the crash into the (already observed) degraded-but-non-fatal behavior.
- Longer-term: wire `n_rs_seq` for the general server "prompt cache reuse" case too, not only via `common_params_speculative::need_n_rs_seq()`, so architectures that support rollback (per `llm_arch_supports_rs_rollback()`) can use genuine partial rollback outside of speculative decoding, avoiding the repeated full-reprocess + memory-growth pattern entirely.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Serve a GGUF model whose architecture is in `llm_arch_supports_rs_rollback()` (e.g. qwen4exp / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next family) with `llama-server`, `--spec-type none`, default `--cache-prompt`.
2. Send two `/v1/chat/completions` (or `/completion`) requests where the second shares a prefix with the first (e.g. same system+user message, or a growing multi-turn conversation).
3. Without any patch: the second request that hits a partial-prefix cache match crashes the server with a GPU memory access fault.
4. With a patch that checks the `seq_rm()` return value and forces a full reprocess on failure: the crash is avoided, but repeating step 2 many times (even with a constant-size, non-growing prompt) shows device memory usage decreasing monotonically per request, eventually causing generation to degrade to a handful of tokens per response.

## Environment

- llama.cpp build 522 / commit `4d91760` (tag `b10818`), 2026-09-05
- Backend: HIP (ROCm), multi-GPU tensor-split
- Architecture: `qwen4exp` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next family), `--spec-type none`, `--cache-prompt` default (enabled)

items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

## Motivation
In modern agentic workflows (e.g., ReAct, function calling, tool use), models spend significant wall-clock time autoregressively generating tokens just to make discrete routing decisions (e.g., spelling out `<tool_call>\n{"name": "get_weather"...}`).

## What is the proposed solution
A special agent mode to fasten tool calls through "Jev-like" hybrid mode

Currently, when tools are provided in `llama-server` or `llama-cli`:
1. The engine prefills the prompt.
2. It enters the autoregressive decode loop ($O(N)$ sequential token passes) using either GBNF grammar constraints or hoping the chat template emits tool tokens correctly.
3. If the model chooses *not* to call a tool, or chooses a simple tool, we still pay the latency penalty of sequential token decoding and grammar state-machine transitions before knowing the routing outcome.

Because the prompt prefill pass **already computes the full KV cache and logits for the final prompt token**, we can resolve binary tool-gating decisions and tool-name enums in **$O(1)$ single forward passes** via logit slicing, falling back seamlessly to standard text generation without wasting the prefilled KV cache.

---

## Proposed Architectural Flow

```
[Prompt + Registered Tools] 
          │
          ▼
   llama_decode() (Prefill)
          │
          ▼
Inspect logits of last token: P(Tool Call) vs P(Chat/Text)
          │
   ┌──────┴────────────────────────────────┐
   ▼                                       ▼
P(Chat) > Threshold               P(Tool) > Threshold
   │                                       │
   │ (Zero KV cache waste)                 ▼
   │ Direct stream to user        Slice logits over registered 
   │ (Standard Autoregressive)    tool names: P(tool_1...tool_N)
                                           │
                                  ┌────────┴─────────────────┐
                                  ▼                          ▼
                         Bounded Enums/Booleans     Unbounded String Args
                         (Parallel Logit Slices)    (Switch to GBNF / AR loop)
```

### 1. Zero-Cost Gating Check (Prefill Inspection)
Right after `llama_decode()` on the prompt batch, before initializing the autoregressive decode loop:
* Inspect the logits of the final sequence position (`llama_get_logits_ith(ctx, -1)`).
* Measure the probability mass of the model's tool delimiter token (e.g., `<tool_call>`, `[TOOL]`, or `{` depending on the active Jinja chat template) against normal text tokens.
* **If text generation is chosen:** Continue the decode loop immediately. The KV cache is already fully initialized; overhead is virtually $0$ ms.

### 2. $O(1)$ Discrete Tool Selection
If the model indicates a tool call:
* Instead of sequentially generating the tool name string (e.g., `"name": "get_weather_data"` across multiple decode steps), the engine can mask the logits over the first tokens of the user-registered tools:
  $$\text{Softmax}\left(\text{logits}[\text{id}(\text{tool}_1), \text{id}(\text{tool}_2), \dots]\right)$$
* Select the candidate with highest calibrated confidence in a single step.

### 3. Argument Resolution Split
* **Bounded arguments (Enums, Booleans):** Handled via single-pass logit slicing.
* **Unbounded arguments (Raw strings, free text):** Switch back to standard autoregressive generation, with GBNF constrained only to that specific string argument.

---

## Key Benefits
1. **Dramatic Latency Reduction in Agent Loops:** Eliminates 10–50 sequential autoregressive steps for routing decisions, reducing decision latency to the prefill time (~15–40 ms on modern hardware).
2. **Zero Wasted Computation on Fallback:** Because the prompt prefill already took place, falling back to standard conversational text streaming incurs zero recomputation or KV-cache invalidation.
3. **No Syntax Failures for Tool Routing:** Eliminates malformed tool name keys and invalid enum tool selections at the root.

---



## Alternatives Considered
* **Full GBNF Grammar Decoding:** Guarantees syntax correctness, but incurs full sequential decode latency ($O(N)$ forward passes) even for basic if/else decisions.
* **Draft Model Speculative Decoding:** Requires loading a second model into VRAM and doesn't solve the structural inefficiency of using autoregression for discrete enum selection.


### Motivation

Save a lot of inference and compute when performing tool calls

### Possible Implementation


1. **`llama-server` (`/v1/chat/completions`):**
   * Introduce an optional flag, e.g., `--speculative-tool-gating` or a request parameter `"tool_choice": "auto_fast"`.
   * If enabled, check the top-K logits of the prefill output against the model's configured tool-call trigger tokens before attaching the full GBNF grammar parser.
2. **C API (`llama.h`):**
   * Expose a helper utility or sampler stage:
     ```c
     // Evaluates probabilities exclusively across a masked subset of candidate tokens
     // on the current prefilled context position without advancing the decode sequence.
     LLAMA_API void llama_sample_token_distribution(
         struct llama_context * ctx,
         const llama_token    * candidate_tokens,
         size_t                 n_candidates,
         float                * out_probs
     );
     ```

### Edge Case: Multi-Token Tool Names & Shared Prefixes

To handle tools that share initial tokens (e.g., `get_weather` vs `get_stock`):

1. **Trie-Based Logit Slicing:** Construct a Token Trie of registered tools. Non-branchi

items.body:
## Overview
Fixes SYCL VMM pool behavior when the model does not fit in physical VRAM.

The VMM pool keeps committed physical pages for the lifetime of the pool. When temporary allocations reach a size that does not fit in physical VRAM, the driver can spill the committed pages into shared system memory, causing a severe performance drop.

This change makes VMM allocation failure non-fatal by falling back to direct USM allocation, and disables the VMM pool by default.

## Additional information

### Changes

* Fall back to direct USM allocation when a VMM commit fails instead of failing the whole operation.

  * Fallback allocations are tracked so that `free()` uses the corresponding allocation API.
* Disable the VMM pool by default with `GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_VMM=0`.

  * The VMM pool can still be enabled explicitly through the environment variable.

### Performance impact

Measured with Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B Q4_K_M on an Intel Arc B570 with `-ngl 99`:

* Prompt processing with the VMM pool enabled: **0.7 t/s**
* Prompt processing with the VMM pool disabled: **6.2 t/s**

Note: the memory overflow (staging into shared system memory) itself occurs in both builds when the model does not fit in physical VRAM with `-ngl 99`. The official build stages through `sycl::malloc_device` and reaches approximately **25 t/s generation** on the same setup; the VMM pool pinning makes it several times worse. Models that fit in physical VRAM are not affected: the 9B model runs normally with `-ngl 99`, and `-ngl auto` does not overflow.

The GPU memory usage was measured with the Windows GPU performance counters while running the same model with the VMM pool disabled: total committed 20.9 GB, of which 8.6 GB was dedicated (VRAM) and 13.2 GB was non-local (shared system memory) - the staging behavior was observed directly.

### Stability

Running with the VMM pool enabled and a model exceeding physical VRAM was also observed to restart the host system (driver-level instability). The staging state brings the system memory close to its limit, where the process being killed was observed. This further motivates disabling the pool by default.

### Related issue

A memory/access-violation crash in `igdrcl64.dll` was also observed when OpenCL GPUs were enumerated with `ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR` unset. The device enumeration changes in the separate de-dpct work prioritize Level Zero devices and remove that path.

See #29229

## Requirements

* I have read and agree to the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

* AI usage disclosure: **YES - GLM-5.3 Flash via OpenCode was used for analysis, implementation, routine edits, and debugging assistance. The author identified the issue and provided the overall direction for the fix.**

items.body:
## Overview Today the model-based drafters throw away most of what the draft model knows. They run the sampler, discard its result, and take the top candidate, and the target then accepts that token only when its own draw lands on the same one. At temperature 0 that is the best available, since the target also always takes its top token. Above 0, they differ - the target samples while the draft still offers its single safest guess - and acceptance falls away as temperature rises. This PR adds two things to make this better. - Make the target use rejection sampling instead of requiring an exact match. - Despite the above, if the draft still gives its top candidate only, it evaluates to min(1, p(x)/1), same as p(x). Hence to make q(x) land, we make the draft probabilistic as well. This time the effective probability that a candidate is chosen from draft is sum_x(q(x)*min(1, p(x)/q(x))). The output distribution is preserved exactly. Accepting with `min(1, p/q)` and drawing the remainder from `norm(max(0, p - q))` is the standard construction; the residual cancels the over-delivery on tokens where the draft is more generous than the target. This is same as the mechanism in Leviathan et al. This PR applies to draft_simple and MTP only. Eagle3 is yet to be evaluated and DFlash is experimentally seen not to benefit with these changes. The likely reason for this is structural. DFlash reads every position of its block out of a single forward pass with no re-decode between them, so the positions are predicted jointly rather than conditioned on one another. Substituting a sampled token at one position leaves the rest of the block continuing from a token that was never drafted. The gain at that position is cancelled by the positions after it, which no longer follow from what was drafted — unlike draft-simple and draft-mtp, where each token is re-decoded and the substitution carries forward. A flag --spec-draft-sampling is added, controlling how the draft is sampled. It takes greedy or probabilistic, defaulting to greedy. This matches vLLM's convention, where draft_sample_method takes the same two values and also defaults to greedy. I have run sweeps with -bs enabled and disabled along with the changes in this PR. Based on the logs obtained, this PR does not affect the functionality of backend sampling, which ensures that the target sampling chain already happens on the GPU. With -bs on, I see the same accepted length and 1-2% change in throughput, which is consistent with what is observed on the master branch with -bs enabled.
Performance

Two machines, eight model configurations each, 11 temperatures from 0.0 to 1.0. Every run is 12 prompts of 256 tokens at --spec-draft-n-max 3, the shipped default. Temperature 0.0 is the control. ### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I was fighting with 30% cpu usage and decreased GPU utilization on AMD Strix halo machine when running Qwen 3.6 35B MoE Q8 generation on ROCm. Vulkan does not have that problem and needs only ~5% cpu to run tg. 
GLM found this issue in src/llama-model.cpp around line 1300:    
```
// there is very little benefit to offloading the input layer, so always keep it on the CPU
pimpl->dev_input = { cpu_dev, &pimpl->cpu_buft_list };
```
This keeps tok_embd on CPU even with -ngl 99, which forces GET_ROWS(tok_embd, inp_tokens) onto the CPU backend at the start of every forward pass. On Stix Halo where CPU and GPU share same DDR5 it hurts a lot.

Possible fix is to mirror the output-layer policy for the input layer when full offload is requested.

41.33 t/s tg (30% CPU usage)

After full GPU offload: 
47.24 t/s tg (2% CPU usage)

items.body:
## Overview

This fixes `create_checkpoint()` deleting the checkpoint a later rewind needs whenever the prompt is shorter than `checkpoint_min_step`.

`create_checkpoint()` currently runs a spacing eviction before appending the new checkpoint. Walking from the oldest entry, it removes checkpoints from another task whose `n_tokens` is within `checkpoint_min_step` (8192 by default) of the previous surviving checkpoint. On prompts shorter than 8192 tokens, effectively every checkpoint falls within that range, so only the oldest one survives.

This removes the recent checkpoint that the prompt-fill loop placed near the end of the prompt at `n_tokens - 4` (`checkpoint_offsets = {4 + n_ubatch, 4}`, #20288). For hybrid/recurrent models, whose recurrent state cannot simply be rolled back, that recent checkpoint is the useful one when a later request rewinds the conversation.

The functional change is about ten lines: apply the spacing rule only once the checkpoint list has reached `n_ctx_checkpoints`, which already provides a hard capacity bound, and replace an existing checkpoint at the same `n_tokens` instead of appending a duplicate.

I found this while replaying a coding-agent transcript on `Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B-MTP-UD-IQ3_XXS.gguf` (HF: `peculiar-ragdoll/Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B-GGUF-MTP`), a dynamic UD-IQ3_XXS re-quantization of Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B. It is a hybrid GDN MoE: 30 of its 40 trunk layers use Gated DeltaNet recurrent state and only 10 use full attention with a KV cache, so rewinding requires restoring the recurrent state from a checkpoint.

The symptom was that reopening each session caused a few hundred already-cached tokens to be processed again, while the server log repeatedly printed `erasing context checkpoint too close`.

**When it shows.** Normal linear chat is unaffected: each turn resumes from the checkpoint created by the previous request before that checkpoint can be evicted. Switching between conversations is also unaffected because the prompt cache saves and restores the slot together with its checkpoints.

The problem appears when a request rewinds within a conversation after it has already advanced: editing or branching an earlier turn, agent harnesses that retry or compact a session, or reopening a session at an earlier point.

Tested on my 14inch MacBook Pro M5 24 GB and my 16inch MacBook Pro M1 Pro 32 GB.

## Additional information

**Stock Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M (Unsloth), `upstream/master = 7798007`, M5**, using 6 turns of ~150 tokens after a 390-token system prompt, then editing turn 4, continuing for two more turns, and finally regenerating the last answer. Generation was greedy with 120-token replies. `prompt_n` is the number of tokens `llama-server` actually processed:

| step                     | master `prompt_n` | master prompt ms | PR `prompt_n` | PR prompt ms |
| ------------------------ | ----------------: | ---------------: | ------------: | -----------: |
| turns 2-6, each          |           144-154 |          440-448 |       144-154 |      440-451 |
| edit turn 4 after turn 6 |               702 |             1459 |            26 |          229 |
| turns 5-6 again          |           145-149 |              448 |       145-149 |      449-451 |
| regenerate last answer   |                 4 |               69 |             4 |           67 |
| total, 9 warm requests   |              1753 |             4647 |          1077 |         3407 |

Both sides produced the same greedy output.

**Same scenario on the M1 Pro**, run as master, PR, then master again as an ordering control:

| step                                                       | master            | PR              | master again      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | --------------- | ----------------- |
| turns 2-6, prompt ms per turn                              | 840-1176          | 831-846         | 840-851           |
| edit turn 4 after turn 6                                   | 704 tok / 3355 ms | 26 tok / 264 ms | 704 tok / 3323 ms |
| regenerate last answer                                     | 4 tok / 102 ms    | 4 tok / 101 ms  | 4 tok / 101 ms    |
| `erasing context checkpoint too close` lines in server log | 23                | 0               | 23                |

The ordering control reproduces the original behavior after the PR run, which makes the edit-turn difference unlikely to be explained by thermal state or cache warming.

**Tiel-Coder-35B-A3B-MTP-UD-IQ3_XXS (Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B, hybrid GDN MoE), `b10488` tree, M5**, using a fixed replay of a 3-session coding-agent transcript, 13 generations, and a ~5.6K-token system prompt, measured as the mean of 3 warm repetitions. Each repetition reopens the sessions at turn 1, which exercises the rewind case.

The three session openers re-processed 260/254/272 tokens before the patch and 40/34/52 after it. Total warm re-processed tokens per repetition dropped from 2436 to 1776, and warm wall time from 18.25 to 17.12 s (−6.2%). In the same plain-chat edit-turn-4 scenario used above, re-processed tokens dropped from 715 to 26.

**Memory.** Master effectively retains 2 to 4 checkpoints on short prompts because the spacing pass removes the rest. After this change, a slot may retain up to `n_ctx_checkpoints` checkpoints before the existing capacity rule starts evicting them.

At the default limit of 32, that means up to 32 times the model's checkpoint state size: about 74 MiB per checkpoint on Tiel and 50 MiB on Qwen3.5-9B. The highest observed usage in the agent replay was 8 live checkpoints / 596 MiB after duplicate positions were removed, and the Qwen3.5-9B chat reached 13 live checkpoints.

`--ctx-checkpoints` already provides an explicit bound. A byte-based budget in addition to the count would be a reasonable follow-up, but I would prefer to keep that separate from this eviction fix unless maintainers want it included here.

An alternative would be to keep applying the spacing rule on ev
