items.body:
## Overview
TL;DR:  3-7x faster CPU mul_mat using VNNI with IMO minimal complexity

I noticed that the vec_dot approach currently taken for mul_mat duplicates the work of unpacking quants a bunch of times.  I put together a generic tiled mul_mat that works with 256x256 windows of int8.  We slide a 256-long window across the source tensors, unpacking quants 256x256 at a time, (this amortizes the unpacking work 256x compared to baseline), and then we sweep an optimized 16x16 microkernel across them to build up a 256x256 float32 output tile.  If this results in too little work for our number of CPUs, I step down the chunk size to 128, 64 etc so that we have more chunks to saturate available cores.

For tall src1 (prefills), this results in 3-7x performance gain (2x compared to repack) on my x86 machine using the optimized microkernel.  The gain goes away as we shrink the rows in src1, reaching break-even at 32 rows and falling behind to 80% of stock performance at pure GEMV.  Error rates are on the order of 5e-04 for max single scalar error, 6e-05 for RMSE across the whole tensor compared to standard vec_dot based mul_mat (microscopically better than repack).  

Integration with the main mul_mat path is similar to llamafile, we return false if we don't support or if we think it will be unprofitable (< 64 rows).

The majority of the code is portable C++ with only the microkernel and 3 inlined bit-unpacking routines as pieces to fill in for a new architecture.  This means we could expand the approach to ARM and other architectures with minimal code addition.

So far, this only supports the k-quant types.  I'm reasonably sure we could expand it to the iq-quants as well, but I haven't gone through all of them to ensure their codebooks stay in bounds of the range my unpacked tiles support.


## Additional information

The VNNI path has some additional complexity.  VNNI takes one chunk of 4 scalars from src0, broadcasted 16x to a 512 bit vector  from one row, and another vector of 4 scalars each from 16 columns of src1 all packed together to execute 16 partial dot products.  This requires a somewhat ugly additional repack of the q8_k quants to enable contiguous reads in the VNNI kernel.  I gated it away from everything else so it only exists for VNNI (and other future archs which may require bespoke packing).  The normal path for AVX2 and other future archs can ignore it.

We assume that K % 256 == 0, this seems safe given that all of the quant types we support use QK_K = 256.

Benchmarks all run using 8 threads on an AMD 9950x3D.  Used 8 instead of 16 to reduce impact of the rest of the system on the benchmarks (it's my desktop).

items.body:
# HTTP 500 when a system message appears mid-conversation (strict chat templates, e.g. Qwen3.x)

## Summary

Any request that carries a `system` message after the first position fails with a 500
from the Jinja template, on **both** `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages`. Real
clients do this routinely — Claude Code injects system/developer messages mid-conversation
(hook context, reminders), so a whole class of agent clients cannot use these models.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Commit | `9731ad3f29da96f588711a0d1eb08cf210721e16` (2026-08-18) |
| Model | `bartowski/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF`, `Q4_K_M` (arch `qwen35`) |
| Server | `llama-server --jinja -c 131072 --parallel 1 -fa 1` |
| GPU | Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB (sm_70), CUDA 12.5 |

## Reproduction

Works — `system` as the Anthropic top-level field:

```bash
curl http://host:11436/v1/messages -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"local","max_tokens":100,
  "system":"Be brief.",
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
# → 200, normal response
```

Fails — `system` as a message after the conversation started:

```bash
curl http://host:11436/v1/messages -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"local","max_tokens":100,
  "messages":[
    {"role":"user","content":"hi"},
    {"role":"assistant","content":"hello"},
    {"role":"system","content":"Be brief."},
    {"role":"user","content":"and now?"}]}'
```

```json
{"error":{"code":500,"message":"While executing CallExpression at line 110, column 28 in source:
...eveloper\" %} {{- raise_exception('System message must be at the beginning...
Error: Jinja Exception: System message must be at ..."}}
```

Identical failure on `/v1/chat/completions` with the same message list, so this is not
specific to the Anthropic endpoint — it is the template being applied to an unmodified
message list.

## Why this matters

Claude Code (and other agent harnesses) place system/developer messages mid-conversation
by design: hook output, periodic reminders, injected context. Against a strict template
every such turn returns 500, and the client retries — in our case
`500 · Retrying in 3s · attempt 4/10` until the session gives up.

## Suggested direction

Most servers normalise the message list before applying the template: hoist system
messages to the front, or merge consecutive ones into the leading system block. We run
exactly that workaround in a local translating proxy and it makes the same models work
with the same client, so the approach is proven — it just lives one hop too far away.

Whether the right fix is normalising in `llama-server` or relaxing the bundled Qwen
template is a maintainer call; the current behaviour means the model rejects valid API
requests rather than the template rejecting an unsupported ordering.

## Offer

Happy to test patches on this setup (3× NVLinked V100, Qwen3.8-27B, real agent harness)
and to report back with reproductions.

### Name and Version

```
version: 10068 (571d0d540)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64
```

Verified still present on `master` (`178a6c44`): `tools/server/server-context.cpp`
has no commits between `571d0d540` and `178a6c44`.

### Operating systems

Mac (macOS 26.3, Apple M5 Pro, Metal)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```sh
llama-server -m Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4_MOE.gguf \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -c 0 -ngl 99 --jinja \
  --slot-save-path ./kv
```

### Problem description

`POST /slots/{id}?action=restore` reports complete success — `n_restored` equals
the full token count and the slot subsequently reports those tokens in
`/slots` — but the restored state is **never reused**. The next request with an
identical prefix reprocesses every token: `cache_n = 0`.

The endpoint therefore appears to work while delivering none of its benefit, and
says nothing about it at default verbosity.

On a hybrid/recurrent model this is not a partial regression, it is total: the
restore is worth exactly zero. Measured here on a 14,906-token prefix — restore
completes in 0.12s versus 75.9s to recompute, and then all 14,914 tokens are
recomputed anyway.

This is a **different bug** from the known in-memory checkpoint issues; see
"Relationship to existing issues" below. In-memory reuse on this setup is
healthy (97.9% hit rate) — only the on-disk path is broken.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Requires: a hybrid/recurrent model (e.g. Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6, DeltaNet, Mamba)
# and llama-server started with --slot-save-path
H='Content-Type: application/json'
U=http://127.0.0.1:8080

# a prompt long enough to be worth caching
P=$(python3 -c "print('### POLICY\n' + '\n'.join(f'Rule {i}: verify precondition {(i*7)%89} then record outcome {(i*13)%83}.' for i in range(300)))")

req() { jq -n --arg p "$1" '{prompt:$p, n_predict:1, cache_prompt:true}'; }

# 1. cold — populates a slot
curl -s $U/completion -H "$H" -d "$(req "$P

Q: a?
A:")" | jq -c '.timings | {cache_n, prompt_n}'
#    → {"cache_n":0,"prompt_n":5529}

# 2. find the slot that actually holds it, and save
ID=$(curl -s $U/slots | jq -r 'map(select(.n_prompt_tokens > 0))[0].id')
curl -s -X POST "$U/slots/$ID?action=save" -H "$H" -d '{"filename":"t.bin"}' | jq -c '{n_saved}'
#    → {"n_saved":5529}

# 3. wipe every slot
for i in $(curl -s $U/slots | jq -r '.[].id'); do curl -s -X POST "$U/slots/$i?action=erase" >/dev/null; done

# 4. restore — reports full success
curl -s -X POST "$U/slots/$ID?action=restore" -H "$H" -d '{"filename":"t.bin"}' | jq -c '{n_restored}'
#    → {"n_restored":5529}

# 5. same prefix again, pinned to that slot
curl -s $U/completion -H "$H" -d "$(req "$P

Q: b?
A:" | jq --argjson s "$ID" '. + {id_slot:$s}')" | jq -c '.timings | {cache_n, prompt_n}'
#    → {"cache_n":0,"prompt_n":5529}   ← BUG: expected a large cache_n
```

Step 5 should reuse the prefix. It reprocesses all of it.

### What is actually happening

The prefix match itself is **correct**. `server-context.cpp:3149`

```cpp
n_past = slot.prompt.tokens.get_common_prefix(input_tokens);
```

returns the full 5,529 — restore does repopulate `slot.prompt.tokens`. The
result is then discarded a few lines later, at `server-context.cpp:3284-3318`:

```cpp
if (pos_min >= pos_min_thold) {
    const auto it = std::find_if(
        slot.prompt.checkpoints.rbegin(),
        slot.prompt.checkpoints.rend(), ...);

    bool do_reset = it == slot.prompt.checkpoints.rend();     // :3300
    ...
    if (do_reset) {
        SLT_TRC(slot, "forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data ...");
        pos_next = 0;
        n_past   = 0;                                          // :3317
    }
}
```

A hybrid/recurrent model cannot partially rewind its recurrent state, so a
context checkpoint is the only way to roll back to a prefix — a requirement
extended from SWA-only to hybrid/recurrent in #16382. After a restore,
`slot.prompt.checkpoints` is **empty**, so `do_reset` is always true.

It is empty for two compounding reasons:

1. **The save file never contained checkpoints.** `server-context.cpp:2529-2531`
   serializes only the token list and the sequence's KV cells:
   ```cpp
   const llama_tokens tokens = slot->prompt.tokens.get_text_tokens();
   const size_t nwrite = llama_state_seq_save_file(ctx_tgt, filepath.c_str(),
                                                   slot->id, tokens.data(), token_count);
   ```
2. **Restore then clears whatever was there.** `server-context.cpp:2576-2577`
   ```cpp
   slot->prompt.clear();              // clears tokens AND checkpoints
   slot->prompt.tokens.insert(tokens);
   ```

So the on-disk path can never satisfy the checkpoint requirement introduced by
#16382. `git log` shows the save/restore payload has not been touched
substantively since `1d36b3670` (2025-05-02); #16382 landed 2025-10-03.

Notably the **in-memory** prompt cache added in #16391 got this right — it
stores a whole `server_prompt`, checkpoints included
(`server-task.cpp`: `prompt = std::move(it_best->prompt);`), and even accounts
for checkpoint bytes in `server_prompt_cache_state::size()`. That is precisely
why RAM reuse works while disk reuse does not.

### Why this is invisible

The reset is logged with `SLT_TRC` → `LOG_TRC` → `LOG_LEVEL_TRACE` (= 4).
At default verbosity, and even at `-lv 3`, nothing is printed. Users see a
successful restore, a correct `n_restored`, correct `/slots` output, and silent
full reprocessing. `-lv 4` is required:

```
slot   operator(): id  3 | task 10 | forcing full prompt re-processing due to
lack of cache data (likely due to SWA or hybrid/recurrent memory, see
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/13194#issuecomment-2868343055)
```

### Control experiment

To confirm checkpoints are the load-bearing mechanism rather than something
specific to restore — with **no save/restore involved at all**, only
`--ctx-checkpoints 0`:

```

## Overview
- I ran an experiment to run a 27B model (from the hybrid Qwen3.5 series) on a laptop that has no GPU and uses single-channel RAM.
- While running concurrent sequences, perf showed that about 27% of the step time is wasted in get_rows and cpy operations for the GDN layer states, even though the state is already in place.
- I added an in-place state update inside the cache, applied only when all sequences read their own cells; otherwise the previous path is used, with an environment variable to go back to the old behavior for comparison. I also made the zeroing of the state memory lazy via mmap instead of memset, so inactive cells do not consume RAM.
- Results on my machine (using the AVX2 kernels from the PrismML fork): for 16 sequences the speed went from 9.5 to 13.5 tokens/s, for 8 sequences from 10.1 to 13.3 tokens/s, and RAM usage for 16 slots with speculative decoding dropped from 12.8 to 8.4 GB.

## Additional information
- This change resolves #28841 (the single-sequence case) and handles any number of sequences.
- Verification: a byte-for-byte unit test passes for 48 cases; perplexity is exactly identical with or without the change (even at ub=32); and the md5 of greedy generation matches exactly.
- Fork version: PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp#207. The new path is for CPU only; the old path is kept when n_rs_seq > 0.
- Note: I wrote this description in Arabic and translated it to English.

## Requirements
- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES — the code was written by Claude Code under my supervision; I defined the problem and the goal, ran the tests and measurements on my computer, and reviewed the results.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I was fighting with 30% cpu usage and decreased GPU utilization on AMD Strix halo machine when running Qwen 3.6 35B MoE Q8 generation on ROCm. Vulkan does not have that problem and needs only ~5% cpu to run tg. 
GLM found this issue in src/llama-model.cpp around line 1300:    
```
// there is very little benefit to offloading the input layer, so always keep it on the CPU
pimpl->dev_input = { cpu_dev, &pimpl->cpu_buft_list };
```
This keeps tok_embd on CPU even with -ngl 99, which forces GET_ROWS(tok_embd, inp_tokens) onto the CPU backend at the start of every forward pass. On Stix Halo where CPU and GPU share same DDR5 it hurts a lot.

Possible fix is to mirror the output-layer policy for the input layer when full offload is requested.

## Summary
On the Vulkan backend, Qwen3.5-27B (architecture qwen35, hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers) generates garbage / truncated output when the batch size is set to 512. The same model and configuration generate correct, coherent text at batch sizes 1024 and 4096.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11 (build 26200)
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (24 GB), AMD proprietary driver
- Backend: Vulkan
- Software: koboldcpp 1.119 (nocuda build, Vulkan backend) which bundles the llama.cpp Vulkan backend. The underlying kernel issue appears to be in ggml-vulkan.

## Model
- Architecture: qwen35 (Gated DeltaNet / linear-attention hybrid, full_attention_interval = 4, 3x DeltaNet + 1x full-attention per group, ssm state_size 128)
- GGUFs tested: Q4_K_M and Q6_K_M quantizations of Qwen3.5-27B, including a variant carrying the built-in MTP/NextN head
- Context: reproduced at both 32768 and 262144

## Repro steps
1. Load the model with the Vulkan backend.
2. Set batch size to 512 (llama.cpp: -b 512; koboldcpp: batchsize=512), ubatch 512.
3. Send a simple generation request (e.g. 'Write a short poem about the ocean.').
4. Observe output: random token fragments / garbage, or generation stops after 1-2 tokens (e.g. 'The.') with an early EOS.

With batch size 1024 or 4096 the same request produces normal coherent output.

## Notes
- MMQ disabled; Flash Attention on/off both reproduce the issue.
- KV cache f16 and q8_0 both reproduce the issue.
- MTP drafting on/off both reproduce the issue.
- The symptom pattern points at the Gated Delta Net kernel path selection: at small batch the autoregressive (non-chunked) path corrupts the logits, while at larger batch the chunked/fused path works correctly.
- Related: #20610 (Qwen3.5-27B garbage on Vulkan), #21888, #24812, #20515.

## Expected behavior
Output quality should be independent of batch size.
items.title: [Vulkan] Qwen3.5-27B (qwen35 hybrid DeltaNet) garbage output at batch size 512; OK at 1024/4096

# `-sm tensor` hangs and leaks VRAM on multi-GPU Volta (V100), `-sm row` unavailable on CUDA

## Summary

On a 3× Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB machine, neither parallel split mode is usable with a hybrid Qwen3.5-architecture model:

- `-sm row` fails at load: `device CUDA1 does not support split buffers`
- `-sm tensor` either aborts on an assertion (`llama-bench`) or **hangs forever while holding VRAM** (`llama-cli`)

`-sm layer` works correctly.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Commit | `9731ad3f29da96f588711a0d1eb08cf210721e16` (2026-08-18) |
| GPUs | 3× Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB, compute capability 7.0 |
| Topology | GPU1 ↔ GPU2 via NVLink (NV2, 2 links); GPU0 via PCIe |
| Driver / CUDA | 580.173.02 / build against CUDA 12.5, `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=70` |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04, gcc 13.3.0 |
| Model | `bartowski/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF`, `Q4_K_M` (arch `qwen35`, 65 blocks, 17 attention + 48 SSM layers) |

## 1. `-sm row`: not supported on CUDA

```
$ llama-cli -m Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf -dev CUDA1,CUDA2 -sm row -ngl 99 -c 512 -n 1 -p hallo
llama_model_load: error loading model: device CUDA1 does not support split buffers
llama_model_load_from_file_impl: failed to load model
```

`src/llama-model.cpp:999` throws when the backend does not export
`ggml_backend_split_buffer_type`. Grepping the tree, only SYCL still provides it:

```
ggml/include/ggml-backend.h        (declaration)
ggml/src/ggml-sycl/ggml-sycl.cpp   (implementation)
src/llama-model.cpp                (caller)
```

If `-sm row` is intentionally CUDA-unsupported now, the CLI help is misleading — it
advertises `row` unconditionally as "split weight across GPUs by rows (parallelized)".
A clearer error, or omitting the mode where unimplemented, would save people the search.

## 2. `-sm tensor`: assertion in `llama-bench`

```
$ llama-bench -m Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf -dev CUDA1,CUDA2 -sm tensor -ngl 99 -fa on -p 4096 -n 128 -r 2
| qwen35 27B Q4_K - Medium | 15.92 GiB | 27.32 B | CUDA | 99 | tensor | 1 | CUDA1 | pp4096 | 730.71 ± 4.18 |
| qwen35 27B Q4_K - Medium | 15.92 GiB | 27.32 B | CUDA | 99 | tensor | 1 | CUDA1 | tg128  |  33.25 ± 0.14 |
ggml/src/ggml-backend-meta.cpp:1578: GGML_ASSERT(meta_buf_ctx->bufs[i]) failed
```

Both benchmarks complete and report plausible numbers; the assertion fires afterwards.

## 3. `-sm tensor`: hang plus VRAM leak in `llama-cli`

```
$ llama-cli -m Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf -dev CUDA1,CUDA2 -sm tensor -ngl 99 -c 512 -n 1 -p hallo --no-warmup
```

No output, no error. The process stayed in `R` state for **7 minutes** for a single-token
generation before being killed manually. During that time it held **8286 MiB on GPU1 and
8286 MiB on GPU2** simultaneously and never released them. On a shared machine this
starves other services: our llama-server unit on the third GPU entered a crash loop
(`cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` for its KV cache, 15 restarts) until the hung
process was killed.

## What works

`-sm layer` across the same two GPUs runs correctly:

```
| ... | 99 | layer | 1 | CUDA1,CUDA2 | pp4096 | 777.09 ± 0.44 |
| ... | 99 | layer | 1 | CUDA1,CUDA2 | tg128  |  29.90 ± 0.52 |
```

Single-GPU reference on the same machine: `pp4096 774.81 ± 1.83`, `tg128 33.64 ± 0.05`.

## Why this report

Volta is largely gone from CI and from most contributors' desks, so these paths are easy
to lose. We have three NVLinked V100s and are happy to run patches, bisects or extra
configurations on request — just say what would help.
items.title: Bug: -sm tensor hangs and leaks VRAM on multi-GPU Volta (V100); -sm row unavailable on CUDA

### Name and Version

version [b11113](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b11113)



### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library)

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -hf unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I don't  think this will fixed at least not satisfactorily. The NPU in the intel core 7 ultra 155h only supports up to 255 models per process which surpasses the over 700 required for gemma, so weights have to be compiled on the fly for the NPU, which is very slow. 

This was heavlily AI assisted: this is my first time touching hardware. i used deepseek v4.1 and the oh my pi harness. i wondered why no one ever talked about using the npu for running ai on laptops, it's because the npu does not support enough models for gemma, or the supported models are too old and not SOTA. 

technically openvino does have a huggingface repo https://huggingface.co/collections/OpenVINO/llms-optimized-for-npu and documentation https://docs.openvino.ai/2025/openvino-workflow-generative/inference-with-genai/inference-with-genai-on-npu.html on how to run LLMs but that's not really the idea of llama.cpp and they require a lot of setup. and the models on huggingface are outdated maybe this is why?. i am using vulkan now on the GPU instead of the NPU for now. i might try using the openvino documentatoin on running llms next 

i am posting this so that no one else wastes 3 days going this route. 

After **255 successful `zeCommandQueueCreate` calls in one context**, the next one fails with

```
L0 zeCommandQueueCreate result: ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED, code 0x78000001 - driver is not initialized
```

while the device and driver are perfectly healthy. The kernel logs the real reason at the same time:

```
intel_vpu 0000:00:0b.0: [drm] *ERROR* ivpu_cmdq_create(): Failed to allocate command queue ID: -16
```

`-16` is `-EBUSY` from the command queue ID allocation (`IVPU_CMDQ_MIN_ID 1` .. `IVPU_CMDQ_MAX_ID 255`,
`drivers/accel/ivpu/ivpu_drv.h`), i.e. the per-context pool of 255 command queue IDs is full. The
reported `ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED` / "driver is not initialized" is misleading: nothing is
uninitialised, the queue budget is exhausted.

This is easy to hit with LLM workloads: the OpenVINO NPU plugin creates **one command queue per
compiled model** (`ZeroCommandQueue::create` from `Plugin::compile_model`,
`src/plugins/intel_npu/src/plugin/src/plugin.cpp`), and pipelines that compile per-layer or
per-subgraph models hold hundreds of them at once. Concretely, llama.cpp's OpenVINO backend
compiles one OpenVINO model per graph fragment and keeps them alive, so a gemma-3-1b run reaches
~419 compilations for the prefill graph alone and dies on the 256th, after which the backend logs
`device NPU is not available, fallback to CPU` and silently runs on the CPU.

## Environment

- Intel Core Ultra 7 155H (Meteor Lake), NPU37XX, PCI `0000:00:0b.0`
- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel `7.0.0-31-generic`, `intel_vpu` 1.0.0 (`Scheduler mode: HW`)
- NPU firmware: `vpu_37xx_v1.bin` 20260630 (`MTL_CLIENT_SILICON-NVR+NN-deployment`) - also seen with
  20260219; the failure is identical with both
- UMD: `intel-level-zero-npu` 1.38.0 (from the `linux-npu-driver` v1.38.0 Ubuntu 24.04 tarball,
  used via `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`) - and the same with 1.35.0 (snap)
- Level Zero loader: `libze_loader.so.1.28.2` (Ubuntu `libze-dev`)
- OpenVINO: 2026.4.0 (python wheel and runtime archive; both NPU plugins reproduce)

## Minimal reproduction (no llama.cpp needed)

```python
import numpy as np
import openvino as ov

core = ov.Core()
p = ov.opset13.parameter([1, 4], ov.Type.f32, name="x")
model = ov.Model([ov.opset13.relu(p)], [p], "relu_test")
cfg = {"NPU_USE_NPUW": "YES", "NPUW_DEVICES": "NPU", "NPUW_WEIGHTS_BANK": "shared"}

kept = []                                  # hold them alive: one queue each
for i in range(300):
    kept.append(core.compile_model(model, "NPU", cfg))
```

```
$ LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<umd-1.38.0>:<openvino-runtime> python npu_hold_test.py
compile 255 FAILED while holding 255 compiled models:
  L0 zeCommandQueueCreate result: ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED, code 0x78000001 - driver is not initialized
```

Failure at exactly 255, every time. Controls, same driver/loader/device:

- one `compile_model` + one `infer` on the NPU: **OK** (`relu([-1,2,-3,4]) == [0,2,0,4]`)
- 300 `compile_model` calls **without** holding them alive (each released before the next): **OK**
- 64 infer requests created from one compiled model: **OK**

So the limit is the number of *simultaneously live* compiled models in one process.

## Reproduction with llama.cpp (the real-world case)

```
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=<umd-1.38.0>:<openvino-runtime> \
ZE_ENABLE_ALT_DRIVERS=libze_intel_npu.so.1 \
GGML_OPENVINO_DEVICE=NPU \
GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_COMPILE_CONFIG='enable-shave-ddr-access-optimization=true' \
llama-cli -m gemma-3-1b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf -c 256 -n 8 -p 'The capital of France is' -st --no-mmproj
```

```
Exception from src/inference/src/cpp/core.cpp:117:          (Core::compile_model)
Exception from src/inference/src/dev/plugin.cpp:54:
Exception from src/plugins/intel_npu/src/plugin/src/plugin.cpp:578:   (CompiledModel ctor)
Exception from src/plugins/intel_npu/src/utils/src/zero/zero_wrappers.cpp:321:  (ZeroCommandQueue::create)
L0 zeCommandQueueCreate result: ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNINITIALIZED, code 0x78000001 - driver is not initialized
```

Number of OpenVINO models compiled for `gemma-3-1b-it-Q4_K_M` in that setup (counted by
instrumenting the translation entry, same numbers on the CPU device so no NPU needed):

| `-n` (decode steps) | compilations |
|---------------------|--------------|
| 1                   | 499          |
| 3                   | 659          |
| 4                   | 738          |

i.e. ~419 for the prefill graph alone (about 210 scheduler fragments x 2 phases), ~80 more per
decode step. All of them are live at once,

## Overview

This PR allows the Hexagon backend to handle a safe subset of quantized `MUL_MAT` cases with broadcasted `src1` dimensions by flattening contiguous rows into a single 2D matrix. The existing HVX 2D matmul kernel already handled this layout, but the backend previously rejected these shapes, causing operations such as Qwen3.5's multi-sequence `ssm_out` projection to fall back to the CPU. It also updates the HMX path to support the flattened layout.

Fixes #26094

items.body:
### Name and Version

version: 10108 (0a50d9909)
built with Clang 21.0.0 for Android aarch64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

Hexagon

### Hardware

Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 (Hexagon v73)
Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 (Hexagon v75)

### Models

Qwen3.5 2B Q4_0

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

#### Problem Description
When Qwen3.5 runs with multiple sequences (`npl > 1`), the recurrent GDN path passes the `ssm_out` input with the following shape:
```
src0: [K, N, 1, 1]
src1: [K, n_seq_tokens, n_seqs, 1]
dst:  [N, n_seq_tokens, n_seqs, 1]
```
It performs `ssm_out` on the 3D tensor and reshapes the result back to `[N, n_tokens]` afterward:
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/ed7adbfefd5e3af5f1c7c04ac67145783def85c5/src/models/qwen35.cpp#L458-L467

The Hexagon quantized `MUL_MAT` support check rejects inputs whose `n_seqs!=1`:
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/ed7adbfefd5e3af5f1c7c04ac67145783def85c5/ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/ggml-hexagon.cpp#L2810-L2812

The rejected operation then falls back to CPU, resulting in poor performance.
| HTP | npl | PP512 (t/s) | TG64 (t/s) | Overall Speed (t/s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v73 | 1 | 461.43 ± 1.31 | 11.43 ± 0.15 | 85.84 ± 0.92 |
| v73 | 2 | 112.44 ± 1.39 | 4.75 ± 0.10 | 31.94 ± 0.56 |
| v73 | 4 | 130.75 ± 3.21 | 7.72 ± 0.07 | 47.18 ± 0.62 |
| v73 | 8 | 128.71 ± 2.93 | 11.77 ± 0.59 | 61.14 ± 1.24 |
| v75 | 1 | 419.93 ± 33.50 | 11.13 ± 0.39 | 82.63 ± 3.45 |
| v75 | 2 | 110.16 ± 4.33 | 3.55 ± 0.06 | 25.43 ± 0.53 |
| v75 | 4 | 109.78 ± 4.72 | 5.44 ± 0.06 | 35.08 ± 0.69 |
| v75 | 8 | 107.58 ± 2.32 | 9.91 ± 0.20 | 51.34 ± 1.02 |

#### Reproduction
```bash
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./lib ADSP_LIBRARY_PATH=./lib \
  ./bin/llama-batched-bench -m /data/local/tmp/gguf/Qwen3.5-2B-Q4_0.gguf \
  -c 8192 -b 2048 -ub 512 -npp 512 -ntg 64 -npl 1,2,4 -dev HTP0 -t 6 --flash-attn on -ngl 99
```
Set `GGML_SCHED_DEBUG=2` and `-v` to print backend assignments.

#### Related Models
The placement of the flattening reshape is not consistent across models. Kimi Linear flattens the input before `MUL_MAT`, whereas Mamba and Qwen3.5 flatten the output afterward. The two orders are mathematically equivalent.
<details>

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/fa72aeccb23947074c12b5fec25f5b6ced28cbfe/src/models/mamba-base.cpp#L139-L144

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/fa72aeccb23947074c12b5fec25f5b6ced28cbfe/src/models/kimi-linear.cpp#L369-L371

</details>

#### A Possible Solution
#25910 added OpenCL support for the same broadcast `MUL_MAT` pattern used by Qwen3.5 GDN.

The existing HVX 2D kernels (including quantized versions) already implement this broadcast case by computing `src1_nrows = ne11 * ne12 * ne13`:
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/fa72aeccb23947074c12b5fec25f5b6ced28cbfe/ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/matmul-ops.c#L937-L946
A solution is to allow this case to use existing HVX kernels:
```cpp
static bool ggml_hexagon_can_use_flat_2d(const struct ggml_tensor * src0,
                                        const struct ggml_tensor * src1,
                                        const struct ggml_tensor * dst) {
    return ggml_hexagon_is_repack_type(src0->type) &&
           src0->ne[2] == 1 && src0->ne[3] == 1 &&
           (src1->ne[2] != 1 || src1->ne[3] != 1) &&
           src1->type == GGML_TYPE_F32 && dst->type == GGML_TYPE_F32 &&
           ggml_is_contiguous(src1) && ggml_is_contiguous(dst);
}
```

The HMX kernel uses `ne1` as `m_total`, so some additional modification is needed.
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/fa72aeccb23947074c12b5fec25f5b6ced28cbfe/ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/matmul-ops.c#L3329-L3334

items.body:
### Name and Version

$ ./llama-cli --version
version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10436, commit 6f04274cc)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Windows AMD64

### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library)

### Command line

```shell
probe.exe model.gguf embd5.f32 repeat 6 1
probe.exe model.gguf embd5.f32 tokens 6 1
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

# Title
CPU backend: `llama_batch.embd` (embedding input) decoding is non-deterministic, while the token path is bitwise deterministic

# Summary
On the CPU backend, repeated identical decodes through the **embedding input path**
(`llama_batch.embd` set, `ubatch->token == NULL`) produce **different logits** — in the same
process, same context, same input, after `llama_memory_clear(mem, true)` between decodes.
The **token path** (`llama_batch.token`) is **bitwise identical** under exactly the same
conditions. `argmax` stays stable, so the practical impact is on *reproducibility*, not on
greedy generation.

# Environment
- commit: `6f04274cc145cf76aafc46eb8c1ea054ca221368`
- build: `cmake -B build-cpu -G "MinGW Makefiles" -DGGML_CUDA=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF` (MSYS2 UCRT64 g++)
- runtime: Windows amd64, CPU backend, `n_gpu_layers = 0`, `n_threads = n_threads_batch = 1`
- model: Qwen3.5-2B (`qwen35`: hybrid SSM + full attention every 4 layers), f16 GGUF
- ctx: `n_ctx=512`, `n_batch=n_ubatch=512`

### Steps to reproduce
1. Prepare one `embd.f32` file = `n_tokens × n_embd` little-endian float32 (random values are fine).
2. Build and run the minimal probe, mode `repeat`: it decodes the same batch N times in the **same context**, calling `llama_memory_clear(llama_get_memory(ctx), true)` before each decode, and reports `bitwise_equal` for each run vs run 0.
3. Also run mode `tokens` (same file interpreted as int32 tokens) as the control.

# Observed
| case | result |
| --- | --- |
| token path, 6 repeats | bitwise identical (cosine 1.00000000) |
| embd path, **1** token, 6 repeats | bitwise identical |
| embd path, **2/3/5** tokens, 6 repeats | **bitwise different** (cosine 0.984–0.9999; `argmax` constant) |
| embd path, all-zero input | all-zero output, bitwise identical |
| embd path, separate processes | different across processes (pairwise cosine 0.9946–0.9971) |

# Additional localization
- **Per-layer comparison** via `llama_get_hidden_state`: layers before the **first full-attention layer** are bitwise identical; divergence starts exactly at that layer (for this model: layers 0–2 identical, layer 3 differs). SSM layers are deterministic.
- **Requires >1 token**: 1 token is deterministic, 2 tokens already are not.
- Results fall into a **small set of states that recur** (e.g. run0==run2, run1==run3==run4), suggesting **buffer/state reuse** rather than fresh randomness.

# Ruled out
- unwritten `inp->tokens` (explicitly zeroing that input in `llm_graph_input_embd::set_input` does not help)
- multi-threading (`n_threads = n_threads_batch = 1`)
- KV capacity / unused KV region (swept `n_ctx` 8…512)
- reading uninitialized/stale KV content (all-zero input yields all-zero output)
- ggml fused ops (`GGML_CPU_DISABLE_FUSION=1`)
- CPU Flash Attention (`flash_attn_type = DISABLED`)

# Expected behavior
Same context + same input + cleared memory ⇒ **identical** output, as on the token path
(and as any user would expect for a pure-CPU deterministic backend).

# Extra context
This surfaced while prototyping **layer-pipeline relay** (compute layers `0..k` with one model instance and inject the resulting hidden state into a truncated model that computes `k+1..N` via `llama_batch.embd`). Greedy generation still matches the non-relay baseline 16/16 steps, but bit-exact reproducibility across processes is not achievable today.

## Overview

This PR implements Speculative Prefill, based on the ICML 2025 paper: *"Speculative Prefill: Turbocharging TTFT with Lightweight and Training-Free Token Importance Estimation"* by Jingyu Liu, Beidi Chen, Ce Zhang ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.02789), [GitHub](https://github.com/Jingyu6/speculative_prefill))

> [!NOTE]
> In contrast to speculative decoding, this is not lossless and can cause model performance degradation.

### Approach
In long-context inference, prefill TTFT scales quadratically with prompt length. Speculative prefill reduces this compute by using a smaller draft model to estimate which context tokens are most relevant to the query before evaluating the main target model:

1. **Draft lookahead**: The draft model prefills the prompt and generates $K$ lookahead tokens (default: 8).
2. **Attention extraction**: Softmax attention matrices (`kq_soft_max`) are captured during draft generation via an evaluation callback.
3. **Importance pooling & chunking**: Attention scores are smoothed with a 1D average-pooling filter ($W = 13$), max-reduced across heads/layers, and aggregated into contiguous chunks ($C = 32$).
4. **Sparse target prefill**: Only the top-$p$ fraction of chunks (plus BOS and prompt boundary tokens) are fed into the target model's KV cache.
5. **Generation**: The target model generates tokens autoregressively as normal.

### Benchmarks & Performance Evaluation

All benchmarks were run natively on Vulkan (`AMD Radeon 8060S`, RADV STRIX_HALO, 128 GiB unified LPDDR5X) using **Qwen3.8-27B (Q6_K_XL)** as target and **Qwen3.5-2B (Q4_K_XL)** as the primary draft model (unless noted otherwise).

#### 1. Draft Model Sizing & Context Scaling

**Draft Model Comparison** ($N = 1609$, $p = 0.15$):

| Configuration | Draft Eval Latency | Target Prefill | Total TTFT | Target Compute | End-to-End Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Baseline (27B alone)** | — | 5,300.8 ms | 5,300.8 ms | 1.00x | 1.00x |
| **27B Target + 27B Draft** | 5,836.5 ms | 789.2 ms | 7,597.2 ms | 6.72x faster | 0.70x (draft overhead) |
| **27B Target + 9B Draft** | 1,486.7 ms | 781.2 ms | 2,505.7 ms | 6.79x faster | 2.12x |
| **27B Target + 2B Draft** | 333.9 ms | 788.8 ms | 1,196.4 ms | 6.72x faster | **4.43x** |

**Context Length Scaling** (27B Target + 2B Draft):

| Keep Ratio ($p$) | $N = 803$ tokens | $N = 1607$ tokens | $N = 3212$ tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **100% (Baseline)** | 2,882.0 ms (1.00x) | 5,324.6 ms (1.00x) | 10,787.7 ms (1.00x) |
| **50%** | 1,795.3 ms (1.61x) | 3,273.8 ms (1.63x) | 6,174.8 ms (1.75x) |
| **30%** | 1,026.3 ms (2.81x) | 2,045.3 ms (2.60x) | 4,004.3 ms (2.69x) |
| **15%** | **685.1 ms (4.21x)** | **1,615.7 ms (3.30x)** | **2,418.1 ms (4.46x)** |

#### 2. Synthetic Retrieval & QA Benchmarks

* **Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIAH)**: 100.0% retrieval accuracy across depths (20%, 50%, 80%) down to $p = 0.15$ (298 / 2,058 tokens kept, 1,798.0 ms vs 6,863.2 ms baseline, **3.82x speedup**).
* **RULER Suite**: 100.0% accuracy across Single Needle (25%, 75%), Multi-Key Retrieval, and Variable Tracking at $p = 0.15$ (**4.11x speedup**, 1,930.7 ms vs 7,925.4 ms). One miss at $p = 0.50$ (depth-75% needle; that row 75.0%).
* **LongBench QA Latency** (HotpotQA, Qasper, 2WikiMQA): Latency reduced from 4,821.5 ms baseline to 1,313.7 ms at $p = 0.15$ (**3.67x speedup**).

### Failure Mode Analysis & Operational Limits

Because speculative prefill drops tokens permanently from target prefill, accuracy drops when the token budget ($p \cdot N$) cannot contain all non-redundant evidence across separate chunks.

#### 1. Draft Model Comparison on Stress Tests (2B vs. 9B)

**High-Entropy Multi-Key Retrieval** (5 keys across 5 sections, ~1,100 tokens):

| Keep Ratio ($p$) | Tokens Kept | Qwen 2B Draft | Qwen 9B Draft | Observed Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **100% (Baseline)** | 971 / 971 | **PASS (5/5)** | **PASS (5/5)** | All keys present and retrieved correctly |
| **50%** | 491 / 971 | FAIL (0/5) | FAIL (2/5) | Partial chunk pruning causes model hesitation/evasion |
| **30%** | 299 / 971 | **PASS (5/5)** | FAIL (2/5) | 2B focused on all 5 nodes; 9B diffused attention |
| **15%** | 140 / 971 | FAIL (0/5) | FAIL (3/5) | Budget allows ~4 chunks (5 needed) $\to$ information loss |
| **8%** | 76–98 / 971 | FAIL (2/5) | FAIL (1/5) | Severe pruning $\to$ both models hallucinate fake IDs |

**Distributed Summation** (Box A: 15 + Box B: 25 + Box C: 60 = 100):

| Keep Ratio ($p$) | Tokens Kept | Qwen 2B Draft | Qwen 9B Draft | Status / Observed Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **100% (Baseline)** | 796 / 796 | `100 units` | `100 units` | **PASS** — All 3 box chunks retained |
| **50%** | 412 / 796 | `100 units` | `100 units` | **PASS** — All 3 box chunks retained |
| **30%** | 252 / 796 | `100 units` | `100 units` | **PASS** — All 3 box chunks retained |
| **15%** | 125 / 796 | `100 units` | `100 units` | **PASS** — Boundary + 3 box chunks fit in 125 tokens |
| **8%** | 61 / 796 | `40 units` | `77 units` | **FAIL** — Box C (`60`) pruned $\to$ silent partial calculation |

**Non-Parametric Multi-Hop QA** (Target Year: `2348`, 12 non-redundant documents):

| Keep Ratio ($p$) | Tokens Kept | Qwen 2B Draft | Qwen 9B Draft | Status / Observed Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **100% (Baseline)** | 473 / 473 | `2348` | `2348` | **PASS** — Both clue documents retained |
| **50%** | 249 / 473 | `2348` | Refusal / Evasion | **PASS (2B)** / **FAIL (9B)** — 9B lookahead diverted to distractor |
| **30%** | 153 / 473 | `2348` | `2348` | **PASS** — Both clue documents retained |
| **15%** | 90 / 473 | `2348` | `2348` | **PASS** — Both clue documents retained |
| **8%** | 58 / 473 | `2280` | `2185` | **FAIL** — Clue 2 pruned $\to$ hallucinated from distractor |

items.body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10398, commit 8e7f22b67)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA
CPU

### Hardware

Intel Core i7 14700F
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 12 GB

### Models

Original observation through Ollama:

* `Qwen3.5 2B Q8_0` (hybrid)

Primary `llama-server` reproduction:

* `Gemma 3 4B IT Q4_K_M`

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I found this while intentionally corrupting a completed slot snapshot as part of a persistent-cache fault-injection test through Ollama.
I have not observed slot files becoming corrupted during normal save or restore operations.
The corrupted state is correctly rejected, but K/V data written before the validation failure can remain in the cache and affect subsequent inference.
In the reproducing case, later completions become empty, erasing the slot does not recover the process, and restarting `llama-server` does.

I reproduced the same behavior with stock `llama-server`, so this is not specific to Ollama.
`llama-completion` does not exercise this path because its prompt-cache path uses the whole-context state API, while this issue is in the per-sequence slot restore path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start `llama-server`:

```bash
llama-server -m gemma-3-4b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf --no-mmproj \
  --slot-save-path /tmp/slots \
  -np 1 -c 4096 -ngl all -fa on --no-webui
```

2. Process the prompt used in this reproduction:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/completion \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.dumps({
      'prompt': 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog near the river bank. ' * 170,
      'n_predict': 1,
      'temperature': 0,
      'cache_prompt': True
  }))")"
```

This produced about 2382 prompt tokens.

Save slot 0:

```bash
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8080/slots/0?action=save" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"filename":"good.bin"}'
```

The resulting state file was `170,469,452` bytes.

3. Corrupt 8 MiB starting at 14 MiB:

```bash
cp /tmp/slots/good.bin /tmp/slots/corrupt.bin

dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/slots/corrupt.bin \
  bs=1048576 count=8 seek=14 conv=notrunc
```

These offsets are specific to this saved state file. They caused some K/V data to be written to the backend buffers before validation failed on a later tensor header, at layer 29 in this run.

As controls, a truncated copy and loading the same state with the incompatible `-fa off` layout both failed before entering the K/V data-write loop. Neither affected subsequent inference.

4. Restore the corrupted state:

```bash
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8080/slots/0?action=restore" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"filename":"corrupt.bin"}'
```

The restore correctly returns HTTP 400.

5. Send a short completion request:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/completion \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"Write one short sentence about the sea.","n_predict":32,"temperature":0,"cache_prompt":false}'
```

In the reproducing case, the relevant response fields are:

```text
tokens_predicted: 32
stop_type: "limit"
content: ""
```

6. Erase slot 0, then repeat the same completion request.

The response remains empty and the process remains affected.

7. Restart `llama-server`. Completions work normally again.

### Suspected cause

`state_read_data()` validates and writes K/V data layer by layer.
If validation fails on a later layer, earlier K/V data may already have been written into the backend buffers.

The rollback is asymmetric:

* whole-context restore uses `clear(true)`, which also clears the K/V buffers
* per-sequence restore uses `seq_rm()`, which removes cell metadata but leaves the underlying K/V data

This can leave corrupted K/V data in cells that are subsequently considered free.
Free cells are expected to be excluded by attention masking. In the reproduced path, corrupted f16 data can contain NaNs that are not neutralized by the masking operation.
A C API reproduction also confirmed NaN logits on CPU and showed that deferred buffer writes can be applied after the existing rollback.
PR #26051 made exceptions from `state_read_data()` enter the existing rollback path. For per-sequence restore, that path removes sequence metadata but does not clear K/V data written before the failure.

### Expected behavior

A failed per-sequence restore should leave later inference and other sequences usable. Restoring the previous contents of the target slot is not required.

### Related

* #26744 - stale K/V in freed cells affects attention through a separate Vulkan-specific mechanism
* #9173 - slot restore failure followed by failure in later processing
* #17527 / PR #17982 - fragmented restore failure before K/V data is written
* #23720 / PR #23981 - checkpoint restore failure involving internally generated checkpoint state

AI tools assisted with code investigation and analysis. I independently reproduced the issue and validated the technical claims in this report.

A minimal fix and regression test are working locally, and I can open a PR. 

### First Bad Commit

I do not believe this is a recent regression. The metadata-only per-sequence rollback predates #26051, and this reproduction reaches it through `state_read_data()` returning `false`.

### Relevant log output

```console
state_read_data: mismatched key type (1 != 248383823, layer 29)
llama_state_seq_load_file: error loading sequence state file: failed to restore kv cache
srv    send_error: task id = 5, error: Unable to restore slot: No available space in KV cache or invalid slot save file
```

The mismatched key value comes from the randomly corrupted bytes and therefore changes between runs.
items.title: Eval bug: failed slot restore leaves corrupted K/V data that breaks subsequent inference

### Summary

Two separate CPU performance regressions on Android arm64 (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2), measured with the official `llama-bXXXXX-bin-android-arm64.tar.gz` release binaries, CPU backend only:

1. **Text generation is ~8 % slower in b10333 than in b10092**, and slightly worse again by b10369.
2. **Prompt processing regressed a further ~13 % between b10333 and b10369** (it was at parity between b10092 and b10333).

| Median | b10092 | b10333 | b10369 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Decode tok/s (192-token generations) | **15.48** | 14.26 (0.921×) | 13.92 (0.899×) |
| Prompt tok/s (~2k-token prompt) | 72.7 | **73.9** (1.017×) | 64.5 (0.887×) |

### Environment

- Device: Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra (SM-S918B), Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, Android 16 / API 36
- Binaries: unmodified official release archives, e.g. `llama-b10369-bin-android-arm64.tar.gz`; the runtime auto-selects the armv9.2 CPU variant
- Model: Qwen3.5-2B `Q4_K_M` (bartowski conversion), 1.30 GiB, fully resident, no swap activity

### Method

`llama-server` run under the shell UID with:

```
llama-server -m Qwen_Qwen3.5-2B-Q4_K_M.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18080 \
  -c 10240 -np 1 -t 5 -tb 8 -Cr 3-7 --cpu-strict 1 -Crb 0-7 --cpu-strict-batch 1 \
  --jinja --no-webui
```

Non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions` requests with `temperature 0`; decode and prompt rates read back from the response `timings` object, so the numbers are the server's own.

Thermal control, since this class of device throttles enough to reorder any comparison:

- every series starts only after battery temperature ≤ 30.0 °C and with charging disabled;
- big-core `scaling_max_freq / cpuinfo_max_freq` headroom is recorded next to every sample;
- the first (page-cache warm-up) sample of every series is discarded;
- decode = 7 samples × 192 tokens; prompt = 4 samples of a ~2,000-token prompt with `cache_prompt: false`.

The regressions are not thermal artifacts: the losing builds ran at **equal or higher** clock headroom than the winning ones (e.g. the b10333 decode series ran entirely at 0.95–1.0 headroom and still lost to a b10092 series that dipped to 0.70).

One observation in the newer builds' favor: server RSS was ~290 MB lower on b10369 (2.66 GB vs 2.95 GB at the same context size).

### What I can offer

- Raw per-sample JSON (rates + thermal headroom per sample) for all six series.
- I can re-run the same harness on candidate builds or bisect the b10092…b10333 window for the decode regression if that helps narrow it down.
items.title: Performance regressions on Android arm64 CPU (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2): text generation ~8% slower since b10333, prompt processing ~13% slower since b10369

items.body:
## Overview

Imagination's proprietary Vulkan compiler cannot compile the subgroup-only reduction variants of the dequant `mul_mat_vec` shaders. `vkCreateComputePipelines` returns `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN`, `ggml_vk_create_pipeline_func` rethrows, and the process dies with an uncaught `vk::SystemError` on the first generated token. Prompt processing runs first and succeeds, so the failure looks like a hang partway into generation.

This affects every type that goes through `reduc16`: Q2_K through Q6_K, TQ2_0, the IQ types, MXFP4 and NVFP4. The legacy quants use the plain subgroup reduction and compile fine, so the subgroup path itself is not the problem.

Falling back to the shared-memory reduction for those shaders fixes it.

## Additional information

### Device

Pixel 11 Pro, PowerVR C-Series CXTP-48-1536 MC1, `VK_DRIVER_ID_IMAGINATION_PROPRIETARY`, driver 1.662.3024, Vulkan 1.4.317. Subgroup size 128, min 32, max 128. 32 KB shared memory, no cooperative matrix, no integer dot product.

The failing pipeline is created with `require_full_subgroups=1`, `requiredSubgroupSize=128`, `wg_denoms=[2,1,1]`, specialization constants `[128,2,1]`, 17320 bytes of SPIR-V.

### What I ruled out

None of these help; the compile still fails:

- dropping `VK_PIPELINE_SHADER_STAGE_CREATE_REQUIRE_FULL_SUBGROUPS_BIT_EXT`
- dropping the `VkPipelineShaderStageRequiredSubgroupSizeCreateInfoEXT` pNext
- dropping both
- forcing the subgroup size to 64
- forcing it to 32

So it is the shader body, not the pipeline flags or the subgroup width.

### Why not the hybrid variant

#20565 proposed hybrid reduction for the same vendor on a Pixel 10. Hybrid does compile here and is correct, but it costs 27% of token throughput on this device:

| reduction | pp128 | tg32 |
|---|---|---|
| shared memory | 21.41 t/s | 5.20 t/s |
| hybrid | 21.41 t/s | 3.78 t/s |

Qwen3.5-2B-Q4_K_M, `-ngl 99 -p 128 -n 32 -r 3`.

### Testing

`test-backend-ops` against the CPU reference, on device:

| type | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Q2_K | pipeline compile fails | 11/11 |
| Q3_K | pipeline compile fails | 11/11 |
| Q4_K | pipeline compile fails | 26/26 |
| Q5_K | pipeline compile fails | 11/11 |
| Q6_K | pipeline compile fails | 11/11 |

Q4_K and Q6_K repeated four times each, same result every run. `llama-bench` on Qwen3.5-2B-Q4_K_M runs end to end after the change; before it aborts at the first generated token.

Gated on `driver_id` rather than `vendor_id` because the evidence is for the proprietary Android driver only. I have not tested Mesa's PowerVR driver.

Related: #28214 (other problems on the same device, not addressed here), #20565.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. AI was used to help create this PR, including the on-device investigation.

# `tool_choice: "required"` is accepted but not enforced on templates with `supports_preserve_reasoning: true`

### Name and Version

```
build_info: b330-84e908c62
```
Built locally for CUDA 13.0, `-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121 -DCMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS="-O2"`.

### Operating systems

Linux (aarch64, NVIDIA GB10 / sm_121)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

`llama-server`, and the chat/grammar layer under `common/` (`chat-auto-parser-generator.cpp`).

### Command line

```
llama-server -m qwen36-NVFP4-MTP-HQ.gguf --host 0.0.0.0 --port 11435 \
  -c 131072 --jinja -ngl 999 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --spec-type draft-mtp
```

### Problem description

`llama-server` accepts `"tool_choice": "required"` on `/v1/chat/completions` without error or
warning, and then does not enforce it, on models whose chat template llama.cpp classifies with
`supports_preserve_reasoning: true`.

Instead of being constrained to emit a tool call, the model generates freely until `max_tokens`
is exhausted. The request returns `finish_reason: "length"` with `predicted_n` equal to the full
budget and no `tool_calls`. In the runs I inspected the tail of the output had degenerated into a
repeating emoji sequence, which is consistent with generation being unconstrained rather than
grammar-limited.

The failure is **silent and expensive**: a caller that relies on `required` for structured output
receives ordinary prose, no error, and pays the maximum token cost of the request every time.

Two servers on the same host, same binary, same build string, both `--jinja`, differ only in the
model/template:

| | fast lane | smart lane |
|---|---|---|
| model | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (NVFP4, MTP) | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct (Q4_K_M) |
| `supports_tool_calls` | true | true |
| `supports_parallel_tool_calls` | true | true |
| `supports_object_arguments` | true | true |
| **`supports_preserve_reasoning`** | **true** | **false** |
| `tool_choice: "required"` | **ignored** | honoured |

`supports_preserve_reasoning` is the only differing capability in `/props → chat_template_caps`.

**On reproducing this without my exact file:** the GGUF above is a local conversion and is not
something you can download, so please do not treat the filename as the repro target. The trigger
appears to be the *chat template* — specifically whichever templates llama.cpp classifies
`supports_preserve_reasoning: true`, i.e. a `<think>`-style reasoning template. Any model whose
`/props → chat_template_caps` reports that flag together with `supports_tool_calls: true` should
show it. `repro.sh` prints both flags up front so it is obvious at a glance whether a given server
is a candidate. I am happy to attach the exact template text if that helps.

### What is NOT the cause (ruled out by measurement)

- **The model.** An identical hand-written GBNF grammar posted to `/completion` forces a perfect
  tool call on both servers, from a prompt with no intent to call anything. Section B of the
  reproducer is this control.
- **Grammar sampling generally.** `root ::= "BANANA"` is honoured on the affected server.
- **Speculative decoding.** The control above succeeds with `--spec-type draft-mtp` active.
- **Reasoning parsing.** Sending `"reasoning_format": "none"` does not change the behaviour.
- **Token budget.** Identical failure at `max_tokens` 500 / 1500 / 3000 / 5000 — all fully
  consumed, `reasoning_content` exactly 801 chars each time.
- **The tool-call syntax.** Both templates emit `<tool_call>…</tool_call>` with `<|im_start|>`.

### Why this looks like a defect rather than unsupported behaviour

`common/chat-auto-parser-generator.cpp` appears to intend enforcement on this path:

```cpp
// ~line 84
bool include_grammar = has_response_format || (has_tools &&
        ((inputs.tool_choice == COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_AUTO && !trigger_marker.empty()) ||
          inputs.tool_choice == COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_REQUIRED));

// ~line 89 — REQUIRED yields a NON-lazy (eager) grammar
data.grammar_lazy = !has_response_format && inputs.tool_choice == COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_AUTO;

// ~line 369 and ~line 500 — for REQUIRED the tool calls are NOT made optional
if (!require_calls) { tool_calls = p.optional(tool_calls); }
```

So a grammar is built, marked eager, and tool calls are non-optional — yet generation is
evidently unconstrained. I have not isolated the specific line where enforcement is lost; that
likely needs a debug build dumping the emitted GBNF for the two templates.

### Steps to Reproduce

Full script at the bottom of this issue. `./repro.sh <host:port>` exits **1** when the bug reproduces and **0**
when `required` is honoured — it was verified to discriminate between the two servers above.

```bash
curl -s http://HOST:PORT/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"local",
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello, how are you today?"}],
  "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_disk_free",
    "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string"}},"required":["host"]}}}],
  "tool_choice":"required","max_tokens":2000,"temperature":0}'
```

Expected: a `tool_calls` response. Actual on an affected template: `finish_reason: "length"`,
`predicted_n` == `max_tokens`, no `tool_calls`.

### Relevant log output

```
finish_reason : length
predicted_n   : 2000
tool_calls    : NONE
content tail  : '🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️…'

# control, same server, hand-written grammar via /completion:
'<tool_call>{"name": "get_disk_free", "arguments": {"host": "beta"}}</tool_call>'
```


### Possibly related open issues

- **#26781** — *"enable_thinking forced true in jinja/caps.cpp capability probe leaks into
  non-DeepSeek templates"*. Same model family (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B), same subsystem, and a very
  similar end state: budget consumed inside `reasoning_content`, no `tool_calls`, a silent dead
  end for an API consumer. **Differences:** that report needs ~38-41 turns of accumulated co

items.body:
## Overview

This PR adds an opt-in `--fuse-qkv` flag to `convert_hf_to_gguf.py`. During HF-to-GGUF conversion, complete per-layer Q/K/V triples are concatenated into a single `attn_qkv` tensor. Weight and bias triples are handled independently; without the flag, conversion is unchanged.

- **Converter**: pre-scans mapped GGUF tensor names, buffers complete Q/K/V triples, and emits fused `ATTN_QKV` weights and biases. Unsupported architectures and incomplete triples are left unchanged.
- **Tensor registration**: registers `MODEL_TENSOR.ATTN_QKV` only for architectures whose loaders and graphs can consume fused QKV.
- **Model loading**: `create_tensor_qkv` loads fused weights when present and defensively supports legacy/custom GGUFs that pair fused weights with separate Q/K/V biases.
- **Graph building**: extends `llm_graph_context::build_qkv` to support explicit Q/K/V geometry and raw contiguous projections. Custom attention graphs now reuse this helper, including Q+gate layouts and unequal K/V head widths.
- **MTP**: fused QKV is supported by the Step-3.5, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.5-MoE, and Qwen3-Next MTP graphs.
- **Model-specific paths**: updates the affected custom loaders/graphs, including Gemma 3n/4, JAIS 2, Kimi Linear, LLaDA, MiniMax-M2, OLMo 2/OLMoE, Qwen3.5/Qwen3-Next, Step-3.5, and DeepSeek OCR paths.

The separate-bias fallback is defensive: converter-produced files fuse complete bias triples, while legacy or custom GGUFs may still store those biases separately.

**Diffstat:** 20 files, **+393 -122**.

## Validation

- `test-llama-archs`: all supported architectures passed.
- Real HF-to-GGUF conversion with PyTorch 2.6.0, with and without `--fuse-qkv`.
- For both layers of a tiny Llama fixture, each fused tensor was verified element-for-element against `concat(Q, K, V)`; fused files contained no separate Q/K/V tensors.
- Both converted GGUFs completed `llama-bench` prompt processing and token generation (`pp8` and `tg8`).
- Before/after helper-refactor parity: exact logits hashes matched for 7 fused main graphs and 4 fused MTP graphs.
- Additional checkpoint/PPL coverage is reported in the PR discussion for OLMo 2, DeepSeek OCR, OLMoE, Gemma 3n/4, LLaDA, Qwen3.5 dense/MoE, JAIS 2, and Kimi Linear.

Numerical identity is backend-dependent because a fused GEMM may use a different execution path from three separate GEMMs; accelerator outputs can differ by normal floating-point noise.

## Additional information

This follows the two-step split discussed in #20628:

1. #21245 (merged) extracted the common `build_qkv` / `create_tensor_qkv` helpers.
2. This PR adds converter-side fusion and extends those helpers for the remaining custom graph geometries.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- AI usage disclosure: YES - used for translation, static review, and implementation assistance.

### Name and Version

$ ./build-cpu/bin/llama-server --version
version: 0.4.0-dev (build 2587, commit 6a1a922d)
built with GNU 11.2.0 for Linux x86_64



### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
./build-cpu/bin/llama-server \
  -m /data/huggingface/unsloth-Qwen3.5-2B-GGUF/Qwen3.5-2B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --ctx-size 2048 \
  --jinja \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 19220
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Enabling `logprobs` on a streaming request with tools returns HTTP 400: `logprobs is not supported with tools + stream`. However, replacing `logprobs` and `top_logprobs` with `n_probs` in the same request returns tool calls and `top_logprobs`.

To reproduce:

```bash
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:19220/v1/chat/completions' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Call get_weather for Singapore."}],
    "tools": [{
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"location": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["location"]
        }
      }
    }],
    "stream": true,
    "logprobs": true,
    "top_logprobs": 2
  }'
```

Response (HTTP 400):

```json
{"error":{"code":400,"message":"logprobs is not supported with tools + stream","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

For comparison:

- Changing only `stream` to `false` returns tool calls and logprobs successfully.
- Keeping `stream:true` and replacing `logprobs` and `top_logprobs` with `n_probs:2` streams tool calls and `top_logprobs` successfully, ending with `finish_reason:"tool_calls"`.
- Adding `tool_choice:"none"` to the original request still produces the same 400 error.

Expected behavior: allow `logprobs` and `top_logprobs` to expose the existing probability output for streaming tool calls, rather than rejecting the entire request.

When `logprobs` is enabled, the current [parameter handling](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/6a1a922d269908a29cbd4b49c27e6a8e7fd10fae/tools/server/server-common.cpp#L1383) rejects requests based on `has_tools && stream` before converting `top_logprobs` to `n_probs`. Passing `n_probs` directly bypasses this check, so the two ways of requesting probabilities behave differently.

If enabling this is not feasible yet, please at least allow requests with `tool_choice:"none"`. This disables tool-call parsing for the generated response, so the tool-call-specific alignment concern does not apply in that case.

I'm happy to submit a PR if the maintainers agree with this approach.

items.body:
## Overview
this is a reimplementation of #24797

That PR was rejected because it could reuse recurrent state at positions it
was never valid for (trimming checkpoint metadata in place, resetting rs_idx
when a rollback exceeds the available snapshots). This takes the opposite
approach and keeps the invariant intact: recurrent state is only ever
restored at the exact position it was saved at.

- checkpoint metadata records the actual validity at save time
  (`pos_min = pos_max` for hybrid/recurrent) instead of relying on what
  `seq_pos_min` happens to report - resolves `[TAG_CHECKPOINTS_FIX_POS_MIN]`
  for these model types
- a checkpoint is only restored when its exact position lies inside the
  common prefix of the new prompt
- checkpoints covering diverged content are erased instead of trimmed
- no changes to `llama_memory_hybrid` semantics; `seq_rm` still fails
  cleanly on impossible rollbacks (now with a debug log)

On top of that, the cache is made useful for agentic clients, which strip
the reasoning of the previous reply so the next request diverges right at
the end of the previous prompt:

- end-of-prompt checkpoints are exempt from `--checkpoint-min-step`
- eviction drops the checkpoint closest to its neighbor instead of the
  oldest one, so early anchors survive edited/compacted histories
- bounded `n_rs_seq` rollback is tried before the checkpoint search
- checkpoint create/restore/erase log at INFO

## Additional information

Related: #24055

Tested with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M on Vulkan (RDNA3.5 APU). Resending
identical 22.8k-token request went from a ~96s full prefill to a 4-tok
cache hit. In a 10-turn agentic session normal turns only process the new
content, a mid-history edit correctly falls back to the last valid
checkpoint, and a compacted history restores an early checkpoint instead of
reprocessing everything. Correctness: at temperature 0 a checkpoint-restored
run produces byte-identical output to a fresh full prefill, and two
independent cold runs are byte-identical to each other.

## Requirements

- [x] I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - Using Fable for rewriting my (ugly) implementation and creating the test cases based on my example workload. Also used it to translate my german pre written pull request to english and add the test results and more details in.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Newer qwen models 3.5+ hybrid models were outputing mostly gibberish and crashing.  I've tested most of these models previously and they were working. Honestly thought I did something at first but then realized it was just an update I'm guessing.

Two related symptoms affect all hybrid architecture models (identifiable by 
ssm_d_conv / ssm_d_state / ssm_dt_rank fields in print_info) on Intel Arc Pro B60 
using server-intel latest (built 2026-06-03). Both are fixed by pinning to b8477.

SYMPTOM 1 - CRASH (qwen3next arch, e.g. Qwen3-Coder-Next):
Model loads fully into VRAM then crashes during warmup mul_mat on SSM/GDN weights.
crash at ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat line:3093.

SYMPTOM 2 - EMPTY/GIBBERISH OUTPUT (qwen35 arch, e.g. Qwen3.6-27B/35B):
Model loads and generates tokens but "content" field in API response is empty or 
contains number spam (e.g. 03129816571033482510583...). All output goes to 
"reasoning_content" as corrupted tokens. On b8477 the same models produce clean 
coherent output in "content".

IMPORTANT CONTEXT - why this is hard to diagnose:
server-intel is a rolling latest tag. Not sure when build/image broke but when I tried most recent build or 2026-06-03 get the broken build. Same 
image tag, completely different behavior depending on pull date. At one point I randomly tested Coder-Next about a week ago and although slow it worked. Now I randomly couldn't get any model 3.5 or above to work without gibberish outputs .... Coder-Next had been working in earlier sessions, then 
silently broke when the image updated i'm guessing, I just can't pinpoint when, unless this is known already.

Pure attention MoE models (qwen3moe arch, no SSM layers) are completely unaffected 
on both builds and work correctly throughout.

Steps to reproduce (using Docker):

1. Pull latest server-intel:
   docker pull ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-intel

2. Run with dual Arc Pro B60:

   docker run --rm \
     --device /dev/dri:/dev/dri \
     --group-add 993 --group-add 44 \
     -e ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0;level_zero:1 \
     -e ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=1 \
     -e UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_LEVEL_ZERO=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_VMM=1 \
     -e GGML_SYCL_DISABLE_GRAPH=1 \
     -p 8010:8010 \
     ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-intel \
     --model /models/Qwen3-Coder-Next-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
     --ctx-size 8192 \
     --host 0.0.0.0 \
     --port 8010 \
     -ngl 999 \
     --split-mode layer \
     --tensor-split 1,1 \
     --flash-attn off \

3. For qwen3next: crash during warmup at ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat line:3093
   For qwen35: server starts, responds, but content field is empty or number spam

4. Replace image with server-intel-b8477 — identical command — both symptoms fixed

---

Side note for Ollama SYCL users:

This same regression affects users of https://github.com/eleiton/ollama-intel-arc
— an excellent community-maintained project providing native SYCL Ollama builds 
for Intel Arc GPUs. It is not a bug in that project. Ollama 0.30.2 pins 
LLAMA_CPP_VERSION=b9479 (confirmed via 
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/v0.30.2/LLAMA_CPP_VERSION) which

## Overview Follow‑up to #26373, address the feedback in PR-26373. **Qualcomm’s Hexagon SDK provides two RPC mechanisms**: native FastRPC and dspqueue. this PR adds **FastRPC-based ggml-hexagon**, an alternative backend for Qualcomm Hexagon NPU on Android & WoA(Windows on Snapdragon), which can coexist with **the existing dspqueue-based** ggml-hexagon implementation. This relationship is similar to ggml‑openvino vs ggml‑sycl (backends for the same hardware), or ggml‑cuda vs ggml‑hip (ggml‑hip reuses existing CUDA kernels) within llama.cpp. ## Big changes compared to PR‑26373 - remove **redundant AP‑side** cache coherency maintenance, allowing the fastrpc‑based ggml‑hexagon to work on WoA devices - 100% reuse of existing Hexagon kernels - reuse the existing build system from the dspqueue‑based ggml‑hexagon - refine ggmlhexagon_init_rpcmempool, so the fastrpc‑based ggml‑hexagon **should** work fine on Snapdragon 8 Elite 5(aka 8Gen5) phones. ## Features 1. single shared mempool + Native FastRPC: lm-head offloading is the primary factor behind the drastic PP and TG throughput advantage seen in this PR, lm‑head offloading is heavily dependent on the single shared mempool design. 2. role-aware cache coherency in **NPU-side**: it distinguishes resident weights from per-batch activations and applies first-touch cache invalidation only once for resident weights. 3. minimal code footprint & coexistence: the fastrpc backend introduces minimal code footprint, can **directly 100% re-use the existing hexagon kernels** and the two backends share one HTP ops source tree (htp/), only a handful of files are truly new or modified. the two backends are **build-time variants of one backend directory and one build system**, selected by a single option: `GGML_HEXAGON=ON` plus `GGML_HEXAGON_USE_MEMPOOL=ON` builds the fastrpc backend (`ggml-hexagon-fastrpc.cpp` + `htp/entry.c` + `htp/ggml_htp.idl`); `GGML_HEXAGON=ON` alone (default) builds the dspqueue backend (`ggml-hexagon.cpp` + `htp/main.c` + `htp/htp_iface.idl`), exactly the upstream behavior. Both variants produce **identically** named artifacts (`libggml-hexagon.so` + `libggml-htp-vXX.so`), the switch has **zero breaking changes**, the official dspqueueu-based ggml-backend builds and runs normally. - `ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/ggml-hexagon-fastrpc.cpp` (new; AP side) - `ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/entry.c` (new; HTP entry) - `ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/dsp-ctx.h` (new, avoid duplicate filename with existing htp‑ctx.h; HTP session context + descriptors) - `ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/htp/ggml_htp.idl` (new; FastRPC IDL) - `ggml/src/ggml-hexagon/CMakeLists.txt` and `htp/CMakeLists.txt` (modified; variant switch) - `scripts/build-run-ggmlhexagon-android.sh` (optional, useful for verifying this PR and simplifying builds/CI for both ggml‑hexagon backends) ## Benchmark results ### Test device Snapdragon 8 Elite (aka 8 Gen 4), QCOM_HTP_V79, VTCM=8MB, HVX+HMX ### PP&TG in dspqueue-based ggml-hexagon ### PP&TG in FastRPC-based ggml-hexagon ### Eight-Model AB Test Results (fastrpc vs dspqueue) | Model | Layers | Attention | lm_head | Model Size | fastrpc PP | dspqueue PP | PP Diff | fastrpc TG | dspqueue TG | TG Diff | |-------|-------:|-----------|---------|-----------|------:|--------:|--------:|------:|--------:|--------:| | qwen1.5-1.8B | 24 | MHA 1:1 | Q6_K | 1.1 GiB | 521.36 | 738.04 | -29.4% | 17.12 | 24.31 | -29.6% | | minicpm5-1b | 24 | GQA 8:1 (16:2) | Q4_0 | ~0.7 GiB | 1161.77 | 1016.62 | +14.3% | 51.95 | 36.14 | **+43.8%** | | Llama-3.2-1B | 16 | GQA 4:1 | Q4_K | 0.7 GiB | 1006.10 | 1063.43 | -5.4% | 41.64 | 28.33 | **+47.1%** | | Qwen3.5-2B | 24 | GQA + Delta | Q6_K | 1.2 GiB | 485.07 | 434.96 | +11.5% | 26.99 | 14.95 | **+80.5%** | | gemma-4-E2B | 35 | GQA 8:1 | Q4_K | 2.9 GiB | 668.14 | 490.09 | **+36.3%** | 27.00 | 24.99 | +8.0% | | Nanbeige-3B | 22 | GQA 6:1 | Q4_0 | 2.4 GiB | 224.14 | 136.73 | **+63.9%** | 8.03 | 9.11 | -11.9% | | gemma-4-E4B | 42 | GQA 4:1 | Q4_K | 4.9 GiB | 403.76 | 426.82 | -5.4% | 14.75 | 12.08 | **+22.1%** | | Qwen3.5-9B | 32 | GQA + Delta | Q6_K | 5.0 GiB | 11.28 | 114.14 | -90.1% | 5.80 | 6.77 | -14.3% | ### How to reproduce the benchmark results The build script (`scripts/build-run-ggmlhexagon-android.sh`) **automatically downloads** and sets up dependencies(**8 models** and dependent SDKs) on first run.

### Name and Version

version:b9754 (52b3df0)
built with Android JNI

### Operating systems

Other? (Please let us know in description)

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

vivo X200 Pro(V2405A)、Dimensity 9400/MT6991、Mali-G925-Immortalis MC12、Android 16/API 36

### Models

Qwen3.5-0.8B-Q4_K_M.gguf + mmproj-F16.gguf

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

On a Mali-G925-Immortalis MC12 (Vulkan 1.3, Android), multimodal (image + text) prefill with Qwen3.5-0.8B-Q4_K_M produces logits that are entirely NaN (248320/248320), which collapses sampling and makes the model emit a continuous run of ! tokens.

Using the same binary and switching only the device selection policy so that all layers land on CPU devices, the same image and the same prompt produce finite, well-distributed logits and correct output.

**Configuration**

n_gpu_layers          = 99      (all layers offloaded to Vulkan)
flash_attn            = enabled
type_k / type_v       = F16
vision encoder (clip) = CPU     (mmproj_use_gpu = false)

**Reproduction**

- Load the text model and the multimodal projector.
- Submit a single image together with a text prompt.
- Input is tokenized to 394 tokens total, of which 225 are image tokens.
- Run decode.

**Observed behavior**

Failing run — layers on Vulkan0
```txt
sched_reserve: graph splits = 2
reserve_compute_meta: graph splits = 1, nodes = 388

[PROBE] CLIP_embd: OK n=230400 zero=0 min=-4.18883 max=0.919084 mean=-0.00249603 mean_abs=0.0735539
[PROBE] eval_chunks: ret=0 n_past=184 | chunks n_tokens=394 n_pos=184

[PROBE] prefill_logits: *** CORRUPTED *** n=248320 nan=248320 inf=0 zero=0 min=3.4e+38 max=-3.4e+38 mean=0 mean_abs=0
[PROBE] prefill_logits head[8]: nan nan nan nan nan nan nan nan
[PROBE] sampled[0] token_id=0 piece='!'
raw output: !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
```
graph splits = 2, so the graph is cleanly partitioned — this is not a case of the scheduler thrashing between backends.
Every logit is NaN — not a subset, not inf, not zeros.
Reproduced twice consecutively with byte-identical probe statistics, so this is deterministic rather than a race.
Working run — same build, layers on CPU devices
```txt
[MODEL] n_gpu_layers=0 policy=CPU_ONLY_DEVICES
[CTX] n_ctx=1536 thr=6 thr_batch=6 flash_attn=1 kv_type=F16 policy=CPU_ONLY_DEVICES
sched_reserve: graph splits = 1

[PROBE] CLIP_embd: OK n=230400 zero=0 min=-4.18883 max=0.919084 mean=-0.00249603 mean_abs=0.0735539
[PROBE] eval_chunks: ret=0 n_past=184 | chunks n_tokens=394 n_pos=184

[PROBE] prefill_logits: OK n=248320 zero=0 min=-11.1491 max=21.9672 mean=-0.196356 mean_abs=1.899
[PROBE] prefill_logits head[8]: 5.851 6.089 7.328 7.357 7.118 7.889
```
The CLIP_embd probe statistics are identical across both runs:

```txt
n=230400  zero=0  min=-4.18883  max=0.919084  mean=-0.00249603  mean_abs=0.0735539
head[8]: -1.951 -0.121 0.3041 -0.1121 -0.03802 0.1002 -0.06389 0.02273
```
Since the vision encoder runs on CPU in both configurations, the image embeddings fed into the language model are the same in both cases. Tokenization is also identical (n_tokens=394, n_past=184). The divergence therefore originates inside the language model's prefill, on the Vulkan path.

Text-only inference on this device with the same settings (ngl=99, flash_attn enabled, KV F16) works correctly, so the failure appears specific to the multimodal prefill — where a CPU-produced embedding tensor is consumed by Vulkan-resident layers. I have not narrowed it down to a specific op.

The model uses Gated Delta Net (hybrid linear attention); the logs show both fused paths being enabled:

```txt
sched_reserve: fused Gated Delta Net (autoregressive) enabled
sched_reserve: fused Gated Delta Net (chunked) enabled
```
I mention this in case the fused GDN kernels are relevant on this GPU, but I have not verified that they are the cause.

Possibly related issues
#21888
#24812
I am not certain these share a root cause; linking them in case they are useful context.

**Version caveat**
This was reproduced on b9754 (52b3df0), which is not current — the latest published release is b10359, roughly 600 builds newer. I have not retested on latest master, and it is entirely possible this has already been fixed.

## Overview

**Co-authors:** @jxia4intel, @sliu39

**PR 2/3** of the Intel Xe optimization series — see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24408 (mega PR, draft) for the full feature set.

**Target platforms:** Xe-LPG Plus, Xe2, Xe3

This PR adds Intel Xe-specific flash attention optimization kernels for both ARLH iGPU (Xe1, UMA, coopmat1) and Xe2/Xe3. Dependency: builds on top of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24404 (Xe-LPG Plus coopmat1 enable). Independent of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24407 (GEMM+CW).

### Flash Attention (Intel Xe)

- New Vulkan shaders: single-phase prefill (`flash_attn_hdim64/96/128`) and two-phase split prefill/decode variants
- Pipelines keyed by `(head_dim, gqa_ratio)` for runtime dispatch across various GQA ratios without combinatorial pipeline proliferation
- Supports non-power-of-two GQA ratios via subgroup splitting (`qk_groups`)
- Intel Xe1 (integrated GPU, UMA, cooperative matrix) and Xe2 paths with separate warptile tuning
- Two-phase decode splits softmax reduction across subgroups; shared QK state copy (`fa_copy_qstate`) between prefill phases
