items.title: Misc. bug: Severe drop in prompt processing speed after b10780 on Vulkan, RDNA3

items.body:
## Environment

- **llama.cpp**: master `8144f31` (2026-08-23) + also reproduced on release b10488 (Windows CUDA 13.3 build)
- **OS**: Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04 (both tested, same cliff)
- **GPU**: RTX 4080 SUPER 16GB, driver 591.86 (CUDA 13.1), nvcc 13.1, sm_89
- **Model**: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` UD-Q3_K_XL (12.2GB); also reproduced with UD-IQ4_XS (13.3GB) and IQ4_XS (14.6GB)
- **Backend**: CUDA, single GPU

## Symptom

With the model **fully resident on GPU** (zero "assigned to device CPU" lines, verified in logs), decode (tg) speed collapses non-linearly once the KV position exceeds roughly 80K tokens — from ~33 t/s at 68K position to **1.4 t/s (714 ms/token) at 91K position**, or outright timeouts. **Prompt processing (pp) stays fast (~1300 t/s) at the same positions.** Zero-context decode is normal (~38-39 t/s) on every configuration below.

## Reproduction matrix (WSL2, llama-server)

Command shape:
```
./llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -ngl 999 --load-mode none \
    -c <CTX> [-fa on] -ctk <Q> -ctv <Q>
```
Then send a chat completion with a ~91K-token filler prompt and `max_tokens=100`.

| Config | VRAM fit (CPU overrides) | pp @91K fill | tg @91K position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-c 131072 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits, 0 CPU lines | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` | fits | fast | **timed out (>25 min)** |
| `-c 98304  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **timed out** |
| `-c 73728  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **33.1 t/s @ 68K position ✅** |

Position sweep with the last config (UD-Q3_K_XL, q8 KV, no FA):

| KV position (prompt tokens) | decode t/s (server-side timing) |
|---|---|
| 45,574 | 35.6 |
| 60,309 | 33.9 |
| 68,642 | 33.1 |
| 91,077 | **1.4 (or timeout)** |

## Key observations

1. **The cliff is positional, not a memory-spill issue.** All 96K/128K configs above report 0 CPU tensor overrides and normal free VRAM headroom; KV quantization level (q4/q5/q8) and `-fa on/off` make no difference to the cliff. Only the *position* matters.
2. **pp is unaffected at the same positions** (~1300 t/s for the 91K fill), so this is specific to the decode path.
3. The drop is far steeper than any plausible O(n) attention-scan cost: 68K→91K position is a 1.34x context increase but a **~24x decode slowdown**.
4. Server logs at the cliff show `eval time = 1055.41 ms / 300 tokens (0.95 tokens per second)` with `graphs reused = 298`, i.e. CUDA graph reuse continues normally while per-token latency explodes.
5. Also reproduced on the same hardware under Windows native (b10488) at large `-c`, so it is not WSL2-specific.

## Suspected area

Decode-path attention over long KV for the hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers (Qwen3.8 / qwen35-family). Possibly a fallback/slow kernel engaged past some KV extent threshold. Possibly related family: #27442 (empty generation >16K on Metal for qwen35moe hybrids), #27572 (draft acceptance collapse with multi-ubatch batches).

## Logs

Full `llama-server` logs for the 131072/q4/FA and 73728/q8/no-FA runs available on request (happy to attach — they contain per-token timing lines, tensor placement, and KV buffer sizes).

## Overview

**Co-authors:** @jxia4intel, @sliu39

**PR 2/3** of the Intel Xe optimization series — see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24408 (mega PR, draft) for the full feature set.

**Target platforms:** Xe-LPG Plus, Xe2, Xe3

This PR adds Intel Xe-specific flash attention optimization kernels for both ARLH iGPU (Xe1, UMA, coopmat1) and Xe2/Xe3. Dependency: builds on top of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24404 (Xe-LPG Plus coopmat1 enable). Independent of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24407 (GEMM+CW).

- Supports non-power-of-two GQA ratios via subgroup splitting (`qk_groups`)
- Intel Xe1 (integrated GPU, UMA, cooperative matrix) and Xe2 paths with separate warptile tuning

items.body:
Building with the default flags, using a 4-bit KV cache (q4_0/q4_1) silently drops prefill to CPU speed. No warning, no offload message, just a ~30x slowdown that is very hard to diagnose from the outside.

What happens: the kernel selection in fattn.cu (ggml_cuda_fattn_kv_type_supported) only accepts f16/f32 KV unless GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS is set at compile time. When the requested KV type is not supported, the scheduler places the whole FLASH_ATTN_EXT op on the CPU backend.

Measured on a single RTX 3090, Qwen3.8-27B, K=q4_1 / V=q8_0, 130K ctx:

| build | prefill |
|---|---|
| default | ~34 t/s |
| -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON | 659-1094 t/s depending on context |

This is the third report of the same silent fallback in #27109 (myself, @aand18, @Cybertiron). Every user who wants 4-bit KV to fit long contexts in limited VRAM has to discover this flag on their own, and release builds ship without it.

Ask: make GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON the default in the CMake option, or at minimum print a clear warning at startup when the requested KV cache types cannot be served by the CUDA FA kernel.

PR #28634 flips the default.

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```
llama-server \
  -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --model-draft mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-mtp \

```

### Problem description

`POST /slots/{id}?action=save|restore` only persists `ctx_tgt` (via
`llama_state_seq_save_file`/`llama_state_seq_load_file`) — on a deployment
running speculative decoding (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`), the draft
model's own context (`ctx_dft`) is never captured or restored at all.

This is a separate, narrower gap from #25913 (checkpoints not persisted,
addressed by #26004): even once #26004 lands, a restored slot's draft
model only gets its state back if a checkpoint happened to already exist
at save time (checkpoints carry their own `data_dft`) — a short
conversation that hasn't hit its first checkpoint yet restores with an
empty draft-model KV cache and no fallback. The raw, currently-live
`ctx_dft` state is simply discarded on save, independent of checkpoint
existence.

Not directly observable as a crash or an error — the restore reports
success either way — but on a speculative-decoding deployment it means
the draft model silently starts cold after every restore whenever no
checkpoint happens to cover the request, undermining part of the benefit
`--slot-save-path` is meant to provide alongside #26004's fix.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start `llama-server` with a draft model (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`)
   and `--slot-save-path`.
2. Send a short prompt (short enough that it completes before the first
   context checkpoint would be created) with `cache_prompt: true`.
3. `POST /slots/0?action=save`.
4. Inspect the save file: only the `ctx_tgt` payload
   (`llama_state_seq_save_file`'s own format) is present; there is no
   companion draft-model state anywhere.
5. `POST /slots/0?action=erase`, then `POST /slots/0?action=restore`.
6. The restore succeeds and reports the correct token count, but
   `ctx_dft` was never touched — the draft model's KV cache is empty,
   identical to a slot that just came up cold, regardless of what #26004
   restores for `ctx_tgt`/checkpoints.

### First bad commit

Not a regression — `SLOT_SAVE`/`SLOT_RESTORE` have never captured
`ctx_dft`; this predates both this report and #26004.

### Relationship to other issues/PRs

- #25913 / #26004: separate root cause (missing checkpoint persistence
  for `ctx_tgt`'s reuse-validity check), already well covered there. This
  report is about `ctx_dft` specifically, which #26004 does not touch.
- We have a working fix (raw `ctx_dft` capture/restore via
  `llama_state_seq_get_size_ext`/`get_data_ext`/`set_data_ext`, stored as
  a companion `<save-file>.dft`, verified live on a production
  Vulkan/AMD-APU draft-mtp deployment) and are happy to open it as a PR,
  either standalone or as a follow-up once #26004 merges (to avoid
  competing for review attention on the same file/handlers at once) —
  see our comment on #26004 for details.
items.title: Misc. bug: /slots save/restore never persists the draft-model context (ctx_dft) on speculative-decoding deployments

### Name and Version
0.3.0-dev (build 37, commit 8e53fce), built with AppleClang 21.0.0 for Darwin arm64 (Metal, default flags, Release)

### Operating systems
Mac

### GGML backends
Metal

### Hardware
2x Apple M1 Max (24-core and 32-core GPU), 64 GB unified memory each — reproduced on both

### Models
- unsloth-style AD-3.84bpw-IQ4_XS-M64 (28 shards) — 16K/64K OK, 128K FAIL
- AD-4.27bpw-Q4_K_M-M64 (33 shards) — 64K FAIL (q4v4 KV) / 16K FAIL (q8v8 KV)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce
llama-server, single slot, GPU flash attention (auto). With prompts beyond a config-dependent threshold:
- prefill completes normally (e.g. 118-140 tok/s at 64K)
- decode emits exactly 1 token then stops (EOS): `eval time = ... / 1 tokens`, answer empty
- server returns HTTP 200 — silent failure, no error anywhere
- at/near the threshold the failure is STOCHASTIC: same server, same config, same prompt size → 64K x3 = PASS, PASS, FAIL on consecutive runs
- threshold moves with model quant (Q4_K_M << IQ4_XS), KV quant (q8v8+b256: 16K vs q4v4+b512: 64K), and possibly n_ctx window size (64K probes 3/3 @ n_ctx 208896 vs 2/3 @ n_ctx 262144, same 64K prompts)
- with mixed-precision KV (-ctk q8_0 -ctv q4_0) Metal rejects FA → attention falls back to CPU → 200K needle tests pass 3/3 (correct but slow) — so the failure is specific to the GPU attention path
- `-fa off` cannot be tested with quantized KV ("quantized V cache requires flash_attn to be enabled"); with f16 KV + `-fa off` decode fails immediately with `Compute error. off = 0, n_batch = 256, ret = -3` on the first token
- memory pressure excluded (failures observed with < 600 MB swap)
- needle-in-haystack probe (3 pins at 10/50/90% depth), warmup, temperature 0

Matrix (all llama-server, GPU FA, IQ4_XS unless noted):
| model | KV | -b/-ub | n_ctx | 16K | 64K | 128K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IQ4_XS | q4v4 | 512 | 208896 | 3/3 | 3/3,3/3,3/3 | 0/3 (1 tok) |
| IQ4_XS | q4v4 | 1024 | 208896 (A machine, +ngram spec) | — | 3/3 (32K/64K) | 0/3 (1 tok) |
| IQ4_XS | q8v8 | 1024 | 262144 | — | 3/3,3/3,0/3 (stochastic!) | not reached |
| Q4_K_M | q4v4 | 512 | 208896 | — | 0/3 | — |
| Q4_K_M | q8v8 | 256 | 208896 | 0/3 | — | — |

### First Bad Commit
Unknown; qwen4exp support landed via #27742 (2026-08-27) — all failures observed on builds containing it. **Retested on master `df03399` (0.4.0-dev build 300, contains #27941, #28023, #28098): the bug reproduces identically.** 64K x1 = 3/3 (prefill 153.8 tok/s, decode 11.1 — sparse-FA perf improvements visible), 128K x1 = **0/3, decode 0.0 (1 tok)** — same signature, same threshold. So #27941 (block position keying), #28023 (indexer head summation) and Metal sparse FA do not resolve it.

### Related
#27856 (HIP: depth-decay only, output correct), #28734 (CUDA: dense top-k TODO), #25722 (Metal: degenerate-token silent empty output, different arch), #21450 (Metal mixed KV rejection — the mechanism that pushes attention to CPU and avoids this bug)

*Disclosure: issue text prepared with AI assistance (GLM-5.3-Flash via ZCode), verified against server logs and raw probe JSONs.*

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: b10752 (b96806d96)
```
Container image `ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-vulkan`, run in router mode
(`--models-preset`), one child `llama-server` per model.

### Operating systems

Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic)

### GGML backends

Vulkan (Mesa RADV)

### Hardware

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 — Radeon 8060S Graphics (RADV STRIX_HALO, gfx1151),
120 GiB GTT, unified memory.

### Models

`Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf` (dense, 27.3B params, `n_ctx_train = 262144`), which
carries MTP layers.

### Problem description

With `--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp` and a large `--ctx-size`, the server
fails **every** request — including a 13-token prompt — dying within ~2s of the
prompt/decode transition and exiting with status 1. The router respawns it, so
the failure presents as a ~53s crash-loop that silently discards all prompt
cache.

The trigger is the **total** `--ctx-size`, not the per-sequence context. That
appears to come from `common/speculative.cpp`, where the MTP draft context is
sized from the target's total context despite the comment stating per-sequence
intent:

```c
// common/speculative.cpp — common_speculative_init_result::common_speculative_init_result()
    auto cparams = common_context_params_to_llama(params);

    if (spec_mtp) {
        cparams.ctx_type = LLAMA_CONTEXT_TYPE_MTP;
    }

    // the draft context holds as many tokens per sequence as the target context
    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx(ctx_tgt);        // <-- total, not per-sequence
```

`llama_n_ctx()` returns the total; `llama_n_ctx_seq()` is the per-sequence
accessor:

```c
// src/llama-context.cpp
uint32_t llama_n_ctx    (const llama_context * ctx) { return ctx->n_ctx();     }
uint32_t llama_n_ctx_seq(const llama_context * ctx) { return ctx->n_ctx_seq(); }
```

The draft context then builds its own memory module from those cparams:

```c
    memory.reset(model.create_memory(params_mem, cparams));
```

Under `--no-kv-unified` this makes the draft context `n_parallel` times larger
than the comment intends. Under `--kv-unified` it is worse, because
`n_ctx_seq` is then set equal to the whole total:

```c
// src/llama-context.cpp
    if (cparams.kv_unified) { cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx;                 }
    else                    { cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx / n_seq_max;     }
```

Note also that `--kv-unified-per-slot` cannot bound this: `llama_context_params`
has `n_ctx`, `n_seq_max` and `kv_unified`, but no per-slot field, so the
server-level cap never reaches the draft context.

### Ablation matrix

All rows below are on the same build, model, and machine, and each was verified
by serving requests. "draft n_ctx" is the value the code above assigns.

| `--ctx-size` | `--parallel` | kv-unified | `--spec-type` | draft `n_ctx` | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 786432 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 786432 | **fails every request** |
| 786432 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod` | — | works (12.8 tok/s, 99.99% cache reuse) |
| 393216 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 393216 | works (24 tok/s) |
| 524288 | 3 | on + `--kv-unified-per-slot 262144` | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 524288 | works (23.7 tok/s) |

Removing `draft-mtp` at the failing `--ctx-size` fixes it outright; restoring
`draft-mtp` at a smaller `--ctx-size` also fixes it. So the fault requires
`draft-mtp` **and** a large total `--ctx-size` together.

Note the third and fourth rows: the working unified config has a draft
`n_ctx_seq` of 524288, larger than the failing split config's 262144. So
per-sequence size is not the trigger — the **total** is.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
llama-server \
  --model Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --ctx-size 786432 --parallel 3 --no-kv-unified \
  --spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp \
  --spec-draft-n-max 4 --spec-draft-n-min 0 --draft-p-min 0.25 \
  --n-gpu-layers 999 --flash-attn on \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 512 --jinja

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"...","max_tokens":8,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say: ok"}]}'
```

The model loads normally and reports `status=loaded`. The first request — any
size — kills the process.

### What was ruled out

- **GPU/driver watchdog.** This machine separately had `amdgpu.lockup_timeout`
  at its 2000 ms default, which produced `ring comp_1.x.1 timeout`, a compute
  queue reset and `vk::DeviceLostError`. That was raised to
  `10000,60000,10000,10000` and the machine rebooted. `dmesg` has shown **zero**
  ring timeouts since, yet the MTP failure persists — so the two are unrelated
  faults and this report is only about the second.
- **Out of memory.** The failing configuration loads cleanly at 82 GiB of 120
  GiB GTT, and no OOM appears in `dmesg`. The failure is on first use, not at
  allocation.
- **Prompt length.** A 13-token prompt fails identically to a 100k one.
- **Tool/grammar constrained sampling.** A request with no `tools` fails too.
- **Build drift.** `b10752-b96806d96` throughout, verified via
  `system_fingerprint`; the container was restarted, never re-pulled.
- **Slot count alone.** `--parallel 3` works fine at smaller `--ctx-size`.

### Suggested fix

```diff
-    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx(ctx_tgt);
+    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx_seq(ctx_tgt);
```

This matches the stated intent of the comment. It would also make the draft
context independent of `--parallel`, which currently multiplies it.

### Possibly related

#23658 reports MTP draft acceptance collapsing at particular `--ctx-size`
values on a ~2048-aligned pattern, attributed there to "slot indexing in how
the MTP draft context shares the KV cache with the target context". That may be
the same sizing/indexing surface presenting as degradation rather than a crash.

### Relevant log output

```
# router, at the moment of failure
E srv    operator(): http client error: Failed to read connection
I srv    operator():
items.title: Eval bug: draft-mtp draft context is sized from llama_n_ctx() (total) rather than llama_n_ctx_seq(), killing the server at decode entry on large --ctx-size

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
The current approach to handling experts in MoE models use one GEMM per expert. These activations are relatively narrow, and cannot use the compute hardware effectively (neither ALU0/1 nor the XMX tiles). Additionally, the small inputs result in particularly inefficient dequantization. 
This can be fixed by grouping many small experts into one kernel, and handling them in one operation.

This patch proposes grouped and optionally fused GEMM kernels tuned on XMX (`joint_matrix`).
Approach:
- Build a host-side schedule of active expert tiles and launch as one grouped kernel instead of one GEMM per expert
- Dequantizes IQ4_NL or IQ3_S weights into f16 tiles in local memory
- Packs routed f32 activations into the VNNI f16 layout consumed by XMX.

## Additional information
Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF:UD-IQ4_XS`.

## Overview Currently with tensor/matrix cores we only use fp16 instructions, so dequant to shared memory -> fp16 GEMM. But many devices have higher throughput int8 tensor/matrix cores, so similar to the existing DP4A-based scalar MMQ path it would be good to have a coopmat int8 MMQ path. I have tried to make this work in the past, but failed due to architectural constraints in the coopmat extension. But based on @pwilkin's ideas in #27493, I finally managed to get it to work with good performance on RDNA3 and 4. This new MMQ cm1 shader supports q4_0, q4_1, q5_0, q5_1, q8_0, q3_k, q4_k, q5_k, q6_k, mxfp4, nvfp4 and iq4_nl on RDNA3 and RDNA4. Strix Halo prompt processing performance is significantly improved, RDNA4 is more neutral, but MoE prompt processing is also up significantly. The shader is limited to those two architectures since it hardcodes their specific coopmat access patterns. More architectures can be added if needed. q4_1, q5_1, q4_k, q5_k and nvfp4 on RDNA4 are disabled for MUL_MAT since they run slower than existing fp16 matmul. ## Overview

Extends the gate/up + GLU fusion, which today only covers small batches (MMVQ/MMVF), to prompt-processing batch
sizes on the MMQ path. For dense FFN layers where `ffn_gate` and `ffn_up` have the same type and shape, the two
matmuls and the GLU now run as one MMQ kernel: the activations are quantized once, the GLU is applied in the
write-back, and the standalone GLU kernel and the second activation quantization disappear.

Enabled for Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0 and IQ4_XS on GPUs with the MMA data layout; other cases take the existing path, I have a plan to enable it other types also. 

Implementation:
- `mul_mat_q` gets a fused variant (`has_fusion`): every thread keeps separate up and gate accumulators, so the
  block uses half the threads and rows of the stock tile (128 threads, 64 rows, 2 blocks/SM) and J is capped at 64.
  Per K step both Y halves are loaded once (cp.async where available, plain copy otherwise), then the up and the gate
  tiles are loaded and multiplied in turn. No stream-K: the GLU needs the full K reduction in one block. Column tiles
  are the innermost grid dimension, so neighbouring blocks reuse the same weight tiles from L2.
- Only the q8_0 / q4_K / q5_K / q6_K / iq4_xs loaders take the `has_fusion` parameter; the fused kernel is only
  compiled for the MMA layout.
- `ggml_cuda_op_glu_single` (unary.cuh) is now shared by the fused MMQ write-back, MMVQ and MMVF; the padding clear
  in `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q` / MMVQ moved to `ggml_cuda_clear_padding`.
- Graph side: the MUL_MAT + MUL_MAT + GLU pattern is matched in `ggml_cuda_try_fuse`; `graph_optimize` keeps the
  activation alive until the GLU node so the allocator cannot alias it with the fused output.

## Additional information

DGX Spark (GB10), CUDA 13.1, pp16384, `-b 2048 -ub 2048 -fa on`, f16 KV, t/s, master and PR in one session:

items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [ ] I am running the latest code. Development is rapid so there are no tagged versions as of now. (Tested on the latest release, **v0.5.0**, b11146, commit 7fe450e19; the relevant server code is unchanged on master as of 2026-09-24.)
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Split the generation timings of a reasoning model into its two phases, reasoning and answer, in `llama-server`'s `timings` and in the `print_timing` log line.

Today `timings` reports one `predicted_n` / `predicted_ms` / `predicted_per_second`, plus one `draft_n` / `draft_n_accepted`, for the whole completion. With a reasoning model and speculative decoding those numbers average two workloads that behave very differently, so the single figure describes neither.

Proposed shape (names are only a suggestion), added next to the existing fields and emitted only when the response actually contained reasoning:

```json
"timings": {
  "predicted_n": 2048, "predicted_ms": 71416.1, "predicted_per_second": 28.66,
  "draft_n": 1902, "draft_n_accepted": 1412,
  "reasoning": {
    "predicted_n": 1825, "predicted_ms": 65216.3,
    "draft_n": 1737, "draft_n_accepted": 1247
  }
}
```

The answer phase is then the difference, so one extra object is enough. The `print_timing` line at the end of a request could carry the same split (`reasoning: 1825 tokens, 28.0 t/s, acc 72% | answer: 223 tokens, 35.6 t/s, acc 100%`).

### Motivation

We tune `--spec-draft-n-max` and pick quants from benchmarks, and a reasoning model's mean decode rate is the wrong number to tune on: how much of the output is reasoning moves with the question, and in agentic coding the reasoning phase is usually most of it.

Measured on llama.cpp v0.5.0 (b11146), Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 on an R9700 (ROCm) + RTX 4070 SUPER (CUDA) split, DFlash2 drafter, `temperature 0`, 2048 output tokens, 93.6k-token prompt, 3 repetitions each (the split was obtained client-side, see below):

| drafter | reasoning t/s | reasoning acc | answer t/s | answer acc | whole request t/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| none | 13.0 | | 12.9 | | 13.0 |
| DFlash2, n-max 3 | 28.0 (1825 tok) | 72% | 35.6 (223 tok) | 100% | 28.7 |
| DFlash2, n-max 7 | 33.7 (2048 tok) | 51% | (not reached) | | 33.6 |

- The answer drafts at 100% acceptance and is capped by `n-max` itself; the reasoning drafts at 51 to 72%. Their mean is a regime that does not exist.
- The phase share also changes between otherwise identical runs: at `temperature 0` the n-max 5 and 7 runs reasoned past the 2048-token cap while n-max 3 answered at token 1825, so two "decode" means compared naively mix different phase proportions.
- In the server log the phase change is visible as a step in `tg_3s` (about 22 t/s during reasoning, about 40 t/s once the answer starts, on a request with a longer answer), but nothing in the timings says where it happened.

The count alone (#27971, `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`, closed by its author) would not be enough for this: the rate and the draft acceptance per phase need the time and the draft counters at the boundary.

### Possible Implementation

We currently get this client-side: stream with `"timings_per_token": true`, and read the cumulative `timings` on the last event whose delta is `reasoning_content`; each phase is a difference of the server's own counters, with no client clock. That works, but it needs streaming and per-token timings on every event, and any client that does not stream cannot get it.

Server-side, the boundary is already known at generation time in two places:

- `task_result_state::update_chat_msg` (tools/server/server-task.cpp) separates `reasoning_content` from `content` incrementally while streaming;
- the `reasoning-budget` sampler (common/reasoning-budget.cpp) tracks the reasoning block token by token (`REASONING_BUDGET_COUNTING` to `REASONING_BUDGET_DONE`), but only when a budget is set.

A snapshot of `server_slot_stats` (`n_gen`, `t_gen_last`, `n_draft_tokens`, `n_draft_accepted`) taken when the first non-reasoning token is emitted would give the `reasoning` object above; tokens of one speculative step share one timestamp, so step granularity is the natural precision.

Happy to test a PR on ROCm (gfx1201) + CUDA.
items.title: Feature Request: split generation timings into reasoning and answer phases (rate and draft acceptance per phase)

items.body: ## Overview This is a port of the existing CUDA graph code to SYCL. The code is mostly a straight port with two SYCL-specific exceptions: 1. The data must be reordered before recording because while SYCL async memory allocation extensions are available, using them leads to a hang during graph recording. 2. The library GEMM functions don't work with graph recording because it throws an exception: "Graph nodes cannot depend on events from outside the graph." This effectively limits the feature to decode for the time being. On A770 the performance improvement during decode is significant; on B70 it is negligible. Thus the feature remains off by default. ## Additional information While investigating performance differences on A770 between the Vulkan and SYCL backends, I found that kernel dispatch time consumed a large percentage of the SYCL time. The large difference was primarily due to the usage of the i915 driver. However there is still a modest gain with the xe driver. ### A770 performance comparison **xe driver** **i915 driver** ## Requirements - I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) - AI usage disclosure: YES. items.body:
When ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft splits allocation on buft max_size, a view-only tail at the end of the context could skip the final alloc_tensor_range. Persistent views (e.g. KV k_stream / v_stream) were then left without ggml_backend_view_init.
Allocate only parent tensors in alloc_tensor_range and initialize all views in a final pass over the context after all splits complete.
## Overview
`ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft` can split a context across multiple buffers when a tensor would exceed the backend buffer-type `max_size` (for example Vulkan's default 1 GiB). If the remaining tail of the context contains only views, the final `alloc_tensor_range` may be skipped, so those views never get `ggml_backend_view_init`.
Persistent KV stream views (`layer.k_stream` / `v_stream`) then keep `tensor->data == NULL` while `view_src` is allocated. Host state save/restore later calls `ggml_backend_tensor_get` / `set` on those views and hits:
`GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated")`
This change:
- allocates only parent tensors inside each split range
- initializes all uninitialized views in one final pass over the context
Also adds `test_view_init_after_max_size_split` in `tests/test-alloc.cpp`
to cover the oversized-parent + view-only-tail case.
## Additional information
Fixes #19839
Fixes #23737
Fixes #21762

Related:
- #21576 (state-IO `!tensor->data` guards; complementary discussion)
I reproduced the assert with Qwen3.6-27B (MTP) when a parent KV tensor exceeded buft `max_size` and the context ended with a view-only tail.
Note on #21576: skipping tensors with `!tensor->data` avoids the assert, but can omit real KV still reachable via `view_src` and misalign the serialized state. This PR fixes the missing view init in the allocator instead.
Prior investigation commit (same patch on older master; kept for reference):
https://github.com/Yoshi4470/llama.cpp/commit/99655d5854e63e736a6a93280e01b7e785a59ba5
## Test plan
- [x] `test-alloc` (includes new `test_view_init_after_max_size_split`)
- [x] Vulkan A/B on the Qwen3.6-27B MTP speculative path (same command, 10 runs each):
  - before (`e3546c794`): 0/10 (assert every time)
  - after (this PR): 10/10 (no assert, completed normally)
- [x] Earlier `amdvlk64.dll` crash after the assert site was resolved by an AMD driver update; treated as separate from this allocator fix
- N/A: equivalent-size CPU repro (not practical on this machine)

### Command used for the A/B runs:
- Vulkan / AMDVLK, Windows, AMD Software 26.6.4
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)
```
llama-cli.exe -np 8 -c 2097152 --no-mmap -m models/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ctkd q4_0 -ctvd q4_0 \
--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 -p "Hello!"
```

## Overview

This PR removes the `sched_need_reserve = true` line from `llama_context::set_causal_attn()`, which previously marked the scheduler to do a full re-reserve on every change of the flag, and fixes the one architecture (`qwen4exp`) whose graph shape depended on the flag.

The re-reserve is unnecessary in this case because `causal_attn` only changes the values written to the KQ mask, not tensor shapes or any other buffer sizes. `qwen4exp` was the one exception that selected the per block/cell bias path based on the flag, so the causal and non-causal graphs differed in tensor shapes and ops. The second commit selects the block path independent of `causal_attn`, from the mask shape only and makes the non-causal case follow the reference rule: every visible block competes on score and only unpooled cells are always selected. The causal case works as before.


## Additional information
<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

For vision inputs, this flag is flipped twice around each non-causal image chunk for Gemma3, Gemma4, and DeepSeek-V4, resulting in two expensive `sched_reserve()` passes per image. This is especially slow for multi-image or video inputs.

The cost of a re-reserve scales with context and ubatch configurations, so larger settings pay more per image (see table below).

Note: `causal_attn` is a graph reuse key (`llm_graph_params` via `cparams`), so a new graph is built regardless of `sched_need_reserve`, so this doesn't change the graph rebuilding behaviour.

Speedup table: llama-server with gemma-4-26B-A4B Q4_0 + BF16 mmproj, 130-token images, cache_prompt=false, prompt_ms median of 3 (before -> after):

| images | config | H200 before -> after | RTX 4090 before -> after |
|-|-|-|-|
| 1 | `-c 8192 -ub 512` | 134 -> 105 ms (1.27×) | 201 -> 119 ms (1.69×) |
| 24 | `-c 8192 -ub 512` | 2278 -> 1562 ms (1.46×) | 3559 -> 1748 ms (2.04×) |
| 24 | `-c 32768 -ub 2048` | 5379 -> 1584 ms (3.40×) | 13377 -> 1759 ms (7.61×) |

Generated output remains identical before and after.

## Overview

Adds an optional Vulkan device-level keepalive for investigating #26196.

When enabled with `GGML_VK_KEEPALIVE_MS`, each Vulkan device periodically submits a minimal GPU operation to help prevent idle GPU memory eviction.

## Overview

Small fixes to the Metal graph capture path in `ggml_metal_graph_compute`:

- Return `GGML_STATUS_SUCCESS` early when the graph has no nodes, avoiding the command-buffer/capture machinery for an empty graph.
- Drop the redundant reset of `ctx->capture_compute`: the decrement at the top of the function already transitions the counter from `0` to `-1`, so a capture happens exactly once (whether or not the capture scope starts successfully).
- Surface a `did you set METAL_CAPTURE_ENABLED=1 ?` hint in the capture error message.
- Pass `ctx->capture_compute == 0` (rather than the raw counter) as the `use_capture` argument to `ggml_metal_op_init`. The counter is a countdown, so any non-zero value (including `-1` after the first compute) coerced to `true` and caused per-node GPU debug-group markers to be emitted on every compute instead of only on the captured one.

## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

items.title: Misc. bug: Severe drop in prompt processing speed after b10780 on Vulkan, RDNA3

items.body:
## Environment

- **llama.cpp**: master `8144f31` (2026-08-23) + also reproduced on release b10488 (Windows CUDA 13.3 build)
- **OS**: Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04 (both tested, same cliff)
- **GPU**: RTX 4080 SUPER 16GB, driver 591.86 (CUDA 13.1), nvcc 13.1, sm_89
- **Model**: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` UD-Q3_K_XL (12.2GB); also reproduced with UD-IQ4_XS (13.3GB) and IQ4_XS (14.6GB)
- **Backend**: CUDA, single GPU

## Symptom

With the model **fully resident on GPU** (zero "assigned to device CPU" lines, verified in logs), decode (tg) speed collapses non-linearly once the KV position exceeds roughly 80K tokens — from ~33 t/s at 68K position to **1.4 t/s (714 ms/token) at 91K position**, or outright timeouts. **Prompt processing (pp) stays fast (~1300 t/s) at the same positions.** Zero-context decode is normal (~38-39 t/s) on every configuration below.

## Reproduction matrix (WSL2, llama-server)

Command shape:
```
./llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -ngl 999 --load-mode none \
    -c <CTX> [-fa on] -ctk <Q> -ctv <Q>
```
Then send a chat completion with a ~91K-token filler prompt and `max_tokens=100`.

| Config | VRAM fit (CPU overrides) | pp @91K fill | tg @91K position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-c 131072 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits, 0 CPU lines | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` | fits | fast | **timed out (>25 min)** |
| `-c 98304  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **timed out** |
| `-c 73728  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **33.1 t/s @ 68K position ✅** |

Position sweep with the last config (UD-Q3_K_XL, q8 KV, no FA):

| KV position (prompt tokens) | decode t/s (server-side timing) |
|---|---|
| 45,574 | 35.6 |
| 60,309 | 33.9 |
| 68,642 | 33.1 |
| 91,077 | **1.4 (or timeout)** |

## Key observations

1. **The cliff is positional, not a memory-spill issue.** All 96K/128K configs above report 0 CPU tensor overrides and normal free VRAM headroom; KV quantization level (q4/q5/q8) and `-fa on/off` make no difference to the cliff. Only the *position* matters.
2. **pp is unaffected at the same positions** (~1300 t/s for the 91K fill), so this is specific to the decode path.
3. The drop is far steeper than any plausible O(n) attention-scan cost: 68K→91K position is a 1.34x context increase but a **~24x decode slowdown**.
4. Server logs at the cliff show `eval time = 1055.41 ms / 300 tokens (0.95 tokens per second)` with `graphs reused = 298`, i.e. CUDA graph reuse continues normally while per-token latency explodes.
5. Also reproduced on the same hardware under Windows native (b10488) at large `-c`, so it is not WSL2-specific.

## Suspected area

Decode-path attention over long KV for the hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers (Qwen3.8 / qwen35-family). Possibly a fallback/slow kernel engaged past some KV extent threshold. Possibly related family: #27442 (empty generation >16K on Metal for qwen35moe hybrids), #27572 (draft acceptance collapse with multi-ubatch batches).

## Logs

Full `llama-server` logs for the 131072/q4/FA and 73728/q8/no-FA runs available on request (happy to attach — they contain per-token timing lines, tensor placement, and KV buffer sizes).

## Overview

**Co-authors:** @jxia4intel, @sliu39

**PR 2/3** of the Intel Xe optimization series — see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24408 (mega PR, draft) for the full feature set.

**Target platforms:** Xe-LPG Plus, Xe2, Xe3

This PR adds Intel Xe-specific flash attention optimization kernels for both ARLH iGPU (Xe1, UMA, coopmat1) and Xe2/Xe3. Dependency: builds on top of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24404 (Xe-LPG Plus coopmat1 enable). Independent of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24407 (GEMM+CW).

### Flash Attention (Intel Xe)

- New Vulkan shaders: single-phase prefill (`flash_attn_hdim64/96/128`) and two-phase split prefill/decode variants
- Pipelines keyed by `(head_dim, gqa_ratio)` for runtime dispatch across various GQA ratios without combinatorial pipeline proliferation
- Supports non-power-of-two GQA ratios via subgroup splitting (`qk_groups`)
- Intel Xe1 (integrated GPU, UMA, cooperative matrix) and Xe2 paths with separate warptile tuning
- Two-phase decode splits softmax reduction across subgroups; shared QK state copy (`fa_copy_qstate`) between prefill phases

items.body:
Building with the default flags, using a 4-bit KV cache (q4_0/q4_1) silently drops prefill to CPU speed. No warning, no offload message, just a ~30x slowdown that is very hard to diagnose from the outside.

What happens: the kernel selection in fattn.cu (ggml_cuda_fattn_kv_type_supported) only accepts f16/f32 KV unless GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS is set at compile time. When the requested KV type is not supported, the scheduler places the whole FLASH_ATTN_EXT op on the CPU backend.

Measured on a single RTX 3090, Qwen3.8-27B, K=q4_1 / V=q8_0, 130K ctx:

| build | prefill |
|---|---|
| default | ~34 t/s |
| -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON | 659-1094 t/s depending on context |

This is the third report of the same silent fallback in #27109 (myself, @aand18, @Cybertiron). Every user who wants 4-bit KV to fit long contexts in limited VRAM has to discover this flag on their own, and release builds ship without it.

Ask: make GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON the default in the CMake option, or at minimum print a clear warning at startup when the requested KV cache types cannot be served by the CUDA FA kernel.

PR #28634 flips the default.
items.title: CUDA: make GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON the default (silent CPU fallback for 4-bit KV)

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 0.3.0-dev (build 1, commit 0f3a71b)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Reproduced against `ggml-org/llama.cpp` commit `0f3a71be15af836d277c9f918adfafb45732677e`.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```
llama-server \
  -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --model-draft mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-mtp \
  --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  --parallel 1 \
  -c 262144 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -fa on \
  --slot-save-path /slot-cache
```

### Problem description

`POST /slots/{id}?action=save|restore` only persists `ctx_tgt` (via
`llama_state_seq_save_file`/`llama_state_seq_load_file`) — on a deployment
running speculative decoding (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`), the draft
model's own context (`ctx_dft`) is never captured or restored at all.

This is a separate, narrower gap from #25913 (checkpoints not persisted,
addressed by #26004): even once #26004 lands, a restored slot's draft
model only gets its state back if a checkpoint happened to already exist
at save time (checkpoints carry their own `data_dft`) — a short
conversation that hasn't hit its first checkpoint yet restores with an
empty draft-model KV cache and no fallback. The raw, currently-live
`ctx_dft` state is simply discarded on save, independent of checkpoint
existence.

Not directly observable as a crash or an error — the restore reports
success either way — but on a speculative-decoding deployment it means
the draft model silently starts cold after every restore whenever no
checkpoint happens to cover the request, undermining part of the benefit
`--slot-save-path` is meant to provide alongside #26004's fix.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start `llama-server` with a draft model (`--model-draft`/`--spec-type`)
   and `--slot-save-path`.
2. Send a short prompt (short enough that it completes before the first
   context checkpoint would be created) with `cache_prompt: true`.
3. `POST /slots/0?action=save`.
4. Inspect the save file: only the `ctx_tgt` payload
   (`llama_state_seq_save_file`'s own format) is present; there is no
   companion draft-model state anywhere.
5. `POST /slots/0?action=erase`, then `POST /slots/0?action=restore`.
6. The restore succeeds and reports the correct token count, but
   `ctx_dft` was never touched — the draft model's KV cache is empty,
   identical to a slot that just came up cold, regardless of what #26004
   restores for `ctx_tgt`/checkpoints.

### First bad commit

Not a regression — `SLOT_SAVE`/`SLOT_RESTORE` have never captured
`ctx_dft`; this predates both this report and #26004.

### Relationship to other issues/PRs

- #25913 / #26004: separate root cause (missing checkpoint persistence
  for `ctx_tgt`'s reuse-validity check), already well covered there. This
  report is about `ctx_dft` specifically, which #26004 does not touch.
- We have a working fix (raw `ctx_dft` capture/restore via
  `llama_state_seq_get_size_ext`/`get_data_ext`/`set_data_ext`, stored as
  a companion `<save-file>.dft`, verified live on a production
  Vulkan/AMD-APU draft-mtp deployment) and are happy to open it as a PR,
  either standalone or as a follow-up once #26004 merges (to avoid
  competing for review attention on the same file/handlers at once) —
  see our comment on #26004 for details.
items.title: Misc. bug: /slots save/restore never persists the draft-model context (ctx_dft) on speculative-decoding deployments

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: b10752 (b96806d96)
```
Container image `ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-vulkan`, run in router mode
(`--models-preset`), one child `llama-server` per model.

### Operating systems

Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic)

### GGML backends

Vulkan (Mesa RADV)

### Hardware

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 — Radeon 8060S Graphics (RADV STRIX_HALO, gfx1151),
120 GiB GTT, unified memory.

### Models

`Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf` (dense, 27.3B params, `n_ctx_train = 262144`), which
carries MTP layers.

### Problem description

With `--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp` and a large `--ctx-size`, the server
fails **every** request — including a 13-token prompt — dying within ~2s of the
prompt/decode transition and exiting with status 1. The router respawns it, so
the failure presents as a ~53s crash-loop that silently discards all prompt
cache.

The trigger is the **total** `--ctx-size`, not the per-sequence context. That
appears to come from `common/speculative.cpp`, where the MTP draft context is
sized from the target's total context despite the comment stating per-sequence
intent:

```c
// common/speculative.cpp — common_speculative_init_result::common_speculative_init_result()
    auto cparams = common_context_params_to_llama(params);

    if (spec_mtp) {
        cparams.ctx_type = LLAMA_CONTEXT_TYPE_MTP;
    }

    // the draft context holds as many tokens per sequence as the target context
    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx(ctx_tgt);        // <-- total, not per-sequence
```

`llama_n_ctx()` returns the total; `llama_n_ctx_seq()` is the per-sequence
accessor:

```c
// src/llama-context.cpp
uint32_t llama_n_ctx    (const llama_context * ctx) { return ctx->n_ctx();     }
uint32_t llama_n_ctx_seq(const llama_context * ctx) { return ctx->n_ctx_seq(); }
```

The draft context then builds its own memory module from those cparams:

```c
    memory.reset(model.create_memory(params_mem, cparams));
```

Under `--no-kv-unified` this makes the draft context `n_parallel` times larger
than the comment intends. Under `--kv-unified` it is worse, because
`n_ctx_seq` is then set equal to the whole total:

```c
// src/llama-context.cpp
    if (cparams.kv_unified) { cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx;                 }
    else                    { cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx / n_seq_max;     }
```

Note also that `--kv-unified-per-slot` cannot bound this: `llama_context_params`
has `n_ctx`, `n_seq_max` and `kv_unified`, but no per-slot field, so the
server-level cap never reaches the draft context.

### Ablation matrix

All rows below are on the same build, model, and machine, and each was verified
by serving requests. "draft n_ctx" is the value the code above assigns.

| `--ctx-size` | `--parallel` | kv-unified | `--spec-type` | draft `n_ctx` | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 786432 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 786432 | **fails every request** |
| 786432 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod` | — | works (12.8 tok/s, 99.99% cache reuse) |
| 393216 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 393216 | works (24 tok/s) |
| 524288 | 3 | on + `--kv-unified-per-slot 262144` | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 524288 | works (23.7 tok/s) |

Removing `draft-mtp` at the failing `--ctx-size` fixes it outright; restoring
`draft-mtp` at a smaller `--ctx-size` also fixes it. So the fault requires
`draft-mtp` **and** a large total `--ctx-size` together.

Note the third and fourth rows: the working unified config has a draft
`n_ctx_seq` of 524288, larger than the failing split config's 262144. So
per-sequence size is not the trigger — the **total** is.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
llama-server \
  --model Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --ctx-size 786432 --parallel 3 --no-kv-unified \
  --spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp \
  --spec-draft-n-max 4 --spec-draft-n-min 0 --draft-p-min 0.25 \
  --n-gpu-layers 999 --flash-attn on \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 512 --jinja

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"...","max_tokens":8,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say: ok"}]}'
```

The model loads normally and reports `status=loaded`. The first request — any
size — kills the process.

### What was ruled out

- **GPU/driver watchdog.** This machine separately had `amdgpu.lockup_timeout`
  at its 2000 ms default, which produced `ring comp_1.x.1 timeout`, a compute
  queue reset and `vk::DeviceLostError`. That was raised to
  `10000,60000,10000,10000` and the machine rebooted. `dmesg` has shown **zero**
  ring timeouts since, yet the MTP failure persists — so the two are unrelated
  faults and this report is only about the second.
- **Out of memory.** The failing configuration loads cleanly at 82 GiB of 120
  GiB GTT, and no OOM appears in `dmesg`. The failure is on first use, not at
  allocation.
- **Prompt length.** A 13-token prompt fails identically to a 100k one.
- **Tool/grammar constrained sampling.** A request with no `tools` fails too.
- **Build drift.** `b10752-b96806d96` throughout, verified via
  `system_fingerprint`; the container was restarted, never re-pulled.
- **Slot count alone.** `--parallel 3` works fine at smaller `--ctx-size`.

### Suggested fix

```diff
-    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx(ctx_tgt);
+    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx_seq(ctx_tgt);
```

This matches the stated intent of the comment. It would also make the draft
context independent of `--parallel`, which currently multiplies it.

### Possibly related

#23658 reports MTP draft acceptance collapsing at particular `--ctx-size`
values on a ~2048-aligned pattern, attributed there to "slot indexing in how
the MTP draft context shares the KV cache with the target context". That may be
the same sizing/indexing surface presenting as degradation rather than a crash.

### Relevant log output

```
# router, at the moment of failure
E srv    operator(): http client error: Failed to read connection
I srv    operator():

## Overview Currently with tensor/matrix cores we only use fp16 instructions, so dequant to shared memory -> fp16 GEMM. But many devices have higher throughput int8 tensor/matrix cores, so similar to the existing DP4A-based scalar MMQ path it would be good to have a coopmat int8 MMQ path. I have tried to make this work in the past, but failed due to architectural constraints in the coopmat extension. But based on @pwilkin's ideas in #27493, I finally managed to get it to work with good performance on RDNA3 and 4. This new MMQ cm1 shader supports q4_0, q4_1, q5_0, q5_1, q8_0, q3_k, q4_k, q5_k, q6_k, mxfp4, nvfp4 and iq4_nl on RDNA3 and RDNA4. Strix Halo prompt processing performance is significantly improved, RDNA4 is more neutral, but MoE prompt processing is also up significantly. The shader is limited to those two architectures since it hardcodes their specific coopmat access patterns. More architectures can be added if needed. q4_1, q5_1, q4_k, q5_k and nvfp4 on RDNA4 are disabled for MUL_MAT since they run slower than existing fp16 matmul. items.body:
## Overview

Extends the gate/up + GLU fusion, which today only covers small batches (MMVQ/MMVF), to prompt-processing batch
sizes on the MMQ path. For dense FFN layers where `ffn_gate` and `ffn_up` have the same type and shape, the two
matmuls and the GLU now run as one MMQ kernel: the activations are quantized once, the GLU is applied in the
write-back, and the standalone GLU kernel and the second activation quantization disappear.

Enabled for Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0 and IQ4_XS on GPUs with the MMA data layout; other cases take the existing path, I have a plan to enable it other types also. 

Implementation:
- `mul_mat_q` gets a fused variant (`has_fusion`): every thread keeps separate up and gate accumulators, so the
  block uses half the threads and rows of the stock tile (128 threads, 64 rows, 2 blocks/SM) and J is capped at 64.
  Per K step both Y halves are loaded once (cp.async where available, plain copy otherwise), then the up and the gate
  tiles are loaded and multiplied in turn. No stream-K: the GLU needs the full K reduction in one block. Column tiles
  are the innermost grid dimension, so neighbouring blocks reuse the same weight tiles from L2.
- Only the q8_0 / q4_K / q5_K / q6_K / iq4_xs loaders take the `has_fusion` parameter; the fused kernel is only
  compiled for the MMA layout.
- `ggml_cuda_op_glu_single` (unary.cuh) is now shared by the fused MMQ write-back, MMVQ and MMVF; the padding clear
  in `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q` / MMVQ moved to `ggml_cuda_clear_padding`.
- Graph side: the MUL_MAT + MUL_MAT + GLU pattern is matched in `ggml_cuda_try_fuse`; `graph_optimize` keeps the
  activation alive until the GLU node so the allocator cannot alias it with the fused output.

## Additional information

# Numbers for different Q4_K_M models
DGX Spark (GB10), CUDA 13.1, pp16384, `-b 2048 -ub 2048 -fa on`, f16 KV, t/s, master and PR in one session:

### Prerequisites

- [ ] I am running the latest code. Development is rapid so there are no tagged versions as of now. (Tested on the latest release, **v0.5.0**, b11146, commit 7fe450e19; the relevant server code is unchanged on master as of 2026-09-24.)
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Split the generation timings of a reasoning model into its two phases, reasoning and answer, in `llama-server`'s `timings` and in the `print_timing` log line.

Today `timings` reports one `predicted_n` / `predicted_ms` / `predicted_per_second`, plus one `draft_n` / `draft_n_accepted`, for the whole completion. With a reasoning model and speculative decoding those numbers average two workloads that behave very differently, so the single figure describes neither.

Proposed shape (names are only a suggestion), added next to the existing fields and emitted only when the response actually contained reasoning:

```json
"timings": {
  "predicted_n": 2048, "predicted_ms": 71416.1, "predicted_per_second": 28.66,
  "draft_n": 1902, "draft_n_accepted": 1412,
  "reasoning": {
    "predicted_n": 1825, "predicted_ms": 65216.3,
    "draft_n": 1737, "draft_n_accepted": 1247
  }
}
```

The answer phase is then the difference, so one extra object is enough. The `print_timing` line at the end of a request could carry the same split (`reasoning: 1825 tokens, 28.0 t/s, acc 72% | answer: 223 tokens, 35.6 t/s, acc 100%`).

### Motivation

We tune `--spec-draft-n-max` and pick quants from benchmarks, and a reasoning model's mean decode rate is the wrong number to tune on: how much of the output is reasoning moves with the question, and in agentic coding the reasoning phase is usually most of it.

Measured on llama.cpp v0.5.0 (b11146), Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 on an R9700 (ROCm) + RTX 4070 SUPER (CUDA) split, DFlash2 drafter, `temperature 0`, 2048 output tokens, 93.6k-token prompt, 3 repetitions each (the split was obtained client-side, see below):

| drafter | reasoning t/s | reasoning acc | answer t/s | answer acc | whole request t/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| none | 13.0 | | 12.9 | | 13.0 |
| DFlash2, n-max 3 | 28.0 (1825 tok) | 72% | 35.6 (223 tok) | 100% | 28.7 |
| DFlash2, n-max 7 | 33.7 (2048 tok) | 51% | (not reached) | | 33.6 |

- The answer drafts at 100% acceptance and is capped by `n-max` itself; the reasoning drafts at 51 to 72%. Their mean is a regime that does not exist.
- The phase share also changes between otherwise identical runs: at `temperature 0` the n-max 5 and 7 runs reasoned past the 2048-token cap while n-max 3 answered at token 1825, so two "decode" means compared naively mix different phase proportions.
- In the server log the phase change is visible as a step in `tg_3s` (about 22 t/s during reasoning, about 40 t/s once the answer starts, on a request with a longer answer), but nothing in the timings says where it happened.

The count alone (#27971, `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`, closed by its author) would not be enough for this: the rate and the draft acceptance per phase need the time and the draft counters at the boundary.

### Possible Implementation

We currently get this client-side: stream with `"timings_per_token": true`, and read the cumulative `timings` on the last event whose delta is `reasoning_content`; each phase is a difference of the server's own counters, with no client clock. That works, but it needs streaming and per-token timings on every event, and any client that does not stream cannot get it.

Server-side, the boundary is already known at generation time in two places:

- `task_result_state::update_chat_msg` (tools/server/server-task.cpp) separates `reasoning_content` from `content` incrementally while streaming;
- the `reasoning-budget` sampler (common/reasoning-budget.cpp) tracks the reasoning block token by token (`REASONING_BUDGET_COUNTING` to `REASONING_BUDGET_DONE`), but only when a budget is set.

A snapshot of `server_slot_stats` (`n_gen`, `t_gen_last`, `n_draft_tokens`, `n_draft_accepted`) taken when the first non-reasoning token is emitted would give the `reasoning` object above; tokens of one speculative step share one timestamp, so step granularity is the natural precision.

Happy to test a PR on ROCm (gfx1201) + CUDA.

items.body: ## Overview This is a port of the existing CUDA graph code to SYCL. The code is mostly a straight port with two SYCL-specific exceptions: 1. The data must be reordered before recording because while SYCL async memory allocation extensions are available, using them leads to a hang during graph recording. 2. The library GEMM functions don't work with graph recording because it throws an exception: "Graph nodes cannot depend on events from outside the graph." This effectively limits the feature to decode for the time being. On A770 the performance improvement during decode is significant; on B70 it is negligible. Thus the feature remains off by default. ## Additional information While investigating performance differences on A770 between the Vulkan and SYCL backends, I found that kernel dispatch time consumed a large percentage of the SYCL time. The large difference was primarily due to the usage of the i915 driver. However there is still a modest gain with the xe driver. ### A770 performance comparison **xe driver** **i915 driver** ## Requirements - I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) - AI usage disclosure: YES. items.body:
When ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft splits allocation on buft max_size, a view-only tail at the end of the context could skip the final alloc_tensor_range. Persistent views (e.g. KV k_stream / v_stream) were then left without ggml_backend_view_init.
Allocate only parent tensors in alloc_tensor_range and initialize all views in a final pass over the context after all splits complete.
## Overview
`ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft` can split a context across multiple buffers when a tensor would exceed the backend buffer-type `max_size` (for example Vulkan's default 1 GiB). If the remaining tail of the context contains only views, the final `alloc_tensor_range` may be skipped, so those views never get `ggml_backend_view_init`.
Persistent KV stream views (`layer.k_stream` / `v_stream`) then keep `tensor->data == NULL` while `view_src` is allocated. Host state save/restore later calls `ggml_backend_tensor_get` / `set` on those views and hits:
`GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated")`
This change:
- allocates only parent tensors inside each split range
- initializes all uninitialized views in one final pass over the context
Also adds `test_view_init_after_max_size_split` in `tests/test-alloc.cpp`
to cover the oversized-parent + view-only-tail case.
## Additional information
Fixes #19839
Fixes #23737
Fixes #21762

Related:
- #21576 (state-IO `!tensor->data` guards; complementary discussion)
I reproduced the assert with Qwen3.6-27B (MTP) when a parent KV tensor exceeded buft `max_size` and the context ended with a view-only tail.
Note on #21576: skipping tensors with `!tensor->data` avoids the assert, but can omit real KV still reachable via `view_src` and misalign the serialized state. This PR fixes the missing view init in the allocator instead.
Prior investigation commit (same patch on older master; kept for reference):
https://github.com/Yoshi4470/llama.cpp/commit/99655d5854e63e736a6a93280e01b7e785a59ba5
## Test plan
- [x] `test-alloc` (includes new `test_view_init_after_max_size_split`)
- [x] Vulkan A/B on the Qwen3.6-27B MTP speculative path (same command, 10 runs each):
  - before (`e3546c794`): 0/10 (assert every time)
  - after (this PR): 10/10 (no assert, completed normally)
- [x] Earlier `amdvlk64.dll` crash after the assert site was resolved by an AMD driver update; treated as separate from this allocator fix
- N/A: equivalent-size CPU repro (not practical on this machine)

### Command used for the A/B runs:
- Vulkan / AMDVLK, Windows, AMD Software 26.6.4
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)
```
llama-cli.exe -np 8 -c 2097152 --no-mmap -m models/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ctkd q4_0 -ctvd q4_0 \
--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 -p "Hello!"
```
## Requirements
- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - Cursor assisted with implementing the finalize-views pass and regression test after I identified the root cause in the alloc split path, and with local verification.

### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description


## Summary

Public GGUFs for [prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf](https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf) use two **new** GGML tensor types that stock `ggml-org/llama.cpp` does not know:

| Name | Tensor type ID | Role |
|------|---------------:|------|
| `PQ2_0` | **142** | 2-bit slots for ternary g128 (`{-1,0,+1}` + FP16 group scale) |
| `PTQ1_0` | **143** | dense trit packing of the same ternary g128 weights |

These are **not** upstream `Q1_0` (type 41) and **not** upstream `Q2_0` (type 42, group 64). They were given high IDs so they can coexist with those types.

Stock `llama-cli` rejects them as unknown types. If a loader treats an unknown type as `Q2_0`, Prism’s card says the result is **garbage** (no Hadamard activation transform).

This is a request to either:

1. **Upstream** `PQ2_0` / `PTQ1_0` (parse + dequant + matmul, including the Hadamard path), or
2. **Reject loudly** with the type name, and document that these files need the Prism fork until they land.

I am not affiliated with Prism ML. I hit this while importing the public GGUFs (also via Ollama `create`, which vendors llama.cpp and fails the same way).

## Public files (Apache 2.0)

Repo: https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf

| File | Size (bytes) | `general.file_type` | Dominant tensor type |
|------|-------------:|--------------------:|---------------------:|
| `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PQ2_0.gguf` | 7,206,168,928 | 141 | **142** (`PQ2_0`) |
| `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf` | 5,946,648,928 | 143 | **143** (`PTQ1_0`) |
| `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-F16.gguf` | 53,808,408,928 | F16 | 1 (not the issue) |
| `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-mmproj-Q8_0.gguf` | 629,246,976 | Q8_0 | 8 (loads; vision only) |

Architecture metadata: `qwen35`. Example tensor: `output.weight` / `token_embd.weight` shape `[5120, 248320]`, type 142 or 143.

Verified SHA256 (HF LFS):

- PQ2_0: `3907dc1658db1f78a9826bf8d5bcb8dc65db0d466388937af57f2294fae62ec1`
- PTQ1_0: `53107f530aa52eb00912263ab1ee29bd199261c87cd7b4ad4ca1318c1fe33ee3`

## How this differs from formats that already work

| Format | Typical file | Type ID | Mainline llama.cpp | Notes |
|--------|--------------|--------:|:------------------:|-------|
| 1-bit Bonsai `Q1_0` | `prism-ml/Bonsai-27B-gguf` `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf` | 41 | Yes (e.g. [#20048](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/20048) / follow-ups) | This is what Ollama listings like `*:bonsai-27b-q1_0` run |
| Ternary `Q2_0` g64 | `*-Q2_0_g64.gguf` | 42 | Yes (CPU/Metal/Vulkan; CUDA tracked separately) | Official upstream ternary packing |
| Fork ternary `Q2_0` g128 | `*-Q2_0.gguf` (Bonsai 1) | 42, **different block size** | No (same id, wrong layout) | [Bonsai-demo ternary status](https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/Bonsai-demo#upstream-status-for-ternary) |
| **Bonsai 2 `PQ2_0` / `PTQ1_0`** | files above | **142 / 143** | **No** | New IDs + Hadamard-rotated ternary |

Bonsai 2 is a new checkpoint (Qwen3.8-27B lineage, hybrid attention, 262K context), not a requant of Bonsai-27B `Q1_0`.

## What Prism’s fork already names

From [PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp](https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp) `ggml/include/ggml.h` (`prism` branch):

```c
GGML_TYPE_Q1_0    = 41,
GGML_TYPE_Q2_0    = 42,
// Prism-private Q2_0 at group size 128 (upstream Q2_0 is group 64). High id so it
// slots above upstream types; type_traits is sized to COUNT (143) with 43..141 unused.
GGML_TYPE_PQ2_0   = 142,
GGML_TYPE_PTQ1_0  = 143, // Prism-private ternary, group 128
GGML_TYPE_COUNT   = 144,
```

The same header also defines `GGML_HINT_SRC0_IS_HADAMARD`. The [HF card](https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf) says weights are stored after a blockwise Hadamard (block 1024); the runtime must apply the matching transform to activations or **refuse to load**. Registering a block size without that path is not enough.

Prism’s own demo README still lists `PQ2_0` as “planned / nothing yet” for the *previous* Ternary-Bonsai-27B drop. Bonsai 2 has already shipped files with types 142/143.

Reference implementation: https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp  
Demo / pinned binaries: https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/Bonsai-demo

## Reproduction (stock llama.cpp)

```bash
hf download prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf \
  Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PQ2_0.gguf \
  --local-dir .

# latest ggml-org/llama.cpp release binary
./llama-cli -m Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PQ2_0.gguf -p "ping" -n 16
```

**Expected:** model loads, or a clear `unknown type 142 (PQ2_0)` error.

**Actual (stock):** unknown type / load failure. Downstream Ollama 0.33.2 `ollama create` reports `Error: tensor "output.weight" size overflow` because its GGUF parser returns type size 0 for 142/143.

Same result for `Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf` (type 143).

`Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-F16.gguf` is a standard F16 GGUF (~50.1 GiB) and is not the format users are meant to deploy.

## Packing (from Prism’s card + fork comments)

- Ternary g128: each weight in `{-1, 0, +1}`, one FP16 scale per 128 weights (~1.72 bits/weight including a small set of higher-precision tensors).
- `PTQ1_0`: dense trits, ~1.75 bpw, ~5.95 GB language model.
- `PQ2_0`: one trit in a 2-bit slot, ~2.13 bpw, ~7.21 GB; this is the pack Prism reports on Apple Silicon.
- Group size **128** (not upstream `Q2_0` group 64, not `TQ1_0`/`TQ2_0` group 256).

I do not have a public spec for the exact `block_pq2_0` / `block_ptq1_0` C layouts in this issue; those live in the Prism fork (`ggml-common.h` / quant kernels). Happy to help

## Overview

The `--models` output of `test-save-load-state` was very heavy: every model printed its token dumps, per-test headers and PASS lines, making it hard to see which models pass.

items.body:
## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

items.title: Eval bug: Speculative decoding (draft-mtp / draft-dspark): greedy output diverges from vanilla on quantized targets

items.body:
## Environment

- **llama.cpp**: master `8144f31` (2026-08-23) + also reproduced on release b10488 (Windows CUDA 13.3 build)
- **OS**: Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04 (both tested, same cliff)
- **GPU**: RTX 4080 SUPER 16GB, driver 591.86 (CUDA 13.1), nvcc 13.1, sm_89
- **Model**: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` UD-Q3_K_XL (12.2GB); also reproduced with UD-IQ4_XS (13.3GB) and IQ4_XS (14.6GB)
- **Backend**: CUDA, single GPU

## Symptom

With the model **fully resident on GPU** (zero "assigned to device CPU" lines, verified in logs), decode (tg) speed collapses non-linearly once the KV position exceeds roughly 80K tokens — from ~33 t/s at 68K position to **1.4 t/s (714 ms/token) at 91K position**, or outright timeouts. **Prompt processing (pp) stays fast (~1300 t/s) at the same positions.** Zero-context decode is normal (~38-39 t/s) on every configuration below.

## Reproduction matrix (WSL2, llama-server)

Command shape:
```
./llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -ngl 999 --load-mode none \
    -c <CTX> [-fa on] -ctk <Q> -ctv <Q>
```
Then send a chat completion with a ~91K-token filler prompt and `max_tokens=100`.

| Config | VRAM fit (CPU overrides) | pp @91K fill | tg @91K position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-c 131072 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits, 0 CPU lines | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` | fits | fast | **timed out (>25 min)** |
| `-c 98304  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **timed out** |
| `-c 73728  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **33.1 t/s @ 68K position ✅** |

Position sweep with the last config (UD-Q3_K_XL, q8 KV, no FA):

| KV position (prompt tokens) | decode t/s (server-side timing) |
|---|---|
| 45,574 | 35.6 |
| 60,309 | 33.9 |
| 68,642 | 33.1 |
| 91,077 | **1.4 (or timeout)** |

## Key observations

1. **The cliff is positional, not a memory-spill issue.** All 96K/128K configs above report 0 CPU tensor overrides and normal free VRAM headroom; KV quantization level (q4/q5/q8) and `-fa on/off` make no difference to the cliff. Only the *position* matters.
2. **pp is unaffected at the same positions** (~1300 t/s for the 91K fill), so this is specific to the decode path.
3. The drop is far steeper than any plausible O(n) attention-scan cost: 68K→91K position is a 1.34x context increase but a **~24x decode slowdown**.
4. Server logs at the cliff show `eval time = 1055.41 ms / 300 tokens (0.95 tokens per second)` with `graphs reused = 298`, i.e. CUDA graph reuse continues normally while per-token latency explodes.
5. Also reproduced on the same hardware under Windows native (b10488) at large `-c`, so it is not WSL2-specific.

## Suspected area

Decode-path attention over long KV for the hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers (Qwen3.8 / qwen35-family). Possibly a fallback/slow kernel engaged past some KV extent threshold. Possibly related family: #27442 (empty generation >16K on Metal for qwen35moe hybrids), #27572 (draft acceptance collapse with multi-ubatch batches).

## Logs

Full `llama-server` logs for the 131072/q4/FA and 73728/q8/no-FA runs available on request (happy to attach — they contain per-token timing lines, tensor placement, and KV buffer sizes).

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
The current approach to handling experts in MoE models use one GEMM per expert. These activations are relatively narrow, and cannot use the compute hardware effectively (neither ALU0/1 nor the XMX tiles). Additionally, the small inputs result in particularly inefficient dequantization. 
This can be fixed by grouping many small experts into one kernel, and handling them in one operation.

This patch proposes grouped and optionally fused GEMM kernels tuned on XMX (`joint_matrix`).
Approach:
- Build a host-side schedule of active expert tiles and launch as one grouped kernel instead of one GEMM per expert
- Dequantizes IQ4_NL or IQ3_S weights into f16 tiles in local memory
- Packs routed f32 activations into the VNNI f16 layout consumed by XMX.
