items.body:
When ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft splits allocation on buft max_size, a view-only tail at the end of the context could skip the final alloc_tensor_range. Persistent views (e.g. KV k_stream / v_stream) were then left without ggml_backend_view_init.
Allocate only parent tensors in alloc_tensor_range and initialize all views in a final pass over the context after all splits complete.
## Overview
`ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft` can split a context across multiple buffers when a tensor would exceed the backend buffer-type `max_size` (for example Vulkan's default 1 GiB). If the remaining tail of the context contains only views, the final `alloc_tensor_range` may be skipped, so those views never get `ggml_backend_view_init`.
Persistent KV stream views (`layer.k_stream` / `v_stream`) then keep `tensor->data == NULL` while `view_src` is allocated. Host state save/restore later calls `ggml_backend_tensor_get` / `set` on those views and hits:
`GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated")`
This change:
- allocates only parent tensors inside each split range
- initializes all uninitialized views in one final pass over the context
Also adds `test_view_init_after_max_size_split` in `tests/test-alloc.cpp`
to cover the oversized-parent + view-only-tail case.
## Additional information
Fixes #19839
Fixes #23737
Fixes #21762

Related:
- #21576 (state-IO `!tensor->data` guards; complementary discussion)
I reproduced the assert with Qwen3.6-27B (MTP) when a parent KV tensor exceeded buft `max_size` and the context ended with a view-only tail.
Note on #21576: skipping tensors with `!tensor->data` avoids the assert, but can omit real KV still reachable via `view_src` and misalign the serialized state. This PR fixes the missing view init in the allocator instead.
Prior investigation commit (same patch on older master; kept for reference):
https://github.com/Yoshi4470/llama.cpp/commit/99655d5854e63e736a6a93280e01b7e785a59ba5
## Test plan
- [x] `test-alloc` (includes new `test_view_init_after_max_size_split`)
- [x] Vulkan A/B on the Qwen3.6-27B MTP speculative path (same command, 10 runs each):
  - before (`e3546c794`): 0/10 (assert every time)
  - after (this PR): 10/10 (no assert, completed normally)
- [x] Earlier `amdvlk64.dll` crash after the assert site was resolved by an AMD driver update; treated as separate from this allocator fix
- N/A: equivalent-size CPU repro (not practical on this machine)

### Command used for the A/B runs:
- Vulkan / AMDVLK, Windows, AMD Software 26.6.4
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)
```
llama-cli.exe -np 8 -c 2097152 --no-mmap -m models/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ctkd q4_0 -ctvd q4_0 \
--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 -p "Hello!"
```
## Requirements
- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - Cursor assisted with implementing the finalize-views pass and regression test after I identified the root cause in the alloc split path, and with local verification.

## Overview

This PR removes the `sched_need_reserve = true` line from `llama_context::set_causal_attn()`, which previously marked the scheduler to do a full re-reserve on every change of the flag, and fixes the one architecture (`qwen4exp`) whose graph shape depended on the flag.

The re-reserve is unnecessary in this case because `causal_attn` only changes the values written to the KQ mask, not tensor shapes or any other buffer sizes. `qwen4exp` was the one exception that selected the per block/cell bias path based on the flag, so the causal and non-causal graphs differed in tensor shapes and ops. The second commit selects the block path independent of `causal_attn`, from the mask shape only and makes the non-causal case follow the reference rule: every visible block competes on score and only unpooled cells are always selected. The causal case works as before.


## Additional information
<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

For vision inputs, this flag is flipped twice around each non-causal image chunk for Gemma3, Gemma4, and DeepSeek-V4, resulting in two expensive `sched_reserve()` passes per image. This is especially slow for multi-image or video inputs.

The cost of a re-reserve scales with context and ubatch configurations, so larger settings pay more per image (see table below).

Note: `causal_attn` is a graph reuse key (`llm_graph_params` via `cparams`), so a new graph is built regardless of `sched_need_reserve`, so this doesn't change the graph rebuilding behaviour.

Speedup table: llama-server with gemma-4-26B-A4B Q4_0 + BF16 mmproj, 130-token images, cache_prompt=false, prompt_ms median of 3 (before -> after):

| images | config | H200 before -> after | RTX 4090 before -> after |
|-|-|-|-|
| 1 | `-c 8192 -ub 512` | 134 -> 105 ms (1.27×) | 201 -> 119 ms (1.69×) |
| 24 | `-c 8192 -ub 512` | 2278 -> 1562 ms (1.46×) | 3559 -> 1748 ms (2.04×) |
| 24 | `-c 32768 -ub 2048` | 5379 -> 1584 ms (3.40×) | 13377 -> 1759 ms (7.61×) |

Generated output remains identical before and after.

### Name and Version

Bionic bundled llama.cpp Vulkan 2.41.0 (crash) / 2.39.0 (ok); llama-server reports version 0.4.1-dev build 1 commit b49650a

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

2x Intel Arc Pro B50 (driver 32.0.101.8805) + Intel Core Ultra 5 235HX, 64GB RAM

### Models

All of these fail identically on 2.40/2.41 Vulkan, all load fine on 2.39 Vulkan:
- bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- unsloth/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512-GGUF (Q5_K_M)
- empero-ai/Qwen3.8-35B-A3B-Distill-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
Counter-case: nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (Q4_K_M) loads fine on 2.41 Vulkan.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## What happened

`llama-server` with the Vulkan backend crash-aborts while loading sliding-window-attention
decoder models when the KV cache is offloaded to the GPU. The process dies with
`exitCode=3221226505` (`0xC0000409`, fail-fast) before becoming healthy.

Exact abort line (stderr):

```text
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)
```

## Regression info

- ✅ `llama.cpp ... 2.39.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **loads in ~5s, serves fine**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.40.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.41.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with `--no-kv-offload` — **loads and serves** (KV cache on CPU)
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with full offload + embedding model (`nomic-embed-text-v1.5.Q4_K_M`,
  full attention, `--embedding`) — **loads and serves**

So it is not a globally broken Vulkan backend: it is the
`Vulkan + KV-cache GPU offload + SWA/hybrid-attention decoder` path that regressed
between 2.39 and 2.40.

## Repro

```bat
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf -ngl 99 --port 18081
```

- Model: `bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF`, `Q4_K_S` (~2.4 GB)
- No other flags (all defaults). Crash happens during `load_model`, before listening.

Notable log lines on the crashing 2.41 run (before the abort):

```text
W resolve_fused_ops: layer 0 is assigned to device Vulkan1 but Flash Attention is assigned to device CPU (usually due to missing support)
W resolve_fused_ops: Flash Attention not supported, set to disabled
W ggml_vulkan: Failed to allocate pinned memory (Requested buffer size exceeds device buffer size limit: ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory)
```

On the working `--no-kv-offload` run the server reports `kv_unified = 'true'`,
`n_slots = 4`, then `model loaded` / `listening`.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 x64 (build 10.0.26200)
- GPU: Intel Arc Pro B50 (discrete) + Intel integrated Graphics
- Driver: Intel `32.0.101.8805` (06.07.2026), `vulkan-1.dll` present (system + app dir)
- Builds: LM Studio / Bionic bundled `llama.cpp-win-x86_64-vulkan-avx2` packs
  `2.39.0` (working) vs `2.40.0` / `2.41.0` (crashing), CPU 14 threads
- The same setup serves the models fine on engine 2.39, so driver / loader / model
  file are ruled out

## Suspected area

New fused-ops / unified-KV graph building for SWA models (`cache_k` pre-allocation
landing in a Vulkan buffer that reports no supported op) introduced between 2.39
and 2.40. Happy to test any debug build / extra logging on this machine
(Arc Pro B50 available).

### First Bad Commit

Regressed between bundled builds 2.39.0 (works) and 2.40.0 (broken). Exact upstream commit unknown — these are third-party Bionic/LM Studio bundles, not direct llama.cpp builds. Happy to bisect if given build instructions for Windows Vulkan.

### Relevant log output


Command:
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf --port 18081 -ngl 99

Log:
load_model: loading model '.../mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf'
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)

Process exits immediately with code 3221226505 (0xC0000409).

We ran **#27952** ("Vulkan: int8 coopmat quantized matmul for RDNA3/4") through our own Vulkan build on a **Radeon RX 7900 XTX** (gfx1100, 24 GB, PCIe 3.0 x16, no ReBAR, 4-core W-2125) with a **27B** model, and wanted to share the results plus a small related fix.

## Context
On this box the 27B runs on the **Vulkan** backend (~3 GB lighter than ROCm/HIP, more VRAM for context). Model: **Qwen3.8-27B, ROCmFP4-FAST quant (~13.6 GB)**, `MTP n-max 4`, `--flash-attn on`, `--cache-type-k/v q8_0`, `-c 131072`.

## A/B benchmark (same GGUF + byte-identical flags, 3 repeats, greedy)

| workload | metric | base Vulkan | +#27952 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| agent (long-ctx) | prompt t/s | 631.0 | **670.1** | **+6.2%** |
| agent | token t/s | 103.1 | **104.9** | +1.7% |
| agent | MTP draft accept | 88% | **100%** | **+12 pp** |
| agent | wall (s) | 4.89 | **4.70** | -3.9% |
| tools (short-ctx) | prompt t/s | 417.0 | 421.8 | +1.2% |
| tools | token t/s | 117.4 | 117.2 | ~0 |

The gain concentrates on the **prefill-heavy / long-context** workload; the standout is **MTP draft acceptance 88% -> 100%**. Cross-reference: the upstream 7B harness (7900 XTX, ReBAR/PCIe4) reports int8-coopmat at +4.6% dense prefill and +18.5% MoE prefill, decode flat - same shape.

## Small related fix (patch below)

In `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/mul_mmq_cm1_funcs.glsl`, when `K` is not a multiple of `BK*BK_STEP`, the A-operand load reads `ib + ks` past `end_k` - which can land on the next row, or on bytes after the tensor whose f16 scale can be **NaN**. Clamping the block index re-reads the row's first block instead; its B side is zeroed, so it contributes nothing:

```
-                pre_a[li * BK_STEP + ks] = block_a_load(ib + ks, loadr_a);
+                /* K need not be a multiple of BK*BK_STEP: a k-step past end_k re-reads the  */
+                /* row's first block (finite), and its B side is zeroed, so it adds nothing. */
+                /* Reading on past the row instead picks up the next row, or bytes after the */
+                /* tensor whose f16 scale can be NaN.                                         */
+                const uint ib_k = ((blk) + ks * BK < end_k) ? (ib + ks) : ib;
+                pre_a[li * BK_STEP + ks] = block_a_load(ib_k, loadr_a);
```

One-line defensive correctness fix, no measurable cost. (Our `mul_mmq_cm1.comp` is otherwise byte-identical to #27952.)

## Offer
Happy to submit a PR - fold the `mul_mmq_cm1_funcs.glsl` fix into #27952, or as a small follow-up. Can share the benchmark harness if useful.

**Env:** RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) - Mesa 26.2.2 (RADV) - Vulkan - llama.cpp c550d2f6 + #27952.

### Name and Version

```
version: 0.4.0-dev (build 10830, commit 0cd7a79f5)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64
```

Note: this is the Unsloth-compiled prebuilt of b10830, not a build from upstream source. I have not yet reproduced it on current master; happy to do that (or run `llama-batched-bench`) if it helps.

### Operating systems

Mac

### GGML backends

Metal

### Hardware

Apple M3 Ultra (Mac15,14), 512 GB unified memory, macOS 26.6.2 (25G83)

### Models

`unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF`, Q8_0 (arch `qwen4exp`, 512-expert MoE, 10 active). Also seen with GLM-5.3-Flash UD-Q4_K_XL (`glm5next`, see below).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

On Metal, decode throughput falls apart when **several long sequences decode in the same batch**. It gets worse faster than linearly in the number of sequences, and worse with longer contexts. With one sequence, decode speed barely changes with context length. The GPU isn't saturated either: separate `-np 1` processes running at the same time on the same GGUF reach 4.6× the throughput of one process decoding the same two sequences as a batch.

**Server** (idle, nothing else sending requests):

```
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q8_0-00001-of-00006.gguf --flash-attn on -np 8 \
  --kv-unified --no-context-shift --jinja --metrics
```

**Probe:** N concurrent `/completion` requests. Each has a *unique* ~K-token prompt, so the prompt cache can't hit. Settings: `cache_prompt: false`, `ignore_eos`, 128 generated tokens, thinking off. Rates come from the server's `timings`. "Aggregate" means total generated tokens divided by the decode window (the time after the last prefill finishes). Milliseconds per forward pass come from the `llamacpp:n_decode_total` delta. The script is below.

**Aggregate decode tok/s:**

| Context | N=1 | N=2 | N=4 | N=8 | ms per decode pass, N=1 → N=max |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 256 | 32.8 | 45 | 60 | **78** | 33 → 112 |
| 4 k | — | — | — | 23 | |
| 8 k | — | — | 23.5 | 11.6 | |
| 16 k | **25.9** | 10.3 | 6.9 | **5.2** | 39 → 195 → 580 → ~1500 |
| 32 k | **25.7** | 8.6 | 5.5 | — | 39 → 233 → 730 |

Per-request speed at N=1 is 32.8 / 28.9 / 26.0 tok/s for 256 / 16 k / 32 k context. At short context, batching works as expected. At 16 k and above, **N=1 gives the highest aggregate**. Adding a second 32 k sequence to the batch adds about 194 ms per pass. Reading that sequence's extra KV at memory bandwidth should add only a few ms.

**Ablations** (restarted server, 16 k context, N=8, ms per decode pass):

| Variant | ms/pass |
|---|---:|
| as above | 1260 |
| `--flash-attn off` | 2488 (worse) |
| per-slot KV (no `--kv-unified`) | 1015 (−20%, doesn't remove the cliff) |
| `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | 1206 (no change) |

**Different architecture, same cliff:** GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5next`, served from the same prebuilt; I know it's still an open PR upstream, #27752) goes from 40 to 10.6 tok/s aggregate at N=4 between 256 and 8 k context. That makes me think the problem is in the Metal batched-decode attention path, not in anything specific to Qwen's hybrid layers.

**Several processes instead of a batch** (same GGUF, mmap'd weights shared, each process `-np 1` with one 32 k sequence):

| Layout at 32 k | Aggregate tok/s | Per stream |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 process, N=1 | 25.7 | 25.7 |
| 1 process, N=2 batched | 8.6 | 4.3 |
| 1 process, N=4 batched | 5.5 | 1.4 |
| **2 processes × N=1** | **39.4** | 19.6 / 19.8 |
| 3 processes × N=1 | 38.0 | 12.9 / 12.9 / 12.2 |

We use two `-np 1` processes behind a load balancer in production as a workaround.

Possibly related, from reading open PRs (I haven't tested any of them): #28439 (wider query tile for `kernel_flash_attn_ext`), #29110 (multi-column mat-vec for ne11 = 2..8), and the note in #28495 that Metal already skips interior all-`-INF` KV blocks. That last point fits the small per-slot-KV gain above.

<details><summary>Probe script (48 lines, stdlib only)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Long-context throughput probe for a llama-server: N concurrent requests, each with a UNIQUE
prompt of ~K tokens (defeats the prompt cache), M generated tokens, thinking off.
Reports server-side prefill and decode rates from `timings`, aggregate decode tok/s over the
steady window, and forward passes (llamacpp:n_decode_total delta) -> ms per pass, tokens per pass."""
import argparse, json, random, time, urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--host", default="localhost:8080")
ap.add_argument("--ctx", type=int, required=True, help="target prompt tokens")
ap.add_argument("-n", type=int, default=8)
ap.add_argument("--gen", type=int, default=128)
ap.add_argument("--label", default="")
a = ap.parse_args()
base = f"http://{a.host}"
def get(path): return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base}{path}", timeout=30))
def post(path, body, timeout=3600):
    r = urllib.request.Request(f"{base}{path}", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(r, timeout=timeout))
def metric(name):
    for l in urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base}/metrics", timeout=10).read().decode().splitlines():
        if l.startswith(name + " "): return float(l.split()[1])
    return 0.0
words = "the of and to in is that for it as with on be at by this from or an are not have was but which one you all can had her were their said each she do how its if will up other about out many then them these so some would make like into him time has look two more write go see number no way could people my than first water been call who oil sit now find long down day did get come made may part".split()
def make_prompt(k, seed):

    text = " ".join(rnd.choice(words) for _ in range(int(k * 1.3)))
    toks = post("/tokenize", {"content": text})["tokens"]
    body = post("/detokenize", {"tokens": toks[:k - 40]})["content"]

items.body:
## Overview

When CUB has no DeviceTopK (every CCCL older than 3.2), ggml_cuda_op_top_k falls back to sorting every key of every row with a segmented radix sort and copying the first k. For wide rows the cost of the sort is large, the qwen4exp QSA indexer runs TOP_K over 4 rows x n_kv columns with k = 2051,and at 131k context that sort costs 5.1 ms per generated token which is about a third of the GPU time per token.

This PR makes the existing radix-select kernel (Until now this has been HIP-only) available to CUB builds without DeviceTopK and uses it in that fallback for rows of >= 8192 columns. The threshold was measured, it wasn't estimated or guessed. On an RTX 3090 (CUDA 12.0, CUB 2.0.1), the segmented sort was still faster at 4096 columns and the radix-select was faster from 8192 on. Builds that have CCCL >= 3.2 keep using DeviceTopK. HIP, MUSA and no-CUB builds are unchanged by this. GGML_CUDA_TOPK_ARGSORT=1 forces the old path so both can be compared within one binary.

## Additional information

Correctness: test-backend-ops -o TOP_K passes 525/525 on both paths (268 cases at >= 8192 columns, up to 524,299 columns, k up to 9,999, 112 with ties).

**Kernel only timings (test-backend-ops perf, TOP_K with k = 16, CUDA graphs off, GPU shared with a running server):** on all 46 test shapes with rows of 8192 columns or more, radix-select beats the segmented sort by about 1.42x at worst and 2.25x in the median and up to 11x for 16-row batches. On 4096-column rows, the sort was still faster (24.1 us vs 38.9 us for radix-select), so the switch happens at 8192 columns rather than the 1024 proposed in the earlier unmerged #28366.

**End to end (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Q4_K_XL, 131k context, MTP draft, same binary, kill-switch A/B, two windows run in both orders):** Nsight Systems traces show the top-k kernels dropping from 5.1 to 0.25 ms per generated token. Decode on cached 128-token continuations increased from 30.3 to 34.9 t/s, +13 to +18% on every one of six position-paired runs, and a fresh 128-token request after the prefill gained +10% as well (one pair). Prefill was unchanged as expected considering the sort does not run there. A separate production-sampling quality screen (480 requests at ~37k and ~119k context, three seeds, argsort path as the control) found no consistent quality regression and 9 to 12% higher decode throughput at ~119k on every seed.

**Some caveats:**
- Tie behaviour differs. The segmented sort always kept the lower index so its output was repeatable. Radix-select, like CUB's DeviceTopK keeps whichever of the exactly tied values it reaches first so the selected set can differ between runs when ties occur. Any tied choice is a valid top-k result and test-backend-ops accepts it. This is the same behaviour #28497 describes for DeviceTopK.
- The 4096/8192 crossover was measured at k = 16 without CUDA graphs on one GPU model. Other k and other GPUs may cross elsewhere. The threshold of 8192 is conservative for the 3090.
- Not measured: MUSA and no-CUB builds (unchanged by this PR), other k at the boundary, an idle GPU.

This was measured on 2x RTX 3090 (sm_86), driver 595.84, CUDA 12.0.140, CUB 2.0.1, where CUB_TOP_K_AVAILABLE is undefined and this fallback is the active path.

Related earlier work: #28366 proposed the same dispatch with a 1024-column threshold and no measurements. It was closed unmerged.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES. The code change was written by an AI assistant (Claude) under my direction and reviewed by me. All builds, tests, profiles and quality measurements were run by me on my own hardware. This description and the commit message are my own words.

unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF  UD-Q4_K_XL -ngl 99, layer split across 5 GPUs,

This is a likely a duplicate of a previous report erroneusly closed by reporter #27856, I can't reopen it so I'm submitting this one with all my detail. The issue #27856 is not a duplicate of #27856, that one appears to be fixed (it reports much more severe deterioration).

When runnig the PR #27742 branch I initaly noticed substantial performance degradation about halving the decode speed starting at 54 tok/s every 50k context size or so.

Using the latest master df03399b8 this is much improved to:
 - 37.2tok/s to 50.8tok/s  at 42k ctx (+37%)
-  22.5tok/s 48.0tok/s  at 111k (+113%),
-  11tok/s to 41.8 tok/s at 250k

but still deteriorating to "nighly speed" on my hardware at the bottom of the context.

Please note both generation is affected (severely) as well aas prefill (a lot less). Prefill almost halves the speed at max 260k context so far less impactful.

I let my LLM run over the code to see what improvements it finds and by the morning indeed it managed to make changes that helped a lot to:
- 37.2tok/s to 50.8tok/s at 42k ctx (+37%)
- 22.5tok/s to 48.0tok/s at 111k (+113%)

It performed some correctness validation that suggests we didn't brake anything, but I'm far from claiming a "fix" at this stage (have yet to validate properly).

The diff is almost 2k lines over 7 patches so it is too big to include here. I will provide it upon request.


### First Bad Commit

it was built from pull/27742/head

### Relevant log output

I also include a brief LLM written sumamry of changes made below:

# qwen4exp decode depth-decay — LLM generated "fix" summary

**Arch:** `qwen4exp` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, 125B-A6B; 12 QSA sparse-attn + 36 Gated-DeltaNet layers, `indexer.top_k=2048`, `compress_ratio=4`).
**Problem:** single-stream decode slows ~linearly with context depth even though QSA is supposed to bound attention to a fixed top-k budget. Root cause (nsys-profiled): the top-k path was running as a **dense** attention scan over all `n_kv`, plus per-token re-pooling of the whole cache and MBs of host→device + P2P input traffic.
**Base:** llama.cpp master `df03399b8`, branch `levers`. **Build/run:** CUDA 12.4.1, `sm_86`, image `llama.cpp:lever2b-cuda124`; **`KV_TYPE=f16` is mandatory** (quantized KV can't reach the sparse MMA kernel at batch 1 on Ampere).

## Results (single-stream decode, t/s, 5×RTX 3090)

37.2tok/s to 50.8tok/s at 42k ctx (+37%)
22.5tok/s to 48.0tok/s at 111k (+113%)
11tok/s to 41.8tok/s at 250k (+280%)

(shallow essentially unchanged: 54.4 → 56.5. Prefill improves as a side effect: 609 → 716 t/s @111k.)

## Changes (7 patches, `llama-levers/000*.patch`)

```
 lever1     src/models/qwen4exp.cpp                 |  9 +++++----   (+ incidental Dockerfile pip fix)
 lever3     src/llama-memory-hybrid-idx.{cpp,h}     |  99 ++++++      block-granular top-k
            src/models/qwen4exp.cpp                 |  72 ++++
 sparse256  ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-mma-f16.cuh    |  3 +           whitelist DKQ=DV=256 MMA
 lever2     src/llama-memory-hybrid-idx.{cpp,h}     | 590 ++++++     persistent pooled block-key cache
            src/llama-kv-cache.{cpp,h}, qwen4exp.cpp
 lever2b    src/llama-memory-hybrid-idx.{cpp,h}     |  59 ++++       device-resident block-member cells
            src/llama-kv-cache.{cpp,h}, qwen4exp.cpp
```

**lever1 — enable the sparse-FA path (the big one).** The enablement PR #27742 shipped top-k as a dense mask with a `// TODO: enable sparse attention`. Un-TODO it: pass `top_k->ne[0]` as `n_kv_max` so flash-attn treats the finite mask entries as a sparse K/V set — O(top_k) instead of O(n_kv). Drops attention from ~11 ms to **0.22 ms/token @250k**.

```c
-    // TODO: enable sparse attention when we are ready
-    ggml_tensor * cur = build_attn_mha(q, k, v, nullptr, kq_mask_top_k, nullptr, nullptr, 0, kq_scale, il);
+    // LEVER1: passing top_k->ne[0] as n_kv_max -> sparse K/V set (deepseek4/GLM-DSA pattern, #27970)
+    ggml_tensor * cur = build_attn_mha(q, k, v, nullptr, kq_mask_top_k, nullptr, nullptr, top_k->ne[0], kq_scale, il);
```

**sparse256 — instantiate the kernel for this head shape.** `may_use_sparse` only whitelisted the MLA shapes; qwen4exp is `DKQ=DV=256, ncols2=8` and that MMA template instance already exists. One clause:

```c
-    return (DKQ == 512 && DV == 512 && ncols1 == 1 && ncols2 == 8) ||
+    return (DKQ == 256 && DV == 256 && ncols1 == 1 && ncols2 == 8) ||
+           (DKQ == 512 && DV == 512 && ncols1 == 1 && ncols2 == 8) ||
            (DKQ == 576 && DV == 512 && ncols1 == 1 && ncols2 == 16);
```

**lever3 — block-granular top-k.** Scores are block-constant and the budget is whole blocks, so select blocks first and expand only the ~513 selected blocks to cell indices (via `blk_cells`), instead of expanding block scores to all `n_kv` cells and sorting those. Removes the O(n_kv) expansion `get_rows` + one O(n_kv) mask add and shrinks the sort by `compress_ratio`. Fully-future blocks get −inf bias; the incomplete tail block's cells ride a small per-token side input.

**lever2 — persistent pooled block-key cache.** The indexer re-gathered, mean-pooled, RMS-normed and re-RoPEd **all** cached blocks every token though only the newest changed. Add a third per-QSA-layer buffer of pooled+normed+roped block keys; each ubatch recomputes only blocks it dirtied (host-side structural compare of member cells — also catches defrag/rollback/seq-ops with no invalidation hooks) and `ggml_set_rows` them

items.body:
## Summary

GPU-resident LRU cache for MoE expert weights that live in host memory (via `-ot ...exps=CPU`, `-ncmoe`, etc.). Decode on a host-offloaded MoE layer is bound by host RAM bandwidth: every token streams the routed experts' weights from system RAM. This PR serves the *recently used* experts from VRAM instead.

Opt-in via `--moe-expert-cache N` (slots per host-resident expert layer; `--moe-expert-cache-inserts` caps uploads per layer per decode step). Fully inert when disabled.

## Motivation / measurements

Measured on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL (512 experts, 10 routed/token, 28 expert layers pinned to host by `-ot`), 2x RTX 3090 + dual-Xeon host (single populated RAM channel per socket):

- Routing was instrumented over a 54k-record mixed workload (code / math / prose / multilingual):
  - **No exploitable static skew**: a top-32 "hot expert" list learned on half the workload covers only ~10% of the other half (uniform = 6.2%). Static pinning of experts is a dead end.
  - **Strong temporal locality**: a per-layer LRU-64 would hit ~67%, LRU-128 ~81%. This is what the cache exploits.
- End-to-end decode: **18.4 -> 24.2 tok/s** (+31%) with 48 slots/layer (~4.1 GiB VRAM) at 2 uploads/layer/step.
- Overhead when enabled but cold is ~zero (measured with uploads disabled).

## Mechanism (no new CUDA kernels)

- Per cached layer: companion tensors `[ne0, ne1, K+1]` for up/gate/down in the device buffer of that layer's router. Slot `K` is permanently zero (the "dummy" slot).
- An I32 `expert id -> slot` table per layer, two copies:
  - device copy: `ggml_get_rows` remaps `selected_experts` into slot ids for a **second `mul_mat_id` chain** over the cache tensors. Uncached ids map to the zero slot and contribute exactly 0.
  - host copy: passed as `src[3]` to the **CPU** `mul_mat_id`, which skips cached ids and zeroes their dst rows.
- The two down-projection outputs are summed - the split is exact by construction (each expert is computed on exactly one side).
- Decode-only (`n_tokens == 1`); batches/prefill build the stock graph, so batch offload is untouched.
- Updates are throttled and **asynchronous**: evictions are published at a decode-boundary sync point, slices are copied by a worker thread via `ggml_backend_tensor_set`, and the new mapping is only published at a later sync point after the copy completed - a running graph can never read a torn slot. (Synchronous uploads were measured to eat the entire win.)

## Known discussion points (why this is a draft)

- The cache is a per-process singleton keyed by the `up_exps` tensor pointer, because `build_moe_ffn` has no model access. Happy to rework the ownership (e.g. hang it off `llama_model`) per your preference.
- The CPU `mul_mat_id` observation callback (`ggml_set_moe_obs_callback`) is a ggml -> llama upcall; suggestions for a cleaner layering welcome.
- Only the separate gate/up + `LLM_FFN_SILU` path is wired; other MoE variants fall back to the stock graph.
- Multi-token decode (speculative/MTP) currently bypasses the cache (`n_tokens == 1` guard); extending the remap to small batches is straightforward if the approach is acceptable.
- The routing-locality result should transfer to other MoE models (uniform aggregate usage but high temporal locality is what load-balancing losses + real text produce), but only Qwen3.8-Flash-Next has been measured.

## Testing

- A/B benchmarks above; outputs coherent over thousands of tokens at 48-81% measured hit rates.
- `test-arg-parser` argument section passes (the URL/404 section fails in my sandbox for network reasons, unrelated).
- Will add a runtime smoke of the final CLI plumbing before marking ready for review.

### Name and Version

`version: 0.4.1-dev (build 1, commit 60b06ab)` (tag b11050), built with AppleClang 21.0.0 for Darwin arm64, `-DGGML_METAL=ON -DGGML_METAL_EMBED_LIBRARY=ON`.

First bad commit: **a2878d30 `metal : single-source fusion table + fusion debug rework` (#28164)** — b10908 is good, b10909 is bad.

### Operating systems

Mac (macOS 26.5.1)

### GGML backends

Metal

### Hardware

Apple M2 Ultra, 128 GB unified memory

### Models

`ggml-org/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF` → `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` (MoE, 26B / A4B). Also checked (no regression, see below): `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` UD-Q3_K_XL and `google/gemma-4-e4b-it-qat-q4_0-gguf`.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Token generation on gemma-4-26B-A4B dropped by ~6-7% at #28164 and is still down on master. Prompt processing is unaffected by that commit (the pp gain in the table below comes from later commits).

```
llama-bench -m gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf -p 512 -n 128 -r 3
```

| build | tg128 t/s | pp512 t/s |
|---|--:|--:|
| b10855 | 84.68 ± 0.36 | 1466.75 |
| b10885 | 85.07 ± 0.46 | 1468 |
| b10899 | 84.77 ± 0.28 | 1462 |
| **b10908** (last good) | **85.17 ± 0.36** | 1467 |
| **b10909** (first bad, = a2878d30) | **79.35 ± 0.24** | 1474 |
| b10917 | 79.49 ± 0.23 | 1555 |
| v0.4.1 | 79.52 ± 0.15 | 1550 |
| b11050 | 79.11 ± 0.29 | 1550 |

**What is *not* the cause.** With `GGML_METAL_FUSION_DEBUG=2`, the per-graph fusion counts are identical before and after the commit (633× RMS_NORM+MUL, 180× RMS_NORM+MUL+ADD, 90× ADD x 7), so no pattern stopped matching. An extra early-out in `ggml_metal_fusion_max()` (skip nodes whose op starts no pattern) had no measurable effect, so it is not the cost of scanning the table either.

**What it is.** The gap is entirely in the concurrency pass:

| | b10908 | b10909 |
|---|--:|--:|
| default | 84.99 | 79.64 |
| `GGML_METAL_FUSION_DISABLE=1` | 72.40 | 69.91 |
| `GGML_METAL_GRAPH_OPTIMIZE_DISABLE=1` | 75.45 | 74.91 |
| `GGML_METAL_CONCURRENCY_DISABLE=1` | **71.24** | **71.16** |
| nodes encoded as `(concurrent)` per decode graph (`GGML_METAL_GRAPH_DEBUG=1`) | **720** | **662** |

`ggml_metal_fusion_max()` chains several patterns back-to-back into a single pack (the `while (i_f < n_idxs && total < GGML_METAL_FUSION_MAX)` loop). The old packing in `ggml-metal-common.cpp` only ever packed one `ggml_can_fuse` chain. Dumping the pack spans on this model shows the difference:

| pack (per layer) | before #28164 | after #28164 |
|---|---|---|
| MoE output add chain | `ADD x7` alone | `ADD x7` **+ `RMS_NORM MUL` of the next block** (f=9) |
| the two branch norms of the layer | `RMS_NORM MUL` (ffn_mlp) and `RMS_NORM MUL ...` (ffn_moe) as **separate packs** | **`RMS_NORM MUL RMS_NORM MUL` in one pack** (f=4) |

gemma4-26B-A4B runs a dense MLP branch and a MoE branch per layer; gluing the input norms of both branches into one pack removes the reorder freedom the concurrency pass had, hence 720 → 662 concurrent nodes and the tg loss. The encoders still fuse exactly the same kernels (a pack of 9 is encoded as ADD x7 + RMS_NORM+MUL), so only the packing granularity changed.

### Fix (tested)

Pack exactly one pattern per call (= one fused kernel), instead of chaining:

```diff
--- a/ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-fusion.cpp
+++ b/ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-fusion.cpp
@@ int ggml_metal_fusion_max(const ggml_cgraph * gf, int idx) {
         return 1;
     }
 
-    int total = 0;
-    int i_f = 0;
-
-    while (i_f < n_idxs && total < GGML_METAL_FUSION_MAX) {
-        int len = 1;
-        const ggml_metal_fusion * fusion = ggml_metal_fusion_next(gf, idxs, n_idxs, i_f, GGML_METAL_FUSION_STRUCTURAL, &len);
-        if (!fusion || total + len > GGML_METAL_FUSION_MAX) {
-            break;
-        }
-
-        total += len;
-        i_f += len;
-    }
-
-    if (i_f == 0) {
+    // pack exactly one pattern (= one fused kernel). chaining patterns back-to-back into a single
+    // pack glues independent sub-graphs together (e.g. the two branch norms of gemma4's dense MLP
+    // and MoE) and reduces the reorder freedom of the concurrency pass.
+    int len = 1;
+    const ggml_metal_fusion * fusion = ggml_metal_fusion_next(gf, idxs, n_idxs, 0, GGML_METAL_FUSION_STRUCTURAL, &len);
+    if (!fusion) {
         return 1;
     }
 
     // map the matched non-empty nodes back to the raw index span (views are included)
-    return std::min(GGML_METAL_FUSION_MAX, idxs[i_f - 1] - idx + 1);
+    return std::min(GGML_METAL_FUSION_MAX, idxs[len - 1] - idx + 1);
 }
```

Results on b11050 with this patch (same machine, same commands):

| | b10908 | b11050 | b11050 + patch |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| gemma-4-26B-A4B tg128 | 85.63 | 79.04 | **85.02** |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B pp512 | 1466 | 1550 | **1542** (later gains kept) |
| concurrent nodes / decode graph | 720 | 662 | **720** |
| fusion counts | 633/180/90 | same | **same** |
| greedy output, 2 prompts × 300 tokens (`llama-server`, temp 0) | — | sha256 A | **identical to b11050** |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q3_K_XL tg128 / pp512 | — | 36.46 / 654 | 36.77 / 656 (fusion counts incl. 108× GATED_DELTA_NET+CPY identical) |
| gemma-4-E4B q4_0 tg128 / pp512 | — | 94.61 / 1680 | 94.50 / 1688 |
| `test-fusion --check tests/fusion/MTL.csv` (127 dummy models) | — | 150 ok / 28 FAIL | 150 ok / **the same 28** FAIL |

The 28 `test-fusion` failures are pre-existing on b11050 (the committed `MTL.csv` seems stale relative to master; the patch does not change any counter). Note also that `test-llama-archs` currently generates no `gemma4` dummy and `MTL.csv` has no gemma4 rows, so this regression is invisible to that test by construction.

Happy to open a PR with the patch if that is preferred.

b10908:  633 fuse: RMS_NORM + MUL / 180 fuse: RMS_NORM + MUL + ADD / 90 fuse: ADD x 7

items.body:
## Overview

One of llama.cpp's strength is the availability of a variety of quantizations which reduce the memory usage and allow running quantized big models on modest hardware.

Running a qwen3.8-flash-next, I was surprised to see high memory usage of 2 GB of compute buffers on each card, which is a lot. This PR cuts compute buffer usage by more than a third in two steps, one of which is very invasive. Further reductions are possible, reducing compute buffer sizes to ~800MB per card on my setup, halving the current utilization.
The two steps are:
- Providing fusions to elide the memory requirements, fusing trivial operations with follow-up kernels
- (Invasive): Providing a callback to enable removal of "deleted" nodes.

| Device | Master | Allocator branch | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SYCL0 | 1893.85 MiB | 1173.85 MiB | 720.00 MiB (38.02%) |
| SYCL1 | 1901.10 MiB | 1181.10 MiB | 720.00 MiB (37.87%) |
| SYCL2 | 1901.10 MiB | 1181.10 MiB | 720.00 MiB (37.87%) |
| Total | 5696.05 MiB | 3536.05 MiB | 2160.00 MiB (37.92%) |
| SYCL host | 415.87 MiB | 415.87 MiB | 0 MiB |


<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
One of the key offenders of high memory usage are OP_CAST nodes, which currently expand the full ubatch into a buffer.

This branch extends the SYCL with support for eliding fused intermediate tensors:

- F16 cast plus F32 add fusion
- QSA score generation, ReLU, and head reduction fusion
- QSA gather fusion
- QSA gather, mask add, and radix top-k fusion

## Additional information


The removal of the buffer has only limited performance impact, because the sizes of the copied structures at 720MB are not prohibitive for GPUs which handle multiple hundred GB/s of throughput, and these operations are saturating this bandwidth.

| Metric | Master median | Allocator fusion median | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| pp16384 | 298.327 tok/s | 305.876 tok/s | +2.53% |
| tg16384 | 15.391 tok/s | 15.555 tok/s | +1.07% |
| pp65535 | 246.356 tok/s | 255.423 tok/s | +3.68% |
| tg65535| 8.830 tok/s | 8.885 tok/s | +0.62% |

However, it saves 720MB of buffers to create more headroom.

I'm not sure how to go about this; the change is very invasive because it needs to interact with the memory allocator to really reduce the number of compute buffers.  This is therefore more a basis for discussion / inspiration, as there are some fundamental dirty parts:
- The graph allocation / de-allocation is aimed to be as non-intrusive as possible, but still creates a bit of a mess
- The Fusions are HUGE, consuming multiple nodes, which may lead to increased maintenance efforts


Still, I believe being able to ditch compute buffers and reduce the insane dead copying from reshapes and casts by integrating them into fusions would help the project overall, and allow users to use the gained memory for MTP or more parallel processing. What are your feelings on this ( @arthw )?
Due to the massive change, I'm not sure this will ever be pulled, so I'm keeping it as a draft.

items.body:
# Vulkan: ~78% decode throughput cliff at 131072 context window — default ~1 GiB suballocation fragmentation; fixed via GGML_VK_SUBALLOCATION_BLOCK_SIZE=4 GiB

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (24 GB, RDNA3, gfx1100) |
| OS / Driver | Windows 11, AMD proprietary driver |
| llama.cpp | 0.2.0-dev (build **10603**, commit c060ca974), Vulkan backend (ggml-vulkan.dll) |
| Model | Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid linear-attention, 64 layers), `Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf` (16.35 GiB) |
| Context | 131072 · KV cache `q8_0`/`q8_0` · `-fa on` · 4 slots unified pool |

## Summary

Decode throughput collapses from **~40 tok/s to ~8.9 tok/s** when the context window is raised from 98304 to 131072. The cliff is caused by the Vulkan backend's default **~1 GiB suballocation block size** fragmenting the large KV/compute pool into **30+ separate VkBuffers**. Setting `GGML_VK_SUBALLOCATION_BLOCK_SIZE=4294967296` restores full throughput at 131072.

## Reproduction

```powershell
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --mmproj mmproj-F16.gguf `
  --ctx-size 131072 -fa on --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --jinja `
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
```

Send a single-stream 1200-token completion (prompt ≈ 31 tokens), measure wall time.

## Results (same request, same binary, single GPU)

| ctx | KV dtype | suballoc block size | wall time | throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 65536 | f16 | default (1 GiB) | ~30 s | **40.4 tok/s** |
| 98304 | q8_0 | default | ~29 s | **40.8 tok/s** |
| **131072** | q8_0 | default | **~145 s** | **8.9 tok/s** ← cliff |
| **131072** | q8_0 | **4 GiB** | **~30 s** | **40.3 tok/s** ← restored |

Note: `llama-bench -p 512 -n 128` (small actual KV usage) stays at 40.4 tok/s even with q8 KV, so the cliff is tied to **pool allocation size**, not KV dtype.

## Diagnosis (`GGML_VK_MEMORY_LOGGER=1`)

At 131072, total device allocation is **21.55 GiB — fully in VRAM, no sysmem fallback** (total host = 152 MiB). The largest individual allocations are ≈ **1018 MiB each**, i.e. the pool is split into 30+ sub-blocks. At 98304 the same split stays below a critical block count and performance is unaffected.

No `OOM` / fallback warnings in logs. Memory location is not the issue — fragmentation of the pool into many independent `VkBuffer` objects is.

## Root-cause hypothesis

Decode at batch=1 touches the full KV/compute pool every step. With 30+ separate ~1 GiB sub-buffers, each step incurs per-buffer descriptor binding / submission overhead (and likely suboptimal memory access locality across disjoint buffers), multiplying the per-token cost by ~4.5×. Raising the suballocation block to 4 GiB keeps the pool in contiguous large buffers and eliminates the overhead.

## Workaround

```
GGML_VK_SUBALLOCATION_BLOCK_SIZE=4294967296
```

(before launching llama-server / llama-bench)

## Suggestions for maintainers

1. Consider raising the default suballocation block size, or sizing it relative to the KV pool (e.g. grow block size when the requested buffer exceeds N GiB).
2. Alternatively, allocate the KV cache as one contiguous buffer when it fits in VRAM, instead of splitting through the suballocator.
3. This appears to be a sibling of other "cliff at specific sizes" issues in the same backend: #25356 (fixed 8-token MMV dispatch thresholds) and #16759 (compute buffer jumps at specific context breakpoints).

---

**AI disclosure:** This report was researched and drafted with the assistance of an AI assistant (opencode). All measurements were performed locally on the machine described above; the evidence chain (memory logger output, A/B benchmark table) is reproducible with the commands provided.

## Overview

Re-enables `-sm tensor` for qwen4exp. #27941 disabled it because `test-llama-archs -a qwen4exp` asserted on the Meta device once the fixture carried a PLE layer, and removed the test's earlier Meta skip for the arch.

The abort is a scheduler placement, not QSA. `test-llama-archs` builds the model with the embeddings host-resident, so the PLE embedding gather (`ggml_get_rows` on `per_layer_token_embd`) is a CPU node. In the qwen4exp graph `hc_init` (the `ggml_repeat_4d` that fans the embedding out to the hc streams) is first materialised inside layer 0's PLE path, after that gather. `ggml_backend_sched_split_graph` pass 2 expands a device assignment upwards only until it meets a CPU-assigned node, so the REPEAT is never reached from the first Meta node and "expand rest" leaves it on the CPU. The later `ggml_reshape_3d(hc_init)` inside the PLE query norm is then a view of a host-resident node inside the meta split, which `ggml_backend_meta_graph_compute` only tolerates for `view_src->op == GGML_OP_NONE`: `GGML_ASSERT(ggml_backend_buffer_is_meta(tensor->buffer))` at ggml-backend-meta.cpp:476. deepseek4 builds the same hc init but its REPEAT is followed directly by a weight matmul, so the expansion reaches it.

Fix: `ggml_build_forward_expand(gf, res_hc)` right after `hc_init` is built. The REPEAT then directly precedes the first device node and pass 2 assigns it there; the embedding reshape stays in the CPU split and is copied in as a split input, the same shape deepseek4's graph has.

`test-llama-archs` on this branch (master e6ab7c1a4 + the change; seed 4097205655; RelWithDebInfo, RADV gfx1151, Mesa 25.2.8):

| arch | Vulkan | Meta (-sm tensor) |
|---|---|---|
| qwen4exp | OK (1.17e-07) | OK (1.17e-07), was GGML_ASSERT |
| deepseek4 | OK (8.44e-07) | OK (8.44e-07) |
| qwen35 | OK (8.33e-08) | OK (8.33e-08) |

Real model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, `-sm tensor` over two RPC devices (#26610 tree with this change, one Vulkan `ggml-rpc-server` per Strix Halo box, ctx 65536) vs a single device, greedy: byte-identical on a short prompt and on a 1.8k-token prompt (1752 generated tokens), and identical to master's single-device output.

## Overview

`handle_models_delete` could deadlock when removing a finished download: the handler waited on the downloader thread while holding a lock the downloader also takes. The finished-download path now signals the downloader to exit and joins outside the lock, so partial `.tmp` files are cleaned up without blocking the status feed.

Running llama.cpp through LM Studio runtime packs, b10760 through b11026 (runtime 2.31.2 - 2.41.0). All of them crash for me. I have Windows Error Reporting records pinning each crash to the exact engine binary via PE timestamp, so this is not a stale-process artifact.

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

7x Volta sm_70 (1x Quadro GV100 + 6x Tesla PG503-216, 32 GB HBM2 each), `--split-mode layer --tensor-split 0 --main-gpu 0`, CUDA graphs disabled via `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1`.

### Models

Reproduces across architectures (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF and DeepSeek-V4-Flash variants, various quantizations), so I don't think it's model-specific. UBatches 256 and 384 both crash at the same rate on the Qwen model.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

During normal long agent sessions (OpenAI-compatible server, one client, very long contexts with heavy prefix reuse) llama-server dies roughly daily — recently ~6 times a day — with a fail-fast (`0xc0000409` in ucrtbase.dll). The last engine line before death is always:

```
CUDA error: invalid argument
current device: 0, in function ggml_cuda_kernel_launch at ggml/src/ggml-cuda/common.cuh:<line varies by build: 1676/1710/1716>
```

The trigger pattern is consistent across three weeks of logs (~100 crashes): a large prefill (tens of thousands of tokens, up to ~112K context) with high partial prefix-cache reuse (`f_keep` 0.98-0.99), dying either right at the prefill→decode boundary (`progress = 1.00`) or mid-prefill around a batch boundary. It is probabilistic: replaying the same session mostly works, and a synthetic append-only stress run (growing prefix, ~3K new tokens per round) passed 40/40 rounds once and crashed in round 2 another time. Note it does NOT strictly require >100K context — I also have samples at 56K, 18K, and even a fresh slot crashing on its first 2-message prefill; deep context just raises the probability.

What I've ruled out by testing, not guessing:
- Engine version. Clean reinstall of runtime 2.33 still crashes (~1/day); 2.34 through 2.41 crash more often (6-10/day). #28177 and #28198 (merged Sep 3/4) look like amplifiers on the multi-GPU launch path, not the root cause.
- KV quantization (`q8_0` K/V): survived 9.5h / ~200K new prefill tokens once, then reproduced the exact same signature. Reduces frequency at best.
- `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1`: verified present in the process PEB environment. Helps on ≤2.33 builds; newer builds have launch paths that bypass it and crash anyway.
- `--no-kv-unified`, split strategy (spread vs priority-order fill): no effect.

Since both `cudaLaunchKernelEx` and the classic launch path reject the same configuration, I suspect a grid/block dimension goes out of range for some batch shape on sm_70 — similar in spirit to #27901 (gridDim.y overflow), but here it seems to need multi-GPU layer split plus partial slot reuse to show up. Volta is presumably not covered by any CI runner, which might be why this survives.

I could not reduce this to a clean `llama-completion` repro yet because the failure needs the prefix-cache reuse pattern of a long agent session; I'm happy to run bisects or test patches against my workload — I have crash logs with exact timestamps, token counts and f_keep values for every occurrence. Related but distinct signatures: #28661 (fattn-mma-f16.cuh:1945, non-standard head dim), #27871/#27901 (GB10 gridDim.y).

**First bad commit:** unknown — every runtime from b10760 to b11026 crashes; the frequency jump around Sep 3/4 suggests #28177 / #28198 amplified an older bug rather than introducing it.

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

It turns out Intel doesn't particularly like loading F32s one at a time and we already have the _2aliagned load logic in mul_mat_vec, so here we use it.

While we do already check all the requirements to load elements 4 at a time across [B]F16 and F32, it turns out [B]F16 loading 4 at a time is sometimes slower on very specific shapes on Intel BMG. Loading 4 at a time is a bit faster on F32, but its not material and I assume might be slower on other platforms.

Note that we also need to validate `a_offset` is 2-aligned in `mul_mat_vec.comp`, which was missing in the original 2-way-load patch.

Fixes #25620

## Overview

mmvq.cu sets nwarps twice; device-side from arch macros + host-side from runtime cc. It is assumed these agree but breaks on a generic code object - gfx11-generic on RDNA3.5 sets __GFX11__ but not __gfx115x__, so the device gets RDNA3_0 (nwarps=8) & the host gets RDNA3_5 (nwarps=1). The reduction then reads unwritten shared memory, outputs NaN at ncols_dst=1. 

Instead, this PR reads nwarps back from the compiled kernel via cudaFuncGetAttributes in place of recomputing host-side.

Tested: gfx11-generic went 10 FAIL to 0 FAIL on n=1 (all NaN/-inf); gfx1151-native stayed 48/48. test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT, type_a=q4_0, llama.cpp 7798007, ROCm 7.2.4, Strix Halo gfx1151. This bug only reproduces on AMD, and the fix has only been tested on AMD.

Original patch is by @talhaHavadar - who requested this PR in #25620

## Overview Currently with tensor/matrix cores we only use fp16 instructions, so dequant to shared memory -> fp16 GEMM. But many devices have higher throughput int8 tensor/matrix cores, so similar to the existing DP4A-based scalar MMQ path it would be good to have a coopmat int8 MMQ path. I have tried to make this work in the past, but failed due to architectural constraints in the coopmat extension. But based on @pwilkin's ideas in #27493, I finally managed to get it to work with good performance on RDNA3 and 4. This new MMQ cm1 shader supports q4_0, q4_1, q5_0, q5_1, q8_0, q3_k, q4_k, q5_k, q6_k, mxfp4, nvfp4 and iq4_nl on RDNA3 and RDNA4. Strix Halo prompt processing performance is significantly improved, RDNA4 is more neutral, but MoE prompt processing is also up significantly. The shader is limited to those two architectures since it hardcodes their specific coopmat access patterns. More architectures can be added if needed. q4_1, q5_1, q4_k, q5_k and nvfp4 on RDNA4 are disabled for MUL_MAT since they run slower than existing fp16 matmul. items.body:
## Overview

Add a narrowly gated shared-memory transpose path for F32 `CONCAT` on AMD
RDNA3.5. This targets a transposed input shape observed during Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
prefill input processing, for example:

```text
src0: [3,    8192]   contiguous
src1: [2048, 8192]   transposed F32 view
dst:  [2051, 8192]   concat(src0, src1), dim 0
```

The kernel uses 256 threads (`32 x 8`) and a padded shared-memory tile
`float tile[32][33]` to coalesce the transposed copy. The contiguous `src0`
portion is copied only by blocks with `blockIdx.y == 0`.

The fast path requires RDNA3.5, `dim == 0`, F32 inputs/output, input width
512/1024/2048, contiguous `src0` and `dst`, strict transpose strides for `src1`,
and a valid grid-z size. **It now also requires at least 64 output channels and
a channel count divisible by 32.** Small-channel and partial-channel-tile cases
use the existing implementation. This supersedes the small-channel regression
limitation described in the previous version of this PR.

Only `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/concat.cu` and `tests/test-backend-ops.cpp` change
(144 insertions, 1 deletion). Related to #21284.

## Additional information

### Revision and validation, 2026-09-23

- Tested base: `b1ff4ca23630ac7c5a275405353ddb5c486332c9`.
- Tested and submitted head: `e478c7ef9f81307f20d22a90256a802986f8bed6`.
- Windows 11, Radeon 8060S / gfx1151, ROCm 7.1; Release, HIP, MMQ MFMA,
  HIP Graphs, No VMM, UMA off, OpenMP off.
- Baseline and candidate `test-backend-ops` builds succeeded.
- Candidate CONCAT correctness: **272/272 twice**. The baseline with identical
  test registration also passed **272/272**. Transposed cases require
  bit-identical output via `std::memcmp`.

Coverage includes state widths 1/3/4; input widths 512/1024/2048; channel counts
31/32/33/64/65/96/97/128/129; `ne2 = 2`; the 8192-channel workload; and fallback
cases for non-whitelisted widths, contiguous F32 and transposed F16.

### Operator performance

A is the tested base plus the same test registration; B adds the production
kernel. After one warmup per version, the order was `A/B/B/A` repeated five
times: ten measured samples per version and shape. The shape is
`ne_a=[3,8192,1,1]`, `dim=0`, `v=16`.

| Input width | A median, microseconds | B median, microseconds | Latency reduction | B CV |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 185.985 | 59.095 | 68.23% | 0.43% |
| 1024 | 4237.470 | 498.305 | 88.24% | 1.43% |
| 2048 | 11100.610 | 1098.770 | 90.10% | 0.41% |

CV is the standard deviation divided by the mean. Baseline CV was 5.32% and
5.44% for widths 1024 and 2048 respectively; the table reports medians rather
than a best run. These are CONCAT operator measurements, **not end-to-end
model speedups**.

Commands after building each version, with ROCm DLLs on `PATH`:

```powershell
.\build-amd\bin\test-backend-ops.exe test -b ROCm0 -o CONCAT
.\build-amd\bin\test-backend-ops.exe perf -b ROCm0 -o CONCAT -p 'type=f32,ne_a=\[3,8192,1,1\].*v=16'
```

The baseline must include the same test-only changes so that both commands
exercise identical shapes.

### Scope and remaining validation

Earlier model-level measurements are historical evidence, not a rerun of this
exact head. Full-model reruns on September 14 were interrupted twice by
unexpected host reboots; the cause remains undetermined. No new end-to-end
performance claim is made for this revision. The current evidence is the
Windows build, CONCAT correctness and operator A/B above; other GPU
architectures have not been validated here.

The PR is already ready for review (`draft=false`), but the bot-added `draft`
label remains. The author account cannot remove it (GitHub returns HTTP 403).
Could a maintainer remove the stale label and check whether the relevant CI
needs approval? At the time of this update, only `labeler` had run successfully
for the new head.

## Requirements

- [x] I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

  analysis, implementation, test/benchmark automation and this PR update. The
  submitted commit includes `Assisted-by: Codex`.

## Overview

f16 KV layout does not engage all memory channels. This PR engages all channels by copying each layers f16 KV once into a scratch so that the KV cache reads are sequential. Reuse of scratch introduced in PR #25494 

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->
Gating set to AMD where effect was measured, RTX 3070 did not benefit, Intel and any other vendor have not been tested.

Consecutive KV rows of one head are read `n_kv_heads × head_dim × 2` bytes apart. Typical model KV geometry spacing is an even multiple of the 256B channel-interleave block that Mesa documents, causing only a subset of memory channels to engage. 
| KV geometry (heads × head_dim) | example models | row spacing | ÷ 256 B | channels engaged (of 16) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 × 128 | small GQA-heavy models | 512 B | 2 | 8 |
| 4 × 128 | Qwen3-Coder-30B *(benchmarked)* | 1024 B | 4 | 4 |
| 2 × 256 | Qwen3.6-35B class *(benchmarked)* | 1024 B | 4 | 4 |
| 4 × 256 | Qwen3.8-27B *(benchmarked)* | 2048 B | 8 | 2 |
| 8 × 128 | Llama-3.1-8B class | 2048 B | 8 | 2 |
| 32 × 128 | MHA-era 7B models | 8192 B | 32 | 1 |


The tradeoff is scratch size, 1 layer of KV
| KV geometry | example models | KV layers | scratch/token | @32k | @128k | % of f16 KV cache |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 × 128 | small GQA-heavy (typ. 32L) | 32 | 1 KiB | 32 MiB | 128 MiB | ~3.1% |
| 4 × 128 | Qwen3-Coder-30B *(measured)* | 48 | 2 KiB | 64 MiB | 256 MiB | 2.1% |
| 2 × 256 | Qwen3.6-35B (hybrid, 10/40 attn) | 10 | 2 KiB | 64 MiB | 256 MiB | 10% |
| 4 × 256 | Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid, 16/65 attn) | 16 | 4 KiB | 128 MiB | 512 MiB | 6.25% |
| 8 × 128 | Llama-3.1-8B class | 32 | 4 KiB | 128 MiB | 512 MiB | 3.1% |
| 32 × 128 | MHA-era 7B models | 32 | 16 KiB | 512 MiB | 2 GiB | 3.1% |


TG is measured unaffected, stridding tax increases at depth. Worst case model (hybrid, 10/40 attention layers) regress ~1% in prefill @ 32k, back within run variance @ 64k. 
All runs: `llama-bench -m <model> -fa 1 -p 512 -n 0 -d 0,16384,32768,65536 -r 1` on Radeon 8060S (RADV STRIX_HALO), f16 KV. Stock = master 3af988fab.

**Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B UD-Q6_K_XL - stock:**

items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Add a Strix Halo (gfx1151 / RDNA3.5) specific tuning for the Vulkan KHR_cooperative_matrix (coopmat) matrix-multiply tiles, to make prompt processing (prefill) faster on models like Qwen3.8-27B.

Today the AMD coopmat path uses one generic large tile for all AMD cards; Strix Halo is an integrated GPU with its own cache sizes and wavefront behavior, so it should get its own tile sizes, picked by measuring.

## Measurements / observations

Setup: Radeon 8050S (32 CU), RADV / Mesa 26.1.8, `uma:1`, Qwen3.8-27B
`UD-Q4_K_S`, `-p 128 -n 32 -b 128 -ub 128 -r 3 -fa on -ngl 99`:

- `pp128: 194.13 ± 1.45 t/s`, `tg32: 12.86 ± 0.10 t/s`
- Prefill is >90% GEMM (`MUL_MAT`), all on the coopmat/MMQ path:

| shape | iq4_xs | q4_K | q5_K |
|---|---|---|---|
| m=17408, k=5120 (FFN up/gate) | 69x 2087us (10.9 TFLOPS) | 17x 2084us (11.0 TFLOPS) | 14x 2045us (11.2 TFLOPS) |
| m=5120, k=17408 (FFN down) | 29x 2587us (8.8 TFLOPS) | 12x 2533us (9.0 TFLOPS) | 14x 2718us (8.4 TFLOPS) |

Path checks (same flags, prove which code runs):

- `GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT=1` → pp128 falls to 106.21 (-45%), tg32
  unchanged. So prefill runs on coopmat, decode does not.
- `GGML_VK_DISABLE_INTEGER_DOT_PRODUCT=1` → pp128 falls to 174.53
  (-10%), tg32 unchanged. So the integer-dot MMQ path is active in
  prefill with a modest share.

History: PR #18749 (generic AMD large tile `{256,128,128}`) gave
+35-75% prefill on 8060S. That tile reuses medium TM/TN/TK values and
was never specialized for gfx1151. The card reports only `16x16x16`
fp16/int8 coopmat shapes (verified with a Vulkan probe), so there is
room left in workgroup geometry, subgroup size, and LDS traffic.

## Related files and functions

All in `ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/` (line numbers at HEAD `002a12ad2`):

- `ggml-vulkan.cpp:4540-4545` — AMD+coopmat large-tile override
  (this is where a gfx1151 branch goes)
- `ggml-vulkan.cpp:4490-4498` — `tm/tn/tk` from probed `coopmat_m/n/k`
- `ggml-vulkan.cpp:4568-4627` — shared-memory guards that silently
  disable tiles that do not fit (must check when adding tiles)
- `ggml-vulkan.cpp:4166-4289` — `ggml_vk_matmul_shmem_support` /
  `ggml_vk_matmul_int_shmem_support` (LDS budget math)
- `ggml-vulkan.cpp:7320-7327` — AMD tile enables (`mul_mat_id_l`
  stays `false`, see #23106)
- `vulkan-shaders/mul_mm.comp:43-47,161-192,383-386` — `LOAD_VEC_A`,
  spec constants, hardcoded A-RowMajor / B-ColumnMajor coop loads
- `vulkan-shaders/mul_mmq.comp:103-104` — `LOAD_VEC_A/B` for int path
- `vulkan-shaders/mul_mmq_funcs.glsl` — int-dot dequant + dot
- Unmerged prototype branch: `0cc4m/vulkan-coopmat-int8`
  (`mul_mmq_cm1.comp`, int8 coopmat MMQ, tip `918f32dcf`)

## Proposed behavior

1. Detect gfx1151 narrowly (AMD + coopmat + not proprietary driver +
   `uma` + 64 KiB shared memory + `STRIX_HALO` device name) and give it
   its own `l/m_warptile_mmq*` values, found by measurement: first
   BM/BN/BK geometry (including non-square), then subgroup 32 vs 64,
   then `LOAD_VEC_A` / LDS bank padding per quant type.
2. Generic AMD path and all other vendors/drivers stay exactly as now.
3. Longer term: rebase and evaluate the int8-coopmat prototype branch,
   starting with NVFP4 (simple dequant, already in the upstream MMQ
   type lists) before attempting `iq4_xs`.

## Notes
- Assisted by a coding AI agent
- Current Commit: 002a12ad25503a93501b2e188c360029830a241a

### Motivation

Prefill at `n=128` is compute-bound (about 380 FLOP/byte vs a machine balance of about 325), while decode (`n=1`) is memory-bandwidth-bound near the ~200 GB/s wall. So tile tuning moves prefill/TTFT without being able to hurt decode much and the per-shape table above shows prefill GEMM at ~9-11 TFLOPS against a ~65 TFLOPS WMMA roof, i.e. mostly headroom. Prior art (#18749) already proved tiles alone can move Strix Halo prefill by tens of percent.

### Possible Implementation

- Step 1: sweep `l_mmq` BM/BN/BK (`{256,128,128}` vs `{256,64,128}`
  vs `{128,128,128}` vs `{256,128,64}`) and `m_mmq` at `n=128`;
  keep `s` tiles stable; verify each candidate survives the
  `matmul_shmem_support` guard via `GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER=1`.
- Step 2: clone the winner with `WARP 64 -> 32` (RDNA3 is natively
  wave32; current tiles use 64).
- Step 3: `LOAD_VEC_A` 4 -> 8 for `q4_K`/`q5_K`/`iq4_xs` int paths,
  `SHMEM_STRIDE_PAD` 8 vs 4/16 on the winning tile.
- Step 4: measure (do not assume) B-operand layout per dtype; expect
  ~0% on fp16.
- Step 5: rebase `0cc4m/vulkan-coopmat-int8`, `test-backend-ops` all
  covered quants, measure pp128/512/2048 + tg32; NVFP4 first, then
  consider `iq4_xs` (43.8% of prefill, covered nowhere today).
- Bench rule: matched `-b/-ub` flags, cool-downs, tg32 guard on every
  step, `test-backend-ops` on every tile change. Tiles must stay
  bit-identical (same accumulation order) or pass greedy exact-match
  (`--temp 0 --top-k 1 --seed 42`).

items.body:
### Name and Version

First bad build: **b10751**. Last good: **b10750**. Still present at **b11057** (today's head).

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10750, ...)   # last good
version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10751, ...)   # first bad
```

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

RTX 2070 SUPER (sm_75, 8 GB), CUDA 12.4 prebuilt Windows release binaries (`llama-<b>-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip`), i7 8-core, 32 GB RAM. Partial offload: `-ngl 31 --n-cpu-moe 21`.

### Models

- Target: `unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-GGUF` → `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf` (MoE, 30 blocks)
- Draft: the repo's own MTP sidecar, `MTP/mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q4_0.gguf`, via `--spec-type draft-mtp`

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

**#25952 (`cuda: fuse MoE weighted expert reduction`) makes speculative decoding non-exact on a CUDA MoE model, and turns MTP speculative decoding into a net slowdown.**

Speculative decoding is supposed to be a pure speed optimisation: with greedy sampling, the output must be identical to decoding without a draft. From b10751 onwards it is not.

I bisected across the 318 releases between a known-good and a known-bad build, using draft acceptance as the signal (it is sharply bimodal, so every step was unambiguous). **b10750 → b10751 is exactly one commit**, `3466812`, which is #25952 and touches only `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/*`.

| | b10750 (last good) | b10751+ (b10964 / b11056 / b11057) |
|---|---|---|
| draft acceptance | **0.823** (mean accepted len 2.65) | **0.481** (1.95) |
| tok/s **with** MTP draft | **46.35** | 35.36 – 36.73 |
| tok/s **without** draft | 38.10 | 37.02 – 38.33 |
| drafted output == greedy output | **yes**, byte-identical | **no** |

Two things to note:

1. **Without a draft the builds are equivalent** (38.10 vs 37.02–38.33), so this is not a general decode regression — it is confined to the speculative path.
2. **On the affected builds the draft is a net loss**: 35.36 tok/s with the draft vs 37.02 without on b10964; 36.73 vs 38.33 on b11057. Users are better off disabling MTP.

b10964 (the build `v0.4.1` designates), b11056 and b11057 all produce **byte-identical output to each other**, so the behaviour is stable and unchanged since it landed.

#### Suspected mechanism

#25952 does "weighting and ordered expert reduction in one CUDA kernel" instead of writing weighted expert outputs to global memory and reducing them separately. That changes the **order of floating-point accumulation** across experts. Small differences in the target model's logits are enough to flip the argmax on some tokens, so the draft's proposals stop matching the target and are rejected — which explains both the halved acceptance and the divergence from greedy output. It is consistent with the fusion itself being *numerically reasonable* but not bit-identical to the unfused path, which speculative decoding's exactness relies on.

Possibly related: #28113 (`MoE models produce garbage output on RDNA3.5 since #27621`) reported a correctness problem from the sibling MoE fusion PR.

#### Steps to reproduce

Run the same prompt twice on one build — once with the draft, once without — with greedy sampling, and compare the output text:

```bash
# A: with the MTP draft
llama-server -m gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --model-draft MTP/mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q4_0.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  -ngl 31 --n-cpu-moe 21 -c 32768 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on -b 512 -ub 512 --port 8080

# B: identical, minus the three draft flags

curl -s localhost:8080/completion -d \
  '{"prompt":"Write one vivid paragraph about the sea.","n_predict":128,"temperature":0,"top_k":1,"seed":1,"cache_prompt":false}' \
  | jq -r .content | sha256sum
```

- On **b10750**, A and B give the same sha256.
- On **b10751 and later**, they differ.

`draft acceptance` in the slot-timing line drops from 0.823 to 0.481 across the same boundary.

Method notes, in the interest of being honest about what was and was not tested:

- Each build was measured with 1 warm-up plus 3 runs; the order was reversed once to rule out thermal or ordering effects, and the numbers reproduced.
- I used the raw `/completion` endpoint with no chat template, so the generated text is not meaningful prose on any build. That does not affect the result: the comparison is always **within a single build**, between drafted and non-drafted decoding of the same prompt with the same settings.
- Greedy output also differs *between* builds, which changes to kernels and fusion can legitimately explain. I make no claim there.
- I have not tested other MoE architectures, other GPUs, or non-MTP draft types. `-np` was left at the server default.

### First Bad Commit

`3466812` — `cuda: fuse MoE weighted expert reduction` (#25952), first released in **b10751**.

Bisected over the 318 releases between b10437 and b10964, 8 builds probed:

```
b10723 GOOD 0.8229   b10736 GOOD 0.8229   b10740 GOOD 0.8229
b10749 GOOD 0.8229   b10750 GOOD 0.8229
b10751 BAD  0.4806   b10775 BAD  0.4806   b10837 BAD  0.4806
```

(b10741–b10748 do not start at all on this setup — `0xC0000409`, apparently the gemma4-assistant window broken by #28159 and fixed by #28183 in b10749. The bisect stepped past them; it does not affect the boundary above.)

### Relevant log output

```
# b10750 — last good
slot print_timing: id  3 | task 0 | draft acceptance = 0.82292 (   79 accepted /    96 generated), mean len =  2.65
  -> 46.35 tok/s

# b10751 and later (b10964, b11056, b11057 all identical)
slot print_timing: id  3 | task 0 | draft acceptance = 0.48062 (   62 accepted /   129 generated), mean len =  1.95
  -> 35.36 tok/s   (vs 37.02 tok/s with no draft at all on the same build)
```

## Overview

Fixes #26220 

After the removal of rocWMMA Flash Attention kernel path, the replacement had slower prompt processing at deep context on RDNA 4. The regression was caused by WMMA tensor cores not being used at all for head dim 256.

This PR widens `flash_attn_ext_f16` device guard to unblock MMA at head dim 256. Without it, the tile kernel is used instead which works, but slows down with more context.  The config table also needed a precision fix for DKQ=256. `nbatch_combine` was too small, causing multi-pass FP16 accumulation errors in test-backend-ops.

Additionally, for DKQ>128 on WMMA K/V is loaded directly from VRAM instead of going through LDS. Without it, MMA is actually slower than the tile kernel.

## Additional information

Below are benchmark numbers to confirm no regressions and the speedup. It's worth to mention that, while prompt processing is faster than current master(a7a6d0d2), it's still about 12-20% slower the old rocWMMA kernel depending on context size. There's definitely room for further improvement.

GPU: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, RDNA4), ROCm 7.2.4
Baseline: master a7a6d0d2, 3 runs per data point

test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT: 2920/2920 passed

items.title: ggml-cuda: enable MMA FlashAttention for head dim 256 on AMD RDNA

items.body:
gfx1151-class RDNA3.5 parts have only 20 CUs, so the RDNA3.0-inherited 256-thread / `I=128` Q4_K
tile leaves the device under-occupied: each workgroup carries a large LDS/register footprint and
too few workgroups are produced to keep all CUs busy.

This switches the three affected Q4_K entries in `mmq-config-rdna3-5.cuh` to a 128-thread / `I=64`
tile:

| J | fallback | before | after |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 64 | true | `256, 2, 128, 64` | `128, 2, 64, 64` |
| 64 | false | `256, 2, 128, 64` | `128, 2, 64, 64` |
| 128 | false | `256, 2, 128, 128` | `128, 1, 64, 128` |

The per-thread accumulator size is unchanged — `J*I/nthreads` is 32 for both the old `256/128` and
the new `128/64` form — but workgroups are half the size and twice as numerous, which balances
better across 20 CUs.

## Test setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Host | LENOVO 83V9 laptop, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 |
| CPU | AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 388, 8C/16T, 23.79 GB RAM |
| GPU | AMD Radeon 8060S, **gfx1151 (RDNA3.5)**, 20 CU, wave32, 16.92 GB shared VRAM, 64 KB LDS/workgroup, driver 32.0.31021.5001 |
| Stack | ROCm 7.2 (HIP 7.2.60201-38d754472, clang 21.0.0git), CMake 3.27.2, Ninja 1.11.0 |
| Base | `1bc7a5af0d14b1fb72f266abbd1237b394187115` |

```
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=<rocm>/bin/clang.exe -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=<rocm>/bin/clang++.exe \
  -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=<rocm>/bin/clang++.exe \
  -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGGML_HIP_NO_VMM=ON \
  -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_KERNELS=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
```

## Correctness

```
test-backend-ops test -b ROCm0 -o MUL_MAT    -p type_a=<q4_K|q5_K|q4_0|q5_0>
test-backend-ops test -b ROCm0 -o MUL_MAT_ID -p type_a=<q4_K|q5_K|q4_0|q5_0>
```

All pass: `MUL_MAT` 64/64, 29/29, 48/48, 14/14; `MUL_MAT_ID` 84/84, 3/3, 74/74, 3/3.

## Performance

```
llama-bench -m <model> -p 2048 -n 128 -b 2048 -ub 512 -ngl 99 -fa 1 -lm none -r 3 -o json
```

8 balanced AB/BA pairs per model against a pristine build of the same base commit. Statistic is the
paired log-ratio of `pp2048` with a two-sided 95% Student-t CI:

| model | pp2048 | 95% CI | wins | significant |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B-Q4_K_M | **+4.354%** | `[+1.697, +7.080]` | 7/8 | yes |
| Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M | +1.964% | `[-0.081, +4.050]` | 7/8 | no (marginal) |
| granite-4.1-8b-q4_k_m | +0.008% | `[-1.400, +1.437]` | 4/8 | no |
| Phi-4-mini-instruct.Q4_K_M | -0.056% | `[-2.239, +2.175]` | 5/8 | no |
| **pooled (32 pairs)** | **+1.552%** | `[+0.507, +2.608]` | 23/32 | yes |

Token generation is unchanged.

**I want to be upfront about the strength of this result**: only the smallest model is individually
significant, two are flat, and the pooled CI barely excludes zero. This is a much weaker result than
I would like for a config change that affects every RDNA3.5 user. An earlier measurement of the same
change against llama.cpp `b10952` gave a larger pooled `+2.929% [+1.932, +3.937]` with 3 of 4 models
individually significant, so there is run-to-run and base-to-base variation here that I cannot fully
account for.

I am happy to run additional models or configurations if that would help, and I would understand if
maintainers prefer to wait for data from other RDNA3.5 parts before taking a change with this blast
radius.

## Scope / caveats

- Measured on a single 20 CU gfx1151 part. I do not have other RDNA3.5 silicon to test on. Parts
  with more CUs may well prefer the wider tile.
- Only touches `mmq-config-rdna3-5.cuh`; RDNA3.0, RDNA4, CDNA and NVIDIA configurations are
  untouched.
items.title: CUDA/HIP: retune the RDNA3.5 Q4_K MMQ tile configuration

items.body:
`ggml_cuda_mul_mat_q()` already sizes MoE tiles against the average number of tokens an expert
receives (`ne12*n_expert_used/ne02`) rather than the full batch, but the condition only covered
RDNA3.0 and RDNA4. RDNA3.5 has the same small-tile preference, so this widens the check from
`GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA3_0` to `GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA3`.

```diff
-    if (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA3_0(cc) || GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA4(cc)) {
+    if (GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA3(cc) || GGML_CUDA_CC_IS_RDNA4(cc)) {
         ncols_opt = (ne12*n_expert_used + ne02 - 1) / ne02;
     }
```

## Why this helps

`ncols_opt` only feeds the tile-width search in `mul_mat_q_switch_J()`; the launch grid still uses
`ncols_max`, so this cannot change dense behaviour. On gfx1151 the un-widened check meant MoE
dispatches sized their tile against the whole batch instead of the per-expert token count, which
is 8x larger for a typical top-4-of-32 model.

I instrumented the tile-width search (same 13-line debug patch applied to **both** the baseline and
the patched build, so the only difference between the two binaries is the line above):

| model | dispatch kind | n | baseline | patched |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| LFM2.5-8B-A1B (32 experts, top-4, `-ub 512`) | `MUL_MAT_ID` | 124 | `ncols_opt=512` → `J=128` | `ncols_opt=64` → `J=64` |
| LFM2.5-8B-A1B | dense `MUL_MAT` | 177 | — | **unchanged** |
| Qwen3-4B | dense `MUL_MAT` | 428 | — | **unchanged** |

All 124 MoE dispatches narrow; **all 605 dense dispatches keep their tile width bit-for-bit**.

Kernel resources for the two Q4_K kernels involved (`-Rpass-analysis=kernel-resource-usage`,
`--offload-arch=gfx1151`):

| kernel | VGPRs | occupancy |
|---|---:|---:|
| `mul_mat_q<Q4_K, 128, false>` (baseline picks this) | 248 | 5 waves/SIMD |
| `mul_mat_q<Q4_K, 64, false>` (patched picks this) | 157 | 9 waves/SIMD |

So the oversized tile was both mostly empty (one expert sees ~64 of the 512 batch tokens) and
occupancy-limited.

## Test setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Host | LENOVO 83V9 laptop, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 |
| CPU | AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 388, 8C/16T, 23.79 GB RAM |
| GPU | AMD Radeon 8060S, **gfx1151 (RDNA3.5)**, 20 CU, wave32, 16.92 GB shared VRAM, 64 KB LDS/workgroup, driver 32.0.31021.5001 |
| Stack | ROCm 7.2 (HIP 7.2.60201-38d754472, clang 21.0.0git), CMake 3.27.2, Ninja 1.11.0 |
| Base | `1bc7a5af0d14b1fb72f266abbd1237b394187115` |

```
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=<rocm>/bin/clang.exe -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=<rocm>/bin/clang++.exe \
  -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=<rocm>/bin/clang++.exe \
  -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGGML_HIP_NO_VMM=ON \
  -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_KERNELS=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
```

## Correctness

```
test-backend-ops test -b ROCm0 -o MUL_MAT    -p type_a=<q4_K|q5_K|q4_0|q5_0>
test-backend-ops test -b ROCm0 -o MUL_MAT_ID -p type_a=<q4_K|q5_K|q4_0|q5_0>
```

All pass: `MUL_MAT` 64/64, 29/29, 48/48, 14/14; `MUL_MAT_ID` 84/84, 3/3, 74/74, 3/3.

## Performance

```
llama-bench -m <model> -p 2048 -n 128 -b 2048 -ub 512 -ngl 99 -fa 1 -lm none -r 3 -o json
```

8 balanced AB/BA pairs per model against a pristine build of the same base commit. Statistic is the
paired log-ratio of `pp2048` with a two-sided 95% Student-t CI (`-r 3` is intra-process and is not
treated as three independent samples):

| model | quant | pp2048 | 95% CI | wins |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| LFM2.5-8B-A1B-UD-Q4_K_M | Q4_K MoE | **+16.198%** | `[+12.704, +19.799]` | 8/8 |
| Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Q2_K | Q2_K MoE | **+6.189%** | `[+5.245, +7.141]` | 8/8 |
| **pooled (16 pairs)** | | **+11.081%** | `[+7.972, +14.279]` | **16/16** |

Token generation is unchanged on the Q4_K MoE model and `+2.188% [+0.905, +3.488]` on the Q2_K one.

## Note on an alternative form

I also measured a larger variant that instead hard-codes `J=64` for a whitelist of MoE shapes
(Q4_K/Q5_K/Q4_0/Q5_0, 16..256 experts, top-k in {2,4,6,8,16}). Head-to-head in a single paired
campaign it was **indistinguishable** from this one-line change on Q4_K MoE
(`+0.307% [-2.265, +2.945]`, 5/8) and **5.841% slower** on Q2_K MoE, which its whitelist does not
cover. The one-line form is therefore both simpler and broader, so that is what is proposed here.

## Scope / caveats

- Measured on a single 20 CU gfx1151 part. I do not have other RDNA3.5 silicon to test on.
- Only affects the MoE (`ids_dst != nullptr`) tile-width choice on RDNA3.5; RDNA3.0, RDNA4, CDNA and
  NVIDIA paths are untouched.
