## Overview

Follow up PR after the `Q2_0` CPU (#24448) and Metal (#25419) backends. This PR adds the CUDA backend for `Q2_0`.

## Supported Models

Supported Models: Ternary-Bonsai-{27B, 8B, 4B, 1.7B}.

*Note*: In our huggingface repos ggufs ending with `_Q2_0_g64.gguf` are packed for this PR; `Q2_0.gguf` ones are the older group-128 packing from our fork. After all backends merge we will rename and replace with the official Q2_0 (group size 64).

```bash
hf download prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-8B-gguf   Ternary-Bonsai-8B-Q2_0_g64.gguf   --local-dir models
hf download prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-gguf  Ternary-Bonsai-27B-Q2_g64.gguf    --local-dir models
```

## Correctness: F16 vs Q2_0 logits KL

To test for correctness we compare the logits from Q2_0 vs F16. Since the Ternary-Bonsai models are natively ternary and it packs perfectly into 2-bits (Q2_0), if we compre logits from Q2_0 vs F16 we should get a KL close to 0.

```bash
./build/bin/llama-perplexity -m models/Ternary-Bonsai-<size>-F16.gguf \
  -f datasets/wikitext-2-raw/wiki.test.raw -c 512 --chunks 20 -ngl 99 --save-all-logits f16.bin

./build/bin/llama-perplexity -m models/Ternary-Bonsai-<size>-Q2_0_g64.gguf \
  -f datasets/wikitext-2-raw/wiki.test.raw -c 512 --chunks 20 -ngl 99 \
  --kl-divergence --kl-divergence-base f16.bin
```

| size | Mean KLD | Same top-1 | PPL(Q2_0)/PPL(F16) |
| ---- | -------- | ---------- | ------------------ |
| 1.7B | 0.000445 | 98.69 % | 1.0017 |
| 4B   | 0.000462 | 98.35 % | 1.0026 |
| 8B   | 0.000446 | 98.53 % | 1.0001 |
| 27B  | 0.000620 | 98.77 % | 1.0004 |

## Speeds: `llama-bench` CUDA (NVIDIA L40S)

```bash
./build/bin/llama-bench -m models/Ternary-Bonsai-<size>-Q2_0_g64.gguf -ngl 99 -p 512 -n 128 -r 5
```

```
| model            |       size |     params | backend | ngl |  test |               t/s |
| ---------------- | ---------: | ---------: | ------- | --: | ----: | ----------------: |
| qwen3 1.7B Q2_0  | 461.79 MiB |     1.72 B | CUDA    |  99 | pp512 | 30390.71 ± 7897.9 |
| qwen3 1.7B Q2_0  | 461.79 MiB |     1.72 B | CUDA    |  99 | tg128 |   530.76 ±   9.90 |
| qwen3 4B Q2_0    |   1.05 GiB |     4.02 B | CUDA    |  99 | pp512 | 16355.03 ± 3005.3 |
| qwen3 4B Q2_0    |   1.05 GiB |     4.02 B | CUDA    |  99 | tg128 |   322.21 ±   1.79 |
| qwen3 8B Q2_0    |   2.15 GiB |     8.19 B | CUDA    |  99 | pp512 | 10490.07 ± 1138.2 |
| qwen3 8B Q2_0    |   2.15 GiB |     8.19 B | CUDA    |  99 | tg128 |   239.52 ±   0.76 |
| qwen35 27B Q2_0  |   7.05 GiB |    26.90 B | CUDA    |  99 | pp512 |  2782.77 ± 214.07 |
| qwen35 27B Q2_0  |   7.05 GiB |    26.90 B | CUDA    |  99 | tg128 |    72.03 ±   0.19 |
```

<details>
<summary>Q2_0 g64 vs g128; speed/size tradeoff (for the curious)</summary>

The g128 is built from our fork, but wanted to compare speeds if anyone is curious.
Prompt processing is similar as expected; token generation is slightly slower for the 8B as expected from the larger size for g64 vs g128. For 27B token generation looks very similar.

| model | block | pp512 (t/s) | tg128 (t/s) | size |

| 8B  | g128 | 11008 | 252.9 | 2.03 GiB |

</details>


## Requirements
<!-- IMPORTANT: Please do NOT delete this section, otherwise your PR may be rejected -->

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md): Yes

- AI usage disclosure: Initial kernels were for group size 128, for the migration to group size 64 and rebasing to master used AI to make the changes (some cuda files were moved and refactored). Mostly followed either Q4_0 or Q1_0.
Manually reviewed all the changes and ran both speed and KL tests for correctness with a fresh build. The Q2_0 group 128 has been used by many people before and they behaved well, the main extra tests here were done to make sure newly converted g64 ggufs match the PR.

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
OMP_PLACES="cores" OMP_PROC_BIND=spread BONSAI_SPECULATIVE=1 ./llama-server -m ./bonsai27b/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-Q2_0.gguf --alias "Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-GGUF" -c 32768 -ngl 99 --spec-draft-model ./bonsai27b/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-dspark-Q4_1.gguf --spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max 4 -ngld 99 --jinja --chat-template-file ./bonsai27b/chat_template_v2.jinja -np 1 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8090 --no-mmap -b 1024 -ub 512 --ctx-checkpoints 4 --webui-mcp-proxy
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### System Specs
```
OS: CachyOS
CPU: Core i9-12900HK
RAM: 64GB DDR5-4800
GPU0: Intel Xe Graphics
GPU1: RTX 3080 Ti (Laptop) 16GB
```

### Problem Description
When running draft-dspark speculative decoding on hardware with constrained VRAM (e.g., a 16GB GPU laptop setup), setting a high context window (-c 32768) on the main model causes a fatal cudaMalloc out-of-memory error during the graph reservation step.The scheduler dynamically catches the batch structure and forces the drafting array to bloat synchronously with the master model context parameter:
```
draft-dspark: raising draft ctx n_batch 1024 -> 32772 (full-context staging + block)
```
Because the fork lacks explicit CLI flags to step down the staging bounds of the speculative model alone, a massive ~5.88 GB compute buffer allocation is requested all at once, leading to an immediate boot crash. Offloading the draft layer to the CPU via --spec-draft-device none stops the crash but reduces generation performance from an exceptional 65+ T/S down to ~15 T/S due to heavy PCIe lane transfer bottlenecks.

### Steps to Reproduce
Load a baseline dense model alongside the custom ternary weights (Q2_0) using a 32K context profile.Direct the execution stream to target draft-dspark fully inside GPU layer maps (-ngl 99, -ngld 99).Run the following command structure:

```
OMP_PLACES="cores" OMP_PROC_BIND=spread BONSAI_SPECULATIVE=1 ./llama-server \
  -m ./bonsai27b/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-Q2_0.gguf \
  -c 32768 \
  -ngl 99 \
  --spec-draft-model ./bonsai27b/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-dspark-Q4_1.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-dspark \
  --spec-draft-n-max 4 \
  -ngld 99 \
  -b 1024 -ub 512
```

items.body:
### Update 2026-09-04: rescoped

The original version of this issue led with a Q2_0 `vec_dot` change for gfx1201. **That work has since landed independently in #26753** (native permute instructions replacing the `__byte_perm` lowering, +35% tg128 on a 9070 XT, merged 2026-08-30). That PR is a better-scoped version of what I described, and I have no interest in relitigating it -- it also establishes the precedent I was asking about, namely that arch-guarded ternary paths are acceptable here.

What follows is what remains unclaimed, plus a measurement finding that I think matters more than any single kernel.

---

### 1. A measurement correction that affects how these formats get evaluated

The common way to judge a quant kernel -- weight bytes divided by decode time, expressed as a percentage of memory-bandwidth roofline -- **systematically understates low-bpw formats**, and I think it has misdirected optimization work (certainly mine).

Holding the model fixed and varying only the weight encoding, decode time is linear in weight bytes with a large constant term:

| model | fit | R^2 |
|---|---|---|
| Bonsai-8B | `ms = 1.5556*GB + 2.275` | 0.99883 |
| Bonsai-27B | `ms = 1.6486*GB + 7.982` | 0.99924 |
| Qwen3.6-27B | `ms = 1.2841*GB + 15.089` | 0.99265 |

Three models, 4-6 points each, spanning up to 7.5x in weight bytes.

Subtract the constant and every format streams weights at the same rate:

```
Bonsai-27B Q2_0 : 7.154 GB / (19.753 - 7.735) ms = 600.1 GB/s
Bonsai-27B Q1_0 : 3.792 GB / (14.196 - 7.735) ms = 610.3 GB/s
Qwen3.6-27B     : 755.9 / 771.5 / 776.4 / 778.8 / 783.4 / 783.5 GB/s across
                  Q4_K_M, Q5_K_XL, MXFP6, Q6_K_XL, F8E4M3, Q8_0
```

The naive metric on that same Qwen data reads 460 -> 557 GB/s and looks like a 20% efficiency gradient across formats. There is no gradient. It is one constant divided by a shrinking numerator, so it *must* fall monotonically as bpw falls.

Concretely: Q2_0 measured "63% of roofline" and I spent a long time hunting the missing 37%. Corrected, it is at 100%. Five separate hypotheses (block layout, byte-granular loads, activation traffic, unpack ALU, visit width) all came back negative because there was nothing to find.

I would suggest that any future low-bpw kernel comparison subtract the per-token constant first, or compare kernel time directly rather than end-to-end decode.

### 2. Q1_0 vec_dot -- still unclaimed, and the win is much larger than I first reported

**Correction to the original version of this issue: I claimed +16%. Measured against clean upstream master it is +110%.** The original figure was taken on my own fork, where other changes had already recovered most of the loss, so the marginal gain there was small. Against master nothing masks it.

Measured on 1x Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), interleaved runs, `-p 0 -n 64 -r 5`, Bonsai-27B Q1_0 (3.53 GiB):

```
master           29.69 / 29.11 t/s
master + patch   61.97 / 61.34 t/s
mean  29.402 -> 61.657 t/s   (+109.7%)
```

Mechanism: the current path issues **20 software `__byte_perm` calls per 32-element chunk** (2 for the nibble indices, 4 for the byte values, 4 to unshuffle -- twice per block). HIP has no hardware `__byte_perm`, so it lowers to a software routine and Q1_0 becomes VALU-bound rather than bandwidth-bound. Replacing it with 8 hardware `v_perm_b32` plus arithmetic removes the bottleneck.

The patch is one helper plus an `#if defined(GGML_USE_HIP)` / `#else`, matching the shape of the Q2_0 path merged in #26753. The `#else` branch is untouched.

Correctness:
- exhaustive equivalence over all 65536 possible `q` values, both paths compiled for gfx1201: **bit-identical**
- `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT`: all 11 `q1_0` cases OK (n=1..9, k=256 and 4096)

Caveats stated plainly: single model, single card, and I have no NVIDIA hardware, so the CUDA path is unverified by measurement -- it is unchanged code inside the `#else`, but I have not run it.

Worth noting alongside this: Q1_0 will not beat Q2_0 on this class of hardware even with the fix, and that appears to be a property of sub-2-bpw formats rather than of any implementation. Independent confirmations:

- ikawrakow, ik_llama.cpp#45 on an RTX-4080: ternary at 305 t/s vs `IQ2_TN` at 320, attributed to "the bit twiddling we need to unpack the ternary bits"
- #19743, RTX 4090 Vulkan: TQ1_0 608 t/s vs TQ2_0 624 t/s

So the fix is worth having, but nobody should expect 1-bit to be the fast path.

### 3. hipBLASLt prefill routes -- unclaimed, and nothing comparable exists

pp1024 +37.5% Q2_0 / +17.8% Q1_0 (warm, self-tuning per-shape algo cache). As far as I can find, there is no ternary or sub-4-bit path through hipBLASLt or Tensile anywhere -- Tensile has no such datatype at all.

### 4. fp8 (E4M3/E5M2) tensor types -- unclaimed

ggml stops at MXFP4/NVFP4. I have working WMMA fp8 kernels on gfx1201, bit-exact verified. Flagging for interest only; happy to take this to a separate discussion if there is appetite.

### Closed negatives, recorded so nobody repeats them

- **Struct-of-arrays weight layout.** `block_q2_0` is 18 bytes with `qs` at offset 2, so its addresses are never 4-byte aligned, which is why the HIP path does 8 scalar byte loads and assembles `qs0`/`qs1` by hand. Splitting scales into a separate array makes the code stream contiguous and allows aligned dword loads. Tested with production arithmetic held fixed and the layout as the only variable, bit-exact: **2.39x at 4096x4096, but 0.99x once the working set exceeds Infinity Cache**. The unaligned loads are fully hidden behind DRAM latency. No win.
- **Activation-quant dedup across sibling matmuls** does not apply to a standard decode graph. ggml already quantizes once per distinct activation (measured 4.08 quantizes vs 6.87 matmuls per layer on a 64-layer model), so there is no sibling redundancy left to remove.

### Where the remaining time actually goes

For completeness, the per-token budget on Bonsai-27B Q2_0 (19.753 ms):

```

## Overview This PR adds Q2_0 support for CPU. Main motivation is to support [Ternary Bonsai models](https://huggingface.co/collections/prism-ml/bonsai) (1.7B, 4B, 8B) and upcoming models. This PR is CPU only (ARM NEON + generic scalar fallback). This completes the Q1_0, Q2_0, Q4_0, Q8_0 family. We have the x86, Metal, CUDA, and Vulkan backends ready to submit later. ### Notes - Format: Each group of 64 weights shares one fp16 scale `d`; weights are packed at 2 bits each with mapping of `{0,1,2,3} => {-1,0,+1,+2} * d` - Our models natively support group size **128**; however, it was requested to do group size **64** for the official Q2_0 format (see [discussion #22019](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/22019)), so this PR uses 64. - We plan to also maintain a sibling **group-128** variant (`PQ2_0`) in our fork since the 0.125 extra bpw becomes significant on larger models. If you have a cleaner way to do this, please let us know. For future release we will pack the models into both Q2_0 and PQ2_0 formats. - Why not use TQ1_0 / TQ2_0? They support group size 256, our models are group size 128, and also cpu-only and harder to accelerate on Metal/CUDA, etc. More info in: [discussion #22019](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/22019) ### Speed/Correctness Summary - **Speeds**: All on Mac M4 Pro (ARM NEON, `-t 8`, `-ngl 0`). - **Correctness**: Compare unpacked (from FP16 gguf) logits vs packed (Q2_0 gguf) logits on. ## Overview

Follow up PR after merging of `Q2_0` CPU PR[#24448].
This PR adds the Metal backend support for `Q2_0`.

## Supported Models

Supported Models: Ternary-Bonsai-{8B, 4B, 1.7B}-Q2_0_g64.gguf, more coming very soon.

*Note*: In our huggingface repos ggufs ending with `_Q2_0_64.gguf` are packed for this PR, `Q2_0.gguf` ones are older packing from our fork that have group 128, after all backends merge will rename and replace with the official Q2_0(group size 64)). 

```bash

hf download prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-4B-gguf  Ternary-Bonsai-4B-Q2_0_g64.gguf  --local-dir models
hf download prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-8B-gguf  Ternary-Bonsai-8B-Q2_0_g64.gguf  --local-dir models
```

## Correctness: Metal vs CPU logits KL

The ensure correctness we run the model twice: 1) Q2_0 CPU 2) Q2_0 Metal. We store the logits for both and compare the KL divergence. Using the standard llama-perplexity tool. 

```bash
# reference logits from the CPU kernel
./build/bin/llama-perplexity -m models/Ternary-Bonsai-<size>-Q2_0_g64.gguf \
  -f datasets/wikitext-2-raw/wiki.test.raw -c 512 --chunks 20 -ngl 0 --save-all-logits cpu.bin
# Metal vs CPU
./build/bin/llama-perplexity -m models/Ternary-Bonsai-<size>-Q2_0_g64.gguf \
  -f datasets/wikitext-2-raw/wiki.test.raw -c 512 --chunks 20 -ngl 99 \
  --kl-divergence --kl-divergence-base cpu.bin
```

## Summary

Adds **`GGML_TYPE_Q2_0`** — PrismML's ternary **1.58-bit** format (as used by `prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-8B-gguf`). Block = 128 weights, one fp16 scale, 2-bit codes `c ∈ {0,1,2,3}` → symbol `c-1 ∈ {-1,0,+1,+2}` (34 bytes/block, 2.125 bpw). PrismML shipped this in a fork and noted an "upstream PR coming soon"; this is a mainline-based implementation of it. Refs PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp#49.

The type slots into the free index 42 (next after `GGML_TYPE_Q1_0 = 41`).

## What's implemented
- **Core:** `block_q2_0`, type-traits, CPU `dequantize_row_q2_0` + `quantize_row_q2_0_ref`, CPU `get_rows`.
- **CUDA/HIP:**
  - dequant → `to_fp16/bf16/fp32` (+ non-contiguous) and `get_rows` (rides the dequant→GEMM prefill path).
  - **MMVQ:** `vec_dot_q2_0_q8_1` using a bit-spread of the 2-bit codes + the `q8_1` stored sum offset (`dot(c-1,u) = dot(c,u) - Σu`), avoiding per-code subtract/borrow.
  - **MMQ:** `load_tiles_q2_0` unpacks into the Q8_0 int8 tile layout and reuses `vec_dot_q8_0_q8_1_{mma,dp4a}`; template instance added + registered in `generate_cu_files.py`.

## Correctness & performance
Greedy output verified coherent ("The capital of France is Paris."). `llama-bench` on **RADV GFX1201 (Radeon AI PRO R9700)**, ROCm 7.2, `Ternary-Bonsai-8B-Q2_0`:

| path | pp512 (t/s) | tg128 (t/s) |
|---|---|---|
| **this PR (HIP, MMQ+MMVQ)** | **3877** | **114** |
| Vulkan backend (KHR coopmat) | 2775 | 132 |
| PrismML's stale fork (HIP) | 250 | 99 |

## Scope / follow-ups
CPU is generic (no arch-specific SIMD); **Vulkan, Metal, and CPU-SIMD kernels + `test-backend-ops` coverage are not yet included** — hence draft. Seeking maintainer guidance on whether a third-party ternary format is in scope for mainline, and on the preferred shape before filling in the remaining backends/tests. Happy to iterate.

*(Implemented with tooling assistance; all benchmarks measured on the hardware above.)*

## Overview **Update**: Initially had two types of Q1_0 (group size 32) and Q1_0_g128 (group size 128) but now only keeping Q1_0 with group size 128. If you see Q1_0_g128 in screenshots anywhere its now Q1_0. This PR adds `Q1_0` a 1-bit quantization/packing support for CPU. Motivation is to support inference for family of [1-bit Bonsai models ](https://huggingface.co/collections/prism-ml/bonsai) which are native in `Q1_0` (group size 128). Basically each group has a shared scale of fp16, and then the weights are packed into 1-bit, i.e. each weight is represented either by a 0 or 1. The 0 would represent -scale, and the 1 would represent +scale. We just released Bonsai 1-bit models, which are 3 models that are natively in Q1_0 format. With help of llama.cpp can run our model at a very fast speed while being decent at evals. (see cpu benchmarks below). I have not really tried optimizing the cpu version as much, mostly tested for correctness, our main focus was Metal/CUDA which will come later in future PRs. Speeds across devices: Evals comparing to simalar param count models (but at a much smaller footprint) ## Additional information ### Models The Q1_0_g128 models can be found here, in this PR mostly used the 1.7B model for testing since this is CPU only. - [prism-ml/Bonsai-8B-gguf](https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Bonsai-8B-gguf) - [prism-ml/Bonsai-4B-gguf](https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Bonsai-4B-gguf) - [prism-ml/Bonsai-1.7B-gguf](https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Bonsai-1.7B-gguf) - See a working demo from our Bonsai-demo repo: [Bonsai-demo](https://github.com/prismml-eng/Bonsai-demo) - See more details here: [1-bit-bonsai-8b-whitepaper.pdf](https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/Bonsai-demo/blob/main/1-bit-bonsai-8b-whitepaper.pdf) ### Testing Process We test two cpu routes: ARM NEON and Generic Scalar Fallback. items.body:
## Environment

- **llama.cpp**: master `8144f31` (2026-08-23) + also reproduced on release b10488 (Windows CUDA 13.3 build)
- **OS**: Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04 (both tested, same cliff)
- **GPU**: RTX 4080 SUPER 16GB, driver 591.86 (CUDA 13.1), nvcc 13.1, sm_89
- **Model**: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` UD-Q3_K_XL (12.2GB); also reproduced with UD-IQ4_XS (13.3GB) and IQ4_XS (14.6GB)
- **Backend**: CUDA, single GPU

## Symptom

With the model **fully resident on GPU** (zero "assigned to device CPU" lines, verified in logs), decode (tg) speed collapses non-linearly once the KV position exceeds roughly 80K tokens — from ~33 t/s at 68K position to **1.4 t/s (714 ms/token) at 91K position**, or outright timeouts. **Prompt processing (pp) stays fast (~1300 t/s) at the same positions.** Zero-context decode is normal (~38-39 t/s) on every configuration below.

## Reproduction matrix (WSL2, llama-server)

Command shape:
```
./llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -ngl 999 --load-mode none \
    -c <CTX> [-fa on] -ctk <Q> -ctv <Q>
```
Then send a chat completion with a ~91K-token filler prompt and `max_tokens=100`.

| Config | VRAM fit (CPU overrides) | pp @91K fill | tg @91K position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-c 131072 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits, 0 CPU lines | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` | fits | fast | **timed out (>25 min)** |
| `-c 98304  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **timed out** |
| `-c 73728  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **33.1 t/s @ 68K position ✅** |

Position sweep with the last config (UD-Q3_K_XL, q8 KV, no FA):

| KV position (prompt tokens) | decode t/s (server-side timing) |
|---|---|
| 45,574 | 35.6 |
| 60,309 | 33.9 |
| 68,642 | 33.1 |
| 91,077 | **1.4 (or timeout)** |

## Key observations

1. **The cliff is positional, not a memory-spill issue.** All 96K/128K configs above report 0 CPU tensor overrides and normal free VRAM headroom; KV quantization level (q4/q5/q8) and `-fa on/off` make no difference to the cliff. Only the *position* matters.
2. **pp is unaffected at the same positions** (~1300 t/s for the 91K fill), so this is specific to the decode path.
3. The drop is far steeper than any plausible O(n) attention-scan cost: 68K→91K position is a 1.34x context increase but a **~24x decode slowdown**.
4. Server logs at the cliff show `eval time = 1055.41 ms / 300 tokens (0.95 tokens per second)` with `graphs reused = 298`, i.e. CUDA graph reuse continues normally while per-token latency explodes.
5. Also reproduced on the same hardware under Windows native (b10488) at large `-c`, so it is not WSL2-specific.

## Suspected area

Decode-path attention over long KV for the hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers (Qwen3.8 / qwen35-family). Possibly a fallback/slow kernel engaged past some KV extent threshold. Possibly related family: #27442 (empty generation >16K on Metal for qwen35moe hybrids), #27572 (draft acceptance collapse with multi-ubatch batches).

## Logs

Full `llama-server` logs for the 131072/q4/FA and 73728/q8/no-FA runs available on request (happy to attach — they contain per-token timing lines, tensor placement, and KV buffer sizes).
items.title: Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid Gated DeltaNet): decode throughput collapses ~25x at context positions >~80K while prompt processing stays fast

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: b10752 (b96806d96)
```
Container image `ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-vulkan`, run in router mode
(`--models-preset`), one child `llama-server` per model.

### Operating systems

Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic)

### GGML backends

Vulkan (Mesa RADV)

### Hardware

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 — Radeon 8060S Graphics (RADV STRIX_HALO, gfx1151),
120 GiB GTT, unified memory.

### Models

`Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf` (dense, 27.3B params, `n_ctx_train = 262144`), which
carries MTP layers.

### Problem description

With `--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp` and a large `--ctx-size`, the server
fails **every** request — including a 13-token prompt — dying within ~2s of the
prompt/decode transition and exiting with status 1. The router respawns it, so
the failure presents as a ~53s crash-loop that silently discards all prompt
cache.

The trigger is the **total** `--ctx-size`, not the per-sequence context. That
appears to come from `common/speculative.cpp`, where the MTP draft context is
sized from the target's total context despite the comment stating per-sequence
intent:

```c
// common/speculative.cpp — common_speculative_init_result::common_speculative_init_result()
    auto cparams = common_context_params_to_llama(params);

    if (spec_mtp) {
        cparams.ctx_type = LLAMA_CONTEXT_TYPE_MTP;
    }

    // the draft context holds as many tokens per sequence as the target context
    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx(ctx_tgt);        // <-- total, not per-sequence
```

`llama_n_ctx()` returns the total; `llama_n_ctx_seq()` is the per-sequence
accessor:

```c
// src/llama-context.cpp
uint32_t llama_n_ctx    (const llama_context * ctx) { return ctx->n_ctx();     }
uint32_t llama_n_ctx_seq(const llama_context * ctx) { return ctx->n_ctx_seq(); }
```

The draft context then builds its own memory module from those cparams:

```c
    memory.reset(model.create_memory(params_mem, cparams));
```

Under `--no-kv-unified` this makes the draft context `n_parallel` times larger
than the comment intends. Under `--kv-unified` it is worse, because
`n_ctx_seq` is then set equal to the whole total:

```c
// src/llama-context.cpp
    if (cparams.kv_unified) { cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx;                 }
    else                    { cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx / n_seq_max;     }
```

Note also that `--kv-unified-per-slot` cannot bound this: `llama_context_params`
has `n_ctx`, `n_seq_max` and `kv_unified`, but no per-slot field, so the
server-level cap never reaches the draft context.

### Ablation matrix

All rows below are on the same build, model, and machine, and each was verified
by serving requests. "draft n_ctx" is the value the code above assigns.

| `--ctx-size` | `--parallel` | kv-unified | `--spec-type` | draft `n_ctx` | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 786432 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 786432 | **fails every request** |
| 786432 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod` | — | works (12.8 tok/s, 99.99% cache reuse) |
| 393216 | 3 | off | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 393216 | works (24 tok/s) |
| 524288 | 3 | on + `--kv-unified-per-slot 262144` | `ngram-mod,draft-mtp` | 524288 | works (23.7 tok/s) |

Removing `draft-mtp` at the failing `--ctx-size` fixes it outright; restoring
`draft-mtp` at a smaller `--ctx-size` also fixes it. So the fault requires
`draft-mtp` **and** a large total `--ctx-size` together.

Note the third and fourth rows: the working unified config has a draft
`n_ctx_seq` of 524288, larger than the failing split config's 262144. So
per-sequence size is not the trigger — the **total** is.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
llama-server \
  --model Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --ctx-size 786432 --parallel 3 --no-kv-unified \
  --spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp \
  --spec-draft-n-max 4 --spec-draft-n-min 0 --draft-p-min 0.25 \
  --n-gpu-layers 999 --flash-attn on \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 512 --jinja

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"...","max_tokens":8,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say: ok"}]}'
```

The model loads normally and reports `status=loaded`. The first request — any
size — kills the process.

### What was ruled out

- **GPU/driver watchdog.** This machine separately had `amdgpu.lockup_timeout`
  at its 2000 ms default, which produced `ring comp_1.x.1 timeout`, a compute
  queue reset and `vk::DeviceLostError`. That was raised to
  `10000,60000,10000,10000` and the machine rebooted. `dmesg` has shown **zero**
  ring timeouts since, yet the MTP failure persists — so the two are unrelated
  faults and this report is only about the second.
- **Out of memory.** The failing configuration loads cleanly at 82 GiB of 120
  GiB GTT, and no OOM appears in `dmesg`. The failure is on first use, not at
  allocation.
- **Prompt length.** A 13-token prompt fails identically to a 100k one.
- **Tool/grammar constrained sampling.** A request with no `tools` fails too.
- **Build drift.** `b10752-b96806d96` throughout, verified via
  `system_fingerprint`; the container was restarted, never re-pulled.
- **Slot count alone.** `--parallel 3` works fine at smaller `--ctx-size`.

### Suggested fix

```diff
-    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx(ctx_tgt);
+    cparams.n_ctx = llama_n_ctx_seq(ctx_tgt);
```

This matches the stated intent of the comment. It would also make the draft
context independent of `--parallel`, which currently multiplies it.

### Possibly related

#23658 reports MTP draft acceptance collapsing at particular `--ctx-size`
values on a ~2048-aligned pattern, attributed there to "slot indexing in how
the MTP draft context shares the KV cache with the target context". That may be
the same sizing/indexing surface presenting as degradation rather than a crash.

### Relevant log output

```
# router, at the moment of failure
E srv    operator(): http client error: Failed to read connection
I srv    operator():
items.title: Eval bug: draft-mtp draft context is sized from llama_n_ctx() (total) rather than llama_n_ctx_seq(), killing the server at decode entry on large --ctx-size

items.body:
When ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft splits allocation on buft max_size, a view-only tail at the end of the context could skip the final alloc_tensor_range. Persistent views (e.g. KV k_stream / v_stream) were then left without ggml_backend_view_init.
Allocate only parent tensors in alloc_tensor_range and initialize all views in a final pass over the context after all splits complete.
## Overview
`ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft` can split a context across multiple buffers when a tensor would exceed the backend buffer-type `max_size` (for example Vulkan's default 1 GiB). If the remaining tail of the context contains only views, the final `alloc_tensor_range` may be skipped, so those views never get `ggml_backend_view_init`.
Persistent KV stream views (`layer.k_stream` / `v_stream`) then keep `tensor->data == NULL` while `view_src` is allocated. Host state save/restore later calls `ggml_backend_tensor_get` / `set` on those views and hits:
`GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated")`
This change:
- allocates only parent tensors inside each split range
- initializes all uninitialized views in one final pass over the context
Also adds `test_view_init_after_max_size_split` in `tests/test-alloc.cpp`
to cover the oversized-parent + view-only-tail case.
## Additional information
Fixes #19839
Fixes #23737
Fixes #21762

Related:
- #21576 (state-IO `!tensor->data` guards; complementary discussion)
I reproduced the assert with Qwen3.6-27B (MTP) when a parent KV tensor exceeded buft `max_size` and the context ended with a view-only tail.
Note on #21576: skipping tensors with `!tensor->data` avoids the assert, but can omit real KV still reachable via `view_src` and misalign the serialized state. This PR fixes the missing view init in the allocator instead.
Prior investigation commit (same patch on older master; kept for reference):
https://github.com/Yoshi4470/llama.cpp/commit/99655d5854e63e736a6a93280e01b7e785a59ba5
## Test plan
- [x] `test-alloc` (includes new `test_view_init_after_max_size_split`)
- [x] Vulkan A/B on the Qwen3.6-27B MTP speculative path (same command, 10 runs each):
  - before (`e3546c794`): 0/10 (assert every time)
  - after (this PR): 10/10 (no assert, completed normally)
- [x] Earlier `amdvlk64.dll` crash after the assert site was resolved by an AMD driver update; treated as separate from this allocator fix
- N/A: equivalent-size CPU repro (not practical on this machine)

### Command used for the A/B runs:
- Vulkan / AMDVLK, Windows, AMD Software 26.6.4
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)
```
llama-cli.exe -np 8 -c 2097152 --no-mmap -m models/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ctkd q4_0 -ctvd q4_0 \
--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 -p "Hello!"
```
## Requirements
- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - Cursor assisted with implementing the finalize-views pass and regression test after I identified the root cause in the alloc split path, and with local verification.

### Name and Version

version: 0.4.1-dev (build 1, commit 5836771) built with AppleClang 17.0.0.17000604 for Darwin x86_64

### Operating systems

Mac

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

Intel Core i9-12900F · 48 GB RAM · x86_64
AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT, 16 GB VRAM (RDNA2)
macOS 15.8 (24H23) · MoltenVK 1.4.2 · Vulkan 1.4.357
Built with -DGGML_METAL=OFF -DGGML_VULKAN=ON

ggml_vulkan: 0 = AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT (MoltenVK) | uma: 0 | fp16: 1 | bf16: 0 | fp4: 0 | warp size: 32 | shared memory: 65536 | int dot: 0 | matrix cores: none

### Models

Primary repro: Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Q4_K_M
Also observed with: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B / 14B-Instruct-Q4_K_M, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` crashes with `decode() failed: vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost` and triggers a macOS GPU driver reset (``Kernel_<timestamp>.gpuRestart``, visible as a screen flicker on both monitors; repeated occurrences eventually froze the display and required a hard power-off).

The trigger is the **interaction of two factors**:

1. The server's default `n_parallel = -1` → **4 slots + `kv_unified = true`** (`common/arg.cpp:1400`, `tools/server/server.cpp:154-157`)
2. A prompt above roughly **70 tokens**

**With `--parallel 1` the exact same prompt works reliably.**

`llama-bench` never reproduces it — it runs a single sequence, which is why `pp512` passes while a 75-token server prompt fails.

Possibly related to #17989 (`--parallel 1` reportedly still initializing 4 slots in some paths); on this build `--parallel 1` does produce `n_slots = 1` in the log.

### Steps to reproduce

```
llama-server -m Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -c 4096
```

Then POST a `/v1/chat/completions` request whose prompt exceeds ~70 tokens. Fails on most attempts. Adding `--parallel 1` to the same command makes it reliable.

### Crossed controls

Same model, same machine, same session:

| Configuration | Prompt | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `--parallel 1` | 188 tokens | OK — 172 tokens generated, coherent (3/3) |
| `--parallel 4` (default) | 188 tokens | **FAIL** — ErrorDeviceLost + GPU reset |
| `--parallel 4` (default) | 51 tokens | OK (12/12 across the session) |

Threshold sweep with 4 slots, prompt sizes as reported by the server's own tokenizer:

| Prompt tokens | Result |
|---:|---|
| 50 | OK |
| 65 | OK |
| ~75 | **FAIL** |

### Hypotheses ruled out, each with a crossed control

- **Not context size** — fails at `-c 1024`, `-c 2048` and `-c 4096` alike; `-c 2048` with a short prompt succeeds.
- **Not generation length** — 128 / 256 / 512 `max_tokens` all pass with short prompts.
- **Not batch size** — `llama-bench` and `llama-server` share identical defaults (`n_batch 2048`, `n_ubatch 512`).
- **Not flash attention** — `-fa off` removes the `resolve_fused_ops: ... Flash Attention is assigned to device CPU` warning from the log and the failure persists.
- **Not a poisoned GPU/driver state** — a successful run happens 90 seconds after a failure + GPU reset, in the very configuration that had just failed.
- **Not model size or architecture** — reproduced with `llama` (8B) and `qwen2`.

### Secondary finding: silent output corruption

Two cases returned syntactically valid responses containing a **single repeated token** (normal `finish_reason`, normal token counts) instead of crashing:

- `Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M` with the default 4 slots — 700 tokens, **1 distinct word**. With `--parallel 1` the same model returns correct output and passes a 13-case functional test suite.
- `Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct-Q4_K_M` **even with `--parallel 1`** — 250 tokens, 1 distinct word, including a U+FFFD character. The same model on CPU (`-ngl 0`) returns correct code and passes all 13 cases; `Qwen2.5-Coder-7B` (same architecture, 4.36 GB) is correct on GPU.

This matters because it is silent: without inspecting the content, the response looks like a normal completion. Possibly related to #20104.

### Note on severity

A GPU driver reset on this platform is visible to the user (screen flicker) and, when repeated, can hang the desktop. On Linux/RADV an over-allocation typically fails cleanly instead.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. First observed on 5836771.

### Relevant log output

srv    load_model: initializing, n_slots = 4, n_ctx_slot = 4096, kv_unified = 'true'
resolve_fused_ops: layer 0 is assigned to device Vulkan0 but Flash Attention is assigned to device CPU (usually due to missing support)

{"error":{"code":500,"message":"decode() failed: vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost","type":"server_error"}}

A matching Kernel_<timestamp>.gpuRestart report is written to /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/ on each failure.
items.title: Eval bug: Vulkan/MoltenVK + AMD discrete GPU: ErrorDeviceLost with the default 4 server slots and prompts above ~70 tokens; --parallel 1 fixes it

### Name and Version

Bionic bundled llama.cpp Vulkan 2.41.0 (crash) / 2.39.0 (ok); llama-server reports version 0.4.1-dev build 1 commit b49650a

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

2x Intel Arc Pro B50 (driver 32.0.101.8805) + Intel Core Ultra 5 235HX, 64GB RAM

### Models

All of these fail identically on 2.40/2.41 Vulkan, all load fine on 2.39 Vulkan:
- bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- unsloth/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512-GGUF (Q5_K_M)
- empero-ai/Qwen3.8-35B-A3B-Distill-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
Counter-case: nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (Q4_K_M) loads fine on 2.41 Vulkan.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## What happened

`llama-server` with the Vulkan backend crash-aborts while loading sliding-window-attention
decoder models when the KV cache is offloaded to the GPU. The process dies with
`exitCode=3221226505` (`0xC0000409`, fail-fast) before becoming healthy.

Exact abort line (stderr):

```text
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)
```

## Regression info

- ✅ `llama.cpp ... 2.39.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **loads in ~5s, serves fine**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.40.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.41.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with `--no-kv-offload` — **loads and serves** (KV cache on CPU)
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with full offload + embedding model (`nomic-embed-text-v1.5.Q4_K_M`,
  full attention, `--embedding`) — **loads and serves**

So it is not a globally broken Vulkan backend: it is the
`Vulkan + KV-cache GPU offload + SWA/hybrid-attention decoder` path that regressed
between 2.39 and 2.40.

## Repro

```bat
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf -ngl 99 --port 18081
```

- Model: `bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF`, `Q4_K_S` (~2.4 GB)
- No other flags (all defaults). Crash happens during `load_model`, before listening.

Notable log lines on the crashing 2.41 run (before the abort):

```text
W resolve_fused_ops: layer 0 is assigned to device Vulkan1 but Flash Attention is assigned to device CPU (usually due to missing support)
W resolve_fused_ops: Flash Attention not supported, set to disabled
W ggml_vulkan: Failed to allocate pinned memory (Requested buffer size exceeds device buffer size limit: ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory)
```

On the working `--no-kv-offload` run the server reports `kv_unified = 'true'`,
`n_slots = 4`, then `model loaded` / `listening`.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 x64 (build 10.0.26200)
- GPU: Intel Arc Pro B50 (discrete) + Intel integrated Graphics
- Driver: Intel `32.0.101.8805` (06.07.2026), `vulkan-1.dll` present (system + app dir)
- Builds: LM Studio / Bionic bundled `llama.cpp-win-x86_64-vulkan-avx2` packs
  `2.39.0` (working) vs `2.40.0` / `2.41.0` (crashing), CPU 14 threads
- The same setup serves the models fine on engine 2.39, so driver / loader / model
  file are ruled out

## Suspected area

New fused-ops / unified-KV graph building for SWA models (`cache_k` pre-allocation
landing in a Vulkan buffer that reports no supported op) introduced between 2.39
and 2.40. Happy to test any debug build / extra logging on this machine
(Arc Pro B50 available).

### First Bad Commit

Regressed between bundled builds 2.39.0 (works) and 2.40.0 (broken). Exact upstream commit unknown — these are third-party Bionic/LM Studio bundles, not direct llama.cpp builds. Happy to bisect if given build instructions for Windows Vulkan.

### Relevant log output


Command:
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf --port 18081 -ngl 99

Log:
load_model: loading model '.../mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf'
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)

Process exits immediately with code 3221226505 (0xC0000409).

items.body:
## Bug Description

GLM-5.2 crashes deterministically when attempting distributed inference across multiple DGX Spark nodes via ggml-rpc. The crash occurs during graph computation with `invalid data ptr` on the worker side and `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` abort on the orchestrator side. This appears analogous to #26424 (DeepSeek V4, Metal) but affects CUDA (sm_121).

## Environment

- **Hardware:** 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, Grace Blackwell, 128GB unified memory each)
- **OS:** DGX OS (Ubuntu-based, aarch64)
- **CUDA:** sm_121 native build
- **llama.cpp:** master `5788b510a` (ggml 0.18.1), built with `-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON`
- **Network:** 1Gbit Ethernet between nodes
- **Model:** GLM-5.2 UD-IQ4_NL (also reproduced with UD-Q4_K_M), unsloth GGUF split files

## Setup

**Workers (3 nodes):**

```
./build/bin/ggml-rpc-server -c --host 192.168.1.XXX --port 50052
```

**Orchestrator (1 node):**

```
./build/bin/llama-server \
  -m ~/models/gguf/glm-5.2/UD-IQ4_NL/GLM-5.2-UD-IQ4_NL-00001-of-00009.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  -ngl 999 -c 4096 \
  --tensor-split 1,1,1,1 \
  --rpc 192.168.1.121:50052,192.168.1.111:50052,192.168.1.128:50052
```

## Expected Behavior

Model loads across 4 nodes and serves inference (works with Gemma-4-26B, Qwen3.6-35B, Mistral-Small-3.2 on identical setup).

## Actual Behavior

Weights distribute successfully (~113GB cache per worker), but crashes during graph_compute:

**Worker output:**

[create_node] invalid data ptr[graph_compute] failed to create graph node 30 (id=197768091778640)
Client connection closed

**Orchestrator output:**

ggml-rpc.cpp:519: Remote RPC server crashed or returned malformed response
recv failed (bytes_recv=0, size_to_recv=8)

Stack trace: `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` → `ggml_backend_tensor_copy` → `ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async` → `llama_context::graph_compute` → `llama_context::decode` (during `common_init_from_params`).

## Reproducibility

- 100% deterministic — same worker, same graph node (30)
- Reproduced with UD-IQ4_NL (~348GB) and UD-Q4_K_M (~434GB)
- Reproduced with `-c 4096` and `-c 131072`
- Reproduced with and without `--no-warmup`
- All 4 nodes on identical commit (`5788b510a`, fresh pull)

## What Works

- Single-node llama.cpp on same hardware (Gemma, Qwen, Mistral)
- 2-node llama.cpp RPC with smaller models (Gemma-4-26B, ~51.8 tok/s)
- GLM-5.2 on single-node (4×RTX 6000, Ollama, Note: Different machine! But same model GLM 5.2 UD-IQ4_NL)

## Related

- #26424 — DeepSeek V4 Flash RPC crash (Metal, similar MoE/MLA architecture)
- GLM-5.2 uses IndexShare and MTP/NextN layers — likely unsupported ops in RPC graph distribution

## Logs

Full orchestrator and worker terminal output, dmesg are attached.

[glm-rpc-orch.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708516/glm-rpc-orch.log)

[glm-rpc-worker3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708521/glm-rpc-worker3.log)

[glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708525/glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log)

items.body:
*Filed by Claude (Anthropic's assistant) on behalf of @elimisteve, who reviewed it before posting. All logs and line references were produced on his machine at commit `11924d4c1`. What I could not verify is stated explicitly below.*

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 547 (11924d4c1)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Commit `11924d4c17abc27383376a1ac6a24fa3e36c1c0c` (master, 2026-08-02).

### Operating systems

Linux (Xubuntu, kernel 6.14)

### GGML backends

CUDA (13.1), CPU

### Hardware

Intel Core i9-13950HX · 188 GiB DDR5 · NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada Generation Laptop GPU, 12 GB

### Models

`unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF`, `UD-Q4_K_XL` (native MXFP4 experts), 5 shards.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` fails to start on `deepseek4` with the **default** `-np -1` (auto), and starts
normally with an explicit `--parallel 1`. Nothing else differs.

Auto mode is an unconditional `n_parallel = 4, kv_unified = true`
(`tools/server/server.cpp:151`):

```cpp
if (params.n_parallel < 0) {
    params.n_parallel = 4;
    params.kv_unified = true;
}
```

Under `kv_unified`, `n_ctx_seq` is deliberately **not** divided
(`src/llama-context.cpp:287`):

```cpp
if (cparams.kv_unified) {
    cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx;      // 131072
} else {
    cparams.n_ctx_seq = cparams.n_ctx / cparams.n_seq_max;
```

Both values reach the dsv4 cache (`src/llama-model.cpp:2259-2268`) — `cparams.kv_unified`
(true) and `cparams.n_ctx_seq` (undivided).

`llama_kv_cache_dsv4` then **discards the unified flag**
(`src/llama-kv-cache-dsv4.cpp:1041-1053`):

```cpp
GGML_UNUSED(unified);

// Keep DSV4 KV/state streams per sequence even when public KV mode is unified.
const bool unified_raw = false;

kv_raw = std::make_unique<llama_kv_cache_iswa>(
        model, hparams_raw, type_k, type_v,
        v_trans, offload, swa_full, unified_raw, kv_size, n_seq_max, n_ubatch, n_pad,
        nullptr, filter_raw, reuse, nullptr);
```

`kv_size` is the constructor parameter received at line 1021 and is forwarded here
unchanged — it is not divided anywhere in between. Downstream, `n_stream` becomes
`n_seq_max` (`src/llama-kv-cache.cpp:82`):

```cpp
n_seq_max(n_seq_max), n_stream(unified ? 1 : n_seq_max), ...
```

So dsv4 combines the **non-unified stream layout** (`n_stream = n_seq_max`) with the
**unified sizing** (`kv_size = n_ctx`, undivided). Each mode is self-consistent on its own —
unified is 1 stream × `n_ctx`; non-unified is `n_seq_max` streams × `n_ctx/n_seq_max` — but
the combination appears to allocate `n_seq_max` streams of the *full* context.

The comment on line 1043 suggests forcing per-sequence streams is intentional for this
architecture. If so, the sizing may need to compensate.

#### Reproduction

Fails (default `-np`):
```
llama-server -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf \
  -ngl 999 --n-cpu-moe 43 --no-repack --load-mode mmap \
  --ctx-size 131072 -b 2048 -ub 512 -fa on -ctk f16 -t 8
```
```
E ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 672.00 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E alloc_tensor_range: failed to allocate CUDA0 buffer of size 704643072
E llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: failed to allocate buffer for kv cache
E srv  llama_server: exiting due to model loading error
```

Succeeds — only `--parallel 1` added:
```
llama-server -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00005.gguf \
  -ngl 999 --n-cpu-moe 43 --no-repack --load-mode mmap --parallel 1 \
  --ctx-size 131072 -b 2048 -ub 512 -fa on -ctk f16 -t 8
```

3/3 reproductions each way.

**Stronger isolation — `-ngl 0`**, which puts no model weights on the GPU at all and still
fails, at a much smaller context:

```
# -ngl 0 --ctx-size 32768, ~4.0 GiB free VRAM reported by nvidia-smi
default -np -1 : E ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer:
                 allocating 1290.30 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
--parallel 1   : I srv load_model: initializing, n_slots = 1, n_ctx_slot = 32768,
                 kv_unified = 'false'      -> starts normally
```

Note the failing 1290 MiB allocation is smaller than the ~4.0 GiB nvidia-smi reported free.
That figure is whole-GPU free memory with other resident processes (a browser compositor and
two small CUDA clients) on the same card, and it precedes the allocations this run had
already made, so it is not directly comparable to the failing request. The meaningful
comparison is the controlled one: same machine, same instant, same command, `--parallel 1`
succeeds and the default does not.

### What I could NOT verify

- **Exact byte counts.** The failing run aborts before printing the KV/compute breakdown, and
  this GPU has other resident consumers, so I have no clean side-by-side `KV self size`
  comparison. I am therefore **not** claiming a specific multiplier — only that the default
  path allocates enough more to fail where `--parallel 1` succeeds.
- **`--parallel 4` with `kv_unified = false`** (i.e. explicit `-np 4` rather than auto). That
  would separate "4 slots" from "unified sizing" as the cause. I could not run it in time;
  the code reading suggests it should succeed, since `n_ctx_seq` would then be divided. If a
  maintainer runs only one extra experiment, this is the one.
- Whether other architectures that similarly override `unified` are affected.
- Which fix is correct.

### Possible directions (untested — no PR proposed)

1. When the caller requested unified but dsv4 forces per-sequence streams, size each stream
   as `kv_size / n_seq_max` rather than `kv_size`.
2. Or mark `deepseek4` as incompatible with `kv_unified`, so `llama-context.cpp` takes the
   dividing branch and the existing non-unified math applies unchanged.

I have not built or benchmarked either, so I am not opening a PR.

### Workaround

Pass `--parallel 1` explicitly. This also leaves `kv_unified` at its `false` default, which
[#19523](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp
items.title: Eval bug: DeepSeek-V4 (deepseek4) fails to start on CUDA with the default -np -1 (auto) — dsv4 KV cache forces per-sequence streams while kv_unified leaves n_ctx undivided

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 0.4.1-dev (build 1, commit 79bfc1d)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Built from master with:
`cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS="gfx1201;gfx1151" -DGPU_TARGETS="gfx1201;gfx1151"`
Base image `rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.2.4-complete`, host ROCm 7.2.4, CachyOS, kernel 7.2.3-1-cachyos.

This commit is after 37b53fd ("qwen4exp: add hc ops", 2026-09-16), which touched
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/dsv4-hc.cu` — so the HIP backend hc ops are present.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

- AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, 32624 MiB) — discrete
- AMD Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo (gfx1151, 16384 MiB carve-out) — integrated
- AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S, 46.7 GiB system RAM, NVMe

### Models

- `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` **UD-IQ3_XXS** (76.3 GiB, 3 shards)
- `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` **UD-Q4_K_XL** (104 GiB, 4 shards)

Both reproduce.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

`llama-server` **livelocks during model load** on the HIP backend once a sufficiently
large share of the model is placed on the GPU. It never reaches `listening on http`,
never prints an error, and never exits. The identical command on the **Vulkan** backend,
same machine, same GPU, same model file, loads normally.

Repro (hangs, HIP):

```bash
llama-server \
  -m Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8099 \
  -dev ROCm1 -ngl 999 \
  -ot 'per_layer_token_embd\.weight=CPU,blk\.[12][0-9]\.ffn_.*_exps=CPU' \
  --load-mode mmap --lazy-mode on --jinja \
  -c 8192 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -b 128 -ub 128 -np 1 --no-warmup
```

Control (works, Vulkan) — byte-identical flags except `-dev Vulkan0`, build 11046
(`60081bb2b`, includes 35822af "vulkan: support qwen4exp hc ops"):

| backend | devices | VRAM reached | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| HIP | `-dev ROCm1` (dGPU only) | 30.7 GB | **livelock, >10 min, killed manually** |
| Vulkan | `-dev Vulkan0` (dGPU only) | 31.1 GB | **loaded in 105 s**, 5.48 tok/s |
| Vulkan | `-dev Vulkan1,Vulkan0 -ts 32,68` (both) | 43.8 GB (31.2 + 12.6) | **loaded in 105 s**, 7.62 tok/s |

The Vulkan runs also push *more* onto the GPU than the HIP run that wedges, so this is
not a case of Vulkan simply doing less work.

### State while hung

```
active threads : 1 of 37          (35 worker threads idle)
container CPU  : 99.5%            (one core of 32)
GPU busy       : 0-3%
disk read      : 0.0 MB/s         (frozen; read_bytes stops advancing entirely)
VRAM           : frozen at 30.7 GB
last log line  : "llama_model_loader: tensor overrides to CPU are used with mmap
                  enabled - consider using --load-mode none for better performance"
```

It stays in this state indefinitely; SIGTERM is ignored, `docker kill` is required.

### This is not OOM

Genuine OOM on this setup fails cleanly in ~30 s with a clear message, e.g.:

```
ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 33482.83 MiB on device 1:
  cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
alloc_tensor_range: failed to allocate ROCm1 buffer of size 35109292288
llama_model_load: error loading model: unable to allocate ROCm1 buffer
```

The livelock produces no such message and occurs at allocations that fit.

### Trigger

Correlates with how much is placed on the GPU, not with any fixed limit:

| config | VRAM | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Q4_K_XL `-ncmoe 42` | 16.18 GB | loads |
| Q4_K_XL `-ncmoe 40` | 19.11 GB | loads |
| IQ3_XXS `-ncmoe 32`, 1 GPU | 20.40 GB | loads (2.49 tok/s) |
| IQ3_XXS `-ot` 2 rules, 2 GPUs | 20.0 GB | **livelock** |
| IQ3_XXS `-ot` 2 rules, 1 GPU | 30.7 GB | **livelock** |
| Q4_K_XL `-ncmoe` 32 / 36 / 38 | — | **livelock** |

### Ruled out

- **Missing hc ops in the HIP backend** — build is after 37b53fd, which added them to
  `ggml-cuda/dsv4-hc.cu`.
- **iGPU / unified-memory (GTT) interaction** — reproduces with the iGPU excluded
  entirely (`-dev ROCm1`), discrete card only.
- **A fixed VRAM ceiling** — the R9700 alone reached 30.7 GB before wedging, well above
  the ~20 GB configs that load fine.
- **Model file corruption** — the same files load and serve correctly under Vulkan.

### Possibly related

#27763 (garbage output when >8 layers on GPU, SM110), #27780 (ggml_abort under load,
SM121), #27797 (gfx1151 multi-segment degradation). Same family of "more on GPU →
misbehaves" reports for qwen4exp, though the symptom here is a hang rather than bad
output or an abort.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected — qwen4exp has only been supported since #27742 (2026-08-27).

### Relevant log output

```
0.00.026.138 I srv    load_model: loading model '.../Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00003.gguf'
0.01.043.114 W llama_model_loader: tensor overrides to CPU are used with mmap enabled - consider using --load-mode none for better performance
<no further output; process spins one thread indefinitely>
```
items.title: Eval bug: qwen4exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) livelocks during model load on HIP; identical config loads on Vulkan

items.body:
## Name and Version

llama.cpp 0.4.0, revs `18443257` and `96ffdc4`. My build pin/config: [pkgs/llama-cpp/default.nix](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/machines/blob/main/pkgs/llama-cpp/default.nix) (source rev + patches), and [shikanime-labs/machines#1357](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/machines/pull/1357) is the backend flip this issue motivated.

## Operating systems

Linux (NixOS 26.11.20260829.d2f6794).

## GGML backends

Vulkan (RADV) — fails as below. ROCm (HIP/rocblas), same rev, same GPU — qwen4exp passes (model loads and decodes: 8-token completion, ~19 tok/s, no asserts, no device loss). deepseek-v4 on ROCm: untested.

## Hardware

AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 128 GB unified LPDDR5X (UMA) (Minisforum MS-S1 MAX)

## Models

- qwen4exp: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF`, revision `UD-Q4_K_XL`
- deepseek-v4: `lmstudio-community/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF`, revision `MXFP4`

## Problem description & steps to reproduce

On AMD Strix Halo (Radeon 8060S iGPU, gfx1151, RADV), any decode of qwen4exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) or deepseek-v4 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) fails. The same build and GGUF of qwen4exp runs cleanly on the same GPU with the ROCm backend (deepseek-v4 not yet retried on ROCm).

Failure modes on Vulkan/RADV:

1. Full offload (`--n-gpu-layers 999`, both archs): weights load to 100%, then the first `llama_context::decode` aborts:

   ```
   /build/source/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:283: GGML_ASSERT(offset + size <= ggml_nbytes(tensor) && "tensor read out of bounds") failed
   ```

2. Partial offload (deepseek-v4, `--n-gpu-layers 48`): the assert is bypassed, weights load, and the first graph compute loses the device:

   ```
   terminate called after throwing an instance of 'vk::DeviceLostError'
     what():  vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost
   ```

   Worker process dies with SIGSEGV (exit 139). Backtrace: `vk_queue_handle_unsynchronized::submit` → `ggml_backend_graph_compute` → `rpc_server::graph_compute`.

Backtrace of the assert path (router child, verbatim frames): `ggml_abort` → `ggml_backend_tensor_get_async` (ggml-backend.cpp:283) → `llama_context::decode` → `llama_decode` → `common_init_from_params` → `server_context_impl::load_model`.

Reproduced identically: over RPC (Vulkan device held by a worker) and node-local; with and without `--no-warmup`; with and without `--fit off`; on two revs (above), the newer of which equals master at test time.

Older-arch models (qwen3.8-27b) run continuously on the same RADV device without incident, so the defect is specific to these new-arch graphs.

The Kubernetes manifests: [shikanime-labs/manifests/apps/llama-cpp](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/manifests/tree/main/apps/llama-cpp) and [shikanime-labs/manifests/apps/llama-cpp-rpc](https://github.com/shikanime-labs/manifests/tree/main/apps/llama-cpp)

Steps to reproduce:

```
llama-server -hf unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL --n-gpu-layers 999 -c 2048
# send any single completion; the ggml-backend.cpp:283 abort fires at first decode
```

DeviceLost variant: lmstudio-community DeepSeek-V4-Flash MXFP4 GGUF with `--n-gpu-layers 48`.

## First Bad Commit

Unknown. Both tested revs fail; the newer (`96ffdc4`) equals master HEAD at test time, so this reproduces on current master.

## Relevant log output

Assert path (full offload, first decode):

```
/build/source/ggml/src/ggml-backend.cpp:283: GGML_ASSERT(offset + size <= ggml_nbytes(tensor) && "tensor read out of bounds") failed
```

DeviceLost path (deepseek-v4, `--n-gpu-layers 48`, worker SIGSEGV exit 139):

```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'vk::DeviceLostError'
  what():  vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost
```

## Related but distinct (checked before filing)

- #27306: RADV/gfx1151 DeviceLost, but mid-prefill under draft-MTP draft decodes, process survives as a zombie. Mine: first decode, no speculative decoding, process dies.
- #27797: qwen4exp on gfx1151 outputs garbage (`//////`), no crash.
- #28497: QSA indexer top-k nondeterminism on CUDA, wrong results, no crash.
- Suspect area consistent with unmerged new-arch op work: deepseek-v4 CPU ops (#23122) and qwen4exp QSA decode reworks. At full offload the failure surfaces as a host-side tensor read OOB; at mixed placement it surfaces as a malformed submit that loses the device.

### Name and Version

```console
$ llama-mtmd-cli --version
version: 0.4.0-dev (build 10809, commit 5266f24da)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64
```

### Operating systems

Mac

### GGML backends

Metal

### Hardware

- MacBook Pro (Mac17,6)
- Apple M5 Max, 18 CPU cores
- 128 GB unified memory

### Models

`ggml-org/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B-Q8_0`

Files from `ggml-org/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B-GGUF`:

- `Qwen2.5-Omni-3B-Q8_0.gguf`
- `mmproj-Qwen2.5-Omni-3B-Q8_0.gguf`

Audio input: llama.cpp's `samples/jfk.wav` (16 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM, 11 seconds).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

This is a follow-up to #23986, but it does not appear to be the same deterministic im2col pipeline-selection bug.

Audio inference usually works when the machine is idle. While the machine is under load from a concurrently running Go test suite, an otherwise identical audio request can silently produce 2,048 tokens of incoherent text instead of a transcription. There is no API error, process crash, Metal command-buffer error, or backend error-state message. The graph completes and returns tokens at normal speed.

The failing run used llama.cpp b10809 through its shared libraries via Kronk/Yzma. The request was:

- Qwen2.5-Omni-3B Q8_0 plus its Q8_0 mmproj
- `samples/jfk.wav`
- prompt: `Transcribe the following audio and then summarize who said it and when.`
- temperature 0.7, top-p 0.9, top-k 40
- 2,048 maximum completion tokens
- Metal offload for the model and multimodal projector
- flash attention `auto`
- one sequence

The complete example is here:
https://github.com/ardanlabs/kronk/blob/08017fa4044718c8b394b95d271622f5647e8c68/examples/audio/main.go

A bad run starts with output resembling:

```text
AB in De Morgan: - Can it
The number·AB. The package. - ,dial AB, the Can the AB: ...
```

and continues with unrelated fragments, replacement characters, mixed scripts, and repeated `AB`-like tokens until `max_tokens` is reached:

```console
Input: 786  Reasoning: 0  Completion: 2048  Total: 2834  TPS: 64.71
```

Running the same example again immediately while idle produced a coherent result and stopped after 40 tokens:

```text
The original content of this audio is: 'and so my fellow americans ask not what your country can do for you ask what you can do for your country' by 'john f kennedy'.
```

### Steps to reproduce

The failure is intermittent and load-sensitive rather than reproducible on every invocation:

1. Install/run llama.cpp b10809 with Metal on Apple Silicon.
2. Load the model and mmproj listed above.
3. Start a concurrent workload (in my case, the Kronk Go test suite).
4. Repeatedly send the audio request described above through the shared-library API.
5. Compare each response with an idle run.

Expected: a coherent transcription/summary, or an explicit backend error if Metal cannot complete the work.

Actual: some loaded runs return a full-length gibberish completion with no reported compute error.

### Controls and observations

I performed the diagnostic checks suggested in #23986:

1. The entire bad log contains no `command buffer`, `failed with status`, or `backend is in error state` message. This appears to be the silent-wrong-results branch, not a dropped Metal command buffer.
2. The bad run compiled and loaded `kernel_im2col_f16`, not `kernel_im2col_ext_f16`. The pipeline selection from the #23986 fix therefore appears to be active.
3. A deterministic direct CLI run on the same files succeeds at idle:

```bash
llama-mtmd-cli \
  -m Qwen2.5-Omni-3B-Q8_0.gguf \
  --mmproj mmproj-Qwen2.5-Omni-3B-Q8_0.gguf \
  --audio samples/jfk.wav \
  -p "Transcribe the following audio and then summarize who said it and when." \
  --seed 1 --temp 0 --no-warmup -n 128
```

4. Eight copies of that fixed-seed CLI command run concurrently also produced the same coherent output, with no command-buffer errors. Those were separate processes; the observed bad run used the shared-library API. I have not yet captured a bad run with the direct CLI or with temperature 0.

This may therefore involve an in-process/shared-library execution path, a race exposed by external system load, or another difference between the API and CLI paths. I am not claiming that the old im2col mismatch returned.


### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>
<!-- Copy-pasted short logs go into the "console" area here -->

The full failing `audio.log` is attached. Relevant excerpts:

```console
ersion: 0.4.0-dev (build 10809, commit 5266f24da)
GPU name: Apple M5 Max
...
get_dummy_batch: warmup with audio size = 3000
reserve_compute_meta: MTL0 compute buffer size = 51.27 MiB
reserve_compute_meta: graph splits = 1, nodes = 990
warmup: flash attention is enabled
...
ggml_metal_library_compile_pipeline: compiling pipeline: base = 'kernel_im2col_f16', name = 'kernel_im2col_f16'
...
clip_encode: output embedding shape [2048, 750, 1]
...
[2,048 tokens of gibberish]
Input: 786  Reasoning: 0  Completion: 2048  Total: 2834  TPS: 64.71
```
</details>

<!-- Long logs that you upload as files go here, outside the "console" area -->

items.body:
Adds support for GLM-5-Next (released as GLM-5.3-Flash), a 321.3B hybrid linear/sparse-attention MoE, plus its vision tower.

## Running it

Two flags are currently required for correct output:

- `NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE=0`. `ggml-cuda/common.cuh` sets `CUBLAS_TF32_TENSOR_OP_MATH` unconditionally, so every fp32 GEMM otherwise runs at 10 mantissa bits. On a fixture this moved top-1 agreement from 0.896 to 0.9995.
- `-fa off`. `build_attn_mha` casts the F32 latent to F16 before `ggml_flash_attn_ext`, which is the one place MLA cannot afford it.

KV cache type is not a correctness requirement. f16 costs +0.0005 PPL at ctx 2048 and is 0.0018 lower at 4096, both within engine-to-engine noise.

## Performance

1x B200, GLM-5.3-Flash UD-IQ1_S, `llama-bench -ngl 999 --flash-attn on -ctk f16 -ctv f16 -lm none -p 512 -n 32 -r 3`. Before is f30bed887, after is 00699716c.

| test | before t/s | after t/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| pp512 | 1121.80 | 1118.93 |
| tg32 | 62.79 | 63.10 |
| tg32 @ d4096 | 53.52 | 59.50 |
| tg32 @ d16384 | 41.02 | 57.99 |
| tg32 @ d65536 | 20.66 | 48.99 |

Perplexity over one chunk is unchanged at 3.3612 +/- 0.40158.

### MTP / NextN speculative decoding

`--spec-type draft-mtp`. `llama-cli -c 32768 --temp 0 --seed 0 -n 256`:

| prompt | MTP off | n=2 | n=3 | n=5 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| short | 58.6 | 86.5 | 80.2 | 63.7 |
| 16K | 55.0 | | 77.2 | |

## AI Usage
Used Claude and Local Models for testing, iteration and code design - manual verification of model / PR usage

items.body:
## Summary

Loading a DFlash2 draft model (`--model-draft`) on the SYCL backend against dual Intel Arc Pro B70 GPUs causes a GPU driver TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery) event — Windows force-resets the GPU driver — rather than a normal crash or clean load. The process disappears with no application-level error logged; the only trace is a `LiveKernelEvent` (Bug Check `0x141` = `VIDEO_TDR_TIMEOUT_DETECTED`) in the Windows Application event log, occurring on both GPUs across repeated attempts. GPU driver status recovers to `OK` afterward, but the server never comes up.

## Environment

- Build: `b10883` (commit `91f6a6cf3`), official Windows SYCL x64 binary, `version: 0.4.0-dev (build 10883, commit 91f6a6cf3)`
- Hardware: 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 (32GB each)
- OS: Windows (native), Level-Zero runtime, driver `32.0.101.8805`
- Target: Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q6_K_XL GGUF (unsloth)
- Draft: Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 Q8_0 GGUF (z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-GGUF)
- `--spec-type` not passed; auto-detected as `draft-dflash` from draft model metadata (confirmed in logs before the hang)

## Repro

```
set UR_L0_ENABLE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1
set ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=1
set GGML_SYCL_ENABLE_VMM=0

llama-server.exe ^
  -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q6_K_XL.gguf ^
  --model-draft Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q8_0.gguf ^
  -ngl 99 -np 1 -c 131072 -t 8 ^
  --load-mode dio -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 ^
  -b 2048 -ub 2048 -fa on --jinja --reasoning off ^
  --metrics --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9019
```

No `--split-mode` flag is passed (default layer/pipeline split across the two GPUs) — this is not the tensor-parallel-specific issue reported separately for the CUDA backend (see linked issue).

## Observed

Console output reaches this point and then the process silently disappears (varies run-to-run exactly how far it gets before vanishing — sometimes right after tensor-warning lines, sometimes after the speculative implementation is registered):

```
I spec common_specu: auto-detected speculative type 'draft-dflash' from the draft model metadata
I srv    load_model: loading model '...Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q6_K_XL.gguf'
E llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: dflash requires ctx_other to be set (this warning is normal during memory fitting)
W operator(): failed to measure the memory of the extra model, fitting without it: failed to create llama_context from model
... (unused-tensor warnings for blk.64.* — expected, same as non-crashing loads)
I cmn          init: llama threadpool init, n_threads = 8
I common_speculative_init_result: loading draft model '...Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-Q8_0.gguf'
I srv    load_model: initializing, n_slots = 1, n_ctx_slot = 131072, kv_unified = 'false'
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: adding speculative implementation 'draft-dflash'
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - n_max=3, n_min=0, p_min=0.00
I common_speculative_impl_draft_dflash: - block_size=8, mask_token_id=248070, n_extract=5, sample_from_anchor=true
```
— then nothing. No further stdout/stderr, no application-error event (Event ID 1000), process no longer present in `tasklist`.

Windows Application event log (via `Get-WinEvent`), timestamped to match the hang, on every attempt (reproduced 3x with different process-launch methods — direct WSL exec, detached WSL background, and native PowerShell `Start-Process` — ruling out a launcher artifact):

```
Provider: Windows Error Reporting
Event ID: 1001
Event Name: LiveKernelEvent
Problem signature: P1: 141   (Bug Check 0x141 = VIDEO_TDR_TIMEOUT_DETECTED)
```

Multiple such events fired per attempt (both GPU device contexts affected, based on distinct P3 addresses corresponding to the two cards). `Get-WmiObject Win32_VideoController` reports `Status: OK` on both GPUs after each hang — the driver recovers, but the model never loads.

For comparison, the same target model with native MTP drafting (`--spec-type draft-mtp`) loads and serves normally on this exact hardware/build family (production config, no TDR events).

## Expected

DFlash2 should load and serve without hanging the GPU driver, matching the behavior of native MTP speculative decoding on the same hardware.

## Notes

- Not reproducible as a normal segfault/exception — no Application Error (Event ID 1000) is ever logged, only the driver-level TDR event, suggesting whatever DFlash2-specific kernel/operation is dispatched here enters a state the Level-Zero/SYCL driver cannot recover from within the timeout, rather than crashing outright.
- Happy to test a patched build or provide `sycl-ls` output / additional driver diagnostics if useful.

### Name and Version

```
$ ./llama-cli --version
version: 0.1.0-dev (build 599, commit ad1de39)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Also observed on `4f31eed` and `6b4344e` (llama-server and llama-cli).

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

AMD Radeon 890M iGPU (gfx1150, RADV 26.1.2, Mesa), Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 32 GB LPDDR5 unified with 16 GiB firmware VRAM carve-out + 32 GiB GTT aperture. Debian 13, kernel 7.1.3. Kernel params include `ttm.pages_limit=8388608`.

### Models

`Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf` + `mmproj-Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-F16.gguf` (also crashed with GLM-OCR Q8 + mmproj; the specific model does not appear to matter - the crash happens at projector load).

### Command line

```bash
./llama-cli -m Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --mmproj mmproj-Qwen3VL-4B-Instruct-F16.gguf \
  --image ui.png -p "What is the dialog title?" \
  -ngl 999 -fa on --temp 0.1 -no-cnv -n 30
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

On this iGPU class, loading ANY mmproj-bearing model balloons GPU-side (GTT/TTM) allocations until the kernel's global OOM killer fires - **at projector load time, before any image is processed**. The process is killed within seconds; with other services resident, the OOM kill cascades (we observed two full-host watchdog resets before isolating it).

Clean single-process repro (no other GPU consumers; process wrapped with `choom -n 1000` so the OOM killer prefers it):

VmSize timeline from `/proc/<pid>/status` sampling:

```
0s VmSize=18184kB    VmRSS=7420kB
2s VmSize=4119524kB  VmRSS=150708kB
4s VmSize=32033928kB VmRSS=28652kB
```

Kernel (verbatim):

```
oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE,nodemask=(null),cpuset=...,global_oom,task_memcg=/system.slice/uit2-repro.scope,task=llama-cli,pid=77433,uid=0
Out of memory: Killed process 77433 (llama-cli) total-vm:33279112kB, anon-rss:4kB, file-rss:52kB, shmem-rss:0kB, UID:0 pgtables:1436kB oom_score_adj:1000
```

Note `total-vm: 33.2 GB` vs `anon-rss: 4 kB` - the memory is almost entirely driver-side, invisible to memory cgroups. We confirmed a `systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=6G` wrapper does **not** contain it (the OOM still fires as `CONSTRAINT_NONE` global; TTM/GTT kernel pages bypass the cgroup). With slower leak progression (CPU projector via `--no-mmproj-offload`) the driver log fills with repeated:

```
radv/amdgpu: Failed to allocate a buffer:
    size      : 1073741824 bytes
    alignment : 262144 bytes
    domains   : 4
```

(1 GiB GTT allocation attempts, `domains: 4`.)

For contrast: the identical artifacts + fixtures run cleanly on a discrete RTX 3090 (Vulkan not involved; CUDA) - this appears iGPU/GTT-specific.

Related prior art: #24626 (absolute per-device memory budget for `--fit` on UMA), #26447 (iGPU Vulkan device-lost at large contexts).

### Suggested fix / ask

Bound or chunk vision-context allocations on UMA/iGPU devices (or document a safe configuration for this class). As-is, every mmproj model is a potential host-crasher on Radeon iGPU systems.

---

*Disclosure: this report was assembled with AI assistance from measurements captured directly on the affected host (VmSize sampling script, kernel journal, RADV logs quoted verbatim above). All data points are from real runs, not generated.*

items.body:
## Overview

Fixes a regression after #24233, which restored HIP integrated GPU detection. On my AMD APU, this also made the ROCm host-buffer path available for HIP integrated GPUs. With that path enabled, prompt input appears corrupted: chat templates and system prompts can be ignored, and generated output becomes garbage.

This change keeps integrated GPU detection/reporting intact, but disables direct ROCm_Host compute on HIP integrated GPUs. The fix does not disable host-buffer exposure entirely, pinned buffers remain available to preserve functionality, while only the problematic direct compute path is blocked.

## Additional information

Tested locally on gfx1151 / RDNA3.5 APU with ROCm 7.14. The corrupted input/output issue is fixed with this patch.
The issue appeared in external harnesses like Pi and OpenCode. It can also be reproduced in the built-in web UI with a sufficiently large combined first input. For example, gemma-4-26B-A4B with 4676 tokens of context or more outputs `<unused49>` indefinitely. Other models can be way more resilient and their output starts by saying 'Based on the text provided, which appears to be a corrupted or "hallucinated" version of a Wikipedia article'.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - I used AI assistance to review and patch the relevant code. I tested and reviewed the final change myself.
