items.body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 9960 (a935fbffe)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000099 for Darwin arm64
```

Homebrew build, Metal backend.

### Operating systems

Mac (macOS 26.5.1, build 25F80), Apple M5, 24 GB unified memory.

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Ornith-1.0-35B-UD-Q3_K_M.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 262144 -np 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa auto --port 8080
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When a Metal allocation fails during init, the server logs the failure, logs that the
backend is unrecoverable, and then finishes starting up anyway. It prints `model loaded`,
binds the port, and answers `/health` with `{"status":"ok"}`. Every completion request
after that returns HTTP 500.

The per-request errors are reported correctly, so this isn't silent corruption. The
problem is that startup completes and `/health` reports ready for a process that can
never serve a request. Anything using `/health` as a readiness probe treats it as up.

I should say up front that `-ngl 99` disabled the auto-fit that would otherwise have
prevented this:

```
W common_fit_params: failed to fit params to free device memory: n_gpu_layers already set by user to 99, abort
```

So the OOM itself is arguably my own fault. The part I think is still a bug is what
happens afterwards — the backend reports itself unrecoverable and the server starts
anyway.

Steps:

1. Pick a context size where the allocation cannot fit. On a 24 GB M5 the Metal device
   reports 18186 MiB, and this model at `-c 262144` needs 19005 MiB. llama.cpp's own
   memory breakdown says so directly:
   ```
   cmn  common_param:   - MTL0    : Apple M5 (18186 MiB, 18185 MiB free)
   load_tensors:  MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 15897.19 MiB
   llama_kv_cache:       MTL0 KV buffer size =  2720.00 MiB
   common_memory_breakdown_print: |   - MTL0 (Apple M5)    | 18186 = ... + (19005 = 15897 +    2782 +     325) +         398 |
   ```
   At `-c 65536` the KV cache drops to ~680 MiB and it fits.
2. Start the server with the command line above.
3. 15 `Insufficient Memory` errors during init, then the backend declares itself
   unrecoverable and the decode fails.
4. Server prints `model loaded` and `listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080`.
5. `/health` → 200 `{"status":"ok"}`.
6. Any completion request → 500, and the OOM count roughly doubles.
7. Re-run at `-c 65536` and the same model starts and serves normally.

### What I'd expect

Exit non-zero at startup, the way other unrecoverable init failures already do — a
quantized V cache without flash attention returns `nullptr` and the server refuses to
start (b9960 `src/llama-context.cpp:3518`; on master the same check is at `:3602`,
reworded to `quantized V cache requires flash_attn to be enabled`).

Failing that, `/health` should reflect it. It currently returns `{"status":"ok"}`
unconditionally once the model is marked loaded (b9960
`tools/server/server-context.cpp:4322`, master `:4448`); the only gate is the
server-state middleware, which fires solely on `!is_ready`.

### Relevant log output

Init (timestamps and log-level prefixes trimmed):

```
ggml_metal_synchronize: error: command buffer 0 failed with status 5
error: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
   ... 15 occurrences ...
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
graph_compute: ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async failed with error -1
process_ubatch: failed to compute graph, compute status: -1
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
cmn  common_conte: llama_decode() failed: -3
srv  llama_server: model loaded
srv  llama_server: listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080
```

One completion request afterwards:

```
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
srv        decode: Compute error. off = 0, n_batch = 2048, ret = -3
srv    send_error: task id = 0, error: Compute error.
srv  update_slots: decode() failed: Compute error.
```

Observed from the client:

```
$ curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' localhost:8080/health
{"status":"ok"}
200

$ curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' localhost:8080/completion \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"prompt":"int add(int a,int b){","n_predict":20,"temperature":0}'
{"error":{"code":500,"message":"Compute error.","type":"server_error"}}
500
```

`Insufficient Memory` count: 15 after init, 28 after one request, 29 including shutdown.

### Notes

Reproduced on b9960 (`a935fbffe`). I haven't run master, but both relevant paths look
unchanged there: the init probe still treats a failed `llama_decode` as non-fatal and
continues (master `common/common.cpp:1576`, b9960 `:1497`), and `/health` is still
unconditional. Worth confirming against master before acting on it.

One model, one machine, Metal only. Speculative decoding was not involved
(`speculative decoding not supported by this context` appears in the log).

items.body:
## Overview

Implements adaptive mtp with a new option `--spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive`

Suggested configuration to use is: `--spec-type draft-mtp-adaptive --spec-draft-n-max 12`

**Note:** It is not recommended to set `spec-draft-n-max` to values lower than 7 with the Adaptive MTP algorithm.  In this instance the algorithm isn't able to reach depths high enough to provide the benefits it aims to achieve.  If you find yourself in a situation where insufficient VRAM prevents you from setting a depth of at least 7, or more preferably 8+, then it's generally going to be best to just stick with regular MTP.

The algorithm is a counting based state machine with a climb counter and a weighted drop-pressure accumulator. The depth climbs one step after a number consecutive verifies that accepted every drafted token; any miss adds (N - acceptance) to the drop pressure and the depth drops one step once it exceeds a certain amount. High depths fall quickly (a total miss adds N), low depths hold, and at the floor no pressure accumulates at all.  The specific climb difficulty and drop pressure values were empirically determined over a wide range of tests.

`--spec-draft-n-max` bounds the upper adaptive range and both the floor and the cold-start depth default to 3.  The default floor of 3 may be adjusted  with `--spec-draft-n-min-adaptive`, although in testing 3 seems to be the best value to choose here.

## Overview of the climb-cost algorithm

It was experimentally determined that a draft MTP depth of 2 or 3 is close to optimal for reasoning and prose. 
More typically an MTP depth of 3 was found to be optimal, and so this was chosen as the baseline default.

When the depth is less than three the algorithm allows for an easy transition from a depth of 1 to 2.
A slightly higher cost from 2 to 3 is used to minimise the depth oscillating between two and three.

To climb past a depth of three requires passing a hardened barrier.  The hardened barrier is in place to
minimise easily reaching a depth of four which is known to be harmful to performance for reasoning and prose.

Beyond a depth of four the barrier to climb higher is gradually reduced.
This allows for predictive runs to quickly ascend as the admission rates indicate that this is useful. 


## Latest Testing and Performance Results
_(Updated 23 Aug 2026)_

Latest performance results can be seen here: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27210#issuecomment-5385811671

Extended discussion of results can be seen here: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27210#issuecomment-5386016928

### Test Setup

- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 (`Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0.gguf`
- Hardware: 2x AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (32.6 GiB each), tensor split, Ryzen 9
  9950X3D2, ROCm, `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,2`, `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=0`
- Server: `llama-server` from branch `adaptive-mtp` (build 10459, 0c6426bcd,
  freshly rebuilt)
- Decode: greedy (temp 0.0, seed 675), top-k 20, top-p 0.95, min-p 0.001,
  ctx 262144, f16 KV, `--parallel 1`, mlock, reasoning on
  (`--reasoning-budget 65536 --reasoning-preserve`)
- 2 repeats per cell; tok/s = mean of `timings.predicted_per_second`
  (generation only, >= 4000 tokens per request)

 
### Configurations Tested

| ID | spec type | args |
|----|-----------|------|
| C0 | none | - |
| C1 | draft-mtp, fixed 3 | `--spec-draft-n-max 3` |
| C2 | draft-mtp, fixed 12, p-min | `--spec-draft-n-max 12 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75` |
| C3 | draft-mtp-adaptive 3..12 | `--spec-draft-n-min-adaptive 3 --spec-draft-n-max 12` |
| C4 | adaptive 3..12 + p-min | C3 + `--spec-draft-p-min 0.75` |
| C5 | ngram-mod | `--spec-ngram-mod-n-match 24 --spec-ngram-mod-n-min 48 --spec-ngram-mod-n-max 64` |
| C6 | adaptive + ngram-mod | C3 args + C5 args |
| C7 | fixed 3 + ngram-mod | C1 args + C5 args |
| C8 | fixed 12 + p-min + ngram-mod | C2 args + C5 args |

### Results

| config | reasoning | prose | code | recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C0 baseline | 30.03 | 30.08 | 30.03 | 29.93 |
| C1 fixed 3 | **51.68** | 55.89 | 69.28 | 81.94 |
| C2 fixed 12 + p-min 0.75 | 38.59 | 43.46 | 71.46 | 151.25 |
| C3 adaptive 3..12 | 51.42 | **56.64** | **78.03** | 147.46 |
| C4 adaptive + p-min 0.75 | 40.67 | 43.35 | 70.92 | 147.43 |
| C5 ngram-mod | 30.03 | 30.10 | 29.98 | 292.88 |
| C6 adaptive + ngram-mod | 51.48 | 56.61 | 73.06 | 321.25 |
| C7 fixed 3 + ngram-mod | 51.65 | 55.90 | 68.36 | 324.10 |
| C8 fixed 12 + p-min + ngram-mod | 41.34 | 43.73 | 64.39 | **325.68** |


## Additional information

The total diff size is +519/-35

This PR touches on 15 files which seems large at first, but this mostly arises from integrating the new command line options.  The bulk of the functional changes take place within speculative.cpp  After the recent code-review (Ref: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27210#issuecomment-5582088497 ), I rewrote the MTP vs Adaptive MTP invocations to keep the original MTP behaviour exactly the same as before, even if the code-path to get there has now changed.  I also believe that I successfully argued for why the GDN changes should remain: Ref: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27210#issuecomment-5590348680

218 lines are for the unit test file.  92 lines are for the header file that contains the algorithm itself.

The rest of the line changes are the wiring of the algorithm into the llama.cpp code base, and the command line option handling.

I tried to keep the size of the functional changes to llama.cpp itself as small as possible, and I tried to keep this diff as independent as I could so that unless it's specifically activated, it won't interfere with normal llama.cpp operations.

## "Horses for Courses"

While Adaptive MTP generally works well for most hardware and models, it can make performance worse on older hardware that cannot run the deep drafting and acceptance steps fast enough to realise the potential gains it offers.  In these instances it is generally better to not enable Adaptive MTP and just stick with regular MTP wi

### Name and Version

### Description

I'm observing a reproducible VRAM memory leak when running DeepSeek V4 Flash GGUF with DSpark speculative decoding enabled. After each PP+TG (prefill + generate) cycle, VRAM usage increases by approximately **10 MB**, and this accumulation continues until the process eventually runs out of memory (OOM).

This issue does **not** occur with:
- Step 3.7 + DSpark
- Qwen3.8-27B + DSpark

Both of the above maintain stable VRAM usage across multiple cycles.

### Environment
- Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731 version) GGUF + DSpark
- Framework: llama.cpp
- Issue: VRAM leak, ~10 MB per PP+TG cycle

### Suspected Root Cause

I suspect this is a **Draft KV Cache leak** specific to the DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 model when used with DSpark. Specifically:

1. **KV cache positions** are written during every draft step but are **never compacted or properly reclaimed**, leading to continuous VRAM growth[reference:0]. A similar issue has been reported in related forks where "positions are written every tree step but never compacted," causing OOM under sustained traffic[reference:1].

2. **DSpark draft KV-cache group poisoning**: The DSpark draft model's KV cache is flagged as an "eagle group" (same as EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP/DFlash)[reference:2]. The multi-group cache-hit lookup requires **every** KV-cache group to report a nonzero hit for cache reuse to succeed — any single group reporting zero short-circuits the entire request's lookup[reference:3].

3. **Sparse and discontinuous draft KV**: DSpark's draft-layer KV is recomputed from the target model's real hidden state every decode step, meaning it has **no cross-request reuse value**[reference:4]. Its stored blocks are sparse and discontinuous (e.g., `[MISS, MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]`)[reference:5], never satisfying the consecutive-hit window required for cache lookup[reference:6].

4. **"One-vote veto" effect**: This permanently poisons the AND-combination lookup for the entire request[reference:7], even though the model's real KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) independently have a working hit rate around 89%[reference:8]. As a result, the prefix caching mechanism is effectively disabled — every new request cannot reuse historical caches and must recompute and write new KV cache entries, causing VRAM to grow until exhaustion.

A similar fix has been proposed in vLLM where DSpark draft KV-cache groups are excluded from the cache-hit lookup poisoning mechanism[reference:9]. The same root cause likely applies to llama.cpp.

### Why Step 3.7 and Qwen3.8-27B Are Not Affected

These models likely have different DSpark implementations or KV cache structures that do **not** trigger this cache lookup conflict, allowing normal cache reuse and stable VRAM usage.

### Suggested Fix Direction

- Exclude DSpark draft KV-cache groups from the prefix caching lookup's "all-groups-must-hit" requirement, similar to the approach taken in vLLM PR #47891[reference:10].
- Alternatively, ensure DSpark draft KV cache positions are properly compacted or reclaimed after each generation cycle, as addressed in PR #23461 for draft/MTP resources.

### Additional Context

There have been related reports of DeepSeek V4 KV cache not being reclaimed on slot release, and DSpark-specific KV cache issues with offloading connectors[reference:13]. This may share a root cause with the hybrid-attention KV handling.

Please let me know if additional logs or reproduction steps would be helpful.

Thanks!

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

### Hardware

Dual E5 v2667v3+ 256GB DDR4 RAM + 4X A100  PG199 32G GPU

### Models

unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF
UD-IQ3_XXS
104 GB
Dspark gguf：
[dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF/blob/main/dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf)


### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### Description

I am experiencing a reproducible VRAM memory leak when running the **DeepSeek V4 Flash** GGUF model (quantization: `UD-IQ3_XXS`, 104 GB) together with the **DSpark** draft model (`dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf`) on llama.cpp.

After each PP+TG (prefill + generate) cycle, VRAM usage increases by approximately **10 MB**, and this accumulation continues until the process eventually runs out of memory (OOM) – typically after a few hundred requests.

items.body:
Summary

When llama-server --embeddings runs a pooled embedding model on the Metal backend, the graph still contains MUL_MAT result_output (the LM head). Its output is never read — result_embd_pooled is a GET_ROWS from result_norm — but it is fully materialized on every request.

For Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (vocab 151669) at 7343 tokens that discarded tensor is f32 [151669, 7343] = 4,454,821,868 bytes (4.15 GiB), and it grows linearly with input length. Past some input size the Metal backend then produces out-of-bounds behavior and the server returns all-NaN vectors. Gating the LM head behind an embeddings + pooling check eliminates the failure and drops the MTL0 compute buffer by roughly 10×.

Symptom

Embeddings come back as all-NaN. nlohmann/json serializes NaN as null, so a client sees a vector of null rather than an error.

  • /health continues returning 200
  • no Metal error is logged
  • no recovery short of restarting the process
  • -ngl 0 (CPU) is completely clean

The onset depends on how far past the threshold the input is:

  • Near the threshold (~7343 tokens at vocab 151669): the triggering request itself returns a valid vector, and every request after it — including a 4-token input — returns all-NaN for the lifetime of the process. This is consistent with the overrun landing in a mapped neighbor allocation rather than in the triggering request's own output.
  • Well past it (28,001 tokens): the triggering request is already all-NaN itself.

Worth stating explicitly because the near-threshold case is the dangerous one — the request that breaks the server looks successful, so a pipeline that validates only the newest response never sees a failure.

Environment

Reproduced on unmodified upstream master:

  • build 1 (192067b), AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101, Darwin arm64, shallow clone of ggml-org/llama.cpp, -DGGML_METAL=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
  • Apple M5 Max, 128 GB unified memory (110100 MiB visible to Metal), macOS
  • llama-server --embeddings, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B f16, -c 32768 -np 1 -b 8192 -ub 8192 -ngl 99

Originally found on two independent forks; the pristine build above was made specifically to rule out fork-local Metal changes, and reproduces identically.

Reproduction

bash
llama-server -m Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-f16.gguf --embeddings \
  -ngl 99 -c 32768 -b 8192 -ub 8192 -np 1 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8084

python3 -c "print('가나다라마바사한글테스트문장입니다'*2000, end='')" > /tmp/long.txt

curl -s localhost:8084/v1/embeddings -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.dumps({'input':open('/tmp/long.txt').read(),'model':'emb'}))")" \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);v=d['data'][0]['embedding'];print('prompt_tokens',d['usage']['prompt_tokens'],'nan',sum(1 for x in v if x is None or x!=x),'/',len(v))"

curl -s localhost:8084/v1/embeddings -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello","model":"emb"}'

items.body:
### Name and Version

I tested `llama-server`, build 10622 (`e3428e434`), MSVC 19.44.35227.0, Windows AMD64.

**I used a locally modified build, not an unmodified upstream reproducer.** Its runtime base is upstream [`c1d0e7a004015f23bc0233470b747b596f29b264`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/commit/c1d0e7a004015f23bc0233470b747b596f29b264). My local HEAD adds documentation; additional uncommitted changes implement native P2P all-reduce selection, validation and event handling, a Volta Flash Attention configuration adjustment, TOPK_MOE fusion-matcher bounds checks, and MTP context synchronization. I also used modified tests. My later diagnostic builds add graph tracing and an experimental wait before reusing an all-reduce event slot.

My local changes may be responsible for the failure. I have not identified a first bad upstream commit or confirmed a fix. I investigated this with help from **GPT-6 Astra**, including local code changes, instrumentation, tests, and log/source analysis. please note that i'm a dumbass and im just sharing my personal experience with it.

### Operating systems / GGML backends

I used Windows / CUDA with a Release build, CUDA toolkit 12.4.99, NVIDIA driver 581.80, and CUDA architectures 70 and 86. My build has `GGML_CUDA=ON`, `GGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=ON`, `GGML_CUDA_FA=ON`, `GGML_CUDA_NCCL=OFF`, and both `GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ` and `GGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS` build options OFF.

### Hardware

- 2 x Tesla V100-SXM2-16GB in TCC mode, with six active NVLink links per GPU before testing.
- RTX 3060 12GB in WDDM mode for the display, excluded from the main model's CUDA visibility in these tests.
- Ryzen 9 5900X, 64GB system RAM.

### Model

I used `Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf`; GGUF name `Qwen3.8-27B`, architecture `qwen35`.

Size: 17,559,178,144 bytes. SHA-256: `3F227079003ADD2511437E5B1E94812E363385225BF6A9B47B0054A72BC8B01E`.

I have not verified the exact public download URL. I ran the controlled tests below with **MTP disabled and no mmproj loaded**. My usual production setup includes a projector on the separate GPU, but I reproduced these failures without it.

### Test settings

I used these settings for **all seven controlled cases** in the results table:

| Setting | Value used |
| --- | --- |
| Batch size | **512** (`--batch-size 512`) |
| Ubatch / microbatch size | **512** (`--ubatch-size 512`) |
| Configured context | 262,144 tokens (`--ctx-size 262144`) |
| Actual test prompt | 4,096 fresh tokens; 0 cached tokens |
| Requested output | 1 token (`n_predict=1`) |
| Split mode | Tensor (`--split-mode tensor`) |
| Tensor split | `1,1` across the two V100s |
| Main model devices | `CUDA0,CUDA1`; all model layers offloaded |
| K cache / V cache | `q8_0` / `q8_0` |
| Flash Attention | On |
| Parallel slots | 1 |
| MTP / speculative decoding | Off |
| mmproj / image projector | Not loaded |
| Fit / startup warmup | Off / off |
| RAM prompt cache setting | 30,720 MiB (`--cache-ram 30720`) |
| Server lifecycle | Fresh server and empty prompt cache for each case |

I varied the all-reduce path, CUDA graphs setting, logging level, and diagnostic build as shown in the results table. In particular, **batch and ubatch stayed at 512/512 in both the failing graph-enabled tests and the passing graph-disabled controls**. These exact values apply to the controlled tests; I do not have confirmed batch/ubatch values for the separate historical 64K observations.

### Problem description

When I enabled CUDA graphs with tensor split and my custom direct P2P all-reduce path, prompt processing stalled and Windows logged fatal NVLink events. My display sometimes froze; in one incident I could still move the mouse. I could still run CPU commands and receive server SSE pings after some faults, so these were not all complete OS freezes. I could not reliably finish cleanup of the test server and telemetry processes, and I had to restart the PC after the failed runs.

I tested **four different failing diagnostic variants, not four identical repetitions**. For each case I started a fresh server with an empty prompt cache and submitted the same 4,096 integer-token prompt, requesting one output token.

| Case | Build / diagnostic change | All-reduce | CUDA graphs setting | Last saved prompt progress | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | Original local candidate, verbosity 4 | Custom P2P | On | 2,048 / 4,096 (50%) | Fatal NVLink events; no completed response |
| F2 | Same candidate, verbosity 5 | Custom P2P | On | 2,048 / 4,096 (50%) | Fatal NVLink events; no completed response |
| F3 | Added tagged graph tracing | Custom P2P | On | 2,048 / 4,096 (50%) | Fatal NVLink events; no completed response |
| F4 | Tracing plus wait for both old result events before slot reuse | Custom P2P | On | 1,536 / 4,096 (37.5%) | Fatal NVLink events; no completed response |
| C1 | Original local candidate | Native host path | On in configuration | 4,096 / 4,096 (100%) | One output token; no adverse driver events in the case window |
| C2 | Original local candidate | Custom P2P | Off | 4,096 / 4,096 (100%) | One output token; no adverse driver events in the case window |
| C3 | Tagged graph tracing | Custom P2P | Off | 4,096 / 4,096 (100%) | One output token; no adverse driver events in the case window |

For C1 I still used **tensor split**, not layer split. I set `GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE=host`, with `requested=host actual=host fallback=none` logged. I enabled graphs in the configuration, but the log did not independently tag actual captures. I have not established long-context or production stability with these short controls.

I recorded the last reported server progress, which does not identify the exact GPU failure instruction or prove GPU work completed. I configured a 262,144-token context, but the controlled input used only 4,096 tokens (1.5625% of that capacity). I have not established a universal midpoint threshold. Separately, I observed first-request local-server failures with roughly 64K pro

### Name and Version

Bionic bundled llama.cpp Vulkan 2.41.0 (crash) / 2.39.0 (ok); llama-server reports version 0.4.1-dev build 1 commit b49650a

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

2x Intel Arc Pro B50 (driver 32.0.101.8805) + Intel Core Ultra 5 235HX, 64GB RAM

### Models

All of these fail identically on 2.40/2.41 Vulkan, all load fine on 2.39 Vulkan:
- bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- unsloth/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512-GGUF (Q5_K_M)
- empero-ai/Qwen3.8-35B-A3B-Distill-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
Counter-case: nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (Q4_K_M) loads fine on 2.41 Vulkan.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## What happened

`llama-server` with the Vulkan backend crash-aborts while loading sliding-window-attention
decoder models when the KV cache is offloaded to the GPU. The process dies with
`exitCode=3221226505` (`0xC0000409`, fail-fast) before becoming healthy.

Exact abort line (stderr):

```text
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)
```

## Regression info

- ✅ `llama.cpp ... 2.39.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **loads in ~5s, serves fine**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.40.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.41.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with `--no-kv-offload` — **loads and serves** (KV cache on CPU)
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with full offload + embedding model (`nomic-embed-text-v1.5.Q4_K_M`,
  full attention, `--embedding`) — **loads and serves**

So it is not a globally broken Vulkan backend: it is the
`Vulkan + KV-cache GPU offload + SWA/hybrid-attention decoder` path that regressed
between 2.39 and 2.40.

## Repro

```bat
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf -ngl 99 --port 18081
```

- Model: `bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF`, `Q4_K_S` (~2.4 GB)
- No other flags (all defaults). Crash happens during `load_model`, before listening.

Notable log lines on the crashing 2.41 run (before the abort):

```text
W resolve_fused_ops: layer 0 is assigned to device Vulkan1 but Flash Attention is assigned to device CPU (usually due to missing support)
W resolve_fused_ops: Flash Attention not supported, set to disabled
W ggml_vulkan: Failed to allocate pinned memory (Requested buffer size exceeds device buffer size limit: ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory)
```

On the working `--no-kv-offload` run the server reports `kv_unified = 'true'`,
`n_slots = 4`, then `model loaded` / `listening`.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 x64 (build 10.0.26200)
- GPU: Intel Arc Pro B50 (discrete) + Intel integrated Graphics
- Driver: Intel `32.0.101.8805` (06.07.2026), `vulkan-1.dll` present (system + app dir)
- Builds: LM Studio / Bionic bundled `llama.cpp-win-x86_64-vulkan-avx2` packs
  `2.39.0` (working) vs `2.40.0` / `2.41.0` (crashing), CPU 14 threads
- The same setup serves the models fine on engine 2.39, so driver / loader / model
  file are ruled out

## Suspected area

New fused-ops / unified-KV graph building for SWA models (`cache_k` pre-allocation
landing in a Vulkan buffer that reports no supported op) introduced between 2.39
and 2.40. Happy to test any debug build / extra logging on this machine
(Arc Pro B50 available).

### First Bad Commit

Regressed between bundled builds 2.39.0 (works) and 2.40.0 (broken). Exact upstream commit unknown — these are third-party Bionic/LM Studio bundles, not direct llama.cpp builds. Happy to bisect if given build instructions for Windows Vulkan.

### Relevant log output


Command:
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf --port 18081 -ngl 99

Log:
load_model: loading model '.../mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf'
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)

Process exits immediately with code 3221226505 (0xC0000409).

items.body:
### Name and Version

llama.cpp build b10194, prebuilt macOS arm64 release binary
Model: ggml-org/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF (Q4_K_M), mmproj Q8_0
macOS on Apple Silicon, Metal

### Operating systems

Mac

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

Other (Please specify in the next section)

### Command line

```shell
llama-mtmd-cli \
  -m Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  -mm mmproj-Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q8_0.gguf \
  --audio clip.wav \
  -p "Transcribe this clip." \
  -n 4 --no-warmup
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Feeding one audio clip to a Voxtral model through `llama-mtmd-cli` runs the audio encoder twice on the same clip. For a single audio input mtmd builds two audio chunks instead of one, so the projector encodes and decodes the clip two times. This roughly doubles the audio encode latency and the number of audio tokens that land in the context.

I first hit this through `llama-cpp-python` and assumed it was a binding bug, but it reproduces with the plain upstream CLI and no Python involved, so I'm reporting it here.

## Steps to reproduce

Any short clip works. I used a 2 second 220 Hz sine tone, but a real speech clip behaves the same.

```
llama-mtmd-cli \
  -m Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  -mm mmproj-Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q8_0.gguf \
  --audio clip.wav \
  -p "Transcribe this clip." \
  -n 4 --no-warmup
```


### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```
0.01.623.953 I mtmd_cli_context: chat template example:
[SYSTEM_PROMPT] You are a helpful assistant[/SYSTEM_PROMPT][INST] Hello[/INST] Hi there</s>[INST] How are you?[/INST]
0.02.211.444 W init_audio: audio input is in experimental stage and may have reduced quality:
    https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/13759
0.02.211.482 I main: loading model: /Users/71293/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--ggml-org--Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF/snapshots/20616573013f28229fff61de74359d3eeff61f6a/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf
0.02.212.065 W WARN: This is an experimental CLI for testing multimodal capability.
0.02.212.066 W       For normal use cases, please use the standard llama-cli
0.02.236.747 I encoding mtmd batch, n_chunks = 1 (done = 1, total = 4)
0.02.623.918 I mtmd batch encoding done in 387 ms
0.02.625.918 I encoding mtmd batch, n_chunks = 1 (done = 2, total = 4)
0.03.093.533 I mtmd batch encoding done in 468 ms
```

`total = 4` for a prompt with one audio input. The chunking comes out as text, audio, audio, text: two text chunks plus the same clip encoded as two separate audio chunks. The two ~400 ms passes are the audio encodes (text chunks encode in about 0 ms).

The count does not change with clip length. At 0.4 s, 2 s, and 6 s I get the same two audio chunks of equal token size, so this is not the encoder windowing a long clip into slices. It is the same clip encoded twice.

## What I expected

One audio input should produce one audio chunk and one encode pass.

The CLI prints the expected experimental-audio warning at startup (discussion #13759), so this may already be known as part of the audio path still being experimental. Filing it with a minimal repro in case it is not tracked. The transcription itself works, the clip is just encoded one time too many.

### Name and Version

version: 0.3.0-dev (build 10706, commit 0190529ec)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64

### Operating systems

Mac

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-cli

### Command line

```shell
bash repro_invalid_media_exit_code.sh
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Invalid Media Exit Code

I used commit: 0190529ec450659b541ff608449401e68c27d098.
And reproducible Command is:

```bash 
bash repro_invalid_media_exit_code.sh

```
The script intentionally returns a non-zero status upon successful reproduction to facilitate automated testing and problem capture.

Confirmed:

```text
BAD-002 exit_code=0
BAD-002 decoder_error=yes
BAD-002 BUG_REPRODUCED: decoder error returned success
BAD-003 exit_code=0
BAD-003 decoder_error=yes
BAD-003 BUG_REPRODUCED: decoder error returned success
BAD-MISSING exit_code=0
BAD-MISSING staging_error=yes
BAD-MISSING BUG_REPRODUCED: staging error returned success
reproduced_cases=3

```

Comparison: `llama-mtmd-cli` returns exit code 1 when reading the same 0-byte PNG. Therefore, the problem is not that libmtmd cannot express failure, but that the standard `llama-cli` does not propagate failure to the process exit status.

Code path:

1. `cli_context::generate_completion()` returns `false` on HTTP/stream errors.

2. `cli_context::run()` calls it but ignores the return value.

3. `--single-turn` then ends the loop.

4. `cli_context::run()` always returns 0.

Additionally, when a non-existent media file is specified on the command line, `stage_media_file()` returns failure, but the current loop will continue processing text prompts without images. The reproduction script includes this comparison.

Potential minimal behavior design:

- `--single-turn`: Returns 1 on media staging, requesting, or generating failures.

- Interactive mode: Displays errors and preserves the session, allowing the user to correct their input; a single failed request should not be treated as a failure of the entire interactive process.

This bug is unrelated to the model and can be reproduced with any multimodal model. Such as:
```
llama-cli -hf ggml-org/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF \
  --audio /path/to/does-not-exist.wav \
  -p "test" -n 1 --no-warmup --simple-io --single-turn
echo "exit code: $?"   # print 0, but already printed: "Error: file does not exist or cannot be opened"
```

AI usage disclosure: I used an AI assistant to help troubleshoot this bug. I personally reproduced and verified this behavior and also understand the relevant code.

The repro_invalid_media_exit_code.sh file is:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -uo pipefail

llama_cli="${LLAMA_CLI:-./build/bin/llama-cli}"

if [[ ! -x "$llama_cli" ]]; then
    echo "llama-cli not found or not executable: $llama_cli" >&2
    exit 2
fi

if ! probe_tmp_dir="$(mktemp -d -t qwen3-vl-invalid-media.XXXXXX)"; then
    echo "failed to create temporary directory" >&2
    exit 2
fi

cleanup() {
    rm -rf -- "$probe_tmp_dir"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

bug_count=0

run_case() {
    local case_id="$1"
    local input_file="$2"
    local output_file="$probe_tmp_dir/$case_id.log"

    "$llama_cli" \
        -hf Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M \
        --image "$input_file" \
        -p "Report whether the media loaded." \
        -ngl all \
        -c 4096 \
        -n 1 \

        --reasoning off \
        --simple-io \
        --single-turn >"$output_file" 2>&1
    local status=$?

    else
        echo "$case_id decoder_error=no"
    fi

    if [[ "$status" -eq 0 ]] && grep -q "Error: Failed to load image or audio file" "$output_file"; then
        echo "$case_id BUG_REPRODUCED: decoder error returned success"
        bug_count=$((bug_count + 1))
    fi
}

run_missing_case() {
    local output_file="$probe_tmp_dir/BAD-MISSING.log"

    "$llama_cli" \
        -hf Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M \

        --no-warmup \

items.title: Misc. bug: Media loading failed and exit code 0 in llama-cli.

items.body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.2.0-dev (build 10618, commit eb25b7263)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64

### Operating systems

Mac

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library), llama-cli

### Command line

```shell
llama-mtmd-cli -hf ggml-org/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF --audio 30s.wav -p "T." -n 1 --no-warmup
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When the audio duration is an exact multiple of 30 seconds (or falls within approximately 20ms of the end of a 30-second cycle), the Whisper audio preprocessor generates an extra audio chunk and encodes it separately. This additional chunk consists entirely of trailing padding (silence) and contains no actual audio. In the logs, this manifests as `total = 4` instead of `total = 3` (or `5` instead of `4` for 60-second audio), resulting in an extra encoding operation taking about 550ms.

The Mel spectrogram has approximately 3,001 frames of padding appended to the end. The chunking logic slices the audio every 3,000 frames. When the number of actual audio frames is a multiple of 3,000 (or exactly one less), this padding fills a complete 3,000-frame window; consequently, it is encoded as a normal chunk rather than being discarded. The "skip last incomplete chunk" check in the code (`if (n_len < frames_per_chunk) break;`) only catches incomplete padding chunks; it fails to catch padding chunks that fill a complete window. (Location: `mtmd_audio_preprocessor_whisper::preprocess` in `tools/mtmd/mtmd-audio.cpp`, lines ~597–601.)

The transcription output is unaffected—I compared the output before and after the fix, and it is byte-identical. Therefore, this is a performance and context-usage issue, not a correctness one.The cost is an extra ~187 context tokens (all silence) and ~550ms of encoding time per instance. While the hit rate might appear low (random durations have a ~0.067% chance), slicing long audio into fixed 30-second segments is a common practice in speech processing pipelines, meaning such callers would trigger this issue for every segment.

Based on the code, the `qwen3a` and `gemma4a` preprocessors in the same file already use the "number of valid frames" as the upper bound for the loop and do not suffer from this issue; only the Whisper preprocessor uses the "total length including padding."

I believe the fix is ​​to have the chunking loop terminate when the remaining frames consist entirely of padding (by using the number of valid audio frames as the upper bound). The change is minimal, and I am willing to submit a PR, but I would like to confirm first if the maintainers agree with this approach.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Create a 16 kHz mono WAV whose length is exactly 480000 samples (30.00 s).
2. Run: llama-mtmd-cli -hf ggml-org/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF --audio 30s.wav -p "T." -n 1 --no-warmup
3. The log shows the audio encoded twice (total = 4) instead of once (total = 3).

Observed on my machine (M2 Max, macOS), by audio duration:
| duration     | samples | chunks encoded | expected |
|--------------|---------|----------------|----------|
| 29.98963 s   | 479834  | 1              | 1  OK    |
| 29.99 s      | 479840  | 2              | 1  BUG   |
| 30.00 s      | 480000  | 2              | 1  BUG   |
| 30.01 s      | 480160  | 2              | 2  OK    |
| 60.00 s      | 960000  | 3              | 2  BUG   |
| 90.00 s      | 1440000 | 4              | 3  BUG   |

AI usage disclosure: I used an AI assistant to help troubleshoot this bug and draft this report. I personally reproduced and verified the crash and also understand the relevant code.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. Related to #26536 (which fixed a similar duplicate-chunk problem for
short inputs) but on a different boundary: that fix changed min_samples; this case is
the chunk-splitting loop treating a full window of trailing padding as a real chunk.

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>
<!-- Copy-pasted short logs go into the "console" area here -->

```console
encoding mtmd batch, n_chunks = 1 (done = 1, total = 4)
mtmd batch encoding done in 557 ms
encoding mtmd batch, n_chunks = 1 (done = 2, total = 4)
mtmd batch encoding done in 553 ms
```
</details>

items.title: mtmd: audio with a duration that is a multiple of 30s produces one extra silent chunk

items.body:
### Name and Version

version: 0.2.0-dev (build 10618, commit eb25b7263)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64

### Operating systems

Mac

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library), llama-cli, llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -hf ggml-org/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF --port 18080 -c 4096
# Then send a request to /v1/chat/completions with a single-sample WAV file provided as input_audio.
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When a WAV file containing is exactly one sample, the process aborts at mtmd.cpp:1553 GGML_ASSERT(buf.size() > sizeof(float)). Because one float occupies 4 bytes, the buffer size is also 4 bytes, the condition evaluates to false (4 > 4 is false). 
I verified the crash on Voxtral; the assertion sits on the shared path before the per-model preprocessor is selected, so it should affect all audio models.
The Whisper preprocessor is designed to zero-pad very short audio clips. Therefore, regardless of whether such extremely short input should ultimately be accepted or result in an error, a single request should not trigger an assertion that kills the entire server process. The erroneous assertion causes the entire server process to abort instead of returning an error for the request.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Build any recent master with audio-capable mtmd.
2. Create a 1-sample 16 kHz mono WAV (see attached script).
3. Feed it to llama-mtmd-cli, or POST it to llama-server as input_audio.
4. CLI aborts with exit code 134; the server process dies and /health stops responding.

AI usage disclosure: I used an AI assistant to help troubleshoot this bug and draft this report. I personally reproduced and verified the crash and also understand the relevant code.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. The assertion is long-standing and was not touched by the recent
short-input fix (#26536), which changed min_samples inside the preprocessor but
not this buffer-size guard at the tokenizer entry.

### Relevant log output

items.title: mtmd: one-sample audio input causes process abort

items.body:
## Overview

Audio preprocessor padded all inputs under 31 sec up to the full 31 sec. This when combined with the spectrogram's 30 sec trailing padding, caused the short audio file to produce about 61 sec of frames, which resulted in an unnecessary extra padding only chunk sent to the encoder. 
My fix changes the minimum input length to 201 samples (exact minimum for FFT reflection padding), which ensures short audio generates only necessary chunks and saves computation.

items.body:
Converting Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507 (HF format, has tekken.json but no tokenizer.json) with plain `python convert_hf_to_gguf.py models/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507 --outfile out.gguf --outtype q8_0` dies with:

```
  File "conversion/base.py", line 1344, in get_vocab_base
    vocab_size = self.hparams.get("vocab_size", len(tokenizer.vocab))
AttributeError: 'MistralCommonTokenizer' object has no attribute 'vocab'
```

The tekken branch in `LlamaModel.set_vocab` (conversion/llama.py, ~line 108) is missing a `return`:

```python
        if self.is_mistral_format:
            return self._set_vocab_mistral()

        path_tekken_json = self.dir_model / "tekken.json"
        path_tokenizer_json = self.dir_model / "tokenizer.json"
        if path_tekken_json.is_file() and not path_tokenizer_json.is_file():
            self._set_vocab_mistral()      # <- falls through
```

so after the mistral vocab is written successfully, it continues into the sentencepiece → llama_hf → gpt2 ladder and gpt2 chokes on the MistralCommonTokenizer wrapper. The `is_mistral_format` branch right above does return, and `conversion/mistral.py` has nothing after its `_set_vocab_mistral()` call either, so the fall-through looks like an oversight (it's been there since #14737 and survived the #17114 file split). Adding `return` fixes the conversion for me and the resulting q8_0 works fine.

items.body:
## Overview

Tokenizing / preprocessing multimodal input is much more CPU-intensive than tokenizing, because it runs on single thread. This can be wasteful if the user just want to count the number of tokens occupied by an image/audio chunk, without actually using the underlay data.

This PR allow create a "placeholder" bitmap that only contains the dimension, no data buffer will be allocated. Preprocessing ops (i.e. image manipulation) will skip processing it

New server APIs are also added to demonstrate this (support counting both tools input tokens and multimodal input tokens)
- `/v1/chat/completions/input_tokens`
- `/v1/responses/input_tokens`

In next PRs:
- Skip preprocess audio
- Move std/mean f32 to cgraph
- Update for places where `process_mtmd_prompt` is being used for counting tokens

## Overview

Supersede https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24300

Also fix https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/24380

Add a generic batching API to mtmd and wire it up to `llama-server`, the goal is to speed up llava-uhd-style models and at the same time, improve video processing speed

Current state:
- `llama-server` can use it correctly
- mtmd API implement is mock up, need to implement the proper logic

TODO:
- [x] add notion of max batch size in mtmd
- [x] add CLI argument for it
- [x] `mtmd_batch_add_chunk` should only accept input with same size
- [x] wire up `mtmd_batch_encode` to use the 4th batch dim, added via #24352 
- [x] blacklist / whitelist models that can support it --> maybe only support `build_vit()` models for now
- update `mtmd-cli` to use batching API --> skip, we don't actually need that

## How it works

1. create a new `mtmd_batch` object
2. call `mtmd_batch_add_chunk` until it returns an error (either batch is full or current chunk can't be batched)
3. call `mtmd_batch_encode` on the batch
4. get the encoded embeddings via `mtmd_batch_get_output_embd`

items.body:
## Overview

- Add a new mtmd API: `mtmd_image_tokens_get_decoder_pos()`
- Deprecate `mtmd_image_tokens_get_nx/ny()`

## Additional information

Target support https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/21045

The mentioned PR proposes a new API `mtmd_image_tokens_get_n_prefix` which is not very flexible. `mtmd_image_tokens_get_decoder_pos` addresses this issue by providing non-linear t,x,y positions for each of the token.

In the case of falcon-ocr, `mtmd_image_tokens_get_decoder_pos` returns linear temporal `t` and x=0;y=0 for the first few text tokens, then switch to spatial position for image tokens:
- `<|image_cls|>`: t=0,x=0,y=0
- `<|image_reg_1|>`: t=1,x=0,y=0
- ...
- `<|image_reg_4|>`: t=4,x=0,y=0
- image patch 0: t=5,x=0,y=0
- image patch 1: t=5,x=1,y=0
- ...
- image patch N: t=5,x=nx,y=ny

items.body:
The goal of this PR is to allow more audio pre-processing mechanism to be added into mtmd

While the code is not very clean, this should already allow:
- Simplify https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/17694
- Potentially support gemma 3n audio

---

## Key points

- Each model's preprocessor now have their own subclass extended from `mtmd_audio_preprocessor`
- Preprocessor can access hparams directly (to read audio params like n_mel, n_fft, etc)
- Each preprocessor also have its own `initialize()` function which will be called on model load, to initialize global cache entries like sin/cos, hann window
- Filter bank is now constructed dynamically thanks to @tdakhran 's implementation of `fill_mel_filterbank_matrix` (the hard-coded value is now removed)

items.body:
Some models like deepseek-ocr (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/17400), gemma3n (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/17961) and LFM2-audio (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/17694) adds quite a lot of code into `clip.cpp` making it hard to track changes.

This PR moves cgraph builder of all vision/audio models into their own file, mirroring the recent refactoring in `libllama` by @pwilkin 

### Migration guide for pending PRs

1. Create a new file under `mtmd/models/your_model.cpp`
2. Implement the code inside newly created file (simply copy your existing `build_*()` function from `clip.cpp` into here)  
   NOTE: You won't be able to access `clip_ctx` directly from here. However, you can add custom fields into `clip_graph` and modify its constructor inside `clip.cpp` to copy fields into `clip_graph`
4. Add class definition into `models.h`
5. Modify `clip_image_build_graph()` in `clip.cpp` to use the new cgraph

items.title: Feature Request: Add Voxtral Realtime

items.body:
Add full support for the Mistral Voxtral Mini 4B Realtime 2602 model, including:

- Causal audio encoder with sliding window attention (window=750), causal conv1d stem, RoPE, SwiGLU FFN, RMSNorm, and 4x stacking
- Voxtral-specific mel spectrogram preprocessor (Slaney scale, fixed-max normalization, streaming padding)
- Dual-stream inference protocol combining audio and text embeddings
- Adaptive RMSNorm (precomputed ada_scale) in the text decoder
- Streaming CLI tool (llama-voxtral-stream) with real-time microphone input via miniaudio, chunked processing, and ring buffer
- GGUF conversion support for Mistral-format Voxtral weights (two-file output: text model + mmproj encoder)
- New tensor types: FFN_ADA_NORM_UP, FFN_ADA_NORM_DOWN
- Tied embeddings handling for the text decoder

*Make sure to read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting a PR*

items.body:
## Summary

Full support for [Voxtral Mini 4B Realtime](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602) (February 2026), Mistral's streaming speech-to-text model, including a new OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint.

Pre-quantized GGUFs: https://huggingface.co/chris0173/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602-GGUF

### What's included

**1. Audio encoder + GGUF conversion** (`convert_hf_to_gguf.py`, `mtmd/`)
- `VoxtralRealtimeEncoderModel` for Mistral-format mmproj conversion
- Causal transformer encoder (sliding window 750, RoPE, SwiGLU, RMSNorm)
- Precomputed `ada_rms_norm_t_cond` at conversion time (zero runtime overhead)
- `PROJECTOR_TYPE_VOXTRAL_REALTIME` with Whisper-compatible mel params

**2. Dual-stream transcription** (`mtmd-helper.cpp`, `mtmd-cli.cpp`)
- `mtmd_helper_eval_voxtral_realtime()` implements the dual-stream protocol
- Audio + text embeddings summed at each position (not prepended like other models)
- Token embedding table loaded from GGUF for the summation
- Full autoregressive decode with greedy sampling
- CLI support: `llama-mtmd-cli --image audio.wav -p "Transcribe"`

**3. Server endpoint** (`tools/server/`)
- `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` — OpenAI Whisper-compatible API
- Supports both `multipart/form-data` (standard) and JSON with base64 (fallback)
- New task type `SERVER_TASK_TYPE_AUDIO_TRANSCRIPTION`
- Follows EMBEDDING pattern: process at DONE_PROMPT, clear KV cache, release slot
- Resolves feature request #15291

### Usage

```bash
# 1. Convert from Mistral format
python3 convert_hf_to_gguf.py /path/to/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602 \
    --outfile voxtral-4b-rt-Q8_0.gguf --outtype q8_0 --mistral-format
python3 convert_hf_to_gguf.py /path/to/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602 \
    --outfile mmproj-voxtral-4b-rt-F16.gguf --outtype f16 --mmproj --mistral-format

# 2a. CLI transcription
llama-mtmd-cli \
    -m voxtral-4b-rt-Q8_0.gguf \
    --mmproj mmproj-voxtral-4b-rt-F16.gguf \
    -ngl 99 \
    -c 8192 \
    --image audio.flac \
    -p "Transcribe this audio." \
    -n 512

# 2b. Server mode
llama-server \
    -m voxtral-4b-rt-Q8_0.gguf \
    --mmproj mmproj-voxtral-4b-rt-F16.gguf \
    -ngl 99 \
    -c 8192 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8080

# 3. Transcription API (OpenAI Whisper-compatible)
# multipart/form-data (standard)
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/audio/transcriptions \
    -F file=@audio.flac \
    -F language=en

# JSON with base64 (alternative)
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/audio/transcriptions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"file":"<base64-encoded-audio>","format":"wav","language":"en"}'
```

Response format:
```json
{"task":"transcribe","language":"en","duration":0.0,"text":"Let him come in then, said the king..."}
```

### Resource requirements

- **VRAM**: ~5.5 GB (3.5 GB text Q8_0 + 2 GB mmproj F16)
- **RAM**: 8 GB recommended (model loading + audio processing)
- **GPU**: any CUDA-capable GPU (tested on RTX 3090)

### Testing

Tested on RTX 3090 with LibriSpeech (7127-75946-0002.flac):

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Audio encode | 169 ms |
| Decode speed | 145 tok/s |
| Total latency | ~6.6 s (for 15s audio) |

Deployed and verified on a Kubernetes cluster with ArgoCD GitOps.

### Dual-stream protocol (architecture note)

Unlike standard multimodal models that prepend media embeddings, Voxtral Realtime **sums** audio and text embeddings at each position:

```
Standard:   [audio_embeddings] [text_tokens] → decoder
Voxtral RT: audio_embd[i] + tok_embd[prompt[i]] → decoder (at every position)
```

This enables streaming with <500ms latency. The prefix consists of `[BOS] + [PAD×32] + [DELAY×6]` = 39 tokens.

### Related

- Feature request (Voxtral RT): #19696
- Previous attempt: #19698 (feedback incorporated — no new binary, no mic, no streaming)
- Feature request (audio endpoint): #15291
- Supersedes: #20625
- Based on work by @Acceldium, refactored into clean incremental changes

### What this does NOT include

- No new standalone binary
- No microphone capture / real-time streaming
- No changes to the generation loop for other models

items.body:
### Name and Version

Bionic bundled llama.cpp Vulkan 2.41.0 (crash) / 2.39.0 (ok); llama-server reports version 0.4.1-dev build 1 commit b49650a

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

2x Intel Arc Pro B50 (driver 32.0.101.8805) + Intel Core Ultra 5 235HX, 64GB RAM

### Models

All of these fail identically on 2.40/2.41 Vulkan, all load fine on 2.39 Vulkan:
- bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- unsloth/Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct-2512-GGUF (Q5_K_M)
- empero-ai/Qwen3.8-35B-A3B-Distill-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF (Q4_K_S)
- lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
Counter-case: nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (Q4_K_M) loads fine on 2.41 Vulkan.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## What happened

`llama-server` with the Vulkan backend crash-aborts while loading sliding-window-attention
decoder models when the KV cache is offloaded to the GPU. The process dies with
`exitCode=3221226505` (`0xC0000409`, fail-fast) before becoming healthy.

Exact abort line (stderr):

```text
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)
```

## Regression info

- ✅ `llama.cpp ... 2.39.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **loads in ~5s, serves fine**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.40.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ❌ `llama.cpp ... 2.41.0` (Vulkan, AVX2) — same model, `-ngl 99` — **aborts as above**
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with `--no-kv-offload` — **loads and serves** (KV cache on CPU)
- ✅ `2.41.0` Vulkan with full offload + embedding model (`nomic-embed-text-v1.5.Q4_K_M`,
  full attention, `--embedding`) — **loads and serves**

So it is not a globally broken Vulkan backend: it is the
`Vulkan + KV-cache GPU offload + SWA/hybrid-attention decoder` path that regressed
between 2.39 and 2.40.

## Repro

```bat
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf -ngl 99 --port 18081
```

- Model: `bartowski/mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-GGUF`, `Q4_K_S` (~2.4 GB)
- No other flags (all defaults). Crash happens during `load_model`, before listening.

Notable log lines on the crashing 2.41 run (before the abort):

```text
W resolve_fused_ops: layer 0 is assigned to device Vulkan1 but Flash Attention is assigned to device CPU (usually due to missing support)
W resolve_fused_ops: Flash Attention not supported, set to disabled
W ggml_vulkan: Failed to allocate pinned memory (Requested buffer size exceeds device buffer size limit: ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory)
```

On the working `--no-kv-offload` run the server reports `kv_unified = 'true'`,
`n_slots = 4`, then `model loaded` / `listening`.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 x64 (build 10.0.26200)
- GPU: Intel Arc Pro B50 (discrete) + Intel integrated Graphics
- Driver: Intel `32.0.101.8805` (06.07.2026), `vulkan-1.dll` present (system + app dir)
- Builds: LM Studio / Bionic bundled `llama.cpp-win-x86_64-vulkan-avx2` packs
  `2.39.0` (working) vs `2.40.0` / `2.41.0` (crashing), CPU 14 threads
- The same setup serves the models fine on engine 2.39, so driver / loader / model
  file are ruled out

## Suspected area

New fused-ops / unified-KV graph building for SWA models (`cache_k` pre-allocation
landing in a Vulkan buffer that reports no supported op) introduced between 2.39
and 2.40. Happy to test any debug build / extra logging on this machine
(Arc Pro B50 available).

### First Bad Commit

Regressed between bundled builds 2.39.0 (works) and 2.40.0 (broken). Exact upstream commit unknown — these are third-party Bionic/LM Studio bundles, not direct llama.cpp builds. Happy to bisect if given build instructions for Windows Vulkan.

### Relevant log output


Command:
llama-server.exe -m mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf --port 18081 -ngl 99

Log:
load_model: loading model '.../mistralai_Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507-Q4_K_S.gguf'
llm-engine\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-backend.cpp:941: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0) in a buffer (Vulkan1) that cannot run the operation (NONE)

Process exits immediately with code 3221226505 (0xC0000409).

items.body:
Some models like deepseek-ocr (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/17400), gemma3n (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/17961) and LFM2-audio (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/17694) adds quite a lot of code into `clip.cpp` making it hard to track changes.

This PR moves cgraph builder of all vision/audio models into their own file, mirroring the recent refactoring in `libllama` by @pwilkin 

### Migration guide for pending PRs

1. Create a new file under `mtmd/models/your_model.cpp`
2. Implement the code inside newly created file (simply copy your existing `build_*()` function from `clip.cpp` into here)  
   NOTE: You won't be able to access `clip_ctx` directly from here. However, you can add custom fields into `clip_graph` and modify its constructor inside `clip.cpp` to copy fields into `clip_graph`
4. Add class definition into `models.h`
5. Modify `clip_image_build_graph()` in `clip.cpp` to use the new cgraph

items.body:
## Description

This PR aims to enhance the integration of Mistral models with llama.cpp by addressing several key issues and introducing new features. Here are the details:

### Context

- The current HF conversion to GGUF does not work directly for Mistral models due to our format that is vLLM based. This means that we have to first convert weights to Hugging Face then to GGUF which is not ideal and can lead to conversion errors if the first conversion is not done correctly. It also means that adding new models to the llama.cpp ecosystem requires first adding them to Transformers.
- We do not support chat templates natively which means chat templates are community based and not guaranteed to work correctly.
- We are using [mistral-common](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-common) internally for tokenization and want the community to use it to unlock full capacities of our models. As mistral-common is a Python library, we have opened a [PR](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-common/pull/113) to add a REST API via FastAPI to make it easier for users who are not in the Python ecosystem.

### Using mistral-common with llama.cpp

We recommend that users only use the `llama-server` tool with the `/completions` route of the server for now, as it is the only one that supports tokens input. We also advise users to set `return_tokens=True` in their requests to let `mistral-common` handle detokenization.

### Added features

1. Model conversion:

We have added a script to convert Mistral models to GGUF directly from Hugging Face. This script is located at `convert_mistral_to_gguf.py` and can be used to convert Mistral models to GGUF format.

2. Model architecture:

We registered the Mistral architecture in llama.cpp to support Mistral models natively. This allows users to use Mistral models with llama.cpp without having to convert them to Hugging Face first.

### Known Limitations:

Our approach does not support multimodality:
- mistral-common handles processing multimodal data but they cannot be passed to llama.cpp via the route.
- llama.cpp only supports multimodality via chat templates, which we do not support.

Also this approach requires users to only use the llama.cpp server with the `/completions` route.

## Example Code

To get started, install mistral-common using the following command:

#### (Optional) Convert the model

```python
HF_TOKEN=... python convert_mistral_to_gguf.py \
mistralai/Devstral-Small-2505 --remote --ctx-train 131072 --outtype bf16
```

#### Launch the mistral-common and llama.cpp servers

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-common.git@improve_llama_cpp_integration[server]
```

Launch the mistral-common server:

```bash
HF_TOKEN=... mistral_common mistralai/Devstral-Small-2505 --port 6000
```

Launch the llama.cpp server:

```bash
./build/bin/llama-server -m models/Devstral-Small-2505-Q4_K_M.gguf --port 8080
```

#### Use the servers

Here is a code snippet demonstrating how to use the new features:

```python
import requests

mistral_common_url = "http://127.0.0.1:6000"
llama_cpp_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8080"

def tokenize(messages, url):
    response = requests.post(f"{url}/tokenize/messages", json=messages)
    return response.json()

def detokenize(tokens, url):
    response = requests.post(f"{url}/detokenize", json={"tokens": tokens})
    return response.json()

def detokenize_message(tokens, url):
    response = requests.post(f"{url}/detokenize", json={"tokens": tokens, "as_message": True})
    return response.json()

def generate(tokens, url):
    response = requests.post(f"{url}/completions", json={
        "prompt": tokens,
        "stream": False,
        "return_tokens": True
    })
    return response.json()

messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are Devstral a cool coding agent that can help users with their coding needs."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Who are you and what can you do?"}
]

tokens = tokenize(messages, mistral_common_url)
print(tokens)

generated = generate(tokens, llama_cpp_url)["tokens"]
print(generated)

detokenized = detokenize(generated, mistral_common_url)
print(detokenized)

detokenized_message = detokenize_message(generated, mistral_common_url)
print(detokenized_message)
```

## Feedback and Contributions

We believe these changes will significantly improve the integration of Mistral models with llama.cpp and provide a better experience for our users. We welcome any feedback or suggestions to further enhance this integration. Also, as we have few experience in the codebase of llama.cpp, we welcome any help to improve the integration and make sure we respect the codebase and the community.

items.body:
## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

Linux

### GGML backends

Vulkan

items.title: Eval bug: Speculative decoding (draft-mtp / draft-dspark): greedy output diverges from vanilla on quantized targets

items.body:
## Environment

- **llama.cpp**: master `8144f31` (2026-08-23) + also reproduced on release b10488 (Windows CUDA 13.3 build)
- **OS**: Windows 11 26200 + WSL2 Ubuntu 22.04 (both tested, same cliff)
- **GPU**: RTX 4080 SUPER 16GB, driver 591.86 (CUDA 13.1), nvcc 13.1, sm_89
- **Model**: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` UD-Q3_K_XL (12.2GB); also reproduced with UD-IQ4_XS (13.3GB) and IQ4_XS (14.6GB)
- **Backend**: CUDA, single GPU

## Symptom

With the model **fully resident on GPU** (zero "assigned to device CPU" lines, verified in logs), decode (tg) speed collapses non-linearly once the KV position exceeds roughly 80K tokens — from ~33 t/s at 68K position to **1.4 t/s (714 ms/token) at 91K position**, or outright timeouts. **Prompt processing (pp) stays fast (~1300 t/s) at the same positions.** Zero-context decode is normal (~38-39 t/s) on every configuration below.

## Reproduction matrix (WSL2, llama-server)

Command shape:
```
./llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q3_K_XL.gguf \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -ngl 999 --load-mode none \
    -c <CTX> [-fa on] -ctk <Q> -ctv <Q>
```
Then send a chat completion with a ~91K-token filler prompt and `max_tokens=100`.

| Config | VRAM fit (CPU overrides) | pp @91K fill | tg @91K position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-c 131072 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits, 0 CPU lines | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0` | fits | ~1300 t/s | **1.4 t/s** |
| `-c 98304  -fa on -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` | fits | fast | **timed out (>25 min)** |
| `-c 98304  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **timed out** |
| `-c 73728  (no FA) -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` | fits | fast | **33.1 t/s @ 68K position ✅** |

Position sweep with the last config (UD-Q3_K_XL, q8 KV, no FA):

| KV position (prompt tokens) | decode t/s (server-side timing) |
|---|---|
| 45,574 | 35.6 |
| 60,309 | 33.9 |
| 68,642 | 33.1 |
| 91,077 | **1.4 (or timeout)** |

## Key observations

1. **The cliff is positional, not a memory-spill issue.** All 96K/128K configs above report 0 CPU tensor overrides and normal free VRAM headroom; KV quantization level (q4/q5/q8) and `-fa on/off` make no difference to the cliff. Only the *position* matters.
2. **pp is unaffected at the same positions** (~1300 t/s for the 91K fill), so this is specific to the decode path.
3. The drop is far steeper than any plausible O(n) attention-scan cost: 68K→91K position is a 1.34x context increase but a **~24x decode slowdown**.
4. Server logs at the cliff show `eval time = 1055.41 ms / 300 tokens (0.95 tokens per second)` with `graphs reused = 298`, i.e. CUDA graph reuse continues normally while per-token latency explodes.
5. Also reproduced on the same hardware under Windows native (b10488) at large `-c`, so it is not WSL2-specific.

## Suspected area

Decode-path attention over long KV for the hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full-attention layers (Qwen3.8 / qwen35-family). Possibly a fallback/slow kernel engaged past some KV extent threshold. Possibly related family: #27442 (empty generation >16K on Metal for qwen35moe hybrids), #27572 (draft acceptance collapse with multi-ubatch batches).

## Logs

Full `llama-server` logs for the 131072/q4/FA and 73728/q8/no-FA runs available on request (happy to attach — they contain per-token timing lines, tensor placement, and KV buffer sizes).
items.title: Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid Gated DeltaNet): decode throughput collapses ~25x at context positions >~80K while prompt processing stays fast

### Git commit

`7fe450e19305b828c199d602c23a8337aaa1f03b` (v0.5.0). Also reproduces on master `6b790a9c29`.

### Operating systems

Linux, Other? (Please let us know in description)

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Since #24406, the Vulkan backend no longer builds when `glslc` does not support `GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix`. The CMake feature test detects this correctly (`-- GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix not supported by glslc`), but two new shaders are compiled as coopmat variants unconditionally anyway, so `vulkan-shaders-gen` fails.

`vulkan-shaders-gen.cpp`:

```cpp
string_to_spv("fa_decode_ph1", "flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp", {}, true, true, false, false);
string_to_spv("fa_decode_ph2", "flash_attn_decode_phase_2.comp", {}, true, true, false, false);
```

These have no `#if defined(GGML_VULKAN_COOPMAT_GLSLC_SUPPORT)` guard. The pipeline creation in `ggml-vulkan.cpp` that references `fa_decode_ph1_cm1_data` / `fa_decode_ph2_cm1_data` (the Intel Xe `pipeline_xe_fa_decode_dual_phases` loop) isn't guarded either. Every other `_cm1` shader and pipeline sits behind that macro, so a coopmat-less glslc was a working configuration before this change. See #10785 / #11052 for the same class of break fixed earlier.

This affects any toolchain whose glslc predates `GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix`. One example is the Android NDK's bundled glslc: NDK r28 (`28.2.13676358`) and r29 (`29.0.14206865`) both report `shaderc v2022.3`. Android cross-builds with `GGML_VULKAN=ON` commonly pass that glslc as `Vulkan_GLSLC_EXECUTABLE`.

Minimal reproduction with the shader alone (same invocation as `vulkan-shaders-gen`):

```sh
$ANDROID_NDK/shader-tools/<host>/glslc -fshader-stage=compute --target-env=vulkan1.2 \
  ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/vulkan-shaders/flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp -o /dev/null
```

A likely fix is to guard both `string_to_spv` calls with `#if defined(GGML_VULKAN_COOPMAT_GLSLC_SUPPORT)`. The Xe dual-phase pipeline creation (or its registration) would get the same guard, so those devices fall back to the regular FA path when the shaders aren't built.

### First Bad Commit

4ceb17191 (vulkan: add Intel Xe flash attention optimization kernels (2/3, Xe-LPG Plus/Xe2/Xe3) (#24406))

### Compile command

```shell
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$ANDROID_NDK/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake \
  -DANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a -DANDROID_PLATFORM=android-28 \
  -DGGML_VULKAN=ON -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
  -DVulkan_GLSLC_EXECUTABLE=$ANDROID_NDK/shader-tools/linux-x86_64/glslc
cmake --build build --target ggml-vulkan
```

### Relevant log output

```shell
-- GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix not supported by glslc
...
FAILED: [code=1] .../flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp.cpp
glslc -fshader-stage=compute --target-env=vulkan1.2 .../vulkan-shaders/flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp -o .../fa_decode_ph1_cm1.spv ...
flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp:11: warning: '#extension' : extension not supported: GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix
flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp:115: error: 'coopmat' : undeclared identifier
flash_attn_decode_phase_1.comp:115: error: '' :  syntax error, unexpected COMMA, expecting LEFT_PAREN
FAILED: [code=1] .../flash_attn_decode_phase_2.comp.cpp
flash_attn_decode_phase_2.comp:118: error: 'coopmat' : undeclared identifier
```

## Overview

**Co-authors:** @jxia4intel, @sliu39

**PR 2/3** of the Intel Xe optimization series — see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24408 (mega PR, draft) for the full feature set.

**Target platforms:** Xe-LPG Plus, Xe2, Xe3

This PR adds Intel Xe-specific flash attention optimization kernels for both ARLH iGPU (Xe1, UMA, coopmat1) and Xe2/Xe3. Dependency: builds on top of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24404 (Xe-LPG Plus coopmat1 enable). Independent of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24407 (GEMM+CW).

### Flash Attention (Intel Xe)

- New Vulkan shaders: single-phase prefill (`flash_attn_hdim64/96/128`) and two-phase split prefill/decode variants
- Pipelines keyed by `(head_dim, gqa_ratio)` for runtime dispatch across various GQA ratios without combinatorial pipeline proliferation
- Supports non-power-of-two GQA ratios via subgroup splitting (`qk_groups`)
- Intel Xe1 (integrated GPU, UMA, cooperative matrix) and Xe2 paths with separate warptile tuning
- Two-phase decode splits softmax reduction across subgroups; shared QK state copy (`fa_copy_qstate`) between prefill phases

items.body: ## Overview This is a port of the existing CUDA graph code to SYCL. The code is mostly a straight port with two SYCL-specific exceptions: 1. The data must be reordered before recording because while SYCL async memory allocation extensions are available, using them leads to a hang during graph recording. 2. The library GEMM functions don't work with graph recording because it throws an exception: "Graph nodes cannot depend on events from outside the graph." This effectively limits the feature to decode for the time being. On A770 the performance improvement during decode is significant; on B70 it is negligible. Thus the feature remains off by default. ## Additional information While investigating performance differences on A770 between the Vulkan and SYCL backends, I found that kernel dispatch time consumed a large percentage of the SYCL time. The large difference was primarily due to the usage of the i915 driver. However there is still a modest gain with the xe driver. ### A770 performance comparison **xe driver** **i915 driver** ## Requirements - I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) - AI usage disclosure: YES. Claude was used to assist with the port from the CUDA backend.

items.body:
When ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft splits allocation on buft max_size, a view-only tail at the end of the context could skip the final alloc_tensor_range. Persistent views (e.g. KV k_stream / v_stream) were then left without ggml_backend_view_init.
Allocate only parent tensors in alloc_tensor_range and initialize all views in a final pass over the context after all splits complete.
## Overview
`ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft` can split a context across multiple buffers when a tensor would exceed the backend buffer-type `max_size` (for example Vulkan's default 1 GiB). If the remaining tail of the context contains only views, the final `alloc_tensor_range` may be skipped, so those views never get `ggml_backend_view_init`.
Persistent KV stream views (`layer.k_stream` / `v_stream`) then keep `tensor->data == NULL` while `view_src` is allocated. Host state save/restore later calls `ggml_backend_tensor_get` / `set` on those views and hits:
`GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated")`
This change:
- allocates only parent tensors inside each split range
- initializes all uninitialized views in one final pass over the context
Also adds `test_view_init_after_max_size_split` in `tests/test-alloc.cpp`
to cover the oversized-parent + view-only-tail case.
## Additional information
Fixes #19839
Fixes #23737
Fixes #21762

Related:
- #21576 (state-IO `!tensor->data` guards; complementary discussion)
I reproduced the assert with Qwen3.6-27B (MTP) when a parent KV tensor exceeded buft `max_size` and the context ended with a view-only tail.
Note on #21576: skipping tensors with `!tensor->data` avoids the assert, but can omit real KV still reachable via `view_src` and misalign the serialized state. This PR fixes the missing view init in the allocator instead.
Prior investigation commit (same patch on older master; kept for reference):
https://github.com/Yoshi4470/llama.cpp/commit/99655d5854e63e736a6a93280e01b7e785a59ba5
## Test plan
- [x] `test-alloc` (includes new `test_view_init_after_max_size_split`)
- [x] Vulkan A/B on the Qwen3.6-27B MTP speculative path (same command, 10 runs each):
  - before (`e3546c794`): 0/10 (assert every time)
  - after (this PR): 10/10 (no assert, completed normally)
- [x] Earlier `amdvlk64.dll` crash after the assert site was resolved by an AMD driver update; treated as separate from this allocator fix
- N/A: equivalent-size CPU repro (not practical on this machine)

### Command used for the A/B runs:
- Vulkan / AMDVLK, Windows, AMD Software 26.6.4
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)
```
llama-cli.exe -np 8 -c 2097152 --no-mmap -m models/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ctkd q4_0 -ctvd q4_0 \
--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 -p "Hello!"
```
## Requirements
- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - Cursor assisted with implementing the finalize-views pass and regression test after I identified the root cause in the alloc split path, and with local verification.
